short_description: What probability can and cannot contribute to the Langlands programme: Sato Tate laws, random walks on trees and isogeny graphs, Thorin measures and generalized gamma convolutions as reformulations of the Riemann hypothesis, and Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups, with code and data.
description:
This monograph asks what probability can contribute to the Langlands programme, and answers on two sides. The first is a limitation, proved in the opening chapter: no argument that sees only the limiting distribution of Frobenius data can detect automorphy, because equidistribution is a consequence of functoriality, not a route to it. The second is what probability does supply: consequences of the conjectures, calibration against data, and probabilistic reformulations.

The book covers Weyl's criterion and the Sato Tate law, random matrix models of the zeros of L functions, Kloosterman sums, random class groups and Selmer groups, Hecke operators as random walks on Bruhat Tits trees, hitting times on supersingular isogeny graphs, log correlated fields, and Bayesian inference for Sato Tate groups. At its centre is the Thorin framework: for a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the statement that the reciprocal of an even completion of its L function is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution. Later chapters turn the same devices on reciprocity, Fermat's last theorem, inverse Laplace transforms, random integers and the Poisson Dirichlet law, Hecke characters and Maass forms. These are reformulations: no new case of reciprocity and no Riemann hypothesis is proved.

Results new to the book include the limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs, the Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis and for the Ramanujan conjecture, the Thorin structure of Hecke passage times, an extreme value representation of the L functions of multiplicative eta products, the Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer, and a consistency theorem for the Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups. Open computational problems close every chapter, and the scripts and data behind the numbers are in the repository.

chapters.title: What Probability Can and Cannot Do
chapters.summary:
What can probability theory say about the Langlands programme? The chapter states the reciprocity and functoriality conjectures through Satake parameters and Frobenius conjugacy classes and isolates their probabilistic shadow: normalised Frobenius classes should be equidistributed for Haar measure on a compact Sato Tate group. Frobenius traces of two elliptic curves at the primes below ten million illustrate the semicircle law of the Sato Tate theorem and the law of a curve with complex multiplication, which has an atom at zero. The chapter's own results express a limitation: equidistribution does not determine automorphy. Altering an automorphic sequence of Hecke eigenvalues on an infinite set of primes of density zero leaves every limiting average unchanged, while Ramakrishnan's refinement of strong multiplicity one for GL(2) makes the altered sequence nonautomorphic. So each automorphic sequence has continuum many nonautomorphic impostors with the same limiting averages, and no function of the limiting empirical laws of the traces characterises automorphy. Probability therefore enters the programme through consequences of the conjectures, as calibration and as a source of reformulations, not as a method of proving reciprocity, and nothing in the chapter proves a case of reciprocity or functoriality. A roadmap matches the methods of the book to its five parts.

#### From the literature

Langlands' letter to Weil (Langlands 1967) and lectures (Langlands 1970); Artin reciprocity (Artin 1927); Weil's converse theorem (Weil 1967); modularity of elliptic curves over the rationals (Wiles 1995; Taylor and Wiles 1995; Breuil, Conrad, Diamond and Taylor 2001); the local Langlands correspondence for GL(n) (Harris and Taylor 2001; Henniart 2000); symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic newforms (Newton and Thorne 2021); Deligne's bound (Deligne 1974); the Sato Tate theorem (Clozel, Harris and Taylor 2008; Taylor 2008; Harris, Shepherd Barron and Taylor 2010; Barnet Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor 2011) through Serre's argument (Serre 1968); Hecke's equidistribution of the angles of a curve with complex multiplication (Hecke 1918); strong multiplicity one (Jacquet and Shalika 1981) and its refinement for GL(2) (Ramakrishnan 1994); converse theorems for GL(n) (Cogdell and Piatetski Shapiro 1994).

#### New results

Both results are the authors' own and are proved in full.

- [Equidistribution does not determine automorphy](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#equidistribution_does_not_determine_automorphy) (Proposition 1.5, page 7; proved): Sato Tate equidistribution of a sequence indexed by the primes cannot certify that it comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) with trivial central character, because altering such a sequence on an infinite set of primes of density zero leaves the limiting empirical averages of all continuous functions unchanged but, by Ramakrishnan's refinement of strong multiplicity one, makes it nonautomorphic, and continuum many equidistributed sequences are not automorphic. New in this book.
- [Statistics unchanged by density zero alterations cannot characterise automorphy](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#density_zero_invariant_statistics_cannot_detect_automorphy) (Corollary 1.6, page 8; proved): No statistic of sequences indexed by the primes that is unchanged when a sequence is altered on a set of primes of density zero, for instance any function of the limit points of its empirical laws, can tell an automorphic sequence from continuum many nonautomorphic ones. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Modular Forms and L Functions for Probabilists
chapters.summary:
How do modular forms and L functions look to a probabilist? The chapter develops, for probabilists, modular forms and cusp forms for SL(2,Z), Eisenstein series, Ramanujan's Delta function and tau function, Hecke operators and the Hecke relations (the three term recursion of the Chebyshev polynomials), Euler products, the Mellin transform and Hecke's functional equation, newforms of level N, Frobenius traces of elliptic curves and the Hasse bound, the modularity theorem, Dirichlet characters, and in outline automorphic representations of GL(n), standard and Rankin Selberg L functions and the generalized Ramanujan conjecture. It isolates two facts used throughout the book. By Deligne's theorem the normalised Hecke eigenvalues of a holomorphic newform are traces of elements of SU(2). The completed L function of Delta is the Mellin transform of the positive function Delta(iy), so its values on the central line, divided by the central value, form the characteristic function of a symmetric random variable, and the Riemann hypothesis for Delta says that this characteristic function has only real zeros. A heuristic of independent Sato Tate draws predicts that tau(p) vanishes for only finitely many primes, probably none (Lehmer's question). The chapter is expository and proves no new result.

#### From the literature

Multiplicativity and the prime power recursion of tau (Mordell 1917) and the Ramanujan bound (Deligne 1971, 1974); Hecke operators and Euler products (Hecke 1937); the functional equation of Delta and the converse theorem at level one (Hecke 1936), extended to level N (Weil 1967); newforms (Atkin and Lehner 1970); the Hasse bound (Hasse 1933 to 1936); modularity of elliptic curves over the rationals (Wiles 1995; Taylor and Wiles 1995; Breuil, Conrad, Diamond and Taylor 2001); standard L functions of GL(n) (Godement and Jacquet 1972); Rankin Selberg L functions (Jacquet, Piatetski Shapiro and Shalika 1983; Shahidi 1981; Moeglin and Waldspurger 1989; Jacquet and Shalika 1981); the Ramanujan conjecture in weight one (Deligne and Serre 1974) and the bound 7/64 for Maass forms (Kim and Sarnak 2003); Lehmer's question (Lehmer 1947) and the density zero of the primes with tau(p) equal to zero (Serre 1981).

#### New results

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

chapters.title: Galois Representations, Reciprocity and Functoriality
chapters.summary:
Which arithmetic objects lie behind the book's probabilistic statements, and which cases of the conjectures are proved? The Chebotarev density theorem is read as equidistribution of Frobenius classes for the uniform law on a finite Galois group. The chapter covers Artin L functions and the Artin conjecture, ℓ adic Galois representations and Serre's open image theorem, reciprocity for GL(1) (class field theory) and for GL(2) over the rationals (Galois representations of newforms and modularity), the Langlands dual group and the Satake isomorphism, functoriality and its known cases, the local Langlands correspondence, potential automorphy and the Sato Tate theorem, and Serre's Sato Tate group with the generalized Sato Tate conjecture. Computations for the S3 extension attached to the weight one form eta(z)eta(23z) of level 23 (the splitting field of x^3 minus x minus 1) at the primes below ten million show Chebotarev frequencies and a bias against completely split primes whose sign the prime squares explain. The chapter proves nothing new about reciprocity or functoriality.

#### From the literature

The Chebotarev density theorem (Chebotarev 1926), effective under the generalized Riemann hypothesis (Lagarias and Odlyzko 1977); Artin L functions (Artin 1924); the Artin conjecture in the tetrahedral and octahedral cases (Langlands 1980; Tunnell 1981) and for odd two dimensional representations (Khare and Wintenberger 2009; Kisin 2009); Serre's open image theorem (Serre 1972); Galois representations of newforms (Eichler 1954; Shimura 1971; Deligne 1971; Deligne and Serre 1974; Ribet 1977); the Satake isomorphism (Satake 1963); functoriality (Langlands 1970) for symmetric powers (Gelbart and Jacquet 1978; Kim and Shahidi 2002; Kim 2003; Newton and Thorne 2021), base change (Langlands 1980; Arthur and Clozel 1989), quaternion algebras (Jacquet and Langlands 1970) and tensor products (Ramakrishnan 2000; Kim and Shahidi 2002); the local Langlands correspondence for GL(n) (Harris and Taylor 2001; Henniart 2000; Scholze 2013); the Sato Tate theorem through potential automorphy (Clozel, Harris and Taylor 2008; Taylor 2008; Harris, Shepherd Barron and Taylor 2010; Barnet Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor 2011); Sato Tate groups (Serre 2012) and their classification for abelian surfaces (Fité, Kedlaya, Rotger and Sutherland 2012); Chebyshev's bias (Rubinstein and Sarnak 1994).

#### New results

chapters.title: Haar Measure, the Weyl Criterion and Sato Tate
chapters.summary:
Why does the Sato Tate law for elliptic curves follow from automorphy, and which part of the argument is probability? The chapter proves the Weyl equidistribution criterion on compact groups from the Peter Weyl theorem, computes Haar measure on SU(2) (semicircle law, Chebyshev polynomials as characters of the symmetric powers, Catalan moments), and gives Serre's proof, through the Wiener Ikehara Tauberian theorem, that the normalised Frobenius traces of a holomorphic newform of weight at least two with trivial character are Sato Tate distributed when every symmetric power L function is holomorphic and nonvanishing on Re s = 1. For newforms without complex multiplication, potential automorphy and symmetric power functoriality supply that hypothesis. For a CM elliptic curve the limit law is an atom at zero plus an arcsine law, the image of Haar measure on the normaliser of the torus, and its Weyl fingerprint (the limits of the Chebyshev averages) is one exactly at multiples of four. Joint Sato Tate for two curves over Q without complex multiplication that are not isogenous over the algebraic closure makes their traces agree only on a set of primes of density zero. The chapter proves no case of functoriality: automorphy is the input, equidistribution the output.

#### From the literature

- Weyl's criterion (Weyl 1916); the Peter Weyl theorem (Peter and Weyl 1927).
- The Sato Tate conjecture (Sato and Tate, in Tate 1965) and its reduction to symmetric power L functions (Serre 1968); the Wiener Ikehara theorem (Ikehara 1931; Wiener 1932).
- Sato Tate for elliptic curves over Q and newforms without complex multiplication (Clozel, Harris and Taylor 2008; Taylor 2008; Harris, Shepherd Barron and Taylor 2010; Barnet Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor 2011); symmetric power functoriality (Newton and Thorne 2021).
- CM curves and Hecke characters (Deuring 1953; Hecke 1918).
- Joint Sato Tate for curves that are not isogenous over the algebraic closure (Harris 2009).
- Vertical Sato Tate over finite fields (Birch 1968).

#### New results

The theorems are due to others; the chapter contributes the exposition, complete proofs of the probabilistic side and numerical checks over the primes below ten million.

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Frobenius Data: Statistics at Scale
chapters.summary:
How fast do the normalised Frobenius traces of an elliptic curve approach the Sato Tate law, what correction of size log x encodes the rank, and how often does a trace take a fixed value? The chapter computes traces by point counting for a curve without complex multiplication, a CM curve, Ramanujan's tau function, two hundred random curves and the Cremona curves 11a1, 37a1, 389a1 and 5077a1 of ranks 0 to 3. It relates the Kolmogorov discrepancy to Weyl sums, recalls that a square root rate would imply the Riemann hypothesis for every symmetric power L function, and compares the scaled discrepancy across curves with the Kolmogorov law of the Brownian bridge. Under the Riemann hypothesis for the symmetric powers, the explicit formula damps each fixed Chebyshev frequency below the scale of independent sampling, and the chapter conjectures that the scaled discrepancy tends to zero in logarithmic density. Under the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, E), the sums of a_p log p / p, divided by log x, tend in logarithmic mean to one half minus the analytic rank, a rank bias from the central zero and the prime squares. For the Lang Trotter conjecture it derives the heuristic, computes the constant of a Serre curve and counts supersingular primes. The data test the explicit formula, not the Birch and Swinnerton Dyer conjecture.

#### From the literature

- Point counting (Schoof 1985; Harvey 2014).
- The Erdős Turán inequality (Erdős and Turán 1948; Niederreiter 1991 for Sato Tate).
- The discrepancy conjecture and the Riemann hypothesis (Akiyama and Tanigawa 1999; Mazur 2008); effective Sato Tate (V. K. Murty 1985; Rouse and Thorner 2017; Thorner 2021).
- Limiting distributions (Kolmogorov 1933; Rubinstein and Sarnak 1994).
- Partial Euler products and the rank (Birch and Swinnerton Dyer 1965; Goldfeld 1982; Kuo and Murty 2005; Conrad 2005; Kim and Murty 2023).
- The Lang Trotter conjecture (Lang and Trotter 1976), with the open image theorem (Serre 1972), supersingular primes (Elkies 1987) and averages over families (Fouvry and Murty 1996; David and Pappalardi 1999).

#### New results

One conjecture, the logarithmic density form of the discrepancy at the square root scale, is the authors' own.

- [Sato Tate discrepancy vanishes at the square root scale in logarithmic density](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sato_tate_discrepancy_logarithmic_density_conjecture) (Conjecture 5.3, page 67; open): For an elliptic curve over the rationals without complex multiplication, the Kolmogorov distance between the empirical law of its first n normalised Frobenius traces and the Sato Tate law is conjectured to be, in logarithmic density, of smaller order than the inverse square root of n that independent sampling gives; the same conjecture records the rate conjectured by Akiyama and Tanigawa. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Frobenius traces, point counting, Schoof algorithm, Kolmogorov discrepancy, Sato Tate discrepancy, effective Sato Tate, Erdős Turán inequality, Akiyama Tanigawa conjecture, Brownian bridge, explicit formula, logarithmic density, rank bias, Birch and Swinnerton Dyer, Lang Trotter conjecture, supersingular primes, Serre curve

chapters.title: Random Matrices and Families of L Functions
chapters.summary:
How do eigenvalues of Haar random matrices from compact classical groups model zeros of L functions, and how does that limit differ from the Sato Tate limit? The chapter states the Weyl integration formula (circular unitary ensemble, eigenvalue repulsion), proves through Gaussian vectors that Haar measure on SU(2) gives the semicircle law, and presents the Diaconis and Shahshahani theorem that traces of powers of a Haar unitary matrix are asymptotically independent complex Gaussians. It states Montgomery's pair correlation theorem for zeros of the Riemann zeta function under the Riemann hypothesis, the Katz and Sarnak symmetry types (unitary, symplectic, even and odd orthogonal) for one level densities of low lying zeros, and the Iwaniec, Luo and Sarnak theorem for holomorphic newforms, under the generalized Riemann hypothesis and for test functions of restricted support, with its consequences for nonvanishing at the central point, and conditional bounds for the average analytic rank of elliptic curves. It closes with the Keating and Snaith moment conjectures for the zeta function and quadratic Dirichlet L functions, and separates two random matrix limits: a fixed group at varying primes (Sato Tate), with vertical versions at a fixed prime (Birch, Kesten McKay), against groups of growing dimension near the central point. The chapter is expository and proves no new theorem.

#### From the literature

- The Weyl integration formula (Weyl 1925 and 1926).
- Traces of powers (Diaconis and Shahshahani 1994; Diaconis and Evans 2001).
- Pair correlation (Montgomery 1973; Odlyzko 1987; Rudnick and Sarnak 1996).
- Symmetry types (Katz and Sarnak 1999; Deligne 1980).
- Low lying zeros of newforms (Iwaniec, Luo and Sarnak 2000); average analytic rank (Brumer 1992; Heath Brown 2004; Young 2006); rank data (Bektemirov, Mazur, Stein and Watkins 2007).
- Moments (Keating and Snaith 2000; Conrey and Ghosh 1998; Conrey and Gonek 2001; Conrey, Farmer, Keating, Rubinstein and Snaith 2005; Jutila 1981; Soundararajan 2000; Shen 2021) and the ratios conjecture (Conrey, Farmer and Zirnbauer 2008).
- Vertical Sato Tate (Birch 1968; Serre 1997; Conrey, Duke and Farmer 1997).

#### New results

The chapter surveys known results; none is the authors'.

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

chapters.title: Kloosterman Sums: Vertical Sato Tate and Random Fourier Series
chapters.summary:
How are Kloosterman sums distributed, and what do their partial sums look like? The chapter reads Kloosterman sums Kl(a; p) as Frobenius traces on the Kloosterman sheaf and presents Weil's bound, Katz's vertical Sato Tate theorem (as the prime grows, the Kloosterman angles become Sato Tate distributed, since the monodromy group is SL(2)) and joint equidistribution of additive shifts. Through the Bruggeman Kuznetsov formula and Selberg's 3/16 theorem it links Kloosterman sums with Maass forms and reads the Linnik Selberg conjecture as the absence of drift; Katz's horizontal conjecture remains open. It then treats the Kloosterman paths of Kowalski and Sawin, whose finite dimensional distributions converge to a random Fourier series with independent Sato Tate coefficients. It proves this convergence from the joint equidistribution by completion and a mean square tail bound, and proves, as its own formulations of facts implicit in or easily derived from Kowalski and Sawin's work, exact second moments of the paths at every odd prime, the covariance and a reflection symmetry of the limit (a Sato Tate Brownian motion), a subgaussian tail bound, and a variance deficit, 1/π² for the imaginary part at the midpoint, when the parameter multiplies the inverse.

#### From the literature

- Kloosterman's bound of order p^(3/4) (Kloosterman 1926).
- The Weil bound |Kl(a, b; p)| ≤ 2√p for ab prime to p (Weil 1948), with the elementary method of Stepanov (1969) in Bombieri's form (1974).
- Katz's vertical Sato Tate theorem and the monodromy of Kloosterman sheaves (Katz 1988), through Deligne's equidistribution theorem (Deligne 1980).
- The Bruggeman Kuznetsov formula (Bruggeman 1978; Kuznetsov 1980) and Kuznetsov's bound x^(1/6+ε) for sums of Kloosterman sums (Kuznetsov 1980).
- Selberg's 3/16 theorem (Selberg 1965) and the bound 975/4096 (Kim and Sarnak 2003).
- Kloosterman paths, the completion formula, the joint equidistribution of shifted sums, finite dimensional convergence to the random Fourier series and its doubly exponential tails (Kowalski and Sawin 2016).
- Maxima of partial sums (Lamzouri 2020; Autissier, Bonolis and Lamzouri 2021) and paths for prime power moduli (Ricotta and Royer 2018).

#### New results

- [Exact second moments of Kloosterman paths at every odd prime](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kloosterman_paths_exact_second_moments) (Proposition 7.13, page 100; proved): Exact formulas, valid at every odd prime, for the mean and the second moments of a normalised partial Kloosterman sum averaged over its parameter, in both natural parametrisations, which the book proves as its own formulation of facts implicit in or easily derived from the work of Kowalski and Sawin. New in this book.
- [Variance deficit of Kloosterman paths when the parameter multiplies the inverse](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kloosterman_paths_variance_deficit) (Corollary 7.14, page 101; proved): When the parameter of a partial Kloosterman sum multiplies the inverse of the summation variable, the limiting variances of its real and imaginary parts fall below those of the Kloosterman random Fourier series by explicit trigonometric terms, by exactly one over pi squared for the imaginary part at the midpoint, which the book proves as its own formulation of facts implicit in or easily derived from the work of Kowalski and Sawin. New in this book.
- [Covariance and reflection symmetry of the Kloosterman random Fourier series](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kloosterman_random_fourier_series_covariance_and_symmetry) (Proposition 7.15, page 102; proved): The random Fourier series with independent Sato Tate coefficients that Kowalski and Sawin found as the limit of Kloosterman paths has the covariance of complex Brownian motion on the first half of the unit interval and an exact reflection symmetry that determines the second half, which leads the book to call it a Sato Tate Brownian motion, and the book proves this as its own formulation of facts implicit in or easily derived from their work. New in this book.
- [Unboundedness and subgaussian tail of the Kloosterman random Fourier series](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kloosterman_random_fourier_series_subgaussian_tail) (Proposition 7.16, page 104; proved): The imaginary part of the Kloosterman random Fourier series at the midpoint is unbounded in both directions yet obeys a Gaussian tail bound, and every square summable real combination of independent Sato Tate variables is subgaussian with variance proxy equal to its variance; the book proves this as its own formulation of facts implicit in or easily derived from the work of Kowalski and Sawin, and notes that the tail bound is far weaker than their doubly exponential estimates. New in this book.

chapters.title: Random Groups: Class Groups, Selmer Groups and Ranks
chapters.summary:
Do class groups, Selmer groups and Shafarevich Tate groups behave like random groups, and what do such models predict for ranks of elliptic curves? The chapter builds the Cohen Lenstra measure, which weights a finite abelian p group by one over its number of automorphisms, from cokernels of Haar random p adic matrices, proving in this one model Hall's identity, the Friedman Washington limit, the p rank law and the moments. It presents the Cohen Lenstra conjecture, the Davenport Heilbronn theorem on 3 torsion in quadratic class groups with its secondary term, the Poonen Rains model of p Selmer groups as intersections of random maximal isotropic subspaces, written as a sum of independent Bernoulli coins, the Bhargava Shankar averages, the BKLPR and Park Poonen Voight Wood models, Goldfeld's conjecture, the minimalist conjecture and parity, and the average rank bounds that Selmer data give. PARI/GP data on quadratic class groups and on 2 Selmer groups and ranks of 6121 curves of small height test the models; the secondary term explains the observed 3 torsion deficit. The chapter marks no result as its own.

#### From the literature

- Hall's identity (Hall 1938) and the random p adic matrix model (Friedman and Washington 1989).
- The Cohen Lenstra heuristics (Cohen and Lenstra 1984), extended by Cohen and Martinet (1990) and corrected at roots of unity by Malle (2008).
- Mean 3 torsion of quadratic class groups (Davenport and Heilbronn 1971) and its secondary term (Bhargava, Shankar and Tsimerman 2013; Taniguchi and Thorne 2013).
- Cohen Lenstra over function fields as q grows, and uniqueness from moments (Ellenberg, Venkatesh and Westerland 2016; Wood 2017).
- The Poonen Rains model (Poonen and Rains 2012), the BKLPR model (Bhargava, Kane, Lenstra, Poonen and Rains 2015), Delaunay's heuristic (Delaunay 2001) and the bounded rank heuristic (Park, Poonen, Voight and Wood 2019).
- Average sizes 3, 4 and 6 of 2, 3 and 5 Selmer groups (Bhargava and Shankar 2015; the last a 2013 preprint).

chapters.title: Hecke Operators as Random Walks on Trees
chapters.summary:
Why do return probabilities of random walk on a free group (Kesten), eigenvalues of large random regular graphs (McKay) and eigenvalues of the Hecke operator T_q on modular forms of growing level or weight (Serre's vertical Sato Tate theorem) share one law, the Kesten McKay law? The chapter works on the Bruhat Tits tree of PGL(2) over the q adic numbers, the (q+1) regular tree on which T_q acts by adjacency. Its tree theorem writes the normalised nonbacktracking sphere operators as combinations of two Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind in the normalised adjacency operator and derives from this identity the Kesten McKay density and moments, the return probability and Green function of simple random walk, and convergence to the Sato Tate semicircle as q grows. The law is Macdonald's p adic Plancherel measure. In weight two and prime level congruent to 1 mod 12 the vertical theorem reads as Benjamini Schramm local convergence of supersingular isogeny graphs to the tree, the elliptic terms of the Eichler Selberg trace formula counting short cycles, with an exact finite level correction tested at 207 prime levels. Horizontal and vertical limits are compared, with Shin's Plancherel density theorem.

#### From the literature

- Return probabilities on free groups and amenability (Kesten 1959); the eigenvalue law of random regular graphs (McKay 1981).
- The Bruhat Tits tree (Ihara 1966; Serre, Trees, 1980); spherical functions and the Plancherel formula (Macdonald 1971); the Ramanujan bound (Deligne 1974; Deligne and Serre 1974).
- The vertical Sato Tate theorem (Serre 1997; Conrey, Duke and Farmer 1997), its Maass form analogue (Sarnak 1987) and effective versions (Murty and Sinha 2009); the automorphic Plancherel density theorem (Shin 2012; Shin and Templier 2016).
- Local convergence of graphs (Benjamini and Schramm 2001); the sphere operator recursion (Lubotzky, Phillips and Sarnak 1988); the Sato Tate theorem (Barnet Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor 2011).

#### New results

The individual statements of the tree theorem are classical; the book claims its formulation and single proof.

- [Tree theorem, a single Chebyshev proof of the Kesten McKay law and the Green function of the regular tree](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#tree_theorem_kesten_mckay_chebyshev_proof) (Theorem 9.1, page 134; proved): One Chebyshev polynomial identity for the sphere operators of the regular tree, on which for prime q the Hecke operator acts by adjacency, yields the Kesten McKay spectral law, its moments, the return probability of simple random walk and its expected number of visits to the starting vertex, and convergence to the Sato Tate semicircle as the degree grows; the individual facts are classical, and the formulation and the single proof are the book's. New in this book.

chapters.summary:
What does the graph Riemann hypothesis say about random walk? The chapter studies the Ihara zeta function of a finite regular graph through the Ihara Bass determinant formula and the Hashimoto nonbacktracking matrix, and proves three forms of the graph Riemann hypothesis equivalent: nontrivial poles on the critical circle, the Ramanujan eigenvalue bound, and return probabilities approaching equilibrium exponentially, no slower than the Kesten rate of the tree (the third form a reformulation). Supersingular isogeny graphs are quotients of the Bruhat Tits tree whose adjacency matrices, Brandt matrices, carry the Hecke eigenvalues of weight two cusp forms of prime level N, so they are Ramanujan. The main theorem: as N grows through primes congruent to 1 mod 12, the Kemeny constant of the supersingular ℓ isogeny graph (the mean hitting time of a uniformly random target) divided by the number of vertices tends to the expected number of visits to the root of simple random walk on the (ℓ+1) regular tree: 2 for ℓ = 2 and 3/2 for ℓ = 3, by Serre's vertical Sato Tate theorem and the Ramanujan bound. A trace series, hitting time bounds, data at 207 levels and isogeny cryptography complete the chapter.

#### From the literature

- The Ihara zeta function (Ihara 1966), extended to all graphs (Sunada 1986), and its determinant formula (Hashimoto 1989; Bass 1992).
- Ramanujan graphs (Lubotzky, Phillips and Sarnak 1988; Margulis 1988; Morgenstern 1994); the Alon Boppana bound (Nilli 1991); the Ramanujan bound (Eichler 1954; Deligne 1974).
- Supersingular isogeny graphs, Brandt matrices and their spectra (Deuring 1941; Eichler 1954; Jacquet and Langlands 1970; Mestre 1986; Gross 1987; Pizer 1990).
- Random regular graphs (Friedman 2008; Bordenave 2020; Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava 2015, 2018; Huang, McKenzie and Yau, preprint 2024).
- Kemeny's constant (Kemeny and Snell 1960); cover times of random regular graphs (Cooper and Frieze 2005).
- Isogeny based cryptography (Charles, Goren and Lauter 2009; Jao and De Feo 2011; Delfs and Galbraith 2016; Wesolowski 2022; Castryck and Decru 2023).

#### New results

The Kemeny limit is new as far as the authors know; of the three forms only the mixing form, a reformulation, is the book's.

- [Three equivalent forms of the graph Riemann hypothesis, Ihara poles, Ramanujan bound and mixing at the Kesten rate](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#graph_riemann_hypothesis_three_equivalent_forms) (Proposition 10.3, page 147; proved): For a connected regular graph the Riemann hypothesis for its Ihara zeta function is equivalent both to the Ramanujan eigenvalue bound and to return probabilities approaching equilibrium at an exponential rate no slower than the rate at which those of the regular tree decay to zero, with the exact rate set by the largest absolute value of a nontrivial eigenvalue; the first equivalence is standard, and the mixing form is the book's reformulation. New in this book.
- [Limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kemeny_constant_supersingular_isogeny_graphs_limit) (Theorem 10.6, page 150; proved): As the characteristic grows through primes congruent to 1 modulo 12, with the prime isogeny degree fixed, the mean time for simple random walk on a supersingular isogeny graph to hit a uniformly random curve is asymptotic to the number of vertices times the expected number of visits of simple random walk on the regular tree of the same degree to its starting point, so about twice the number of vertices for 2 isogenies. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Ihara zeta function, Ihara Bass formula, nonbacktracking matrix, graph Riemann hypothesis, Ramanujan graph, Alon Boppana bound, Kesten rate, supersingular isogeny graph, Pizer graph, Brandt matrix, Kemeny constant, mean hitting time, Green function, vertical Sato Tate, Eichler Selberg trace formula, isogeny based cryptography, CGL hash

chapters.title: Infinite Divisibility of Euler Products
chapters.summary:
When is an Euler product a characteristic function? Khinchine observed that for σ > 1 the ratio ζ(σ+it)/ζ(σ) is the characteristic function of a compound Poisson, hence infinitely divisible, law. For an automorphic L function the same expansion gives a signed Lévy Khintchine exponent. The chapter proves that for the discriminant form Δ, whose eigenvalue τ(2) is negative, the normalised L function is not a characteristic function for any σ > 1, and that the Rankin Selberg pole forces infinitely many negative Hecke eigenvalues for every holomorphic newform with real eigenvalues. Rankin Selberg convolutions restore positivity and, with Landau's lemma and isobaric sums, give L(1+it, π) ≠ 0 for unitary cuspidal π on GL(n), n ≥ 2, unless π twisted by |det|^(it) is self dual. Left of Re s = 1 the chapter reviews Bohr Jessen value distribution, universality, large deviations and random multiplicative functions. It then proves that the Sato Tate random Euler product, with independent Satake angles from the Sato Tate law, is a mean one martingale with second moment ζ(2σ) whose logarithm at a real point obeys a central limit theorem, with drift minus half the variance, as σ decreases to 1/2.

#### From the literature

- The Lévy Khintchine formula, as in Sato (1999); infinite divisibility of the zeta distribution (Khinchine 1938).
- Landau's lemma (Landau 1905); nonvanishing of ζ on Re s = 1 (Hadamard 1896; de la Vallée Poussin 1896).
- Rankin Selberg L functions (Jacquet and Shalika 1981; Jacquet, Piatetski Shapiro and Shalika 1983; Shahidi 1981; Moeglin and Waldspurger 1989; Rudnick and Sarnak 1996); nonvanishing on Re s = 1 for GL(n) (Jacquet and Shalika 1976) and its positivity proof (Sarnak 2004).
- Value distribution and universality (Bohr and Jessen 1930, 1932; Jessen and Wintner 1935; Voronin 1975; Bagchi 1981; Laurinčikas and Matsumoto 2001), Selberg's central limit theorem (Selberg 1946), large deviations (Lamzouri 2011).
- Random multiplicative functions (Wintner 1944; Harper 2020); the Sato Tate theorem for Δ (Barnet Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor 2011).

#### New results

The authors call the two results on the random Euler product elementary but have not found them stated in this form.

- [The normalised L function of the discriminant form is not a characteristic function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#discriminant_form_l_function_not_characteristic_function) (Proposition 11.3, page 160; proved): Because the Ramanujan tau function takes negative values, on every vertical line to the right of the critical strip the L function of the discriminant modular form somewhere exceeds in modulus its value at the real point of that line, so, unlike the Riemann zeta function, it gives no characteristic function there. New in this book.
- [Mean and second moment of the Sato Tate random Euler product](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sato_tate_random_euler_product_mean_and_second_moment) (Proposition 11.12, page 167; proved): A random model of the L function of a cusp form, with independent Satake angles drawn from the Sato Tate law, converges as a martingale to the right of the critical line, with mean one and mean square equal to the Riemann zeta function at twice the real part. New in this book.
- [Central limit theorem for the Sato Tate random Euler product near the critical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sato_tate_random_euler_product_central_limit_theorem) (Theorem 11.13, page 167; proved): In the Sato Tate random model of the L function of a cusp form, the logarithm at a real point approaching the critical line is asymptotically normal, with a variance that grows logarithmically and a negative drift equal to half the variance. New in this book.

#### Key terms

infinitely divisible law, Lévy Khintchine formula, Lévy measure, compound Poisson law, zeta distribution, signed Lévy measure, Ramanujan tau function, Rankin Selberg positivity, Landau's lemma, Mertens inequality, nonvanishing on Re s = 1, Bohr Jessen theorem, Voronin universality, random Euler product, random multiplicative function, Sato Tate random model, central limit theorem

chapters.title: Log Correlated Fields
chapters.summary:
How does the logarithm of an L function behave along a window of the critical line, rather than at one random point? The chapter treats log |ζ(1/2+it)| and log |L(6+it, Δ)|, for the Ramanujan discriminant form Δ, as log correlated fields, and presents Selberg's central limit theorem, the Keating Snaith model and the hybrid Euler Hadamard product, branching random walks and the Fyodorov Hiary Keating conjecture on maxima over unit windows, Gaussian multiplicative chaos, random multiplicative functions and pair correlation of zeros. Its own results are an elementary lemma explaining the exponential left tail at finite height by simple zeros, the covariance of the random Euler product field (a standard computation), first moment asymptotics, with and without a ballot constraint, for Brownian motion on a tree, a conjectured variance formula for log |L(6+it, Δ)| at finite height with an explicit arithmetic constant, and three translations into the Pólya variable, Thorin measure and extreme value language of later chapters, two assuming the Riemann hypothesis for Δ. Computations of L(s, Δ) at heights 500 to 2500 test the predictions; the translations are exact consequences of cited theorems, not evidence for or against the Riemann hypothesis.

#### From the literature

- Selberg's central limit theorem (Selberg 1946; Tsang 1984; short proof by Radziwiłł and Soundararajan 2017), and conditional versions for other L functions (Selberg 1992; Bombieri and Hejhal 1995).
- Random matrix moments (Keating and Snaith 2000), the moment conjecture (Conrey, Farmer, Keating, Rubinstein and Snaith 2005), the hybrid Euler Hadamard product (Gonek, Hughes and Keating 2007).
- Maxima of branching random walks (Bramson 1978; Addario Berry and Reed 2009; Aïdékon 2013).
- The Fyodorov Hiary Keating conjecture (Fyodorov, Hiary and Keating 2012), proved to first order (Najnudel 2018 under the Riemann hypothesis; Arguin, Belius, Bourgade, Radziwiłł and Soundararajan 2019) and to tightness (Arguin, Bourgade and Radziwiłł, preprints 2020 and 2023).
- Gaussian multiplicative chaos (Kahane 1985) and zeta as complex chaos (Saksman and Webb 2020).
- Better than square root cancellation for random multiplicative functions (Harper 2020).
- The n level correlations of automorphic L function zeros (Rudnick and Sarnak 1996).

#### New results

- [Exponential left tail of the log modulus near simple zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#exponential_left_tail_near_simple_zeros) (Proposition 12.4, page 175; proved): An elementary fact about real analytic functions with simple zeros, which the book applies to the Hardy function of the discriminant form to explain the exponential left tail of the empirical distribution of the log modulus of its L function on windows of the critical line whose zeros are simple. New in this book.
- [Variance at finite height of the log modulus of the L function of Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#finite_height_variance_conjecture_for_delta) (Conjecture 12.6, page 178; open): Conjectures an explicit formula for the variance of the log modulus of the L function of the discriminant form on its critical line at finite height, combining the random matrix constant with an arithmetic constant, obtained by writing out the moment conjecture and hybrid Euler Hadamard product heuristics for this form; the book's computations at heights 500 to 2500 agree with it within sampling error. New in this book.
- [Log correlated covariance of the random Euler product field](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#covariance_of_random_euler_product_field) (Proposition 12.7, page 180; proved): Writes out the standard computation showing that the prime sum of the random Euler product, for the Riemann zeta function and for the discriminant form, is a log correlated field, whose covariance at distance u between 0 and 1 is one half of the logarithm of the smaller of 1/u and the logarithm of the prime cutoff, up to a bounded error. New in this book.
- [First moments with and without the ballot constraint for Brownian motion on a tree](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#tree_brownian_motion_first_moments_with_ballot_constraint) (Proposition 12.8, page 181; proved): Asymptotics of the first moments of the number of high leaves, with and without a ballot constraint on the paths, for Brownian motion indexed by a regular tree, a continuous model in which the ballot computation is exact; they explain heuristically the logarithmic correction to the maximum of a branching random walk (a theorem of Bramson, Addario Berry and Reed, and Aïdékon), and so the constant three quarters in the Fyodorov Hiary Keating conjecture. New in this book.
- [Selberg central limit theorem for Delta as a statement about the characteristic function of the Pólya variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#selberg_clt_for_delta_via_polya_characteristic_function) (Proposition 12.16, page 193; conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta), for the Gaussian limit only): Expresses the log modulus of the L function of the discriminant form on its critical line through the characteristic function of its Pólya variable plus an explicit archimedean term, so that, under the Riemann hypothesis for this form, Selberg's central limit theorem becomes a statement about lognormal fluctuations of the characteristic function of an explicit probability law. New in this book.
- [The log modulus of the L function of Delta as the logarithmic potential of its Thorin measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#log_modulus_of_delta_as_thorin_potential) (Proposition 12.17, page 194; conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta)): Under the Riemann hypothesis for the discriminant form, the log modulus of the characteristic function of its Pólya variable on the real line is the logarithmic potential of the Thorin measure carried by the squared ordinates of the zeros, and it is strictly concave between consecutive zeros. New in this book.
- [The L function of Delta on the critical line through the extreme value variable M*](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#critical_line_of_delta_through_extreme_value_variable) (Proposition 12.18, page 194; proved): Writes the L function of the discriminant form on its critical line, times a gamma factor, as the Fourier transform of a finite measure, the law of the logarithm of a gamma variable restricted to the event that it exceeds a scaled maximum of independent exponential variables, and identifies that measure with the central value L(6, Delta) times the law of the shifted Pólya variable. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Selberg central limit theorem, log correlated field, logarithmically correlated Gaussian field, branching random walk, Fyodorov Hiary Keating conjecture, FHK conjecture, maximum of zeta on short intervals, Gaussian multiplicative chaos, Keating Snaith model, hybrid Euler Hadamard product, random multiplicative function, pair correlation, GUE, Ramanujan tau function, discriminant modular form, Pólya variable, Thorin measure

chapters.title: Pólya Kernels, Generalized Gamma Convolutions and Thorin Measures
chapters.summary:
Pólya studied Riemann's Xi function as the Fourier transform of a positive kernel and asked which kernels have transforms with only real zeros. This chapter carries his programme from ζ to the L function of the discriminant modular form Δ, in the language of generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) and Thorin measures. Suitably weighted, Δ on the imaginary axis in logarithmic coordinates is the density of a symmetric random variable W, the Pólya variable, whose moment generating function is Λ(6+z, Δ)/Λ(6, Δ); so the Riemann hypothesis for Δ is equivalent to the characteristic function of W having only real zeros. Hadamard factorisation gives, unconditionally, a product over the zeros and a variance identity for W, a trace formula in miniature. The main theorem shows that the Riemann hypothesis for Δ holds if and only if Λ(6, Δ)/Λ(6+√s, Δ) is the Laplace transform of a GGC, whose Thorin measure then puts unit mass at each squared ordinate; the same holds for every self dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n), n ≥ 2, with nonzero central value. These are reformulations, not proofs; the chapter poses as open the construction of that GGC without reference to the zeros, Hilbert's eighth problem for GL(2).

#### From the literature

- The Fourier integral of Riemann's Xi function and real zero theorems (Pólya 1926, 1927).
- Heat flow and the de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976), its nonnegativity (Rodgers and Tao 2020), also for the extended Selberg class (Dobner 2021).
- Pólya frequency functions (Schoenberg 1951; Karlin 1968) and the Laguerre Pólya class (Levin 1964).
- Generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992).
- Bessel hitting times and the Riemann ξ function (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001).
- A positive proportion of zeros on the critical line for level one Hecke eigenforms (Hafner 1983, after Selberg 1942).
- From the first author: the Thorin representation of the reciprocal Xi function (Polson 2017) and the equivalence of real zeros and the Thorin property for real entire functions of order at most one (Polson 2018).

#### New results

The Notes call these theorems elementary consequences of Hecke's theory and Hadamard's factorisation.

- [Pólya kernel of the discriminant form Delta and its characteristic function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#polya_kernel_of_the_discriminant_form) (Theorem 13.6, page 203; proved): The discriminant modular form on the imaginary axis, read in logarithmic coordinates and weighted, is the density of a symmetric random variable whose moment generating function is the normalised completed L function of the form, so that the Riemann hypothesis for this form is equivalent to the characteristic function of an explicit probability law having only real zeros. New in this book.
- [Hadamard product and variance identity for the Pólya variable of Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#hadamard_product_and_variance_identity_for_delta) (Theorem 13.7, page 204; proved): Unconditionally, the normalised completed L function of the discriminant form is a product over its zeros with no exponential factor, and the variance of its Pólya variable equals twice the sum of the inverse squares of the zero ordinates, a trace formula in miniature that the book checks against computed zeros. New in this book.
- [Riemann hypothesis for Delta as a generalized gamma convolution property](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#riemann_hypothesis_for_delta_as_ggc_property) (Theorem 13.8, page 205; proved): Proves that the Riemann hypothesis for the L function of the discriminant form is equivalent to a reciprocal of its completed L function, in the square root variable, being the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, whose Thorin measure is then the sum of unit masses at the squared zero ordinates; it is a reformulation and proves no case of the Riemann hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Thorin criterion for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of self dual automorphic L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#grh_for_self_dual_l_functions_as_ggc_property) (Theorem 13.10, page 207; proved): For a self dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n), n at least 2, with nonvanishing central value, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to a reciprocal of the completed L function, in the square root variable, being the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, whose Thorin measure then sits on the squared zero ordinates; a reformulation that proves no case of the generalized Riemann hypothesis. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Pólya kernel, Polya kernel, Pólya variable, Riemann Xi function, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, complete monotonicity, Hadamard factorisation, Laguerre Pólya class, Pólya frequency function, de Bruijn Newman constant, Ramanujan Delta function, discriminant modular form, Riemann hypothesis for Delta, generalized Riemann hypothesis, GRH, self dual automorphic representation, Hilbert's eighth problem

chapters.title: The Thorin Framework for Automorphic L Functions
chapters.summary:
Can the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for an automorphic L function be restated as positivity of a probability law? For every cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals the chapter builds a nonnegative self dual completion and reads its zeros in the variable s = z^2, where their squared ordinates become Thorin atoms. Extending the first author's 2018 equivalence for Laguerre Pólya functions, it proves that GRH is equivalent to each of six statements: the reciprocal of the completion is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC); a Lévy function of the zeros is completely monotone; a logarithmic derivative is a Stieltjes function, or satisfies a Herglotz inequality; the power sums of the atoms, computable from central Taylor coefficients, form a Stieltjes moment sequence; and, for a nonnegative Pólya kernel, so do the rescaled even cumulants of the Pólya variable. It also reads the central order of vanishing as a degenerate Thorin atom, relaxes GRH to parabolic conditions along the de Bruijn heat flow, tests the criteria on eleven L functions, and gives a regularised version of order two for Selberg zeta functions, where it means no exceptional eigenvalue. These equivalences are reformulations and prove no case of GRH.

#### From the literature

Generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992) and the reciprocal Xi function (Polson 2017); the Thorin equivalence for Laguerre Pólya functions (Polson 2018); Bernstein's theorem (Bernstein 1929); Stieltjes functions and their Nevanlinna Pick characterisation (Schilling, Song and Vondraček 2012); the Stieltjes moment problem (Stieltjes 1894; Akhiezer 1965) and Hankel criteria for real zeros (Grommer 1914); standard L functions of GL(n) (Godement and Jacquet 1972; Jacquet and Shalika 1976); de Bruijn's heat flow theorem (de Bruijn 1950), Newman's conjecture (Rodgers and Tao 2020; Dobner 2021) and zero dynamics under the heat flow (Csordas, Smith and Varga 1994; Polymath 2019); the rank part of Birch and Swinnerton Dyer in analytic rank at most one (Gross and Zagier 1986; Kolyvagin 1988); the bound 7/64 toward Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture (Kim and Sarnak 2003).

#### New results

- [Self dual completion of a cuspidal automorphic L function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#self_dual_completion_automorphic_l_function) (Lemma 14.6, page 215; proved): Builds from the L function of any cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals an even entire completion, real and nonnegative on the real axis and positive at the centre, with all zeros in the open critical strip and a genus zero product in the squared variable. New in this book.
- [Thorin equivalence for even entire functions with zeros in a strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_equivalence_even_entire_functions) (Theorem 14.7, page 216; proved): For an even entire function of order less than two, real on the real axis, equal to one at the origin and with zeros in a vertical strip, all zeros lie on the imaginary axis exactly when any one of several positivity properties holds (a generalized gamma convolution, a completely monotone Lévy function, a Stieltjes or Herglotz property of the logarithmic derivative, a Stieltjes moment sequence of power sums), extending an equivalence of the first author's 2018 paper for Laguerre Pólya functions. New in this book.
- [Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of automorphic L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_criteria_generalized_riemann_hypothesis_automorphic) (Theorem 14.8, page 219; proved): The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the L function of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, and the Riemann hypothesis for zeta, are each equivalent to several positivity statements, among them that the reciprocal of the self dual completion, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure sits at the squared ordinates of the zeros, and a Hankel criterion computable from central derivatives; the theorem is an equivalence that extends the first author's 2018 paper, and it proves no case of either hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of a cuspidal automorphic L function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#polya_kernel_automorphic_l_function) (Lemma 14.12, page 221; proved): The L function of every cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals has a real even kernel with doubly exponential decay whose two sided Laplace transform is its normalised self dual completion, although the kernel need not be positive. New in this book.
- [Cumulant criterion for the generalized Riemann hypothesis via the Pólya variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#cumulant_criterion_generalized_riemann_hypothesis) (Proposition 14.13, page 222; proved): When the Pólya kernel of an automorphic L function is nonnegative, the even cumulants of the associated symmetric random variable are, up to sign and scale, the power sums of the Thorin atoms, so the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to a Stieltjes moment property of the rescaled cumulants. New in this book.
- [Central order of vanishing as a degenerate Thorin atom at the origin](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#central_order_of_vanishing_as_degenerate_thorin_atom) (Proposition 14.14, page 222; conditional on the generalized Riemann hypothesis for L(s, pi), for the Laplace transform representation only (the slope limit is unconditional)): The order of vanishing of a self dual automorphic L function at the centre, such as the analytic rank of an elliptic curve, appears as a Thorin atom of mass half the order escaping to the origin, unconditionally as a log log slope and, under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, in a Laplace transform representation. New in this book.
- [Gaussian tilting of the Pólya kernel and the Thorin property along the heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gaussian_tilting_polya_kernel_thorin_property) (Theorem 14.17, page 225; proved): Tilting the Pólya kernel of an automorphic L function by a Gaussian factor narrows the strip containing the zeros and makes them all real once the tilt is large enough (de Bruijn's theorem, the first part), and the book adds that, when the kernel is nonnegative, the reciprocal of the tilted transform in the squared variable is then the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, unconditionally for every tilt of at least one eighth. New in this book.
- [Regularised Thorin equivalence for even entire functions of order two](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#regularised_thorin_equivalence_order_two) (Proposition 14.20, page 229; proved): For even entire functions of order at most two whose zeros have summable inverse fourth powers, such as the completed Selberg zeta function of a compact hyperbolic surface, all Thorin atoms are positive exactly when the reciprocal is the Laplace transform of a centred sum of exponential variables, which for the surface means no exceptional Laplace eigenvalue (for arithmetic surfaces Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture, which this equivalence does not prove). New in this book.

#### Key terms

Thorin measure, Thorin atom, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, self dual completion, Xi function, generalized Riemann hypothesis, GRH, automorphic L function, GL(n), completely monotone function, Lévy function, Stieltjes function, Herglotz function, Stieltjes moment problem, Thorin Hankel criterion, Pólya kernel, Polya kernel, Pólya variable, analytic rank, Birch and Swinnerton Dyer conjecture, de Bruijn Newman constant, Gaussian tilting, Selberg zeta function, Selberg eigenvalue conjecture, Laguerre Pólya class

chapters.title: Local Thorin Structure
chapters.summary:
How does the Thorin test of the previous chapter read for a single Euler factor? For a cuspidal representation of GL(2) over the rationals, the reciprocal of the completed Euler factor at an unramified prime, read in s = z^2, is, outside one degenerate case, the Laplace transform of a probability law exactly when the Ramanujan Petersson bound holds there, and is then a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb: Ramanujan is local Thorin, as the generalized Riemann hypothesis is global Thorin. This equivalence proves no case of the Ramanujan conjecture. The local combs enter Weil's explicit formula damped by powers of the prime, and become point processes for Sato Tate random Euler products. Global Thorin is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields, hence unconditional by Weil's theorem, and to the Ramanujan property for regular graphs, which supersingular isogeny graphs have. By Keilson's theorem, passage times of the Hecke walk on the Bruhat Tits tree are GGCs whose atoms fill the Kesten band with the arcsine law, a central limit theorem and large deviations; hitting times on Ramanujan and isogeny graphs are exponential up to an error of order one over the number of vertices. The extreme value law of the Dedekind eta function is max infinitely divisible.

#### From the literature

Ramanujan's conjecture (Ramanujan 1916), proved for holomorphic forms by Deligne (1974), and the bound 7/64 for Maass forms (Kim and Sarnak 2003); generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); the Pringsheim Landau theorem (Landau 1905; Widder 1941); Weil's explicit formula (Weil 1952; Iwaniec and Kowalski 2004); one level densities (Iwaniec, Luo and Sarnak 2000; Katz and Sarnak 1999); the Riemann hypothesis for curves (Weil 1948); Ramanujan graphs (Ihara 1966; Lubotzky, Phillips and Sarnak 1988; Pizer 1990); passage times of birth death processes (Keilson 1971; Kent 1980; Fill 2009); Kesten's spectral radius (Kesten 1959); the Aldous Brown inequality (Aldous and Brown 1992; Aldous and Fill 2002).

#### New results

- [Local Thorin criterion for a single Euler factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#local_thorin_criterion_single_euler_factor) (Theorem 15.3, page 236; proved): The reciprocal of a completed Euler factor of degree two, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law exactly when its trace parameter lies in the tempered interval with the degenerate endpoint 2 excluded, and the law is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb. New in this book.
- [Thorin criterion for the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at a prime](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#ramanujan_petersson_local_thorin_criterion) (Corollary 15.4, page 237; proved): For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over the rationals with trivial central character, the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at an unramified prime (outside the degenerate case of trace 2) holds exactly when the reciprocal of the symmetrised Euler factor, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, which is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb (Ramanujan is local Thorin, as the generalized Riemann hypothesis is global Thorin); the corollary is an equivalence and proves no case of the conjecture. New in this book.
- [Prime terms of the explicit formula as damped local Thorin combs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#explicit_formula_prime_terms_from_local_thorin_combs) (Proposition 15.8, page 239; proved): In Weil's explicit formula for the discriminant modular form, the contribution of each prime is the oscillatory part of the sum of the test function over that prime's local Thorin comb, with its sign changed and each Fourier coefficient damped by a power of the prime. New in this book.
- [Intensity of the Thorin point process of Sato Tate random Euler products](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sato_tate_thorin_point_process_intensity) (Proposition 15.10, page 241; proved): For Euler products with independent Sato Tate angles, the ordinates of the local Thorin combs form a point process with an explicit intensity that vanishes quadratically at the origin, and each local law has expected mean the square of the logarithm of the prime. New in this book.
- [Thorin criterion for the Riemann hypothesis of curves over finite fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_criterion_riemann_hypothesis_curves_over_finite_fields) (Theorem 15.11, page 243; proved): For a curve over a finite field with q elements, none of whose Frobenius eigenvalues equals the square root of q, the reciprocal of its completed zeta function in the squared variable is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann hypothesis for the curve holds, so by Weil's theorem global Thorin holds unconditionally there, with a Thorin measure made of finitely many periodic combs. New in this book.
- [Thorin criterion for Ramanujan graphs and supersingular isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_criterion_ramanujan_graphs) (Theorem 15.13, page 243; proved): A finite connected regular graph of degree q plus one, without the eigenvalue twice the square root of q, is Ramanujan exactly when the reciprocal of its completed Ihara zeta function, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, and both hold unconditionally for supersingular isogeny graphs. New in this book.
- [Thorin structure of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_structure_hecke_walk_passage_times_tree) (Theorem 15.15, page 245; proved): The first time that continuous time simple random walk on a regular tree (the Hecke walk, on the Bruhat Tits tree when the degree is a prime plus one) reaches distance n from its start is a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin atoms, given by the zeros of the sphere polynomials of the tree, lie in the Kesten band and follow the arcsine law as n grows, with an exact mean, a variance linear in n and a central limit theorem; Thorin support in the Kesten band is the random walk form of the Ramanujan bound, and this unconditional theorem about the tree proves no case of the Ramanujan conjecture for automorphic forms. New in this book.
- [Large deviations of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#large_deviations_passage_times_regular_tree) (Theorem 15.16, page 246; proved): Passage times of the Hecke walk on a regular tree satisfy a large deviation principle with an explicit rate function, computed from the arcsine limit of their Thorin atoms. New in this book.
- [Exponential approximation of hitting times on Ramanujan graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#exponential_hitting_times_ramanujan_graphs) (Theorem 15.18, page 249; proved): On a Ramanujan graph that is not bipartite, all Dirichlet rates of a target but the slowest lie in the Kesten band, and the hitting time of any vertex from the uniform start is exponential up to an explicit error of order one over the number of vertices. New in this book.
- [Unconditional exponential law for hitting times on supersingular isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#exponential_hitting_times_supersingular_isogeny_graphs) (Corollary 15.19, page 249; proved): On supersingular isogeny graphs the hitting time of any curve by a continuous time random walk from a uniform start is unconditionally exponential up to an explicit error of order one over the number of vertices. New in this book.
- [Max infinite divisibility of the extreme value law of the Dedekind eta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#max_infinite_divisibility_eta_extreme_value_law) (Proposition 15.20, page 251; proved): The maximum of scaled exponential variables whose distribution function is the product behind the Dedekind eta function is max infinitely divisible, with a completely monotone exponent function, an exponent measure built from divisor sums, a Poisson splitting and the same structure for every multiplicative eta product; the Mellin transform of the exponent, also stated, is classical. New in this book.
