chapters.title: Van Dantzig Pairs and Transport
chapters.summary:
How does the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for automorphic L functions read in the languages of van Dantzig's problem (F and 1/F(it) both characteristic functions), Wald couples and generalized gamma convolutions (GGC)? For a self dual completion with nonnegative Pólya kernel (Riemann xi, Ramanujan Delta, eta products), GRH is equivalent to the reciprocal being the characteristic function of a symmetric Pólya frequency density, to a Wald couple of the Pólya variable with a GGC, and to Lukacs (Laguerre Pólya) class membership. The sine squared transport turns the Lévy measure of log f at a basepoint into the Thorin density of f(α)/f(α+√s), and, formally through Weil's explicit formula, the primes into the squared ordinates of the zeros; shifted basepoints give Thorin representations, unconditional from the edge of the critical strip, and a Thorin form of the Hinkkanen Lagarias criterion. Euler products give zeta subordinators with marginal and first passage (ballot) laws in generalized divisor functions, and a Hausdorff moment test on Taylor coefficients probes the Patie class of van Dantzig solutions. The equivalences are reformulations and prove no case of a Riemann hypothesis.

#### From the literature

- The van Dantzig problem (van Dantzig 1958) and the Lukacs class (Lukacs 1968, 1970).
- Wald couples and the Wald couple form of the Riemann hypothesis (Roynette and Yor 2005), after Hartman's reciprocal Gamma theorem (Hartman 1976).
- The Lukacs class criteria for the Riemann hypothesis and the Lee Yang property, and the Patie class (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024), from Bernstein gamma functions (Patie and Savov 2018); Lee and Yang (1952), Newman (1974, 1976).
- Generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); examples of Ostrovskii (1970), Hinds (1974) and Biane, Pitman and Yor (2001).
- The positivity criterion for xi (Hinkkanen 1997; Lagarias 1999); Weil's explicit formula (Weil 1952); Kendall's identity (Kendall 1957); the ballot theorem (Takács 1967).

#### New results

The Notes claim the equivalences and the shifted representation for automorphic L functions (for zeta, earlier work cited above), the damped cosine transport, the subordinator laws and the Patie test; the duality theorem restates Polson (2018) without its claim that the symmetric variable X is infinitely divisible, and the sine squared lemma is from that paper.

- [Duality of imaginary zeros, Thorin's condition, van Dantzig pairs and Wald couples](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_condition_van_dantzig_wald_duality) (Theorem 16.5, page 258; proved): A real entire function of order at most one that is symmetric about a point has all its zeros on the vertical line through that point exactly when Thorin's condition holds (its reciprocal, centred there and evaluated along the square root, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution); when the centred function is also a moment generating function, this yields a van Dantzig pair and a Wald couple. Corrects a statement of Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, arXiv:1804.10043.
- [Generalized Riemann hypothesis as a van Dantzig pair, a Wald couple and Lukacs class membership](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#grh_van_dantzig_wald_lukacs_equivalence) (Theorem 16.6, page 259; proved): For an automorphic L function whose Pólya kernel is nonnegative, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to three probabilistic statements (a Pólya frequency partner law, a Wald couple with a generalized gamma convolution, membership in the Lukacs class), as Roynette and Yor, Polson, and Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar showed for the Riemann zeta function; these are reformulations and prove no case of the hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Sine squared transport from a Lévy measure to a Thorin density](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sine_squared_transport_lemma) (Lemma 16.7, page 263; proved): When the logarithm of a positive analytic function has a Lévy Khintchine representation with a positive measure at a basepoint, its reciprocal along the square root is, up to a stable factor, a generalized gamma convolution transform whose Thorin density is the sine squared transport of that measure and can be read from the logarithmic derivative on one vertical line. First stated in Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, arXiv:1804.10043.
- [Shifted Thorin representation of completed automorphic L functions and a Thorin form of the Hinkkanen Lagarias criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#shifted_thorin_representation_automorphic) (Theorem 16.8, page 265; proved): Moving the basepoint of a completed automorphic L function to the right of all its zeros makes its reciprocal along the square root a generalized gamma convolution transform with an explicit Thorin density, unconditionally from the edge of the critical strip on, and the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the positivity of these densities for every positive shift; this extends to automorphic L functions what Polson proved for the Riemann xi function. New in this book.
- [Damped cosine Lévy measure of the zeros and its sine squared transport](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#damped_cosine_measure_sine_squared_transport) (Proposition 16.9, page 267; conditional on the generalized Riemann hypothesis for L(s, pi)): Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the reciprocal of a completed automorphic L function with its basepoint moved a distance epsilon to the right of the centre, evaluated along the square root, factors into a positive one half stable transform and the exponential of a Thorin type integral whose density, a signed combination of Poisson kernels at the ordinates of the zeros, is the sine squared transport of the damped cosine measure of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Marginal law of the zeta subordinator through generalized divisor functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#zeta_subordinator_marginal_law) (Proposition 16.10, page 272; proved): The compound Poisson subordinator built from the Euler product of the Riemann zeta function takes values in the logarithms of the positive integers, with probabilities given by the Dirichlet coefficients of a real power of zeta. New in this book.
- [First passage law of the zeta subordinator with drift, a ballot formula in generalized divisor functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#zeta_subordinator_first_passage_law) (Theorem 16.11, page 273; proved): When a linear drift minus the zeta subordinator first passes above a level, the passage time is fixed by a random positive integer, the exponential of the subordinator at that time, whose law is an explicit ballot formula in generalized divisor functions, a Lagrange inversion for Dirichlet series. New in this book.
- [Hausdorff moment test for membership of completed L functions in the Patie class of van Dantzig solutions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#patie_class_hausdorff_test) (Proposition 16.13, page 275; proved): If a completed L function belonged to the class of van Dantzig solutions that Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar build from Bernstein gamma functions, the ratios of its central Taylor coefficients would be the values of the Laplace exponent at the integers and their second differences would form a completely monotone sequence, a necessary condition that can be tested numerically. New in this book.

#### Key terms

van Dantzig problem, van Dantzig pair, Lukacs class, Wald couple, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, Pólya frequency function, Lee Yang property, sine squared transport, shifted Thorin representation, zeta subordinator, Patie class, Bernstein gamma function, generalized Riemann hypothesis, GRH

chapters.title: Squarefree Integers and Thorin Atoms
chapters.summary:
Squarefree integers have Dirichlet series ζ(s)/ζ(2s), whose poles at ρ/2 come from the nontrivial zeros ρ of the Riemann zeta function. The chapter reads this through the Pólya density of the Riemann xi function and the Thorin measure of its reciprocal: under the Riemann hypothesis (RH) the poles in the strip 0 < Re s < 1/2 correspond to the Thorin atoms, and the constant in the sum of μ(n)²/n is a combination of two tilted Pólya means, with a number field analogue. RH is equivalent to an x^{1/4+ε} error for the exponentially smoothed squarefree count, and to a mean square bound for the squarefree error. After Gamma(2) smoothing the squarefree error is exactly minus half the mean of the Mertens function at a random point, and Gamma(ν) smoothing gives a positive average of it exactly when ν ≤ 2. Off the critical line each pair of zeros contributes an exponential time plus a Brownian passage time, smearing its atom into a nearly Cauchy profile. For imaginary quadratic fields a Pólya kernel is positive when |d| < π² and takes negative values whenever 2 and 3 are inert. The RH equivalences are reformulations and prove no case of RH.

#### From the literature

- Sums of μ(n)²/n^α (Mathematics Stack Exchange 2016).
- Ω(x^{1/4}) for the squarefree error (Evelyn and Linfoot 1931; Stark 1966); oscillations beyond 3x^{1/4} and Keith Conrad's descent for the sharp count (Mossinghoff, Oliveira e Silva and Trudgian 2021); on RH, x^{1/3+ε} (Montgomery and Vaughan 1981) and x^{11/35+ε} (Liu 2016); short interval variance (Gorodetsky, Matomäki, Radziwiłł and Rodgers 2021).
- Pólya's kernel (Riemann 1859; Pólya 1926) and its positivity, credited by Biane, Pitman and Yor (2001) to Chung and to Newman (1976).
- The positivity criterion for xi (Hinkkanen 1997; Lagarias 1999); the shifted Thorin family of xi (Polson 2018).
- Lazarević's inequality (Lazarević 1966); no positive real zero of L(s, χ_d) for -3·10^8 ≤ d < 0 (Watkins 2004).

#### New results

The Notes call the Gamma(2) Mertens representation, the threshold ν ≤ 2 and the two kernel sign theorems new as far as the authors know; the zeta Thorin equivalence is from Polson (2017).

- [Squarefree constant as two tilted Pólya means and a sum over the zeros of zeta](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#squarefree_constant_tilted_polya_means) (Theorem 17.4, page 284; proved): The constant in the asymptotic formula for the sum of the reciprocals of the squarefree integers up to x is an explicit elementary constant plus a combination of two tilted means of the Pólya law of the Riemann xi function, equivalently a sum over the zeros of zeta. New in this book.
- [Riemann hypothesis as the generalized gamma convolution property of the reciprocal xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#reciprocal_xi_ggc_riemann_hypothesis) (Proposition 17.5, page 284; proved): The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the reciprocal of the Riemann xi function, centred at one half and evaluated along the square root, being the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, whose Thorin atoms are then the squared ordinates of the zeros; this is a reformulation, not a proof. First stated in Polson (2017, version 26 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Riemann hypothesis for a Dedekind zeta function as a generalized gamma convolution property](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dedekind_zeta_thorin_ggc_equivalence) (Proposition 17.6, page 285; proved): For a number field whose Dedekind zeta function does not vanish at the centre, the Riemann hypothesis for that function is equivalent to the reciprocal of its completion along the square root being a generalized gamma convolution transform with Thorin atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros; this is a reformulation, not a proof. New in this book.
- [Riemann hypothesis and the exponentially smoothed squarefree count](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#exponentially_smoothed_squarefree_count_rh) (Theorem 17.7, page 286; proved): The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to an error of order x to the power one quarter plus epsilon in the exponentially smoothed count of squarefree integers, and under the Riemann hypothesis with simple zeros the smoothed count has an explicit expansion over the halved zeros. New in this book.
- [Riemann hypothesis and the mean square of the squarefree error](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#squarefree_error_mean_square_rh) (Theorem 17.8, page 287; proved): The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to a bound of order X to the power three halves plus epsilon for the integral, over the dyadic interval from X to 2X, of the square of the error term in the count of squarefree integers. New in this book.
- [Gamma smoothed squarefree count under the Riemann hypothesis, uniformly in the shape](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gamma_smoothed_squarefree_count_bound_uniform_in_shape) (Proposition 17.10, page 288; conditional on the Riemann hypothesis): Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, averaging the squarefree count over a Gamma law of shape n at least one and mean x gives an error of order x to the one quarter times n to the one eighth, up to epsilon powers, uniformly in n. New in this book.
- [Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree error as an average of the Mertens function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gamma2_smoothed_squarefree_error_mertens_representation) (Theorem 17.11, page 289; proved): After smoothing by a Gamma(2) law the error in the count of squarefree integers is exactly minus one half of the mean of the Mertens function at a random point with an explicit density, and that density is twice the gap between a continuous and an integer rate mixture of Gamma(2) densities. New in this book.
- [Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree count, the Riemann hypothesis and its explicit expansion](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gamma2_smoothed_squarefree_count_riemann_hypothesis) (Corollary 17.12, page 290; proved): The Gamma(2) smoothed count of squarefree integers has an error smaller than the square root of X unconditionally, the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to an error of order X to the one quarter plus epsilon, and under the Riemann hypothesis with simple zeros the smoothed count has an explicit expansion over the halved zeros. New in this book.
- [Sharp threshold for Gamma smoothing of the squarefree count as a positive average of the Mertens function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gamma_smoothing_mertens_positivity_threshold) (Theorem 17.14, page 291; proved): Smoothing the count of squarefree integers by a Gamma law of shape nu turns its error into an average of the Mertens function with positive weights exactly when nu is at most 2, so Gamma(2) is the largest shape for which this holds. New in this book.
- [Constant of the logarithmic squarefree ideal sum over a number field as a sum over Dedekind zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#squarefree_ideal_constant_number_fields) (Theorem 17.16, page 293; proved): Over any number field, the constant in the asymptotic formula for the sum of the reciprocal norms of the squarefree ideals is an explicit term in the discriminant and the signature plus a sum over the zeros of the Dedekind zeta function. New in this book.
- [Brownian subordination of the reciprocal xi function off the critical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#xi_off_critical_line_brownian_subordination) (Corollary 17.15, page 293; proved): With its basepoint at or to the right of the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function in the critical strip, the reciprocal xi function along the square root is, unconditionally, the Laplace transform of a sum over pairs of conjugate zeros of an exponential time plus a Brownian first passage time, so each Thorin atom is smeared by its own Brownian clock. New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic Dedekind zeta function and its positivity for small discriminants](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#imaginary_quadratic_polya_kernel_positivity) (Theorem 17.17, page 294; proved): The completed Dedekind zeta function of an imaginary quadratic field is the Fourier transform of an explicit even, doubly exponentially decaying kernel built from ideal counts, and this kernel is positive for the four fields whose discriminant is smaller than pi squared in absolute value. New in this book.
- [Pólya kernels of imaginary quadratic fields in which 2 and 3 are inert take negative values](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#imaginary_quadratic_polya_kernel_sign_change) (Theorem 17.18, page 295; proved): For every imaginary quadratic field in which both 2 and 3 are inert, a set of infinitely many fields that includes those with discriminants -19, -43, -67 and -163, the Pólya kernel of the Dedekind zeta function takes negative values. New in this book.
- [How often the Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field is positive](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#density_of_positive_imaginary_quadratic_polya_kernels) (Open Problem 17.2, page 297; open): The book asks whether a positive proportion of imaginary quadratic fields have a positive Pólya kernel, and whether finitely many splitting conditions on small primes force positivity. New in this book.

#### Key terms

squarefree integers, square free numbers, Möbius function, Pólya kernel, Thorin atoms, generalized gamma convolution, Euler Kronecker constant, Dedekind zeta function, exponential smoothing, Gamma smoothing, Mertens function, Lazarević inequality, Conrad descent, Omega theorem, imaginary quadratic field, inert primes, Riemann hypothesis, RH

chapters.title: Dirichlet Beta and the Gaussian Field
chapters.summary:
The chapter works out the Thorin framework of the Riemann xi function for the Dirichlet beta function, the L function of the character modulo 4 of the Gaussian field Q(i). Its Pólya kernel is the eta cube theta series, positive by Jacobi's identity, but its Lévy measure is signed, so Thorin positivity is arithmetic rather than termwise. The chapter recalls the closed form of the Thorin density, the generalized gamma convolution (GGC) property for basepoints at least one and the equivalence of the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for beta with Thorin positivity; shows by Kronecker's theorem that bounds using only the sizes of prime atoms are sharp; and writes the Thorin density of beta as that of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) minus that of zeta. Its own results, some unconditional only below about the height to which GRH for beta is verified, are positivity on the real axis, localisation of negative Thorin density near zeros off the line, a comparison lemma with sharp constant 1 + √2, the minimum of the logarithmic derivative on the real axis (an analogue of Lagarias's theorem), and the Thorin measure as the argument. None proves a Riemann hypothesis.

#### From the literature

- Jacobi's identity for the eta cube and Euler's pentagonal identity; the theta series proof of the functional equation (Iwaniec and Kowalski 2004).
- The Riemann hypothesis as positivity of the logarithmic derivative of xi right of the critical line (Hinkkanen 1997; Lagarias 1999), and its minimum on vertical lines at the real axis (Lagarias 1999; Garunkštis 2000, 2002; Broughan 2009).
- The grouping of zeros off the line (Levinson and Montgomery 1974).
- Verifications of GRH for small conductors (Platt 2016) and of the Riemann hypothesis (Platt and Trudgian 2021).
- The Pólya variable of xi is not infinitely divisible (Roynette and Yor 2005).
- From the authors' papers: the argument form for xi (Polson 2017); the sine squared lemma and a complex character modulo 5 where the minimum property fails (Polson 2018).

#### New results

Polson (2018) first stated for real primitive characters the closed form of the Thorin density, the GGC property above basepoint one and the equivalence of GRH with the GGC property.

- [Lévy form of the completed Dirichlet beta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_levy_form) (Theorem 18.4, page 304; proved): To the right of the critical strip the logarithm of the completed Dirichlet beta function has a Lévy Khintchine form whose Lévy measure is signed, a positive archimedean density plus prime atoms carrying the signs of the character modulo 4. New in this book.
- [Signed sine squared lemma for Thorin densities](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#signed_sine_squared_lemma) (Lemma 18.6, page 304; proved): The sine squared lemma of Polson (2018), with a first step of Roynette and Yor, which turns the Lévy measure of a function into the Thorin density of its shifted reciprocal, extends linearly to signed Lévy measures once the positivity conclusion is dropped. New in this book.
- [Thorin density of the reciprocal completed Dirichlet beta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_thorin_density) (Theorem 18.7, page 305; proved): To the right of the critical strip the shifted reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet beta function has an explicit Thorin representation whose density is the real part of the logarithmic derivative on a vertical line divided by an explicit factor. First stated in Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, arXiv:1804.10043.
- [GGC property of the shifted reciprocal Dirichlet beta function for basepoints at least one](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_ggc_basepoints_at_least_one) (Theorem 18.8, page 306; proved): Unconditionally, for every basepoint at least one, the shifted reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet beta function is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and a positive Thorin density; for basepoints above one this is a case of a theorem of Polson (2018). New in this book.
- [Termwise Thorin positivity threshold for the Dirichlet beta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_termwise_thorin_threshold) (Proposition 18.9, page 307; proved): Bounding the prime atoms of the Dirichlet beta function by their absolute values proves positivity of its Thorin density at every height only for basepoints above an explicit threshold close to 2.28. New in this book.
- [GRH for the Dirichlet beta function as Thorin positivity](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_grh_as_thorin_positivity) (Theorem 18.10, page 308; proved): The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet beta function is equivalent to the generalized gamma convolution property of its shifted reciprocals at every basepoint right of the critical line, and to positivity of the real part of its logarithmic derivative there (the criterion of Hinkkanen and Lagarias), a reformulation and not a proof. First stated in Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, arXiv:1804.10043.
- [Thorin domination in the Gaussian field](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gaussian_field_thorin_domination) (Theorem 18.13, page 310; proved): Through the factorisation of the Dedekind zeta function of the Gaussian field, the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is that of the Gaussian field minus that of the Riemann zeta function, and the generalized Riemann hypothesis for beta is equivalent to the first dominating the second on every line right of the critical line. New in this book.
- [Kronecker sharpness of termwise Thorin bounds for the Dirichlet beta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_kronecker_sharpness) (Proposition 18.14, page 310; proved): By Kronecker's theorem, bounds on the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function that use only the sizes of the prime atoms are sharp, so they prove positivity on a line only above a height that grows exponentially as the basepoint approaches one. New in this book.
- [Unconditional Thorin positivity of the Dirichlet beta function near the real axis](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_thorin_positivity_near_real_axis) (Theorem 18.15, page 311; proved): On every line right of the critical line the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is positive near the origin, unconditionally, because the logarithm of the completed function is the cumulant generating function of a symmetric law with a positive density. New in this book.
- [Localisation of negative Thorin density for the Dirichlet beta function below the verified height](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_negative_thorin_windows) (Corollary 18.17, page 312; proved): Read as a statement on Thorin densities, the grouping of zeros of Levinson and Montgomery shows that the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is positive on every line right of the critical line up to half a unit below the height to which its generalized Riemann hypothesis has been verified, and that a failure of the hypothesis could make it negative only in windows of half width less than one half around ordinates of zeros off the line. New in this book.
- [Comparison lemma for pairs of zeros with sharp constant one plus root two](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#zero_pair_comparison_lemma_sharp_constant) (Lemma 18.18, page 312; proved): An elementary lemma with a sharp constant on how the contribution of a symmetric pair of zeros to the real part of a logarithmic derivative, divided by the distance to the critical line, varies with that distance. New in this book.
- [Comparison of the logarithmic derivative across vertical lines](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#log_derivative_comparison_across_vertical_lines) (Theorem 18.19, page 312; proved): At heights not too close to a zero off the critical line, and so unconditionally at heights up to 1.21 below the height to which the generalized Riemann hypothesis for beta has been verified, the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function divided by the distance to the critical line does not increase as the line moves right, and the same holds for the Riemann xi function and for real primitive characters. New in this book.
- [Explicit lower bound for the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_explicit_log_derivative_lower_bound) (Corollary 18.20, page 313; proved): At heights not too close to a zero off the critical line, the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function on lines right of the critical line has an explicit lower bound that grows like a multiple of the logarithm of the height. New in this book.
- [Minimum on the real axis of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_minimum_on_real_axis) (Theorem 18.21, page 313; proved): On each line right of the critical line with real part at most 3.15, the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function is smallest on the real axis, unconditionally at heights up to 1.21 below the height to which its generalized Riemann hypothesis has been verified, and that hypothesis is equivalent to this minimum property at every height on the lines up to real part one. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of the Dirichlet beta function as its argument](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_thorin_measure_is_argument) (Theorem 18.22, page 314; proved): Extending a theorem of Polson (2017) for the Riemann xi function, the cumulative Thorin measure of the shifted completed Dirichlet beta function on a zero free vertical line equals its argument divided by pi, which gives a Riemann von Mangoldt type asymptotic and, under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the zero counting function in the limit at the critical line. New in this book.
- [GRH for the Dirichlet beta function as a monotone argument](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_grh_as_monotone_argument) (Corollary 18.23, page 315; proved): The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet beta function is equivalent to the argument of its completed function being nondecreasing along every zero free vertical line right of the critical line (for the Riemann xi function, part of a theorem of Polson 2017), a reformulation and not a proof. New in this book.
- [Eta cube kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not completely monotone](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#eta_cube_kernel_not_completely_monotone) (Proposition 18.24, page 316; proved): Neither the one sided Pólya kernel of the Dirichlet beta function, divided by its variable, nor the cube of the eta function on the imaginary axis is completely monotone, so the kernel is not a positive mixture of gamma densities of shape two. New in this book.
- [Thorin domination, localisation and comparison for real primitive characters](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#real_characters_thorin_domination_and_comparison) (Theorem 18.25, page 317; proved): The Thorin decomposition through the quadratic field, the generalized gamma convolution property for basepoints at least one (above one a theorem of Polson 2018), the domination criterion for the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the localisation of negative density by the grouping of zeros of Levinson and Montgomery, and the comparison across vertical lines extend from the Dirichlet beta function to every real primitive character, as does positivity near the real axis when the theta kernel of the character is positive. New in this book.
- [Coupling of the Thorin variables of the Gaussian field below basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gaussian_field_thorin_coupling_below_one) (Open Problem 18.1, page 318; open): Asks for a construction from the Gaussian primes of the splitting of the Thorin variable of the Gaussian field into Riemann zeta and Dirichlet beta parts that could survive to the left of basepoint one, using the phases of the prime atoms. New in this book.
- [Lower bound for the decrease of the argument in a negative window](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_negative_window_argument_bound) (Open Problem 18.2, page 318; open): Asks for a lower bound on how much a hypothetical pair of zeros off the critical line makes the argument of the completed Dirichlet beta function decrease, strong enough to be contradicted by a mean value estimate. New in this book.
- [Minimum on the real axis on all lines to the right](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_beta_minimum_on_all_lines) (Open Problem 18.3, page 318; open): Asks to extend the minimum on the real axis of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function to every line right of the critical line below the verified height, and to every height on the lines with real part at least one. New in this book.
- [Positivity on the reciprocal side from eta products](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#eta_reciprocal_side_positivity) (Open Problem 18.4, page 318; open): Asks whether the complete monotonicity of the reciprocals of the eta cube and eta products passes, through incomplete Mellin transforms, to a positive representation on the reciprocal side of the completed Dirichlet beta function or of the L function of the character modulo 12. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Dirichlet beta function, L(s, chi_{-4}), automorphic induction, eta cube, Pólya kernel, Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, signed Lévy measure, GRH, Hinkkanen Lagarias criterion, Levinson Montgomery, Riemann von Mangoldt formula, chi_12

chapters.title: Signed Thorin Measures
chapters.summary:
By the Thorin criterion, the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for a self dual automorphic L function holds exactly when its Thorin measure, with atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros, is positive. The chapter computes, with no hypothesis on the zeros, a smoothed signed version of that measure: the Stieltjes inversion, at distance epsilon above the cut, of the logarithmic derivative of the clock Λ(c + √s)/Λ(c). Zeros on the critical line give positive Lorentzians; a pair of zeros off the line gives a zero mass term with a negative lobe, which vanishes as epsilon tends to zero and can be masked by a nearby zero on the line, so one width excludes nothing by itself; positivity at every width, with no real zeros, is the Herglotz form of the criterion, which contains GRH and is not evidence for it. Uncertified computations for zeta, the real character modulo 12 and the Ramanujan Delta function find the signed density positive on finite windows and match zero counts by the argument principle with sign changes on the critical line. An opening section explains where Scholze's work enters the Langlands programme and why it does not enter these computations.

#### From the literature

- Continuation and functional equation of the standard L functions of GL(n) (Godement and Jacquet 1972), after Hecke (1918, 1936, 1937) and Tate (1967); the conductor (Jacquet, Piatetski Shapiro and Shalika 1981).
- Galois representations for torsion classes (Scholze 2015); a new proof (Scholze 2013) of the local Langlands correspondence of Harris and Taylor (2001) and Henniart (2000); potential automorphy over CM fields (Allen, Calegari, Caraiani, Gee, Helm, Le Hung, Newton, Scholze, Taylor and Thorne 2023); L parameters (Fargues and Scholze 2026).
- Stieltjes inversion (Stieltjes 1894; Akhiezer 1965); Pólya's kernel (Pólya 1926); theta functions with positive real zeros (Louboutin and Munsch 2013).
- Zero verifications (Backlund 1914; Rumely 1993; Platt and Trudgian 2021; Hiary, Ireland and Kyi 2027) and Turing's method (Turing 1953; Booker 2006).
- From the authors' papers: the Thorin theory of xi that the criterion extends (Polson 2018); positivity of the Thorin density of xi forces every extremal zero onto the critical line (Polson 2026).

#### New results

Its one proposition is an elementary consequence of the product over the zeros.

- [Negative lobe of the signed Thorin density](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#signed_thorin_density_negative_lobe) (Proposition 19.1, page 325; proved): In the signed Thorin density obtained by Stieltjes inversion of the logarithmic derivative of an automorphic clock, zeros on the critical line give positive Lorentzians, a pair of zeros off the line contributes a term of total mass zero, negative near its centre when the smoothing width is below twice the ordinate times the distance of the zero from the line and tending to zero with the width, and with no real zeros positivity at every width is equivalent to all zeros lying on the line. New in this book.
- [Characterising positive Pólya kernels of self dual L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#positive_polya_kernels_characterisation) (Open Problem 19.1, page 329; open): Asks which self dual L functions with root number one have a positive Pólya kernel, and whether at fixed degree positivity is decided by finitely many coefficients and the conductor. New in this book.
- [Masking of the negative lobe of a signed Thorin density](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#negative_lobe_masking) (Open Problem 19.2, page 329; open): Asks under which conditions on the nearby zeros positivity of the signed Thorin density at a single smoothing width rules out a zero off the critical line, given that a zero on the line can mask the negative lobe. New in this book.

#### Key terms

signed Thorin density, Herglotz function, Pick function, Nevanlinna function, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Turing's method, Pólya kernel, chi_12, Ramanujan Delta function, potential automorphy, local Langlands correspondence

chapters.title: Reciprocity through the Swap
chapters.summary:
How much of Langlands reciprocity, the equality of Galois and automorphic L functions, can be stated as probability about Frobenius data? Quadratic reciprocity, Gauss's sign and the Schaar Landsberg reciprocity for Gauss sums are rederived from the characteristic function of the normal law. On a Frobenius probability space (Dirichlet's measure), reciprocity is almost sure equality, Chebotarev and Rankin Selberg become orthonormality, and reciprocity in law gives uniqueness and irreducibility. Labelling the prime factors of a zeta distributed random integer by equidistributed Frobenius data gives a Gamma process limit: Frobenius functionals converge to generalized gamma convolutions (GGC), reciprocity laws become vanishing Thorin measures, a zero two law holds (conjectured in the mixed case), and the drift of the split primes toward their Gamma limit is Ihara's Euler Kronecker constant over the degree, up to finitely many Euler factors and a prime power term. The Thorin framework (Pólya kernels, explicit formula, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples) gives a kernel symmetry form of Hecke's converse theorem, a Gamma shape test of irreducibility, a complete monotonicity criterion for Artin's conjecture with GRH from a Galois heat trace, rigidity at a single prime and a Thorin converse theorem at level one. None of this proves a new case of reciprocity, Artin's conjecture or GRH: the criteria restate them or give sufficient conditions.

#### From the literature

- Reciprocity for quadratic Gauss sums (Schaar 1850, Landsberg 1893), Gauss's sign (Gauss 1811), quadratic reciprocity from the theta transformation (Dym and McKean 1972), generalized Gauss sums (Berndt, Evans and Williams 1998).
- The Chebotarev density theorem (Chebotarev 1926) via Brauer induction (Brauer 1947); the Rankin Selberg pole, strong multiplicity one (Jacquet and Shalika 1981; Shahidi 1981; Jacquet, Piatetski Shapiro and Shalika 1983; Moeglin and Waldspurger 1989).
- Prime factors of random integers (Billingsley 1972; Lloyd 1984), the Gamma process (Kingman 1993), generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992), Euler Kronecker constants (Ihara 2006).
- Converse theorems (Hecke 1936; Weil 1967; Jacquet and Langlands 1970; Cogdell and Piatetski Shapiro 1994); Weil's explicit formula and positivity criterion (Weil 1952, 1972).

#### New results

- [Reciprocity in law between Artin and cuspidal automorphic representations](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#reciprocity_in_law) (Corollary 20.15, page 345; proved): On a probability space of prime powers weighted by Dirichlet's measure, asymptotic agreement in mean square of Frobenius traces with Hecke eigenvalues follows from reciprocity, determines the partner up to isomorphism on either side, forces irreducibility and gives agreement within any tolerance outside a set of primes of density zero, but asserts no existence. New in this book.
- [Congruence conditions see exactly the abelian part of an Artin representation](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#congruences_see_exactly_the_abelian_part) (Proposition 20.16, page 346; proved): The limiting conditional mean of the trace of an irreducible Artin representation given a congruence condition modulo N on the prime power is nonzero only for one dimensional representations that factor through the field of N th roots of unity, a reformulation of Chebotarev's theorem for the compositum with a cyclotomic field in which the Kronecker Weber theorem becomes measurability with respect to congruences. New in this book.
- [Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#frobenius_labelled_factorisation_gamma_process_limit) (Theorem 20.18, page 349; proved): As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, the logarithms of its prime power factors, multiplied by the parameter minus one and labelled by any equidistributed sequence of points such as Frobenius classes or Sato Tate angles, converge in law to the jumps of a standard Gamma subordinator carrying independent labels drawn from the equidistribution law, and the labelled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma random measure, so that equidistribution becomes a Gamma process. New in this book.
- [Chebotarev as a Gamma process with Dirichlet class shares and an arithmetic arcsine law](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#chebotarev_gamma_process_and_arithmetic_arcsine_law) (Corollary 20.20, page 351; proved): The parts of the logarithm of a zeta distributed random integer carried by the primes of each Frobenius class are independent and asymptotically Gamma with shape the Chebotarev density, their shares are asymptotically Dirichlet and independent of the exponential total, and for a quadratic character the share carried by the inert primes converges in law to the arcsine law. New in this book.
- [Frobenius functionals of a zeta random integer converge to generalized gamma convolutions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#frobenius_functionals_converge_to_generalized_gamma_convolutions) (Theorem 20.21, page 352; proved): Weighting the rescaled logarithms of the prime power factors of a zeta distributed random integer by a nonnegative continuous function of equidistributed labels, such as Frobenius data, gives in the limit a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is an image of the label law, and, when the set where the weight is positive is a continuity set of that law, the probability that the weighted sum vanishes is the parameter minus one raised to the Thorin mass, to leading logarithmic order. New in this book.
- [Thorin criteria for reciprocity laws as vanishing of Thorin measures](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_criteria_for_reciprocity) (Theorem 20.22, page 353; proved): For pairs of Artin representations, abelian characters, quadratic reciprocity and pairs of elliptic curves, the squared discrepancy of Frobenius data gives in the limit a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure vanishes exactly when the two kinds of data agree, which restates Kronecker Weber and quadratic reciprocity and computes the shape of their failure, for example a scaled chi squared law when the sign factor is omitted from quadratic reciprocity. New in this book.
- [Zero two law for the discrepancy subordinator of two Artin or two cuspidal representations](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#zero_two_law_for_frobenius_discrepancy_subordinators) (Theorem 20.23, page 355; proved): When the squared discrepancy between the Frobenius traces of two Artin representations, or between the Hecke eigenvalues of two cuspidal automorphic representations, sets the intensity of a random integer, its rescaled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma law whose integer shape is the squared distance between the two, which is zero or two when both are irreducible Artin representations or both are cuspidal. New in this book.
- [Mixed zero two law conjecture for an Artin and a cuspidal automorphic representation](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#mixed_zero_two_law_conjecture) (Conjecture 20.24, page 356; open): The book conjectures that for an irreducible Artin representation and a cuspidal automorphic representation of the same dimension the rescaled discrepancy subordinator has as limit either a point mass at zero or a Gamma law of shape two, the former exactly when their local factors agree at almost all primes, which is the orthogonality half of reciprocity and asserts no existence. New in this book.
- [Mixed zero two law for automorphic Artin representations and unconditional moment bounds](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#mixed_zero_two_law_known_cases_and_moment_bounds) (Proposition 20.25, page 356; proved): The mixed zero two law holds whenever the Artin representation is automorphic, hence in dimension one, for odd two dimensional representations and for two dimensional representations with solvable image, the rescaled discrepancy has bounded first and second moments unconditionally, and a limit concentrated at zero implies reciprocity in law. New in this book.
- [Euler Kronecker drift in the Gamma limit of Chebotarev classes](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#euler_kronecker_drift_of_chebotarev_gamma_limit) (Theorem 20.26, page 357; proved): The rescaled part of the logarithm of a zeta distributed random integer carried by the primes of a Frobenius class approaches its Gamma limit at a rate linear in the parameter minus one, with an explicit drift built from logarithmic derivatives of Artin L functions at one and a prime power term, and for the primes that split completely the drift is Ihara's Euler Kronecker constant of the field, with the Euler factors at the excluded primes removed, divided by the degree, plus a nonnegative term. New in this book.
- [Hecke's criterion as the symmetry of a Pólya kernel built from Frobenius traces](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#hecke_criterion_as_polya_kernel_symmetry) (Proposition 20.27, page 360; proved): A restatement of Hecke's theorem in which the functional equation of a Dirichlet series with polynomially bounded coefficients becomes the evenness or oddness of its Pólya kernel, so that at level one the modularity of Galois data is the symmetry of one function on the line built from Frobenius traces. New in this book.
- [Gamma shape of the Rankin Selberg subordinator detects irreducibility of an Artin representation](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gamma_shape_detects_irreducibility) (Theorem 20.28, page 362; proved): The rescaled Rankin Selberg subordinator of an Artin representation, built from squared Frobenius traces, converges to a Gamma law whose shape is the sum of the squared multiplicities of its irreducible constituents, so the representation is irreducible exactly when the limit is exponential, the Galois counterpart of cuspidality on the automorphic side. New in this book.
- [Complete monotonicity of the Galois heat trace as a criterion for holomorphy and GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#galois_heat_trace_complete_monotonicity_criterion) (Theorem 20.30, page 363; proved): For a self dual L function with meromorphic continuation of finite order and a functional equation, a heat trace computed from Frobenius traces, the conductor and the gamma factor equals half the sum over zeros minus half the sum over poles of a Gaussian in the ordinate, and it is completely monotone exactly when the L function is entire with all zeros on the critical line, a restricted form of Weil's positivity criterion that reformulates Artin's conjecture together with GRH and proves neither. New in this book.
- [The Galois heat trace detects a change of Frobenius data at a single prime](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#galois_heat_trace_sees_every_prime) (Proposition 20.31, page 365; proved): Changing the local factors of an L function that is entire with all zeros on the critical line at a nonempty set of primes thin enough that the sum of log p over the square root of p converges, a single prime included, while keeping the conductor, the gamma factor and Satake parameters of absolute value at most one, destroys the complete monotonicity of the Galois heat trace, unlike any statement about the distribution of Frobenius data. New in this book.
- [Euler half line Thorin criterion for holomorphy, functional equation and GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#euler_half_line_thorin_criterion) (Theorem 20.32, page 366; proved): If the reciprocal of a self dual completed Euler product, read on the half line beyond one after a square root change of variable, is a constant times the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a sum of point masses of positive integer weight, then the completed L function is entire, satisfies its functional equation, is bounded in vertical strips and has all zeros on the critical line, and conversely for an entire completion of order one with nonzero central value and all zeros on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Thorin converse theorem at level one](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_converse_theorem_level_one) (Corollary 20.33, page 367; proved): A Thorin form of Hecke's converse theorem in which self dual Galois data of conductor one, with the gamma factor of a weight divisible by four and the Ramanujan bound, come from a cusp form for the full modular group satisfying GRH whenever the normalised reciprocal Euler product is a constant times the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a sum of point masses of positive integer weight, a hypothesis stated on the Euler half line and stronger than reciprocity since it contains GRH. New in this book.
- [Unconditional generalized gamma convolution family from the Rankin Selberg square of an Artin representation](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#rankin_selberg_square_ggc_family) (Proposition 20.34, page 368; proved): For every Artin representation and every base point beyond one, the normalised reciprocal of the completed Rankin Selberg square is an explicit exponential factor times the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin density is the sine squared transport of a measure built from squared Frobenius traces plus a gamma factor term, so positivity holds unconditionally on the Euler half line. New in this book.
- [Thorin converse theorem for twists that are not self dual](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_converse_theorem_for_twists_problem) (Open Problem 20.1, page 370; open): The book asks for a version of its Euler half line Thorin criterion for twists that are not self dual, strong enough to combine with the converse theorem of Cogdell and Piatetski Shapiro. New in this book.
- [Descending the base point of transported Thorin densities of the Rankin Selberg square](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#descending_the_base_point_problem) (Open Problem 20.2, page 370; open): The book asks whether the transported Thorin densities of the Rankin Selberg square of an automorphic Artin representation, with the drift split off, stay nonnegative for base points between the centre and the edge of the critical strip, and which features of Frobenius data control their sign. New in this book.
- [Signed Thorin measures separating Artin's conjecture from GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#signed_thorin_measures_artin_conjecture_problem) (Open Problem 20.3, page 370; open): The book asks for a property of Frobenius data on the Euler half line that forces the integer weights of the signed Thorin measure of an Artin L function to be positive, which is Artin's conjecture, without forcing its atoms to be real, which is GRH. New in this book.
- [A Fejér summation for primes making the Galois heat trace positive](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#fejer_summation_for_primes_problem) (Open Problem 20.4, page 371; open): The book asks for positive Fejér type weights on prime powers under which positivity of the weighted Galois heat trace follows from Frobenius data alone, as Fejér positivity does for the heat trace of the circle, which through the complete monotonicity criterion would give holomorphy and GRH. New in this book.
- [Reciprocity in law versus reciprocity](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#reciprocity_in_law_versus_reciprocity_problem) (Open Problem 20.5, page 371; open): The book asks to show that an irreducible Artin representation reciprocal in law with a cuspidal automorphic representation agrees with it at all but finitely many primes, a strong multiplicity one statement across the Galois and automorphic sides. New in this book.
- [The mixed zero two law under meromorphy and for an even icosahedral representation](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#mixed_zero_two_law_problem) (Open Problem 20.6, page 371; open): The book asks to derive the dichotomy of its mixed zero two law from meromorphy of the mixed Rankin Selberg L function near the edge of the critical strip, to reduce the rest of the conjecture to reciprocity in law, and to prove the conjecture for one even icosahedral Artin representation. New in this book.
- [Joint marked Gamma processes of an Artin and a cuspidal representation](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#joint_marked_processes_problem) (Open Problem 20.7, page 371; open): The book asks whether the joint limit of the Frobenius labelled Gamma processes of an Artin representation and a cuspidal automorphic representation exists, and whether its label law either sits on the set where the two traces agree or gives their squared discrepancy a Thorin mass bounded below in terms of the dimension. New in this book.
- [Signs of the Euler Kronecker drifts of Chebotarev classes](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#signs_of_euler_kronecker_drifts_problem) (Open Problem 20.8, page 371; open): The book asks to characterise the Galois number fields whose split primes approach their Gamma limit from above, which requires a negative Euler Kronecker constant, and to relate the signs of the drifts of the Frobenius classes to Chebotarev biases and races. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Langlands reciprocity, Artin conjecture, cuspidal automorphic representation, Frobenius trace, Chebotarev density theorem, Rankin Selberg, reciprocity in law, quadratic reciprocity, Gauss sum, Kronecker Weber theorem, zeta distribution, Gamma process, arcsine law, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, zero two law, Euler Kronecker constant, Pólya kernel, converse theorem, explicit formula, heat trace, complete monotonicity, GRH, van Dantzig pair, Wald couple

chapters.title: Hitting Times and Reciprocity
chapters.summary:
How do hitting times express reciprocity laws? The chapter reads Kemeny's constant, spanning trees and resistances of reversible chains, hitting rates of prime factors, explosion of pure birth processes and Brownian exit as arithmetic identities. For the supersingular ℓ isogeny walk in characteristic N, Kemeny's constant is a harmonic sum of the factors of the order of J_0(N)(F_ℓ), point counts of elliptic curves of conductor N when all newforms are rational; Hasse Weil bounds follow, and for N congruent to 1 modulo 12 the Kirchhoff index and an isomorphism criterion, for most primes r, between the r parts of the critical (sandpile) group and of J_0(N)(F_ℓ); the asymptotic class number of Tsfasman and Vlăduţ is the spanning tree entropy of the (ℓ+1) regular tree. Chebotarev densities are hitting rates of the largest prime factors of a zeta distributed random integer; the Thorin converse theorem becomes a statement on explosion times, with GRH in its hypothesis; and the functional equation of every odd primitive Dirichlet L function is the identity between the image and eigenfunction expansions of a signed Brownian exit law. No new case of reciprocity, of Artin's conjecture or of GRH is proved.

#### From the literature

- Hashimoto's spanning tree formula for isogeny graphs (Hashimoto 1989; Li 2019), read as reciprocity, with the laws of the critical groups as ℓ varies (Munier and Shnidman 2023).
- Brandt matrices (Eichler 1954; Gross 1987), the Eichler Shimura congruence relation (Shimura 1971), and Ogg's conjecture (Ogg 1975), proved by Mazur (1977).
- The asymptotic class number of X_0(N) (Tsfasman and Vlăduţ 2002), spanning trees of regular graphs (McKay 1983), tree entropy (Lyons 2005), vertical Sato Tate (Serre 1997).
- The Kirchhoff index (Gutman and Mohar 1996; Zhu, Klein and Lukovits 1996) and the commute time identity (Chandra, Raghavan, Ruzzo, Smolensky and Tiwari 1996).
- The largest prime factor of a zeta distributed random integer (Lloyd 1984).
- Brownian exit and the functional equation of Dirichlet's beta function (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001, after Ciesielski and Taylor 1962); theta identities from heat kernels (Salminen and Vignat 2024).

#### New results

- [Two prime Kemeny formula for supersingular isogeny walks](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#two_prime_kemeny_formula_for_supersingular_isogeny_walks) (Theorem 21.1, page 377; proved): Kemeny's constant of the random walk along isogenies of prime degree ℓ between the supersingular elliptic curves in characteristic N is a harmonic sum of the factors of the number of points of J_0(N) over the field with ℓ elements, and, when every newform of level N is rational, ℓ+1 times the sum of the reciprocal point counts modulo ℓ of the isogeny classes of elliptic curves of conductor N. New in this book.
- [Isomorphism criterion for sandpile groups of supersingular isogeny graphs and the modular Jacobian](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sandpile_group_and_modular_jacobian_isomorphism_criterion) (Proposition 21.5, page 379; proved): For a prime N congruent to 1 modulo 12 and primes r outside a finite set, the r part of the critical (sandpile) group of the supersingular ℓ isogeny graph in characteristic N, which Munier and Shnidman identify with a quotient of the Hecke algebra, is isomorphic to the r part of the group of points of J_0(N) over the field with ℓ elements exactly when Frobenius at ℓ acts nontrivially on each torsion module of J_0(N) cut out by a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra above r; the criterion is new. New in this book.
- [Resistances and commute times of supersingular isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kirchhoff_index_and_commute_times_of_supersingular_isogeny_graphs) (Theorem 21.6, page 381; proved): For a prime N congruent to 1 modulo 12, the sum of all effective resistances (the Kirchhoff index) of the supersingular ℓ isogeny graph in characteristic N and the mean commute time between its vertices are explicit multiples of its Kemeny constant, a harmonic sum of the factors of the number of points of J_0(N) over the field with ℓ elements. New in this book.
- [Hasse Weil bounds for Kemeny constants and spanning tree counts of isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#hasse_weil_bounds_for_kemeny_constants_and_spanning_trees) (Corollary 21.7, page 381; proved): The Weil bound on Hecke eigenvalues becomes two sided bounds, linear in the genus, on the Kemeny constant of every supersingular isogeny walk of prime level and, for prime levels congruent to 1 modulo 12, two sided bounds, exponential in the genus, on the number of spanning trees of the isogeny graph. New in this book.
- [Tree entropy of the regular tree as the asymptotic class number of J_0(N) over a finite field](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#tree_entropy_as_asymptotic_class_number_of_modular_jacobians) (Theorem 21.8, page 382; proved): As the prime level N grows, the exponential growth rate per unit of genus of the number of points of J_0(N) over the field with ℓ elements, an asymptotic class number given by a theorem of Tsfasman and Vlăduţ, is the spanning tree entropy of the (ℓ+1) regular tree, which therefore also governs the spanning tree counts of the supersingular isogeny graphs of levels congruent to 1 modulo 12; the reading as a tree entropy is, as far as the authors know, new. New in this book.
- [Chebotarev densities as hitting rates of the largest prime factors of a random integer](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#chebotarev_densities_as_hitting_rates_of_largest_prime_factors) (Theorem 21.10, page 385; proved): For a zeta distributed random integer whose prime factors carry equidistributed labels such as Frobenius classes, in the limit as the zeta parameter tends to one, the largest prime factor with label in a given set arrives, on the scale of the exponential integral, after an exponential time whose rate is the measure of that set, so that reciprocity laws say that a discrepancy set is hit at rate zero; for a single label this is Lloyd's limit law, and the labelled form is new. New in this book.
- [Explosion time criterion for zeros on the critical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#explosion_time_criterion_for_zeros_on_the_critical_line) (Theorem 21.11, page 387; proved): A symmetric entire function of order at most one, nonzero at the centre, has all its zeros on the critical line exactly when a normalised reciprocal of its values along a half line is the Laplace transform of the explosion time of a pure birth process, whose birth rates are then the squared ordinates of the zeros; this is an equivalence restating the book's Thorin duality, after Polson (2018), and proves no Riemann hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Thorin converse theorem at level one as an explosion time](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_converse_theorem_at_level_one_as_explosion) (Corollary 21.12, page 388; proved): If a normalised reciprocal of the completed L function of a self dual Galois representation of conductor one, along a half line, is the Laplace transform of the explosion time of a pure birth process, then the representation comes from a level one cusp form satisfying the generalized Riemann hypothesis, and conversely, with a Wald couple between the explosion time and the Pólya variable when the Pólya kernel is nonnegative; the hypothesis contains the generalized Riemann hypothesis, so no new case of reciprocity follows. New in this book.
- [A new proof of the functional equation of odd primitive Dirichlet L functions by a signed Brownian exit law](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#functional_equation_of_odd_dirichlet_l_functions_from_signed_brownian_exit) (Theorem 21.13, page 389; proved): Weighting the starting point of a Brownian motion killed at the ends of an interval by an odd primitive Dirichlet character, the image and eigenfunction expansions of the resulting signed exit law give the classical theta transformation formula and functional equation of the L function, with its Gauss sum root number, extending to every odd primitive character a derivation known for the character modulo 4 (Biane, Pitman and Yor; Salminen and Vignat). New in this book.
- [Limiting law of sandpile groups of supersingular isogeny graphs in the level aspect](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#limiting_law_of_sandpile_groups_of_isogeny_graphs_in_the_level_aspect) (Open Problem 21.1, page 392; open): Find the limiting law, as the prime level grows, of the r parts of the critical groups of supersingular isogeny graphs, a question raised by Munier and Shnidman, describe the critical groups at the primes that the isomorphism criterion excludes, and extend the comparison with the modular Jacobian to the prime 2 and to other levels. New in this book.
- [Vertex hitting times of isogeny walks and Gross's formula](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#vertex_hitting_times_of_isogeny_walks_and_gross_formula) (Open Problem 21.2, page 392; open): Find the distribution over discriminants of the combination of central values of quadratic twists that Gross's formula attaches to hitting times between the reductions of curves with complex multiplication, and decide what the hitting time of the support of the Gross divisor computes. New in this book.

chapters.title: Fermat's Last Theorem and Thorin Measures
chapters.summary:
Is there a Thorin measure form of Fermat's last theorem? The chapter reads the two kinds of one forms in the proof, weight one modular forms (the Langlands Tunnell theorem that starts Wiles's argument) and weight two forms as holomorphic differentials on X_0(N) (the genus zero of X_0(2) that ends it), through Frobenius label laws, Pólya kernels, generalized gamma convolutions, Thorin measures and hitting times. Weight one newforms are those with finitely supported label laws. The answer has three parts: no Thorin statement is equivalent to Fermat's last theorem in a useful sense; given the modularity of semistable elliptic curves (Wiles; Taylor and Wiles), Ribet's level lowering theorem and Mazur's torsion theorem, the last step is the emptiness of the level two Hecke Thorin measure (one supersingular curve in characteristic 2, class number one of the Hurwitz quaternions); and the proof for prime exponents at least 5 is restated as the incompatibility of that empty measure with a positive Eisenstein Thorin shape of the Frey curve, the shape of a Gamma law and a local density in Koblitz's conjecture. No step of the proof is reproved, and no new case of modularity is proved.

#### From the literature

- Modularity of semistable elliptic curves (Wiles 1995; Taylor and Wiles 1995), extended by Breuil, Conrad, Diamond and Taylor (2001); the account of Darmon, Diamond and Taylor (1995).
- The Frey curve and the reduction to modularity (Hellegouarch 1975; Frey 1986; Serre 1987), Ribet's level lowering (Ribet 1990) and level raising (Ribet 1984).
- Mazur's torsion theorem (Mazur 1977), giving irreducibility for Frey curves (Serre 1987).
- The Langlands Tunnell theorem (Langlands 1980; Tunnell 1981); weight one forms and Artin representations (Deligne and Serre 1974; Khare and Wintenberger 2009; Kisin 2009).
- Wilton's congruence for tau modulo 23 (Wilton 1930), explained by Serre (1968).
- Converse theorems (Weil 1967; Conrey and Farmer 1995); Sato Tate (Barnet Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor 2011).
- Koblitz's conjecture and its local densities (Koblitz 1988; Zywina 2011), with vanishing criteria of Serre (1972) and Katz (1981).

#### New results

- [Gamma law of the Eisenstein discrepancy of an elliptic curve](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gamma_law_of_the_eisenstein_discrepancy) (Proposition 22.11, page 409; proved): For an elliptic curve and a prime p, the rescaled logarithmic weight that a zeta distributed random integer puts on the primes at which p does not divide the number of points of the curve converges to a Gamma law whose shape, the classical local density at p in Koblitz's conjecture (Koblitz; Zywina), is also the rate at which the prime factors of the integer hit those primes; the reading of this density as the shape of a Gamma law and as a hitting rate is the book's. New in this book.
- [Fermat's last theorem restated as two Thorin statements](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#fermat_last_theorem_restated_as_two_thorin_statements) (Theorem 22.13, page 412; proved): Given the modularity of semistable elliptic curves (Wiles; Taylor and Wiles), Ribet's level lowering theorem and Mazur's torsion theorem, the known proof of Fermat's last theorem for prime exponents at least five is restated as the incompatibility of a positive Eisenstein Thorin shape of the Frey curve with the empty Hecke Thorin measure at level two; no step of the proof is reproved, and its content stays in those theorems. New in this book.
- [Hasse Weil bound from hitting times on supersingular isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#hasse_weil_bound_from_hitting_times) (Open Problem 22.1, page 415; open): Find a probabilistic proof, for instance through hitting times or a heat kernel on the supersingular isogeny graph, of the bound of Eichler and Shimura with Weil on the Hecke eigenvalues of weight two newforms of prime level. New in this book.
- [Taylor Wiles patching as a Gamma process](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#taylor_wiles_patching_as_a_gamma_process) (Open Problem 22.2, page 415; open): Ask whether the auxiliary primes of the Taylor Wiles patching method can be taken as the atoms, in a fixed Chebotarev class, of the Gamma process of the prime factors of a zeta distributed random integer, with the patched objects as limits in law. New in this book.
- [A probabilistic Mazur theorem for Eisenstein shapes of curves with rational 2 torsion](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#probabilistic_mazur_theorem_for_eisenstein_shapes) (Open Problem 22.3, page 415; open): Ask for a proof through the Gamma law of the Eisenstein discrepancy and isogeny walks, rather than through Mazur's torsion theorem, that an elliptic curve over the rationals with all its 2 torsion rational has positive Eisenstein shape at every prime at least five. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Fermat's last theorem, FLT, modularity theorem, Taylor Wiles patching, Frey curve, Ribet's level lowering, Mazur's torsion theorem, Langlands Tunnell theorem, weight one modular forms, Wilton congruence, Ramanujan tau, Pólya kernel, Polya kernel, heat trace, 11a1, GGC, Thorin measure, Kemeny constant, Hurwitz quaternions, Eisenstein discrepancy, Eisenstein Thorin shape, Gamma law, Koblitz's conjecture, mod p Galois representation, hitting rate

chapters.title: Inverse Laplace Transforms
chapters.summary:
How far can inverse Laplace transforms carry an L function between its Galois side, an Euler product of Frobenius traces, and its automorphic side, a modular form with zeros? The chapter reads an L function through four faces: the Lévy measure of log L, its sine squared transform (a Thorin density when the coefficients are nonnegative), the Pólya kernel (a modular form on the imaginary axis), and Thorin densities near the critical line. It collects the classical inversions and shows that Gaussian averages of the transported density recover every Frobenius trace with explicit error, that the Thorin measure of a self dual L function at a shifted basepoint is a superposition of folded Cauchy laws at the ordinates of the zeros, that atomic generalized gamma convolutions are Gamma times B spline variables, and that the Sato Tate law minimises the Good and Gaskins roughness among densities vanishing on the alcove walls. The example is the weight one eta product η(z)η(23z). Passing from Galois to automorphic data assumes Artin's conjecture (Hecke's theorem in the example); no new case of reciprocity or of the generalized Riemann hypothesis is proved.

#### From the literature

Lerch's theorem and the Bromwich and Post Widder inversion formulas (Widder 1941), Post Widder as a law of large numbers (Feller 1971); Stieltjes inversion (Stieltjes 1894; Akhiezer 1965); Bohr's inversion and uniqueness theorems (Besicovitch 1932); Hecke's Mellin integral (Hecke 1936), Weil's converse theorem (Weil 1967) and weight one forms (Deligne and Serre 1974); the tail of the Thorin variable (Roynette and Yor 2005), here via Doetsch's transfer theorem (Doetsch 1974); Perron's formula (Perron 1908); B splines (Curry and Schoenberg 1966) and Pólya frequency functions (Schoenberg 1951); the Gamma times Dirichlet mean factorisation (James, Roynette and Yor 2008); roughness penalties (Good and Gaskins 1971, 1980; de Montricher, Tapia and Thompson 1975); minimal Fisher information (Huber 1974) and the alcove's Dirichlet spectrum (Bérard 1980).

#### New results

New are the explicit Gaussian error bounds and the Good and Gaskins reading of the Sato Tate law; the Cauchy superposition restates for self dual L functions what Polson (2017) proved for xi.

- [Explicit Gaussian window error for Bohr inversion of the sine squared transport](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#gaussian_window_bohr_inversion_of_the_sine_squared_transport) (Theorem 23.5, page 423; proved): A quantitative form of Bohr's mean value inversion, in which Gaussian averages of the one minus cosine transform of a discrete signed measure recover the weight of each atom with an explicit, exponentially small error, so that the transform is injective. New in this book.
- [Frobenius traces recovered from the transported density with explicit error](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#frobenius_traces_from_the_transported_density) (Corollary 23.6, page 424; proved): The von Mangoldt coefficients of an L function, and so the Frobenius traces of an Artin representation, are read off Gaussian averages of its sine squared transported density, with an explicit error bound at every finite window. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure at a shifted basepoint as zeros plus folded Cauchy noise](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#zeros_plus_cauchy_noise_at_a_shifted_basepoint) (Theorem 23.9, page 428; proved): For a self dual L function the Thorin measure of the completed function, at a basepoint to the right of all zeros, is half a sum of folded Cauchy laws centred at the ordinates of the zeros, and moving the basepoint adds Cauchy noise, which restates for every self dual L function what Polson (2017) proved for the Riemann xi function. First stated in Polson (2017, version 26 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Sato Tate law as the Good and Gaskins roughness minimiser, with shrinkage of symmetric power moments](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sato_tate_law_minimises_the_good_gaskins_roughness) (Theorem 23.12, page 435; proved): The Sato Tate law is the unique minimiser of the Good and Gaskins roughness penalty among densities on the alcove whose square root vanishes on the walls (an inequality of Huber for SU(2) and the Rayleigh principle in general), and for SU(2), near it, the penalised likelihood estimate shrinks each empirical symmetric power moment by an explicit factor. New in this book.
- [Stable recovery of Frobenius traces from a finite window of the transported density](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#stable_recovery_of_frobenius_from_a_window) (Open Problem 23.1, page 437; open): Asks whether stable recovery of the coefficient at n of an L function from its transported density needs a window of length of order n, which would be an uncertainty principle for the Galois side. New in this book.
- [Good and Gaskins penalised likelihood for Thorin densities of L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#good_gaskins_penalised_likelihood_for_thorin_densities) (Open Problem 23.2, page 437; open): Asks for a roughness penalised likelihood estimate of the Thorin density of an L function from finitely many zeros or from a noisy transported density, the form of its maximiser, and a comparison of its error with exact inversion by Gaussian means. New in this book.

#### Key terms
