chapters.title: Random Integers and the Poisson Dirichlet Law
chapters.summary:
How do the prime factors of a random integer, coloured by their Frobenius classes, approach Chebotarev's law? The chapter relates random integers to the Poisson Dirichlet law and Ferguson's Dirichlet process through the zeta distributed random integer and the Gamma process limit of its labelled factorisation. It shows that the normalised labelled factorisation converges to the Dirichlet process with Haar base measure, so that Frobenius functionals converge to an exponential variable times a Dirichlet mean (the Markov Krein identity); that integers weighted by a power of zeta, or by an Euler product with nonnegative logarithmic coefficients, give the whole Ewens family, with Ewens parameter the exponent of the singularity at one; that a size biased prime factor of a uniform integer below x lies in a class with probability the Chebotarev density plus an explicit term of order 1/log x, while the share of distinct prime factors converges only at rate 1/log log x; and that empty classes bound from below the Kolmogorov distance of class shares to their Beta limits. Mertens constants per class are expressed through L(1, χ) and its logarithmic derivative.

#### From the literature

The Poisson Dirichlet law (Kingman 1975); Billingsley's theorem (Billingsley 1972; Knuth and Trabb Pardo 1976), its proof by size biased sampling (Donnelly and Grimmett 1993); Dickman's function (Dickman 1930); the Erdős Kac theorem (Erdős and Kac 1940) and the Sathe Selberg formula (Sathe 1953; Selberg 1954); the zeta random integer (Lloyd 1984); the Dirichlet process (Ferguson 1973) and the identity for Dirichlet means (Cifarelli and Regazzini 1990); the Frobenius class of the largest prime factor (Dawsey 2017); Mertens constants per Chebotarev class (Bardestani and Freiberg 2013); frobenian sets (Serre 1976); Poisson Dirichlet limits for weighted integers (Elboim and Gorodetsky 2024) and arithmetic semigroups (Arratia, Kochman and Miller 2014) and the unlabelled limits for the zeta power random integer (Sun 2026); generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992, 2015).

#### New results

New are the labelled limits, the size biased expansion, the independence of class and share, and the empty class atom with its Kolmogorov bound.

- [Chebotarev as a Dirichlet process for the labelled factorisation of a random integer](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#chebotarev_as_a_dirichlet_process) (Theorem 24.3, page 447; proved): As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, its prime factorisation labelled by Frobenius classes, normalised, converges to Ferguson's Dirichlet process with Haar measure as base measure, and every Frobenius functional converges to an exponential variable times a Dirichlet mean. New in this book.
- [Labelled Ewens family from the random integers weighted by the coefficients of powers of zeta](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#dirichlet_process_limit_of_the_zeta_power_random_integer) (Theorem 24.4, page 450; proved): For random integers weighted by the Dirichlet coefficients of a power of the zeta function, the labelled prime factorisation converges to a Gamma random measure and its normalisation to a Dirichlet process, so powers of zeta realise the whole Ewens family with Frobenius labels; the unlabelled limits for this random integer are due to W. Sun (2026). New in this book.
- [Expansion in 1/log x of the Frobenius class of a size biased prime factor of a random integer](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#size_biased_prime_factor_frobenius_class_expansion) (Theorem 24.5, page 451; proved): The probability that a size biased prime factor of a uniform random integer below x has Frobenius in a given conjugacy class is the Chebotarev density plus an explicit term of order 1/log x built from Euler's constant and the Euler Kronecker constant of the class; this is part (ii) of a theorem whose parts on the largest prime factor (Dawsey) and on distinct prime factors (Mertens's theorem per class, after Bardestani and Freiberg) are known. New in this book.
- [Asymptotic independence of the Frobenius class and the share of a size biased prime factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#independence_of_class_and_share_of_a_size_biased_prime_factor) (Theorem 24.6, page 454; proved): The share of a size biased prime factor of a random integer is asymptotically uniform, as Donnelly and Grimmett showed, and asymptotically independent of its Frobenius class, which follows the Chebotarev densities, both for uniform integers below x and for the zeta random integer. New in this book.
- [Empty Chebotarev classes and a lower bound for the rate of the Dirichlet process limit](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#empty_chebotarev_class_and_lower_bound_for_the_rate) (Theorem 24.8, page 457; proved): For the zeta random integer with parameter close to one, a Frobenius class is empty with probability of exact order a power of the distance to one, the exponent being the Chebotarev density of the class and the constant an explicit classical one, and this atom at zero bounds from below the Kolmogorov distance between the share of the class and its Beta limit; these are parts (i) and (ii) of a theorem whose part (iii) is a case of Serre's theorem on frobenian sets. New in this book.
- [Ewens parameters of Euler products are pole orders](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#ewens_parameters_are_pole_orders) (Theorem 24.9, page 459; proved): For a random integer weighted by an Euler product whose logarithm has nonnegative coefficients, given at the primes by a continuous function of equidistributed labels, the normalised labelled factorisation converges to a Dirichlet process with the weighted equidistribution measure as base measure, and the Poisson Dirichlet parameter is the exponent of the singularity at s equal to one, the order of the pole when there is one; the unlabelled Poisson Dirichlet limits for weighted integers below x are due to Elboim and Gorodetsky (2024), and for arithmetic semigroups to Arratia, Kochman and Miller (2014). New in this book.
- [Upper bound for the rate of the Dirichlet process limit of Chebotarev shares](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#upper_bound_for_the_rate_of_chebotarev_shares) (Open Problem 24.1, page 462; open): Asks for an upper bound matching the lower bound for the Kolmogorov distance between the share of a Frobenius class in a zeta random integer and its Beta limit, and for a Wasserstein bound on the share vector at the rate at which the means converge. New in this book.
- [Signs of the Mertens deficits of the identity class in symmetric group fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#signs_of_the_mertens_deficits) (Open Problem 24.2, page 462; open): Asks how the sign of the deficit of the identity Frobenius class among the distinct prime factors of random integers is distributed over number fields with symmetric Galois group ordered by discriminant, and along families of trinomials. New in this book.
- [An arithmetic operation realising the product closure of generalized gamma convolutions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#an_arithmetic_product_for_frobenius_functionals) (Open Problem 24.3, page 462; open): Asks which operation on representations or L functions, if any, realises Bondesson's closure of generalized gamma convolutions under products of independent variables for the limits of Frobenius functionals. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Poisson Dirichlet distribution, GEM distribution, Ewens sampling formula, Ewens measure, Dirichlet process, Dirichlet mean, Markov Krein identity, Cifarelli Regazzini identity, Gamma process, random integer, zeta distribution, Dickman function, Billingsley theorem, Erdős Kac theorem, Erdos Kac theorem, Chebotarev density theorem, Frobenius class, size biased sampling, largest prime factor, Mertens constants, Euler Kronecker constant, frobenian set, generalized gamma convolution, Thorin measure, Bondesson, HCM

chapters.title: Degree One
chapters.summary:
What do the book's probabilistic readings of reciprocity give in degree one, where reciprocity is a theorem of class field theory? Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions becomes a Dirichlet process limit for the residue classes of the prime factors of a zeta distributed random integer, with Mertens constants for progressions from L(1, χ) and Landau's count of integers avoiding a class as the atom at zero; Hecke's equidistribution of the angles of Gaussian primes becomes a Dirichlet process on the circle. For an elliptic curve with complex multiplication, Deuring's theorem gives a Frobenius angle law half uniform and half an atom, and the chapter proves that base change to the CM field squares the Rankin Selberg Euler product exactly, so the Gamma shape of the Rankin Selberg subordinator over that field is 2, while a curve without complex multiplication by that field keeps shape 1: an unconditional test for complex multiplication. For a primitive real Dirichlet character with L(1/2, χ) nonzero, the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for L(s, χ) is shown equivalent to a generalized gamma convolution representation with Thorin measure on the squared ordinates of the zeros, a reformulation and not a proof, and a shifted Thorin representation holds unconditionally at every basepoint from 1 on.

#### From the literature

- The Kronecker Weber theorem and Artin's reciprocity law (Artin 1927; account in Neukirch 1999), Hecke's Grössencharaktere (Hecke 1920) and Tate's thesis (Tate 1950).
- Mertens' theorem for arithmetic progressions (Williams 1974) and the Dirichlet process (Ferguson 1973).
- Landau's theorem on sums of two squares (Landau 1908) and Wirsing's mean value theorem (Wirsing 1961).
- Equidistribution of the angles of Gaussian primes (Hecke 1920), with its discrepancy under GRH (Kubilius 1955).
- The L function of an elliptic curve with complex multiplication is a Hecke L function (Deuring 1953).
- The primes with a_p = 0 have density zero on a curve without complex multiplication (Serre 1981); Faltings' isogeny theorem (Faltings 1983).

#### New results

The catalogued theorems carry the book's Gamma shape and Thorin results to degree one; none proves a case of GRH.

- [Complex multiplication doubles the Gamma shape of the Rankin Selberg subordinator](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#complex_multiplication_doubles_the_gamma_shape) (Theorem 25.7, page 475; proved): Over its CM field the Rankin Selberg Euler product of an elliptic curve with complex multiplication is exactly the square of its Euler product over the rationals, so the limiting Gamma shape of the associated subordinator doubles from 1 to 2, while a curve without complex multiplication by that field keeps shape 1, which gives an unconditional test for complex multiplication. New in this book.
- [Thorin form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for a real Dirichlet character](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_form_of_grh_for_real_dirichlet_characters) (Theorem 25.8, page 477; proved): For a real primitive Dirichlet character whose L function does not vanish at the centre, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to a generalized gamma convolution representation of the completed L function with Thorin measure on the squared heights of the zeros, and a shifted representation holds unconditionally; this reformulates the hypothesis and does not prove it. New in this book.
- [Limit law for the discrepancy of the Hecke angles of Gaussian primes](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#hecke_angle_discrepancy_limit_law) (Open Problem 25.1, page 480; open): Asks whether the normalised discrepancy of the Hecke angles of Gaussian primes has a limit law, the Kolmogorov law that a Brownian bridge predicts or a different law forced by arithmetic, and the same for the other imaginary quadratic fields of class number one. New in this book.
- [Euler Kronecker constants of Hecke characters and the rate of the Gaussian prime Dirichlet process](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#euler_kronecker_constants_of_hecke_characters) (Open Problem 25.2, page 480; open): Asks for the constants that govern how fast the Dirichlet process of Gaussian prime angles is approached, the sign pattern of the deficits of arcs, and an analogue for arcs of the theorem on atoms at zero. New in this book.
- [An effective Gamma shape test for complex multiplication](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#effective_gamma_shape_test_for_complex_multiplication) (Open Problem 25.3, page 480; open): Asks for an explicit bound on the number of primes after which the empirical Gamma shape provably decides whether an elliptic curve has complex multiplication by a given field. New in this book.

#### Key terms

GL(1), degree one, class field theory, Kronecker Weber, Artin reciprocity, Dirichlet characters, Hecke characters, Grössencharaktere, Gaussian primes, Hecke angles, Dirichlet process, zeta distributed random integer, Mertens constants for progressions, Landau Ramanujan constant, Wirsing's theorem, complex multiplication, CM elliptic curves, Deuring's theorem, Rankin Selberg subordinator, Gamma shape test, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, generalized Riemann hypothesis, GRH

chapters.title: Maass Forms and Brownian Motion
chapters.summary:
How far does the book's dictionary extend to the Maass cusp forms, the other half of the automorphic spectrum of SL(2, Z)? The modular surface is a probability space, Brownian motion on it is ergodic, and, following McKean, the Selberg trace formula is a heat trace identity for Brownian loops. The chapter proves that Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture for a congruence subgroup, open in general, is equivalent to complete monotonicity of its Maass cusp form heat trace with every eigenvalue lowered by 1/4. This is a reformulation, not a proof: unconditionally it gives complete monotonicity for every congruence subgroup only after the smaller shift the Kim Sarnak bound allows, and the full statement for SL(2, Z), where the conjecture is known. Weyl's law keeps the spectrum from being a Thorin measure. Treating closed geodesics as Beurling primes, it proves an unconditional Thorin representation of the geodesic Euler product Z(s+1)/Z(s) at every basepoint to the right of 1, and a Poisson Dirichlet limit for random geodesic integers. It also reads the Ramanujan conjecture for Maass forms at a prime as local Thorin positivity, places even icosahedral Artin representations among Maass forms of eigenvalue 1/4, and states the Eichler Selberg trace formula behind vertical Sato Tate.

#### From the literature

- Maass forms (Maass 1949), the trace formula, the Selberg zeta function and Weyl's law (Selberg 1956; Hejhal 1976, 1983), and the eigenvalues of SL(2, Z) (Hejhal 1992; Booker, Strömbergsson and Venkatesh 2006).
- The Kim Sarnak bound toward the Ramanujan and Selberg conjectures (Kim and Sarnak 2003).
- The hyperbolic heat kernel and the Brownian reading of the trace formula (McKean 1972).
- The prime geodesic theorem (Huber and Selberg; Sarnak 1982 for SL(2, Z); Soundararajan and Young 2013) and reciprocal geodesics (Sarnak 2007).
- Automorphy of dihedral (Maass 1949), tetrahedral (Langlands 1980) and octahedral (Tunnell 1981) Artin representations.
- The Eichler Selberg trace formula (Eichler 1957, Selberg 1956; Zagier 1977) and vertical Sato Tate (Serre 1997; Conrey, Duke and Farmer 1997).

#### New results

None of the catalogued theorems proves a new case of the Selberg or Ramanujan conjectures.

- [Ramanujan conjecture at a prime as local Thorin positivity for Maass forms](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#ramanujan_at_a_prime_as_local_thorin_positivity_for_maass_forms) (Corollary 26.1, page 485; proved): A normalised Euler factor of a Hecke Maass form at a prime, read in the square root of the Laplace variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, and then of a generalized gamma convolution with an explicit Thorin comb, exactly when the Hecke eigenvalue obeys the Ramanujan bound with the value 2 excluded, which restates the Ramanujan conjecture at that prime without proving it. New in this book.
- [Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture is equivalent to complete monotonicity of the Maass cusp form heat trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#selberg_eigenvalue_conjecture_as_complete_monotonicity) (Theorem 26.4, page 488; proved): Proves an equivalence and not the conjecture, which is open in general, namely that Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture for a congruence subgroup holds if and only if the heat trace of its Maass cusp forms, with every eigenvalue lowered by one quarter, is completely monotone; unconditionally it proves complete monotonicity only with the eigenvalues lowered by the smaller amount that the Kim Sarnak bound allows, for every congruence subgroup (part ii), and the full statement for SL(2, Z), where the conjecture is known (part iii), while Weyl's law keeps the spectrum from being a Thorin measure. New in this book.
- [Thorin representation of the geodesic Euler product Z(s+1)/Z(s)](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_representation_of_the_geodesic_euler_product) (Theorem 26.5, page 491; proved): At every basepoint to the right of 1, the ratio of values of the geodesic Euler product Z(s+1)/Z(s) of a compact hyperbolic surface or of the modular surface, read in the square root of the Laplace variable, is unconditionally the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution with an explicit nonnegative Thorin density divided by that of a one half stable law, and the same holds for Dedekind zeta functions and for the Rankin Selberg L function of an automorphic representation with its contragredient. New in this book.
- [Poisson Dirichlet limit for random geodesic integers](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#random_geodesic_integers_are_poisson_dirichlet) (Theorem 26.6, page 493; proved): A random product of closed geodesics drawn with zeta type weights near the pole behaves like a random integer, with Gamma process and Poisson Dirichlet limits, Dickman's law for the largest factor and a normal law for the number of distinct factors. New in this book.
- [Thorin representation of the geodesic Euler product at the centre](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_representation_of_the_geodesic_euler_product_at_the_centre) (Open Problem 26.1, page 498; open): Asks whether, closer to the centre of the critical strip, the geodesic Euler product of a compact surface still has a positive Thorin density once its pole is removed, despite divergent spectral sums. New in this book.
- [A Chebotarev theorem for the closed geodesics of the modular surface](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#chebotarev_theorem_for_closed_geodesics) (Open Problem 26.2, page 498; open): Asks for the densities of arithmetic labels of the closed geodesics of the modular surface ordered by length, and for the matching Dirichlet process limit and Mertens constants. New in this book.
- [Even icosahedral Artin representations and Maass forms of eigenvalue one quarter](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#even_icosahedral_representations_and_maass_forms_of_eigenvalue_one_quarter) (Open Problem 26.3, page 498; open): Proposes testing numerically the complete monotonicity of the Galois heat trace of an even icosahedral Artin representation and searching for the Maass form of eigenvalue one quarter that Artin's conjecture predicts. New in this book.
- [Cutoff for Brownian motion on the principal congruence covers X(N)](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#cutoff_for_brownian_motion_on_congruence_covers) (Open Problem 26.4, page 498; open): Asks whether Brownian motion on the principal congruence covers of the modular surface mixes abruptly, with cutoff at a time of order log N as for random walks on expanders, and how the cusps affect the profile. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Extreme Values and the L Functions of Eta Products
chapters.summary:
On the imaginary axis the product in the Dedekind eta function is the distribution function of a maximum of independent exponential clocks. A Mellin transform argument then gives the extreme value representation, new in this book: the L function of Ramanujan's Delta function, and of every eta product ∏ η(mτ)^(r_m) with nonnegative integer r_m and Σ m r_m = 24 (among them the thirty multiplicative eta products), is entire and equals at every complex point the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function at such a maximum. For real positive s it is the probability that an independent gamma variable beats the maximum, so these L values lie strictly between 0 and 1 and increase to 1, and the central L value of the elliptic curve 11a, an Artin L value, Catalan's constant and π/4 become probabilities. Modularity becomes self similarity of the law, the Pólya kernel of Delta a Bayesian posterior, and Jacobi's triple product a link to the Kolmogorov distribution; a Monte Carlo estimator follows. The Riemann hypothesis for Delta is restated only as a reformulation, and the representation does not locate zeros.

#### From the literature

- Gumbel limits for maxima (Fisher and Tippett 1928, Gnedenko 1943); Rényi's representation (Rényi 1953).
- Entire continuation of L(s, Delta) and its incomplete gamma expansion (Hecke 1936); the weight one eta product of level 23 as an Artin L function (Hecke 1937).
- Multiplicative eta products (Dummit, Kisilevsky and McKay 1985) and multiplicative eta quotients (Martin 1996).
- The newform of 11a (Eichler 1954, Shimura 1971), the Birch and Swinnerton Dyer formula (Birch and Swinnerton Dyer 1965), and rank zero from analytic rank zero (Kolyvagin 1988, Gross and Zagier 1986).
- Riemann's xi as a moment of a Brownian excursion functional (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001); zeros off the line without an Euler product (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936); real zero criteria (Pólya 1926, de Bruijn 1950, Newman 1976).
- Kolmogorov's law (Kolmogorov 1933); diffusion passage times as sums of exponentials (Kent 1980).

#### New results

The Notes claim the representation and its consequences as the authors' own.

- [Product formula of the Dedekind eta function as the distribution function of a maximum of exponential clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#eta_product_as_distribution_function_of_exponential_maximum) (Proposition 27.1, page 500; proved): The infinite product in the Dedekind eta function, read on the imaginary axis, is the distribution function of the maximum of independent exponential clocks with rates proportional to the positive integers, with explicit tails and a density given by the weight two Eisenstein series. New in this book.
- [Extreme value representation of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#l_function_of_ramanujan_delta_as_extreme_value_expectation) (Theorem 27.2, page 502; proved): At every complex point the L function of Ramanujan's Delta function equals the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at a maximum of independent exponential clocks, and at positive real points it is the probability that an independent gamma variable beats that maximum. New in this book.
- [L values of Ramanujan's Delta at positive real points lie strictly between 0 and 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#real_l_values_of_ramanujan_delta_lie_in_unit_interval) (Corollary 27.3, page 503; proved): Every value of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta function at a positive real point lies strictly between zero and one, being the probability of an event that has positive probability together with its complement. New in this book.
- [Strict monotonicity of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta on the positive real axis](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#l_function_of_ramanujan_delta_increases_to_one) (Corollary 27.4, page 503; proved): On the positive real axis the L function of Ramanujan's Delta function increases strictly and tends to one, proved by a coupling of gamma variables. New in this book.
- [Modularity of Ramanujan's Delta as self similarity of an extreme value law](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#modularity_of_delta_as_self_similarity_of_extreme_value_law) (Proposition 27.5, page 504; proved): The modular transformation of Ramanujan's Delta function becomes an exact self similarity of the law of the maximum of exponential clocks behind it, which exchanges the two tails of that law. New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of Ramanujan's Delta as a Bayesian posterior](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#polya_kernel_of_delta_as_posterior_law) (Proposition 27.6, page 505; proved): The Pólya kernel of Ramanujan's Delta function is the law of the logarithm of a gamma variable of shape six and rate two pi, conditioned to exceed the maximum of exponential clocks behind Delta, so its moment generating function is a ratio of completed L values. New in this book.
- [Extreme value representation of L functions of eta products](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#extreme_value_representation_of_eta_product_l_functions) (Theorem 27.7, page 506; proved): For every eta product, that is every product of the functions eta(m tau) raised to nonnegative integer powers r_m with the sum of m r_m equal to 24 (the thirty multiplicative eta products among them), the L function is entire and equals at every complex point the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at an explicit maximum of exponential clocks, so its values at positive real points are probabilities strictly between zero and one that increase strictly to one. New in this book.
- [Squared Kolmogorov variable as a maximum of exponentials and an identity in law with the eta extreme value](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kolmogorov_distribution_as_maximum_of_exponentials) (Proposition 27.9, page 510; proved): The square of the largest absolute value of a Brownian bridge, whose law is Kolmogorov's, is in law a maximum of independent exponential variables, and Jacobi's triple product becomes an identity in law linking it to the extreme value law behind the Dedekind eta function. New in this book.
- [Brownian or Bessel functional with the extreme value law behind the Dedekind eta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#brownian_functional_with_eta_extreme_value_law) (Open Problem 27.1, page 510; open): Asks for a natural Brownian or Bessel functional whose law is the extreme value law behind the Dedekind eta function or Ramanujan's Delta function, or a proof that no first passage or last exit time of a one dimensional diffusion has it. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Dedekind eta function, eta product, multiplicative eta products, eta quotient, Ramanujan Delta function, tau function, extreme value representation, maximum of exponentials, Gumbel law, regularised incomplete gamma function, Mellin transform, modular self similarity, Pólya kernel, Polya kernel, Eisenstein series E2, elliptic curve 11a, Artin L function, Catalan's constant, Kolmogorov distribution, Jacobi triple product, Monte Carlo L function

chapters.title: Haar Measure and the p* Formula
chapters.summary:
The chapter sets Haar measure as the law of Frobenius on compact Sato Tate groups beside Haar measure as a prior in statistical inference. It computes left and right Haar measures and the modular function of the affine group of the line, which acts simply transitively on the upper half plane, shows that hyperbolic area is the image of left Haar measure, and presents Duke's equidistribution of Heegner points (CM points) as a noncompact analogue of Sato Tate. For transformation models it proves the classical theorems that Barndorff Nielsen's p* formula is exact and that invariant credible sets of the right Haar prior (Fraser's structural and Fisher's fiducial distributions) have exact frequentist coverage; in its examples the left Haar (Jeffreys) prior undercovers, with exact coverages for normal errors. The main new result concerns a conjugacy class, such as a Satake parameter, of a compact connected simple Lie group observed through noise whose density is a class function: Jeffreys' prior is Haar measure, whose image on classes is the Sato Tate measure, while the Berger Bernardo reference prior is uniform on the maximal torus, the arcsine law for SU(2). Haar normalisations of volumes, Tamagawa numbers and period formulas close the chapter.

#### From the literature

- Existence and uniqueness of Haar measure (Haar 1933; von Neumann 1934, 1936; Weil 1940).
- Equidistribution of Heegner points (Duke 1988, after Iwaniec 1987 and Linnik 1968) and Waldspurger's formulas (Waldspurger 1981, 1985).
- Fisher's conditional and fiducial arguments (Fisher 1934, 1935) and structural inference (Fraser 1968).
- The p* formula and its exactness in transformation models (Barndorff Nielsen 1980, 1983).
- Right Haar priors and best invariant procedures (Stein 1965; Hora and Buehler 1966); marginalisation paradoxes (Dawid, Stone and Zidek 1973).
- Reference priors (Bernardo 1979; Berger and Bernardo 1992), for orbits (Chang and Eaves 1990).
- Volumes of spaces of lattices (Siegel 1945) and the Tamagawa number of SL2 (Weil 1961).

#### New results

The other theorems of the chapter are classical, as its Notes say.

- [Reference prior for a conjugacy class of a compact Lie group observed through class function noise](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#reference_prior_for_conjugacy_classes_is_torus_haar_measure) (Proposition 28.16, page 529; proved): When an element of a compact connected simple Lie group is observed through noise whose density is a class function with finite nonsingular Fisher information, Jeffreys' prior is Haar measure, whose image on conjugacy classes is the Sato Tate measure, while the Berger Bernardo reference prior for the class is uniform on the maximal torus, which for SU(2) gives the arcsine law instead of the semicircle law. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Haar measure, left Haar measure, right Haar measure, modular function, unimodular group, affine group, ax+b group, Iwasawa decomposition, hyperbolic area, Duke's theorem, Heegner points, CM points, transformation model, structural inference, fiducial inference, p* formula, p star formula, Barndorff Nielsen formula, saddlepoint approximation, right Haar prior, probability matching prior, Jeffreys prior, marginalisation paradox, reference prior, Berger Bernardo algorithm, Chang Eaves prior, Satake parameter, Weyl integration formula, Tamagawa number

chapters.title: Bayesian Identification of Sato Tate Groups
chapters.summary:
How can one tell from Frobenius traces which Sato Tate group an abelian variety has? The chapter recasts the moment matching of Fité, Kedlaya, Rotger and Sutherland as Bayesian model selection: the working model treats the normalised traces as an exchangeable sample from the image of Haar measure under the trace, and equidistribution takes the place of the strong law of large numbers. Its consistency theorem, new in this book, is deterministic: for a sequence equidistributed for a true law, atoms allowed, with finite divergence from one candidate and a log likelihood ratio continuous off the atoms, the clipped log Bayes factor of two candidates is asymptotically linear, and its slope tends, as the clipping level grows, to the difference of the Kullback Leibler divergences of the truth from the two candidates. For elliptic curves over the rationals this gives explicit rates for detecting complex multiplication. The chapter also treats Wald's sequential probability ratio test, moments against the likelihood, the trace laws of USp(4), SU(2)×SU(2) and diagonal SU(2), three genus 2 curves (one outside the candidate list), misspecification, and nonparametric and arithmetic priors. The theorems assume equidistribution and prove nothing new about the Sato Tate conjecture.

#### From the literature

- The 52 Sato Tate groups of abelian surfaces (Fité, Kedlaya, Rotger and Sutherland 2012) and the moment method in genus 2 (Kedlaya and Sutherland 2009).
- Sato Tate for elliptic curves without complex multiplication (Barnet Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor 2011) and joint Sato Tate (Harris 2009).
- Exchangeability (de Finetti 1937; Hewitt and Savage 1955), consistency of maximum likelihood (Wald 1949), the Kullback Leibler divergence (Kullback and Leibler 1951).
- The sequential probability ratio test (Wald 1947; Wald and Wolfowitz 1948).
- Supersingular primes (Elkies 1987); hyperelliptic Jacobians without complex multiplication (Zarhin 2000).
- Misspecification (Berk 1966; Kleijn and van der Vaart 2006).
- Dirichlet processes (Ferguson 1973), Pólya trees (Lavine 1992), canonical moments (Dette and Studden 1997), empirical Bayes (Robbins 1956), endomorphism rings (Costa, Mascot, Sijsling and Voight 2019).

#### New results

Both results are the authors' own by the chapter's Notes.

- [Consistency of Bayes factors under equidistribution](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#consistency_of_bayes_factors_under_equidistribution) (Theorem 29.1, page 536; proved): For any deterministic sequence, such as normalised Frobenius traces, that is equidistributed for a true law with finitely many atoms and finite Kullback Leibler divergence from one candidate law, and with a log likelihood ratio continuous off the atoms, the clipped log Bayes factor between two candidate laws is asymptotically linear in the number of observations, and as the clipping level grows its slope tends to the difference of the divergences of the true law from the two candidates, with no independence assumed. New in this book.
- [Bayes factor rates for detecting complex multiplication of elliptic curves](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#bayes_factor_rates_for_complex_multiplication_of_elliptic_curves) (Corollary 29.3, page 538; proved): For an elliptic curve over the rationals, the clipped Bayes factor of a complex multiplication model against a Sato Tate model with a small atom at zero, computed from the normalised Frobenius traces at the good primes, has an explicit limiting rate per prime, as the clipping level grows, that is negative without complex multiplication and positive with it. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Sato Tate group, Sato Tate distribution, abelian surface, genus 2 curve, Frobenius traces, L polynomial, Bayes factor, Bayesian model selection, posterior consistency, Kullback Leibler divergence, relative entropy, equidistribution, exchangeability, working model, misspecification, sequential probability ratio test, SPRT, complex multiplication, supersingular primes, arcsine law, semicircle law, USp(4), Weyl integration formula, moment method, Galois endomorphism type, Dirichlet process, Pólya tree, empirical Bayes

chapters.title: Open Problems
chapters.summary:
Where can probability say something definite about the open problems of the Langlands programme? This chapter states twelve problems, each with its status and attributions, what probability and computation contribute, and what would be needed; it proves no theorem and settles no case of any of them. Five restate known problems: the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture for Maass forms with Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture, read through Sarnak's density hypothesis as a large deviation bound; the Lang Trotter conjecture, read as a local limit theorem; Sato Tate groups of abelian varieties and motives with the Katz Sarnak symmetry types; functoriality of tensor products in general and of symmetric powers for Maass forms; and deterministic Ramanujan graphs of every degree. The book poses the other seven: Brownian bridge limits of the Sato Tate empirical process in families of elliptic curves, in a problem on discrepancy that starts from the conjecture of Akiyama and Tanigawa, an inverse problem asking whether twisted prime sums can detect closeness to a newform, a probabilistic proof of the Thorin form of the Riemann hypothesis for Ramanujan's Delta, the reach of the extreme value representation, second order Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs, Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups of abelian surfaces, and the family law of the rank bias.

#### From the literature

The discrepancy conjecture of Akiyama and Tanigawa (1999); Deligne's theorem for holomorphic forms (Deligne 1974); Selberg's bound 3/16 (Selberg 1965) and the bounds of Kim and Sarnak (2003); Plancherel equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues (Sarnak 1987); infinitely many supersingular primes (Elkies 1987); Lang Trotter on average (Fouvry and Murty 1996; David and Pappalardi 1999); Sato Tate over totally real fields (Clozel, Harris, Shepherd Barron and Taylor 2008 and 2010; Barnet Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor 2011); the 52 Sato Tate groups of abelian surfaces (Fité, Kedlaya, Rotger and Sutherland 2012); symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic newforms (Newton and Thorne 2021); explicit near Ramanujan graphs (Mohanty, O'Donnell and Paredes 2022); Chebyshev's bias (Rubinstein and Sarnak 1994); generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992).

#### New results

The book's seven problems are catalogued as open.

- [Brownian bridge limit of the Sato Tate empirical process in families of elliptic curves](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sato_tate_discrepancy_brownian_bridge_in_families) (Open Problem 30.3, page 549; open): Asks for which growth rates of the number of primes, measured against the conductor, the normalised Sato Tate empirical process of a random elliptic curve converges to a Brownian bridge and its scaled discrepancy to the Kolmogorov law. New in this book.
- [Inverse problem for automorphy from twisted sums over primes](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#inverse_problem_for_automorphy_from_twisted_prime_sums) (Open Problem 30.4, page 550; open): Asks whether rates and fluctuations of the twisted prime sums of a sequence, at the square root scale and uniformly over Dirichlet characters, can decide whether the sequence is close to the normalised Hecke eigenvalues of a holomorphic newform. New in this book.
- [Hilbert's eighth problem for GL2 in Thorin form](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_form_of_hilberts_eighth_problem_for_ramanujan_delta) (Open Problem 30.8, page 554; open): Asks for a probabilistic proof that the heat sum over the zeros of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta is completely monotone, a statement the book shows to be equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis for that L function. New in this book.
- [Extreme value representation for locating zeros and for other newforms](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#extreme_value_representation_zeros_and_other_newforms) (Open Problem 30.9, page 555; open): Asks whether the law of the maximum in the extreme value representation of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta can locate or count its zeros, and which newforms admit a representation of the same kind. New in this book.
- [Second order term of Kemeny constants of supersingular 2 isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#second_order_kemeny_constants_of_supersingular_isogeny_graphs) (Open Problem 30.10, page 556; open): Asks whether the correction to the first order law for Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs has a limiting distribution across the characteristics, and whether it stays bounded. New in this book.
- [Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups for abelian surfaces and effective bounds](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#bayesian_identification_of_sato_tate_groups_for_abelian_surfaces) (Open Problem 30.11, page 557; open): Asks to extend the book's consistency theorem for Bayes factors between Sato Tate groups to the groups of abelian surfaces and to motives of higher rank, and to bound, polynomially in the logarithm of the conductor and without the Riemann hypothesis, how many primes the identification needs. New in this book.
- [Family limit law of the rank bias of elliptic curves](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#family_limit_law_of_the_rank_bias_of_elliptic_curves) (Open Problem 30.12, page 557; open): Asks whether, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for the L function of each curve, the fluctuations of the rank bias in weighted sums of Frobenius traces, normalised by the logarithm of the conductor, have a limit law over the elliptic curves of a fixed analytic rank, zero or one, and whether it is the law predicted by their low lying zeros. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: A Computational Programme
chapters.summary:
How should the computations suggested by a probabilistic reading of the Langlands programme be organised, scaled and reported? This chapter gathers the open computational problems posed at the ends of the earlier chapters into one programme, the agenda of the second author's computational work. It sets standards for experiments on deterministic arithmetic sequences: certified computation where possible (point counts, Hecke matrices, isogeny graphs, zeros with rigorous error bounds), statistical tests whose statistic, null law and reference population are fixed in advance, breadth across families rather than depth when the conjectured limit is a law, and tables that can be regenerated from a script and a seed. The problems fall into six workstreams: Frobenius data at scale (point counting in average polynomial time, a Sato Tate atlas, Lang Trotter constants, Koblitz's conjecture, Chebotarev races); families and random matrices (one level densities, moments, spacings of zeros); buildings, graphs and hitting times (Plancherel rates, Kemeny constants, critical groups of isogeny graphs); L functions as laws (Thorin measures, the de Bruijn Newman constant, complete monotonicity and Pólya kernel tests); inference (classifiers for Sato Tate groups, Haar priors); and Kloosterman sums, Cohen Lenstra statistics and log correlated fields. A table gives each problem a scale and a priority, and a first year plan orders six steps, later ones reusing the infrastructure of earlier ones. The chapter poses tasks and proves nothing.

#### From the literature

The programme builds on point counting in average polynomial time (Harvey 2014; Harvey and Sutherland 2014), the LMFDB and PARI/GP (The PARI Group 2023), and compares data with results and predictions such as the moment conjectures of Keating and Snaith (2000), the random Fourier series limit of Kloosterman paths (Kowalski and Sawin 2016), the maxima predicted by Fyodorov, Hiary and Keating (2012) and the Haar model for the sandpile groups of supersingular isogeny graphs (Munier and Shnidman 2023). Its Notes recall the machine computations of Birch and Swinnerton Dyer (1965) behind their conjecture.

#### New results

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: A Probability Toolkit
chapters.summary:
The appendix collects the probability used in the book for readers trained in number theory, with short proofs or standard references: weak convergence, Lévy's continuity theorem and the method of moments on a compact interval; Weyl's equidistribution criterion, Haar measure, the Weyl integration formula for SU(2) and the Peter Weyl theorem; the Kolmogorov discrepancy and the Kolmogorov distribution; the Wiener Ikehara and Hardy Littlewood Karamata Tauberian theorems and infinitely divisible laws; Kolmogorov's two and three series theorems, random series with independent phases, Kronecker's theorem and the Gärtner Ellis large deviation principle; Bernstein's theorem on completely monotone functions, generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) and their Thorin measures, and Pólya frequency functions; the extremal types theorem, the Rényi representation and the maximum of scaled exponentials whose distribution function is the product in the Dedekind eta function; reversible Markov chains on graphs, with spectral decomposition, hitting times, Kac's formula, mixing on Ramanujan graphs and a complete proof of the spectral formula for Kemeny's constant; and Kullback Leibler divergence, Bayes factors, the sequential probability ratio test and posterior consistency. chapters.title: Code for the Computations
chapters.summary:
Which code lies behind the numbers and figures of the book, and how is it organised? This appendix prints the core routines in condensed, cumulative Python listings that call PARI/GP through cypari2, with NumPy, SciPy and mpmath, and states in comments the values they return: Frobenius traces of elliptic curves by Legendre symbols, checked against PARI's ellap, and point counts on genus two curves; a PARI/GP function that builds supersingular isogeny graphs of prime degree from a root of a Hilbert class polynomial and the classical modular polynomials, whose adjacency matrices for primes congruent to 1 mod 12 are the Brandt matrices; Kemeny constants by the spectral formula, and hitting times both by direct solution and through the fundamental matrix; a Monte Carlo and quadrature evaluation of the extreme value representation of L(s, Delta) with the regularised incomplete gamma function; the Hadamard product over the zeros of L(s, Delta) behind its generalized gamma convolution, with a correction for the zeros above the cutoff; and clipped log Bayes factors between Sato Tate groups. A last section lists the stage scripts and JSON result files with the chapters that use them, the folders that hold the code of the later chapters, the archive of the scripts in a layout with relative paths, and the scripts that draw the figures, with notes on the order in which the scripts run and the files they read and write, on which of them reproduce the stored results when rerun and which do not run as they stand, on the two chapters that came without scripts, on the few printed numbers that come from checks made for the book, and on the scripts of Chapters 25 and 26, which have not been rerun for it. The appendix states no theorem.

#### From the literature

The routines rely on PARI/GP (The PARI Group 2023) and on the fundamental matrix of a finite Markov chain (Kemeny and Snell 1960); the appendix presents code and the values it returns, not results.

#### New results

No new results of this appendix are catalogued.

#### Key terms

code, source code, Python, PARI/GP, cypari2, NumPy, SciPy, mpmath, reproducibility, scripts, JSON results, Frobenius traces, point counting, Legendre symbols, ellap, genus two curves, supersingular isogeny graph, Brandt matrix, Hilbert class polynomial, classical modular polynomial, Kemeny constant, hitting times, fundamental matrix, extreme value representation, incomplete gamma function, Monte Carlo, Hadamard product, zeros of L(s, Delta), lfunlambda, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Bayes factor, Sato Tate group

results.name: Equidistribution does not determine automorphy
results.summary: Sato Tate equidistribution of a sequence indexed by the primes cannot certify that it comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) with trivial central character, because altering such a sequence on an infinite set of primes of density zero leaves the limiting empirical averages of all continuous functions unchanged but, by Ramakrishnan's refinement of strong multiplicity one, makes it nonautomorphic, and continuum many equidistributed sequences are not automorphic.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the set of primes, $\pi(x)$ the number of primes $p\le x$, and $\mathbb{A}$ the adele ring of $\mathbb{Q}$. A set $S\subset\mathcal{P}$ has density zero if $\#\{p\le x:p\in S\}/\pi(x)\to0$ as $x\to\infty$. A sequence $(x_p)_{p\in\mathcal{P}}$ of real numbers comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A})$ with trivial central character if $x_p=\operatorname{tr}A_p(\pi)$ for all but finitely many primes $p$, where $A_p(\pi)$ is the unitarily normalised Satake parameter of $\pi$ at $p$, and it is automorphic if it comes from some such $\pi$; both notions are unchanged when finitely many terms are changed. A sequence $(x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ is equidistributed with respect to the Sato Tate law $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}(dx)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx$ on $[-2,2]$ if $\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\phi(x_p)\to\int\phi\,d\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$ as $x\to\infty$ for every continuous function $\phi$ on $[-2,2]$. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the set of sequences $(x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ that are equidistributed with respect to $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$. (1) $\mathcal{E}$ has the cardinality of the continuum and contains continuum many sequences no two of which agree at all but finitely many primes. The automorphic sequences fall into countably many classes under the relation of agreeing at all but finitely many primes, so all but countably many of those sequences are not automorphic. (2) Let $(x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ come from $\pi$, and let $(x'_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ differ from $(x_p)$ exactly on an infinite set $S$ of density zero. Then $(x'_p)$ is not automorphic, and $(x'_p)\in\mathcal{E}$ if and only if $(x_p)\in\mathcal{E}$.
results.label: prop:01limits

results.name: Statistics unchanged by density zero alterations cannot characterise automorphy
results.summary: No statistic of sequences indexed by the primes that is unchanged when a sequence is altered on a set of primes of density zero, for instance any function of the limit points of its empirical laws, can tell an automorphic sequence from continuum many nonautomorphic ones.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the set of primes and $\pi(x)$ the number of primes $p\le x$; a set $S\subset\mathcal{P}$ has density zero if $\#\{p\le x:p\in S\}/\pi(x)\to0$ as $x\to\infty$. Call a sequence $(x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ automorphic if there is a cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A})$, where $\mathbb{A}$ is the ring of adeles of $\mathbb{Q}$, with trivial central character such that $x_p=\operatorname{tr}A_p(\pi)$ for all but finitely many primes $p$, where $A_p(\pi)$ is the unitarily normalised Satake parameter of $\pi$ at $p$. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the set of sequences $(x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ that are equidistributed with respect to the Sato Tate law, that is, with $\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\phi(x_p)\to\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-2}^{2}\phi(t)\sqrt{4-t^2}\,dt$ as $x\to\infty$ for every continuous function $\phi$ on $[-2,2]$. Let $\Phi$ be any function on $[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ that is unchanged when a sequence is altered on a set of density zero; for instance any function of the set of weak limit points of the empirical measures $\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\delta_{x_p}$ as $x\to\infty$, which is unchanged by such alterations. Then for every automorphic $(x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ there are continuum many sequences in $[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}$ that are not automorphic and on which $\Phi$ takes the value it takes on $(x_p)$; if $(x_p)\in\mathcal{E}$, they all lie in $\mathcal{E}$. In particular $\Phi$ cannot characterise automorphy.
results.label: cor:01functional

results.name: Sato Tate discrepancy vanishes at the square root scale in logarithmic density
results.summary: For an elliptic curve over the rationals without complex multiplication, the Kolmogorov distance between the empirical law of its first n normalised Frobenius traces and the Sato Tate law is conjectured to be, in logarithmic density, of smaller order than the inverse square root of n that independent sampling gives; the same conjecture records the rate conjectured by Akiyama and Tanigawa.
results.statement: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ of conductor $N$ without complex multiplication. For a prime $p \nmid N$ put $a_p = p + 1 - \#E(\mathbb{F}_p)$ and $x_p = a_p/\sqrt{p} \in [-2,2]$. Let $p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes not dividing $N$, let $F_n$ be the empirical distribution function of $x_{p_1}, \dots, x_{p_n}$, let $F_{\mathrm{ST}}(t) = \int_{-2}^{t} \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4-u^2}\,du$ be the distribution function of the Sato Tate law on $[-2,2]$, and let $D_n = \sup_{t \in [-2,2]} |F_n(t) - F_{\mathrm{ST}}(t)|$ be the Kolmogorov discrepancy. For $x \ge 2$ let $n = n(x)$ be the number of primes $p \le x$ with $p \nmid N$. Conjecture (open): (a) (a conjecture of Akiyama and Tanigawa) $D_n = O(n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$; (b) $\sqrt{n}\,D_n \to 0$ in logarithmic density, that is, for every $\delta > 0$ the set $S_\delta$ of real $x \ge 2$ with $\sqrt{n}\,D_n > \delta$ has logarithmic density zero, $\frac{1}{\log X}\int_{S_\delta \cap [2,X]} \frac{dx}{x} \to 0$ as $X \to \infty$.
results.label: conj:05bridge

results.name: Exact second moments of Kloosterman paths at every odd prime
results.summary: Exact formulas, valid at every odd prime, for the mean and the second moments of a normalised partial Kloosterman sum averaged over its parameter, in both natural parametrisations, which the book proves as its own formulation of facts implicit in or easily derived from the work of Kowalski and Sawin.
results.statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime, write $e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}$, and for $x\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times$ let $\bar x$ denote its inverse. For $t\in[0,1]$ let $I=\{1,\dots,m\}$ with $m=\lfloor t(p-1)\rfloor$, viewed as a set of residues modulo $p$, let $-I=\{p-x:x\in I\}$, and put $R_I=\sum_{x\in I}e(\bar x/p)$ and $G_I=\sum_{x\in I}e(x/p)$. Let $a$ be uniform in $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$. (1) For $S_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in I}e\bigl((ax+\bar x)/p\bigr)$, \[\mathbb{E}|S_p|^2=\frac{p|I|-|R_I|^2}{p(p-1)},\qquad\mathbb{E}S_p^2=\frac{p\,|I\cap(-I)|-R_I^2}{p(p-1)}.\] (2) For $S'_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in I}e\bigl((x+a\bar x)/p\bigr)$, \[\mathbb{E}|S'_p|^2=\frac{p|I|-|G_I|^2}{p(p-1)},\qquad\mathbb{E}S_p'^2=\frac{p\,|I\cap(-I)|-G_I^2}{p(p-1)}.\] In both cases the mean is $\mathbb{E}S_p=-p^{-1/2}(p-1)^{-1}R_I$, respectively $\mathbb{E}S'_p=-p^{-1/2}(p-1)^{-1}G_I$, which tends to $0$ as $p\to\infty$.
results.label: prop:06bsecond

results.name: Variance deficit of Kloosterman paths when the parameter multiplies the inverse
results.summary: When the parameter of a partial Kloosterman sum multiplies the inverse of the summation variable, the limiting variances of its real and imaginary parts fall below those of the Kloosterman random Fourier series by explicit trigonometric terms, by exactly one over pi squared for the imaginary part at the midpoint, which the book proves as its own formulation of facts implicit in or easily derived from the work of Kowalski and Sawin.
results.statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}$, and $\bar x$ the inverse of $x\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times$. For $t\in[0,1]$ let $S'_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{1\le x\le\lfloor t(p-1)\rfloor}e\bigl((x+a\bar x)/p\bigr)$ with $a$ uniform in $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$, and write $u_+=\max(u,0)$. As $p\to\infty$ the variances of the real and imaginary parts of $S'_p(a,t)$ converge to \[\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Re}S'=\tfrac12\bigl(t+(2t-1)_+\bigr)-\frac{\sin^2(2\pi t)}{4\pi^2},\qquad\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Im}S'=\tfrac12\bigl(t-(2t-1)_+\bigr)-\frac{\sin^4(\pi t)}{\pi^2}.\] At $t=\frac12$ the correction to the real part vanishes, so its limiting variance is $\frac14$, and the imaginary part loses exactly $1/\pi^2$: $\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Im}S'_p(a,\tfrac12)\to\frac14-\frac1{\pi^2}=0.1487$.
results.label: cor:06bdeficit

results.name: Covariance and reflection symmetry of the Kloosterman random Fourier series
results.summary: The random Fourier series with independent Sato Tate coefficients that Kowalski and Sawin found as the limit of Kloosterman paths has the covariance of complex Brownian motion on the first half of the unit interval and an exact reflection symmetry that determines the second half, which leads the book to call it a Sato Tate Brownian motion, and the book proves this as its own formulation of facts implicit in or easily derived from their work.
results.statement: Let $(\mathrm{ST}_h)_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be independent real random variables, each with the Sato Tate law, the semicircle law on $[-2,2]$ with density $\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}$. Put $c_0(t)=t$ and $c_h(t)=(e^{2\pi iht}-1)/(2\pi ih)$ for $h\ne0$, and let $K(t)=\sum_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}c_h(t)\,\mathrm{ST}_h$ for $0\le t\le1$, the series being the limit of its symmetric partial sums over $|h|\le H$ as $H\to\infty$. Write $u_+=\max(u,0)$. For $s,t\in[0,1]$, \[\mathbb{E}\,K(s)\overline{K(t)}=\min(s,t),\qquad\mathbb{E}\,K(s)K(t)=(s+t-1)_+.\] Consequently $\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Re}K(t)=\frac12\bigl(t+(2t-1)_+\bigr)$, $\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Im}K(t)=\frac12\bigl(t-(2t-1)_+\bigr)$, and $\operatorname{Re}K(t)$, $\operatorname{Im}K(t)$ are uncorrelated. Moreover, almost surely, \[K(1-t)=K(1)-\overline{K(t)}\qquad(0\le t\le1),\] so $\operatorname{Im}K(1-t)=\operatorname{Im}K(t)$, $K(1)=2\operatorname{Re}K(\tfrac12)=\mathrm{ST}_0$, and $\operatorname{Im}K(0)=\operatorname{Im}K(1)=0$.
results.label: prop:06bcov

results.name: Unboundedness and subgaussian tail of the Kloosterman random Fourier series
results.summary: The imaginary part of the Kloosterman random Fourier series at the midpoint is unbounded in both directions yet obeys a Gaussian tail bound, and every square summable real combination of independent Sato Tate variables is subgaussian with variance proxy equal to its variance; the book proves this as its own formulation of facts implicit in or easily derived from the work of Kowalski and Sawin, and notes that the tail bound is far weaker than their doubly exponential estimates.
results.statement: Let $(\mathrm{ST}_h)_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be independent real random variables, each with the Sato Tate law, the semicircle law on $[-2,2]$ with density $\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}$, and let $K(t)=t\,\mathrm{ST}_0+\sum_{h\ne0}\frac{e^{2\pi iht}-1}{2\pi ih}\,\mathrm{ST}_h$ for $0\le t\le1$, the series being the limit of its symmetric partial sums. The random variable $\operatorname{Im}K(\tfrac12)=\frac1\pi\sum_{h\ \mathrm{odd}}\mathrm{ST}_h/h$ is unbounded above and below, and for every $M>0$, \[\mathbb{P}\bigl(\operatorname{Im}K(\tfrac12)>M\bigr)\le e^{-2M^2},\] the Chernoff bound of a centred Gaussian variable with the same variance $\frac14$. More generally, every real random variable $X=\sum_h\gamma_h\mathrm{ST}_h$ with $\sum_h\gamma_h^2<\infty$, in particular every real linear combination of the real and imaginary parts of finitely many values of $K$, satisfies $\mathbb{E}e^{\lambda X}\le e^{\lambda^2\mathrm{Var}(X)/2}$ for all real $\lambda$.
results.label: prop:06btail

results.name: Tree theorem, a single Chebyshev proof of the Kesten McKay law and the Green function of the regular tree
results.summary: One Chebyshev polynomial identity for the sphere operators of the regular tree, on which for prime q the Hecke operator acts by adjacency, yields the Kesten McKay spectral law, its moments, the return probability of simple random walk and its expected number of visits to the starting vertex, and convergence to the Sato Tate semicircle as the degree grows; the individual facts are classical, and the formulation and the single proof are the book's.
results.statement: Let $q\ge2$ be an integer, let $\mathcal{T}_q$ be the $(q+1)$ regular tree with graph distance $d$ and a fixed vertex $o$, let $A$ be its adjacency operator, let $X=q^{-1/2}A$, a bounded self adjoint operator on $\ell^2(\mathcal{T}_q)$, and let $\mu_q$ be the spectral measure of $X$ at $\delta_o$, so that $\langle\delta_o,\phi(X)\delta_o\rangle=\int\phi\,d\mu_q$ for continuous $\phi$. For $n\ge0$ let $A_n$ be the operator $A_nf(v)=\sum_{d(v,w)=n}f(w)$, with $A_0=I$, and put $B_n=q^{-n/2}A_n$. Write $U_n$ for the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind, $U_n(\cos\theta)=\sin((n+1)\theta)/\sin\theta$, and $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}(dx)=\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx/(2\pi)$ for the Sato Tate measure on $[-2,2]$. Then: (1) $B_1=U_1(X/2)$ and $B_n=U_n(X/2)-q^{-1}U_{n-2}(X/2)$ for $n\ge2$. (2) $c_n=\int U_n(x/2)\,d\mu_q(x)$ equals $q^{-n/2}$ for $n$ even and $0$ for $n$ odd. (3) $\mu_q$ is supported on $[-2,2]$ with the Kesten McKay density \[\mu_q(dx)=\frac{q+1}{(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2})^2-x^2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{4-x^2}}{2\pi}\,dx .\] (4) If $S$ is simple random walk on $\mathcal{T}_q$ started at $o$, then $\int x^{2m}\,d\mu_q=(q+1)^{2m}q^{-m}\,\mathbb{P}(S_{2m}=o)$ for $m\ge0$. (5) The walk returns to $o$ with probability $1/q$, and the Green function $G(1)=\sum_{n\ge0}\mathbb{P}(S_n=o)$, the expected number of visits to $o$, equals $q/(q-1)$. (6) $\mu_q$ converges weakly to $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$ as $q\to\infty$.
results.label: thm:07tree

results.name: Three equivalent forms of the graph Riemann hypothesis, Ihara poles, Ramanujan bound and mixing at the Kesten rate
results.summary: For a connected regular graph the Riemann hypothesis for its Ihara zeta function is equivalent both to the Ramanujan eigenvalue bound and to return probabilities approaching equilibrium at an exponential rate no slower than the rate at which those of the regular tree decay to zero, with the exact rate set by the largest absolute value of a nontrivial eigenvalue; the first equivalence is standard, and the mixing form is the book's reformulation.
results.statement:
Let $q\ge1$ be an integer and let $G$ be a finite connected $(q+1)$ regular graph on $n$ vertices, possibly with loops and multiple edges, with adjacency matrix $A$ (a loop contributing $2$ to the diagonal) and eigenvalues $q+1=\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$. Its Ihara zeta function is $Z_G(u)=\prod_{\mathfrak p}(1-u^{
u(\mathfrak p)})^{-1}$, the product over the classes $\mathfrak p$, under cyclic rotation, of primitive closed paths of oriented edges without backtracking and without tail, with $
u(\mathfrak p)$ the length; by the Ihara Bass determinant formula it is a rational function of $u$, and its poles in $\{\pm1,\pm1/q\}$ are called trivial. $Z_G$ satisfies the graph Riemann hypothesis if every nontrivial pole lies on the circle $|u|=q^{-1/2}$, and $G$ is Ramanujan if every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ with $|\lambda|
e q+1$ satisfies $|\lambda|\le2\sqrt q$. Let $P=A/(q+1)$ be the transition matrix of simple random walk on $G$, let $\lambda_*=\max\{|\lambda_j|:|\lambda_j|
e q+1\}$ (with $\lambda_*=0$ if there is no such eigenvalue), let $ eta=1$ if $G$ is bipartite and $ eta=0$ otherwise, let $\delta_t=\max_{x} igl|P^t(x,x)-(1+ eta(-1)^t)/n igr|$, and let $ho_q=2\sqrt q/(q+1)$. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $Z_G$ satisfies the graph Riemann hypothesis; (2) $G$ is Ramanujan; (3) $\limsup_{t	o\infty}\delta_t^{1/t}\leho_q$. Moreover $\limsup_t\delta_t^{1/t}=\lambda_*/(q+1)$ exactly, so the return probabilities of a Ramanujan graph approach equilibrium at an exponential rate no slower than the rate $ho_q$ at which the return probabilities of simple random walk on the $(q+1)$ regular tree tend to zero.
results.label: prop:08three

results.name: Limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs
results.summary: As the characteristic grows through primes congruent to 1 modulo 12, with the prime isogeny degree fixed, the mean time for simple random walk on a supersingular isogeny graph to hit a uniformly random curve is asymptotic to the number of vertices times the expected number of visits of simple random walk on the regular tree of the same degree to its starting point, so about twice the number of vertices for 2 isogenies.
results.statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime. For a prime $N\equiv1\pmod{12}$ with $N\ne\ell$, let $G_N(\ell)$ be the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph in characteristic $N$, whose vertices are the $h=(N-1)/12$ isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$, each curve having one edge for each of its $\ell+1$ subgroups of order $\ell$, joining it to the quotient curve; dual isogenies pair the edges, so that $G_N(\ell)$ is an undirected $(\ell+1)$ regular graph, possibly with loops and multiple edges. For simple random walk $(X_t)$ on $G_N(\ell)$, whose stationary law $\pi$ is uniform, let $\tau_y=\min\{t\ge0:X_t=y\}$ and let $K_N=\sum_y\pi(y)\,\mathbb{E}_x\tau_y$ be the Kemeny constant, which does not depend on the starting vertex $x$. As $N\to\infty$ through primes $N\equiv1\pmod{12}$, with $\ell$ fixed, \[\frac{K_N}{h}\longrightarrow\frac{\ell}{\ell-1}.\] Equivalently, the mean hitting time of a uniformly random target, from any fixed start or from a uniformly random one, is asymptotic to $\ell h/(\ell-1)$; for $\ell=2$ it is about $2h$.
results.label: thm:08kemeny

results.name: The normalised L function of the discriminant form is not a characteristic function
results.summary: Because the Ramanujan tau function takes negative values, on every vertical line to the right of the critical strip the L function of the discriminant modular form somewhere exceeds in modulus its value at the real point of that line, so, unlike the Riemann zeta function, it gives no characteristic function there.
results.statement: Let $\Delta$ be the discriminant modular form of weight $12$ and level $1$, with Fourier coefficients $\tau(n)$, and let $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-11/2-s}$ be its $L$ function in the unitary normalisation, with centre $s=\tfrac12$. For every $\sigma>1$ we have $\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|L(\sigma+it,\Delta)|>L(\sigma,\Delta)>0$. In particular $t\mapsto L(\sigma+it,\Delta)/L(\sigma,\Delta)$ is not a characteristic function.
results.label: prop:ch09notcf

results.name: Mean and second moment of the Sato Tate random Euler product
results.summary: A random model of the L function of a cusp form, with independent Satake angles drawn from the Sato Tate law, converges as a martingale to the right of the critical line, with mean one and mean square equal to the Riemann zeta function at twice the real part.
results.statement: Let $(\theta_p)$, indexed by the primes $p$, be independent random variables with the Sato Tate law $\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$ on $[0,\pi]$, and let $L_{\mathrm{rand}}(s)=\prod_p(1-e^{i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}(1-e^{-i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}$ be the Sato Tate random Euler product. For real $\sigma>1/2$ and real $t$ the product $L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma+it)$, the limit of the partial products over the primes $p\le P$ as $P\to\infty$, converges almost surely and in $L^2$, and \[\mathbb{E}\bigl[L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma+it)\bigr]=1,\qquad\mathbb{E}\bigl|L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma+it)\bigr|^2=\zeta(2\sigma).\]
results.label: prop:ch09martingale

results.name: Central limit theorem for the Sato Tate random Euler product near the critical line
results.summary: In the Sato Tate random model of the L function of a cusp form, the logarithm at a real point approaching the critical line is asymptotically normal, with a variance that grows logarithmically and a negative drift equal to half the variance.
results.statement: Let $(\theta_p)$, indexed by the primes $p$, be independent random variables with the Sato Tate law $\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$ on $[0,\pi]$, and let $L_{\mathrm{rand}}(s)=\prod_p(1-e^{i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}(1-e^{-i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}$ be the Sato Tate random Euler product; for real $\sigma>1/2$ every factor is positive and $\log L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma)=\sum_p\sum_{k\ge1}2\cos(k\theta_p)/(kp^{k\sigma})$ converges almost surely. Let $V(\sigma)=\sum_pp^{-2\sigma}$, so that $V(\sigma)=\log\frac{1}{2\sigma-1}+O(1)$ as $\sigma\to\frac12^+$. Then \[\frac{\log L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma)+\frac12V(\sigma)}{\sqrt{V(\sigma)}}\Longrightarrow N(0,1),\qquad\sigma\to\tfrac12^+,\] where $\Longrightarrow$ denotes convergence in law and $N(0,1)$ is the standard normal law.
results.label: thm:ch09clt

results.name: Exponential left tail of the log modulus near simple zeros
results.summary: An elementary fact about real analytic functions with simple zeros, which the book applies to the Hardy function of the discriminant form to explain the exponential left tail of the empirical distribution of the log modulus of its L function on windows of the critical line whose zeros are simple.
results.statement: Let $f$ be a real analytic function on a neighbourhood of a compact interval $[a,b]$, with finitely many zeros $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_r$ in $(a,b)$, all simple, and no zero at $a$ or at $b$. Then, as $x\to\infty$, the Lebesgue measure of the set $\{t\in[a,b]:\log|f(t)|<-x\}$ equals $2e^{-x}\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{1}{|f'(\gamma_j)|}+O(e^{-2x})$.
results.label: prop:09blefttail

results.name: Variance at finite height of the log modulus of the L function of Delta
results.summary: Conjectures an explicit formula for the variance of the log modulus of the L function of the discriminant form on its critical line at finite height, combining the random matrix constant with an arithmetic constant, obtained by writing out the moment conjecture and hybrid Euler Hadamard product heuristics for this form; the book's computations at heights 500 to 2500 agree with it within sampling error.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, be the discriminant cusp form of weight $12$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, let $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$, whose critical line is $\operatorname{Re}s=6$, and for each prime $p$ let $\theta_p\in[0,\pi]$ be defined by $\tau(p)=2p^{11/2}\cos\theta_p$. Let $\gamma_{\mathrm E}$ be Euler's constant and put $A_\Delta=\sum_p\bigl(\log(1-\frac1p)+\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{(2\cos m\theta_p)^2}{m^2p^m}\bigr)$ and $V_\Delta(T)=\frac12\bigl(\log\bigl(2\log\frac{T}{2\pi}\bigr)+\gamma_{\mathrm E}+1+A_\Delta\bigr)$. Conjecture: for $t$ uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, $\operatorname{Var}\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=V_\Delta(T)+o(1)$ as $T\to\infty$.
results.label: conj:09bvar

results.name: Log correlated covariance of the random Euler product field
results.summary: Writes out the standard computation showing that the prime sum of the random Euler product, for the Riemann zeta function and for the discriminant form, is a log correlated field, whose covariance at distance u between 0 and 1 is one half of the logarithm of the smaller of 1/u and the logarithm of the prime cutoff, up to a bounded error.
results.statement: Let $(U_p)$, indexed by the primes, be independent random variables uniformly distributed on the unit circle, and for $P\ge3$ and real $h$ put $X_P(h)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{p\le P}U_pp^{-1/2-ih}$. Then $\operatorname{Cov}(X_P(h),X_P(h'))=\frac12\sum_{p\le P}\frac{\cos((h - h')\log p)}{p}=\frac12\log\min\bigl(\log P,\frac{1}{|h - h'|}\bigr)+O(1)$, uniformly in $P$ and in $0<|h - h'|\le1$. The same holds for the field $X^\Delta_P(h)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{p\le P}\lambda(p)U_pp^{-1/2-ih}$, where $\lambda(p)=\tau(p)/p^{11/2}$ and $\tau(n)$ are the coefficients of the discriminant cusp form $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, with $\lambda(p)^2/p$ in place of $1/p$ in the sum, that is, $\operatorname{Cov}(X^\Delta_P(h),X^\Delta_P(h'))=\frac12\sum_{p\le P}\frac{\lambda(p)^2\cos((h - h')\log p)}{p}=\frac12\log\min\bigl(\log P,\frac{1}{|h - h'|}\bigr)+O(1)$ with the same uniformity.
results.label: prop:09bcov

results.name: First moments with and without the ballot constraint for Brownian motion on a tree
results.summary: Asymptotics of the first moments of the number of high leaves, with and without a ballot constraint on the paths, for Brownian motion indexed by a regular tree, a continuous model in which the ballot computation is exact; they explain heuristically the logarithmic correction to the maximum of a branching random walk (a theorem of Bramson, Addario Berry and Reed, and Aïdékon), and so the constant three quarters in the Fyodorov Hiary Keating conjecture.
results.statement: Let $b\ge2$ be an integer and $\sigma>0$, and let $\{B_v(s):0\le s\le n\}$, indexed by the $b^n$ leaves $v$ of the $b$ ary tree of depth $n$, be Brownian motion indexed by the tree: each edge carries an independent Brownian path of duration one and variance $\sigma^2$ per unit time, and $B_v$ is the concatenation of the paths along the edges from the root to $v$. Put $c=\sigma\sqrt{2\log b}$, $\theta=c/\sigma^2=\sqrt{2\log b}/\sigma$ and $x_n=cn - a\log n$ for a constant $a>0$. Fix $y\ge0$. Let $N_n(y)$ be the number of leaves with $B_v(n)\ge x_n+y$, and $Z_n(y)$ the number of leaves with $B_v(n)\in[x_n+y,x_n+y+1]$ and $B_v(s)\le\frac snx_n+y+1$ for all $s\in[0,n]$. As $n\to\infty$, $\mathbb{E}N_n(y)\sim\frac{\sigma}{c\sqrt{2\pi}}\,n^{\theta a-\frac12}e^{-\theta y}$ and $\mathbb{E}Z_n(y)\sim\kappa\,(1+y)\,n^{\theta a-\frac32}e^{-\theta y}$, with $\kappa=2(\theta-1+e^{-\theta})/(\sigma^3\theta^2\sqrt{2\pi})$. In particular the choice $a=\frac1{2\theta}$ makes $\mathbb{E}N_n(y)$ of order one, while $a=\frac3{2\theta}$ makes $\mathbb{E}Z_n(y)\to\kappa(1+y)e^{-\theta y}$, and for that choice $\mathbb{E}N_n(y)$ grows like $n$.
results.label: prop:09bballot

results.name: Selberg central limit theorem for Delta as a statement about the characteristic function of the Pólya variable
results.status_text: conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta), for the Gaussian limit only
results.conditions: the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta), for the Gaussian limit only
results.summary: Expresses the log modulus of the L function of the discriminant form on its critical line through the characteristic function of its Pólya variable plus an explicit archimedean term, so that, under the Riemann hypothesis for this form, Selberg's central limit theorem becomes a statement about lognormal fluctuations of the characteristic function of an explicit probability law.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, let $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ and $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)$, let $W$ be a random variable with density $\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)$ on $\mathbb{R}$ (the P\'olya variable of $\Delta$), and let $\varphi_W(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{itW}$. For real $t$, $\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=\log|\varphi_W(t)|-\log|\Gamma(6+it)|+\log(\Gamma(6)L(6,\Delta))$, and, as $|t|\to\infty$, $\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=\log|\varphi_W(t)|+\frac\pi2|t|-\frac{11}2\log|t|+C_\Delta+O(1/|t|)$, with $C_\Delta=\log(120\,L(6,\Delta))-\frac12\log2\pi=3.6355$. Consequently, if all zeros of $\Lambda(s,\Delta)$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=6$ (the Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\Delta)$), then for $t$ uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ the quantity $\bigl(\log|\varphi_W(t)|+\frac\pi2t-\frac{11}2\log t+C_\Delta\bigr)/\sqrt{\frac12\log\log T}$ converges in law to the standard normal distribution as $T\to\infty$.
results.label: prop:09bpolya

results.name: The log modulus of the L function of Delta as the logarithmic potential of its Thorin measure
results.status_text: conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta)
results.conditions: the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta)
results.summary: Under the Riemann hypothesis for the discriminant form, the log modulus of the characteristic function of its Pólya variable on the real line is the logarithmic potential of the Thorin measure carried by the squared ordinates of the zeros, and it is strictly concave between consecutive zeros.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ and $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)$; let $W$ have density $\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and $\varphi_W(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{itW}$. Assume the Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\Delta)$, so that the zeros of $\Lambda(s,\Delta)$ are $6\pm i\gamma_k$ with $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\dots$, listed with multiplicity. Let $\tau_\Delta=\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$, and let $Y=\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2$ with $E_k$ independent standard exponential variables. For real $t\ne\pm\gamma_k$, $\log|\varphi_W(t)|=\sum_k\log\bigl|1-\frac{t^2}{\gamma_k^2}\bigr|=\int_{(0,\infty)}\log\bigl|1-\frac{t^2}{x}\bigr|\,\tau_\Delta(dx)=-\log|\mathcal{L}_Y(t^2)|$, where $\mathcal{L}_Y(u)=\prod_k(1-u/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$ is the meromorphic continuation to $\mathbb{C}$ of the moment generating function $\mathbb{E}e^{uY}$, $u<\gamma_1^2$. Moreover, on each interval between consecutive zeros, $t\mapsto\log|\varphi_W(t)|$ is strictly concave.
results.label: prop:09bpotential

results.name: The L function of Delta on the critical line through the extreme value variable M*
results.summary: Writes the L function of the discriminant form on its critical line, times a gamma factor, as the Fourier transform of a finite measure, the law of the logarithm of a gamma variable restricted to the event that it exceeds a scaled maximum of independent exponential variables, and identifies that measure with the central value L(6, Delta) times the law of the shifted Pólya variable.
results.statement: Let $E_{j,n}$, $1\le j\le24$, $n\ge1$, be independent standard exponential variables and $M^*=\max_{j,n}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)$, so that the discriminant cusp form $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, satisfies $\Delta(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}\mathbb{P}(M^*\le y)$ for $y>0$. Let $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ and $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)$, let $G$ have the gamma law of shape $6$ and unit rate, independent of $M^*$, and write $\mathbb{E}[X;A]=\mathbb{E}[X\,1_A]$ for an event $A$. For real $t$, $\frac{\Gamma(6+it)}{\Gamma(6)}\,L(6+it,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[G^{it};\,G\ge2\pi M^*\bigr]$. The finite measure $\nu(B)=\mathbb{P}(\log G\in B,\ G\ge2\pi M^*)$ has total mass $L(6,\Delta)$ and equals $L(6,\Delta)$ times the law of $W+\log2\pi$, where $W$ is the P\'olya variable of $\Delta$, with density $\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)$ on $\mathbb{R}$.
results.label: prop:09bmstar

results.name: Pólya kernel of the discriminant form Delta and its characteristic function
results.summary: The discriminant modular form on the imaginary axis, read in logarithmic coordinates and weighted, is the density of a symmetric random variable whose moment generating function is the normalised completed L function of the form, so that the Riemann hypothesis for this form is equivalent to the characteristic function of an explicit probability law having only real zeros.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, be the discriminant cusp form of weight $12$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, let $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ and $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)$, and let $W$ be a random variable with the probability density $\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)$, $u\in\mathbb{R}$ (the P\'olya kernel of $\Delta$). Then $W$ is symmetric, has moments of all orders and an entire moment generating function, and for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{E}[e^{zW}]=\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)/\Lambda(6,\Delta)$. In particular $\mathbb{E}[e^{itW}]=\Lambda(6+it,\Delta)/\Lambda(6,\Delta)$ is real and even, and the Riemann hypothesis for $\Delta$ (all zeros of $\Lambda(s,\Delta)$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=6$) is equivalent to the statement that the characteristic function of $W$ has only real zeros.
results.label: thm:ch10kernel

results.name: Hadamard product and variance identity for the Pólya variable of Delta
