results.summary: Unconditionally, the normalised completed L function of the discriminant form is a product over its zeros with no exponential factor, and the variance of its Pólya variable equals twice the sum of the inverse squares of the zero ordinates, a trace formula in miniature that the book checks against computed zeros.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ and $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)$, and let $W$ have density $\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Write each zero of $z\mapsto\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)$ as $z=i\gamma$ (no such $z$ is real, since $\Lambda(6+x,\Delta)>0$ for real $x$), and list one representative of each pair $\{\gamma,-\gamma\}$ with $\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0$ as $\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\dots$, with multiplicity and in order of increasing real part. Unconditionally, $\sum_k|\gamma_k|^{-2}<\infty$ and for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$, $\frac{\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)}{\Lambda(6,\Delta)}=\prod_k\bigl(1+\frac{z^2}{\gamma_k^2}\bigr)$. Consequently $\mathbb{E}W=0$ and $\operatorname{Var}W=2\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2}$, where the right side is real because nonreal $\gamma_k$ occur in conjugate pairs.
results.label: thm:ch10hadamard

results.name: Riemann hypothesis for Delta as a generalized gamma convolution property
results.summary: Proves that the Riemann hypothesis for the L function of the discriminant form is equivalent to a reciprocal of its completed L function, in the square root variable, being the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, whose Thorin measure is then the sum of unit masses at the squared zero ordinates; it is a reformulation and proves no case of the Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ and $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)$. A probability law on $[0,\infty)$ is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) if it is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws; equivalently (Thorin) its Laplace transform is $\exp\bigl(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\frac st)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)$, $s\ge0$, with drift $a\ge0$ and a positive measure $\tau$ on $(0,\infty)$, finite on compact sets, the Thorin measure, satisfying $\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty$ and $\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty$. The following are equivalent: (i) all zeros of $\Lambda(s,\Delta)$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=6$; (ii) the function $s\mapsto\Lambda(6,\Delta)/\Lambda(6+\sqrt s,\Delta)$, $s>0$, is the Laplace transform of a GGC. When they hold, writing the zeros as $6\pm i\gamma_k$ with $\gamma_k>0$, listed with multiplicity, the GGC has drift $0$ and Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$, it is the law of $X=\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2$ with $E_k$ independent standard exponential variables, and its L\'evy measure has density $k(x)/x$, where $k(x)=\sum_ke^{-\gamma_k^2x}$, $x>0$, is completely monotone.
results.label: thm:ch10ggc

results.name: Thorin criterion for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of self dual automorphic L functions
results.summary: For a self dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n), n at least 2, with nonvanishing central value, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to a reciprocal of the completed L function, in the square root variable, being the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, whose Thorin measure then sits on the squared zero ordinates; a reformulation that proves no case of the generalized Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a self dual cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$, $n\ge2$, with completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation, conductor included, so that $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ is entire of order one, real on the real axis, and satisfies $\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon\Lambda(1-s,\pi)$ with $\varepsilon=\pm1$. A probability law on $[0,\infty)$ is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) if it is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws; equivalently its Laplace transform is $\exp\bigl(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\frac st)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)$, $s\ge0$, with $a\ge0$ and a positive measure $\tau$ on $(0,\infty)$, finite on compact sets, the Thorin measure, satisfying $\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty$ and $\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty$. Suppose $\Lambda(\frac12,\pi)\ne0$. Then the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\pi$ (all zeros of $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$) holds if and only if $s\mapsto\Lambda(\frac12,\pi)/\Lambda(\frac12+\sqrt s,\pi)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, and then its Thorin measure is $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$ over the ordinates $\gamma_k>0$ of the zeros $\frac12\pm i\gamma_k$.
results.label: thm:ch10general

results.name: Self dual completion of a cuspidal automorphic L function
results.summary: Builds from the L function of any cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals an even entire completion, real and nonnegative on the real axis and positive at the centre, with all zeros in the open critical strip and a genus zero product in the squared variable.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$, $n\ge1$, with unitary central character, not a unitary twist $|\cdot|^{iy}$ of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$, and let $\Lambda(s,\pi)=\gamma(s,\pi)L(s,\pi)$ be its completed $L$ function in the unitary normalisation, in which the Dirichlet series $L(s,\pi)=\sum_ma_\pi(m)m^{-s}$ converges absolutely for $\operatorname{Re}s>1$ and $\gamma(s,\pi)=N_\pi^{s/2}\prod_{j=1}^n\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\mu_j)$, with $N_\pi$ the conductor, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$ and archimedean parameters $\mu_j$ with $\operatorname{Re}\mu_j>-\frac12$; $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ is entire of order one and satisfies $\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon(\pi)\Lambda(1-s,\tilde\pi)$ with $|\varepsilon(\pi)|=1$, $\tilde\pi$ the contragredient. Let $r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)$, $\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}$ and $F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)/\Xi_\pi(0)$, and when $\pi\cong\tilde\pi$ let $\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)/z^r$. Then (i) $\Xi_\pi$ is entire, even, and $\Xi_\pi(\bar z)=\overline{\Xi_\pi(z)}$, so it is real on $\mathbb{R}$; (ii) for real $x\ne0$, $\Xi_\pi(x)=|\Lambda(\frac12+x,\pi)|^2/x^{2r}\ge0$, $\Xi_\pi(0)>0$, and $\Xi_\pi(x)>0$ for $|x|\ge\frac12$; (iii) $\Xi_\pi$ has order at most one, and every zero $z$ of $\Xi_\pi$ satisfies $|\operatorname{Re}z|<\frac12$; (iv) $F_\pi$ is entire of order at most $\frac12$ with $F_\pi(0)=1$, and if the zeros of $\Xi_\pi$ are listed in pairs $\pm z_k$ with multiplicity and $s_k=z_k^2$, then $F_\pi(s)=\prod_k(1-s/s_k)$ with $\sum_k|s_k|^{-1}<\infty$; (v) if $\pi\cong\tilde\pi$ then $\varepsilon(\pi)=(-1)^r$, and $\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi$ is entire, even and real on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(0)\ne0$. The same statements hold for $\Xi_\zeta(z)=\xi(\frac12+z)$, where $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, which is moreover strictly positive on $\mathbb{R}$.
results.label: lem:10bcompletion

results.name: Thorin equivalence for even entire functions with zeros in a strip
results.summary: For an even entire function of order less than two, real on the real axis, equal to one at the origin and with zeros in a vertical strip, all zeros lie on the imaginary axis exactly when any one of several positivity properties holds (a generalized gamma convolution, a completely monotone Lévy function, a Stieltjes or Herglotz property of the logarithmic derivative, a Stieltjes moment sequence of power sums), extending an equivalence of the first author's 2018 paper for Laguerre Pólya functions.
results.statement:
Let $E$ be an entire function with $E(-z)=E(z)$, $E( ar z)=\overline{E(z)}$ and $E(0)=1$, of order less than two, whose zeros lie in a strip $|\operatorname{Re}z|\le\sigma_0$. List its zeros as pairs $\pm z_k$ with multiplicity, put $t_k=-z_k^2$ and $F(s)=E(\sqrt s)=\prod_k(1+s/t_k)$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,	au(dt))$, $s\ge0$, with drift $a\ge0$ and Thorin measure $	au$, a positive measure on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,	au(dt)<\infty$ and $\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,	au(dt)<\infty$; a Stieltjes function is a function on $(0,\infty)$ of the form $a/s+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\sigma(dt)/(s+t)$ with $a,b\ge0$ and $\sigma$ a positive measure with $\int\sigma(dt)/(1+t)<\infty$. Then $k(x)=\sum_ke^{-t_kx}$ converges absolutely and locally uniformly on $(0,\infty)$, the sums $S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}$, $n\ge1$, converge absolutely and are real, and the following are equivalent. (a) Every zero of $E$ lies on $i\mathbb{R}$; equivalently $t_k\in(0,\infty)$ for all $k$. (b) $1/F$ restricted to $(0,\infty)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (c) $1/F(s)=\mathbb{E}e^{-sX}$ for $s\ge0$, where $X=\sum_kE_k/t_k$ with $E_k$ independent standard exponential variables; that is, $1/F$ is a GGC transform with drift $0$ and Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{t_k}$. (d) $k$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$. (e) $F$ has no zero in $(0,\infty)$ and $F'/F$ is a Stieltjes function on $(0,\infty)$. (e') $E$ has no real zero, and $\operatorname{Im}(F'/F)(s)\le0$ at every $s$ with $\operatorname{Im}s>0$ and $F(s)
e0$. (f) There is a positive measure $
u$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $S_{j+1}=\int u^j
u(du)$ for all $j\ge0$; equivalently, the Hankel matrices $(S_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^N$ and $(S_{i+j+2})_{i,j=0}^N$ are positive semidefinite for every $N$. When these hold, $
u=\sum_kt_k^{-1}\delta_{1/t_k}$, the Stieltjes function in (e) is $\sum_k(s+t_k)^{-1}$, and the Bernstein measure of $k$ (the positive measure $\mu$ with $k(x)=\int e^{-tx}\mu(dt)$) is $\sum_k\delta_{t_k}$.
results.label: thm:10babstract

results.name: Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of automorphic L functions
results.summary: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the L function of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, and the Riemann hypothesis for zeta, are each equivalent to several positivity statements, among them that the reciprocal of the self dual completion, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure sits at the squared ordinates of the zeros, and a Hankel criterion computable from central derivatives; the theorem is an equivalence that extends the first author's 2018 paper, and it proves no case of either hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$, $n\ge1$, with unitary central character, not a unitary twist $|\cdot|^{iy}$ of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$, with contragredient $\tilde\pi$ and completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)=\gamma(s,\pi)L(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation: the Dirichlet series $L(s,\pi)=\sum_ma_\pi(m)m^{-s}$ converges absolutely for $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, $\gamma(s,\pi)=N_\pi^{s/2}\prod_{j=1}^n\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\mu_j)$ with $N_\pi$ the conductor, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$ and archimedean parameters $\mu_j$ with $\operatorname{Re}\mu_j>-\frac12$, and $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ is entire of order one with $\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon(\pi)\Lambda(1-s,\tilde\pi)$, $|\varepsilon(\pi)|=1$, so that the critical line is $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$. Let $r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)$, $\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}$ and $F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)/\Xi_\pi(0)$. List the zeros of $\Xi_\pi$ as pairs $\pm z_k$ with multiplicity, write $z_k=i\gamma_k$, call $t_k=-z_k^2=\gamma_k^2$ the Thorin atoms of $\pi$, and put $k_\pi(x)=\sum_ke^{-t_kx}$ and $S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}$ for $n\ge1$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,\tau(dt))$, $s\ge0$, with drift $a\ge0$ and Thorin measure $\tau$, a positive measure on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty$ and $\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty$; a Stieltjes function is a function on $(0,\infty)$ of the form $a/s+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\sigma(dt)/(s+t)$ with $a,b\ge0$ and $\sigma$ a positive measure with $\int\sigma(dt)/(1+t)<\infty$. The following are equivalent. (a) The generalized Riemann hypothesis holds for $\pi$, that is, all zeros of $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ lie on $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$ (equivalently, it holds for $\tilde\pi$). (b) $s\mapsto1/F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(0)/\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (c) $1/F_\pi$ is the Laplace transform of $\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2$, with $E_k$ independent standard exponential variables: a GGC with drift zero and Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$. (d) The L\'evy function $k_\pi(x)=\sum_ke^{xz_k^2}$, which converges for every $x>0$, is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$. (e) $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ has no real zero other than $\frac12$, and $F_\pi'/F_\pi$ is a Stieltjes function; equivalently (Herglotz criterion) $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ has no real zero other than $\frac12$ and $\operatorname{Im}(F_\pi'/F_\pi)(s)\le0$ whenever $\operatorname{Im}s>0$ and $F_\pi(s)\ne0$. (f) $(S_{j+1})_{j\ge0}$ is a Stieltjes moment sequence; equivalently (Thorin Hankel criterion) all Hankel matrices $(S_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^N$ and $(S_{i+j+2})_{i,j=0}^N$ are positive semidefinite. The same holds for the Riemann zeta function with $\Xi_\zeta(z)=\xi(\frac12+z)$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, and, when $\pi\cong\tilde\pi$, with $\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)/z^r$ in place of $\Xi_\pi$, in which case every Thorin atom has half the multiplicity.
results.label: thm:10bmain

results.name: Pólya kernel of a cuspidal automorphic L function
results.summary: The L function of every cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals has a real even kernel with doubly exponential decay whose two sided Laplace transform is its normalised self dual completion, although the kernel need not be positive.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$, $n\ge1$, with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$, with completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation, contragredient $\tilde\pi$, $r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)$ and self dual completion $\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}$. There is a real, even, continuous function $\Phi_\pi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int\Phi_\pi=1$ and constants $c,C>0$ such that $|\Phi_\pi(u)|\le C\exp(-ce^{c|u|})$ and $\Xi_\pi(z)/\Xi_\pi(0)=\int_{-\infty}^\infty\Phi_\pi(u)e^{zu}\,du$ for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$.
results.label: lem:10bkernel

results.name: Cumulant criterion for the generalized Riemann hypothesis via the Pólya variable
results.summary: When the Pólya kernel of an automorphic L function is nonnegative, the even cumulants of the associated symmetric random variable are, up to sign and scale, the power sums of the Thorin atoms, so the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to a Stieltjes moment property of the rescaled cumulants.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$, $n\ge1$, with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$, with completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation, contragredient $\tilde\pi$, $r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)$ and self dual completion $\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}$. List the zeros of $\Xi_\pi$ as pairs $\pm i\gamma_k$ with multiplicity, let $t_k=\gamma_k^2$ and $S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}$, and let $\Phi_\pi$ be the P\'olya kernel of $\pi$, the real even continuous function with $\Xi_\pi(z)/\Xi_\pi(0)=\int\Phi_\pi(u)e^{zu}du$ for all complex $z$. Suppose $\Phi_\pi\ge0$ and let $W_\pi$ be a random variable with density $\Phi_\pi$ (the P\'olya variable of $\pi$). Then the odd cumulants of $W_\pi$ vanish and the even ones are $\kappa_{2n}(W_\pi)/(2n)!=(-1)^{n+1}S_n/n$, $n\ge1$. Consequently the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\pi$ holds if and only if the sequence $m_j=(-1)^j(j+1)\kappa_{2j+2}(W_\pi)/(2j+2)!$, $j\ge0$, is a Stieltjes moment sequence (the sequence of moments $\int u^j\nu(du)$ of a positive measure $\nu$ on $[0,\infty)$). In particular the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\pi$ implies $(-1)^{n+1}\kappa_{2n}(W_\pi)>0$ for all $n$.
results.label: prop:10bcumulants

results.name: Central order of vanishing as a degenerate Thorin atom at the origin
results.status_text: conditional on the generalized Riemann hypothesis for L(s, pi), for the Laplace transform representation only (the slope limit is unconditional)
results.conditions: the generalized Riemann hypothesis for L(s, pi), for the Laplace transform representation only (the slope limit is unconditional)
results.summary: The order of vanishing of a self dual automorphic L function at the centre, such as the analytic rank of an elliptic curve, appears as a Thorin atom of mass half the order escaping to the origin, unconditionally as a log log slope and, under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, in a Laplace transform representation.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$, with $\pi\cong\tilde\pi$ ($\tilde\pi$ the contragredient), completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation, $r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\ge1$ and $H(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)/z^r$. Unconditionally, $\lim_{s\to0^+}d\log|\Lambda(\frac12+\sqrt s,\pi)|/d\log s=r/2$. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\pi$, for $s>0$, $H(0)/\Lambda(\frac12+\sqrt s,\pi)=s^{-r/2}\,\mathbb{E}e^{-sX}=\int_0^\infty e^{-sx}(m_r*\mu_X)(dx)$, where $m_r(dx)=x^{r/2-1}dx/\Gamma(r/2)$ on $(0,\infty)$, $X=\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2$ is the generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$ built from the zeros $\pm i\gamma_k$ of $H$ listed with multiplicity ($E_k$ independent standard exponential variables), and $\mu_X$ is the law of $X$. The infinite measure $m_r$ is the increasing limit as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ of $\epsilon^{-r/2}$ times the gamma law of shape $r/2$ and rate $\epsilon$, whose Thorin measure is $\frac r2\delta_\epsilon$: a Thorin atom of mass $r/2$ escaping to the origin.
results.label: prop:10brank

results.name: Gaussian tilting of the Pólya kernel and the Thorin property along the heat flow
results.summary: Tilting the Pólya kernel of an automorphic L function by a Gaussian factor narrows the strip containing the zeros and makes them all real once the tilt is large enough (de Bruijn's theorem, the first part), and the book adds that, when the kernel is nonnegative, the reciprocal of the tilted transform in the squared variable is then the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, unconditionally for every tilt of at least one eighth.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$, $n\ge1$, with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$, with completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation, self dual completion $\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}$ ($\tilde\pi$ the contragredient, $r$ the order of $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ at $s=\frac12$) and P\'olya kernel $\Phi_\pi$, the real even continuous function with $|\Phi_\pi(u)|\le C\exp(-ce^{c|u|})$ for some $c,C>0$ and $\Xi_\pi(z)/\Xi_\pi(0)=\int\Phi_\pi(u)e^{zu}du$ for all complex $z$. For $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ let $H_{\pi,\lambda}(t)=\int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{\lambda u^2}\Phi_\pi(u)e^{itu}\,du$. For $\sigma\ge0$, condition $\Theta_\sigma$ says that every zero $z$ of $\Xi_\pi$ satisfies $|\operatorname{Re}z|\le\sigma$, equivalently that every zero of $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ lies in $|\operatorname{Re}s-\frac12|\le\sigma$; let $P_\sigma=\{x+iy:x\le\sigma^2-y^2/(4\sigma^2)\}$ for $\sigma>0$ and $P_0=(-\infty,0]$. Suppose $\Theta_\sigma$ holds for $\pi$ and let $\lambda\ge0$. (i) (de Bruijn) The zeros of $H_{\pi,\lambda}$ lie in $|\operatorname{Im}t|\le\sigma_\lambda$, where $\sigma_\lambda=(\max(\sigma^2-2\lambda,0))^{1/2}$; Gaussian tilting moves the Thorin atoms (the squares of the zeros of $H_{\pi,\lambda}$) from $-P_\sigma$ into $-P_{\sigma_\lambda}$, and for $\lambda\ge\sigma^2/2$ all zeros of $H_{\pi,\lambda}$ are real. (ii) If $\Phi_\pi\ge0$, let $W_{\pi,\lambda}$ have density proportional to $e^{\lambda u^2}\Phi_\pi(u)$. For every $\lambda\ge\sigma^2/2$ the function $s\mapsto H_{\pi,\lambda}(0)/H_{\pi,\lambda}(i\sqrt s)=1/\mathbb{E}e^{\sqrt sW_{\pi,\lambda}}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{x_k(\lambda)^2}$, where $\pm x_k(\lambda)$ are the real zeros of $H_{\pi,\lambda}$. Unconditionally ($\sigma=\frac12$), $H_{\pi,\lambda}$ has only real zeros for every $\lambda\ge\frac18$, and (ii) holds for these $\lambda$.
results.label: thm:10btilting

results.name: Regularised Thorin equivalence for even entire functions of order two
results.summary: For even entire functions of order at most two whose zeros have summable inverse fourth powers, such as the completed Selberg zeta function of a compact hyperbolic surface, all Thorin atoms are positive exactly when the reciprocal is the Laplace transform of a centred sum of exponential variables, which for the surface means no exceptional Laplace eigenvalue (for arithmetic surfaces Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture, which this equivalence does not prove).
results.statement: Let $E$ be an entire function, even, real on $\mathbb{R}$, with $E(0)=1$, of order at most two, whose zeros $\pm z_k$ (listed with multiplicity) satisfy $\sum_k|z_k|^{-4}<\infty$; let $t_k=-z_k^2$ and $F(s)=E(\sqrt s)$. Then $F(s)=e^{bs}\prod_k(1+s/t_k)e^{-s/t_k}$ for some real $b$, and the following are equivalent: (a) all $t_k>0$; (b) for independent standard exponential variables $E_k$ the series $Y=b+\sum_k(E_k-1)/t_k$, which converges in $L^2$, is real valued and satisfies $1/F(s)=\mathbb{E}e^{-sY}$ for $s\ge0$; (c) $1/F$ agrees on $(0,\infty)$ with a function holomorphic and zero free on $\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]$. The law of $Y$ in (b) is infinitely divisible with L\'evy measure $x^{-1}\sum_ke^{-t_kx}dx$ on $(0,\infty)$; when $\sum_kt_k^{-1}=\infty$ its first moment $\int_0^1\sum_ke^{-t_kx}dx$ near the origin is infinite, which is why the centring is needed.
results.label: prop:10bregularised

results.name: Local Thorin criterion for a single Euler factor
results.summary: The reciprocal of a completed Euler factor of degree two, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law exactly when its trace parameter lies in the tempered interval with the degenerate endpoint 2 excluded, and the law is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb.
results.statement: Let $L>0$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$, and put $f_x(s)=(2-x)/(2\cosh(L\sqrt s)-x)$ for $s>0$. Then $f_x$ is the Laplace transform of a probability law on $[0,\infty)$ if and only if $-2\le x<2$. In that case, writing $x=2\cos\theta$ with $0<\theta\le\pi$, the law is a generalized gamma convolution with drift $0$ and Thorin measure $\tau_{\theta,L}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{t_k}$, $t_k=((\theta+2\pi k)/L)^2$, namely the law of $\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}E_k/t_k$ with $E_k$ independent standard exponential variables, with mean $L^2/(2-x)$.
results.label: thm:10clocal

results.name: Thorin criterion for the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at a prime
results.summary: For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over the rationals with trivial central character, the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at an unramified prime (outside the degenerate case of trace 2) holds exactly when the reciprocal of the symmetrised Euler factor, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, which is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb (Ramanujan is local Thorin, as the generalized Riemann hypothesis is global Thorin); the corollary is an equivalence and proves no case of the conjecture.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ with trivial central character, in the unitary normalisation, and let $p$ be a prime at which $\pi$ is unramified, with Euler factor $L_p(s)=(1-\alpha p^{-s})^{-1}(1-\beta p^{-s})^{-1}$, $\alpha\beta=1$; unitarity of the local component $\pi_p$ makes the Satake set $\{\alpha,\beta\}$ stable under $z\mapsto\bar z^{-1}$, so either $|\alpha|=1$ or $\alpha$ is real, and in both cases $x_p=\alpha+\beta$ is real. Put $E_p(w)=p^wL_p(w)^{-1}=2\cosh(w\log p)-x_p$ and assume $x_p\ne2$. The Ramanujan Petersson conjecture holds at $p$ (that is, $|\alpha|=|\beta|=1$) if and only if $s\mapsto E_p(0)/E_p(\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a probability law on $[0,\infty)$, and then this law is a generalized gamma convolution (a law whose Laplace transform is $\exp(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,\tau(dt))$ with drift $a\ge0$ and Thorin measure $\tau\ge0$) with Thorin measure $\tau=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{((\theta_p+2\pi k)/\log p)^2}$, where $x_p=2\cos\theta_p$ with $0<\theta_p\le\pi$.
results.label: cor:10cramanujan

results.name: Prime terms of the explicit formula as damped local Thorin combs
results.summary: In Weil's explicit formula for the discriminant modular form, the contribution of each prime is the oscillatory part of the sum of the test function over that prime's local Thorin comb, with its sign changed and each Fourier coefficient damped by a power of the prime.
results.statement: Normalise the discriminant modular form $\Delta$ so that $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_n\tau(n)n^{-11/2-s}$ and $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s-11/2}\Gamma(s+\frac{11}2)L(s,\Delta)$, with nontrivial zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity, and for a prime $p$ write $\tau(p)p^{-11/2}=2\cos\theta_p$ with $\theta_p\in[0,\pi]$. Let $h$ be even and holomorphic in $|\operatorname{Im}t|<\frac12+\varepsilon$ with $h(t)\ll(1+|t|)^{-1-\delta}$ there, and also a Schwartz function on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $H(x)=\int h(t)e^{-ixt}dt$, so that Weil's explicit formula reads $\sum_\gamma h(\gamma)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}}h(t)\,2\operatorname{Re}[-\log2\pi+\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(6+it)]\,dt-\frac1\pi\sum_p\sum_{m\ge1}2\cos(m\theta_p)\log p\,p^{-m/2}H(m\log p)$. With $L=\log p$, let $c_p(h)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}[h((\theta_p+2\pi k)/L)+h((-\theta_p+2\pi k)/L)]$ be the comb sum of $p$, the sum of $h$ over the ordinates of the local zeros of $w\mapsto2\cosh(wL)-2\cos\theta_p$. Then for every prime $p$ the contribution of $p$ to the prime side of the explicit formula is obtained from the oscillatory part $c_p(h)-\frac L\pi H(0)=\frac{2L}\pi\sum_{m\ge1}\cos(m\theta_p)H(mL)$ of the local comb sum by changing the sign and multiplying the $m$th Fourier coefficient by $p^{-m/2}$.
results.label: prop:10cdictionary

results.name: Intensity of the Thorin point process of Sato Tate random Euler products
results.summary: For Euler products with independent Sato Tate angles, the ordinates of the local Thorin combs form a point process with an explicit intensity that vanishes quadratically at the origin, and each local law has expected mean the square of the logarithm of the prime.
results.statement: Let $\theta$ have the Sato Tate law $\frac2\pi\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$ on $[0,\pi]$ and let $\epsilon=\pm1$ be an independent fair sign. (1) The configuration $\{\theta,-\theta\}$ on the circle $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ has intensity $\frac2\pi\sin^2\psi\,d\psi$, and $\epsilon\theta$ has density $\frac1\pi\sin^2\psi$ on $(-\pi,\pi]$. (2) For a prime $p$ whose angle $\theta_p$ has the Sato Tate law, the ordinates $(\pm\theta_p+2\pi\mathbb{Z})/\log p$ of its local Thorin comb (the ordinates of the zeros of $w\mapsto2\cosh(w\log p)-2\cos\theta_p$) form a symmetric point process on $\mathbb{R}$ with intensity $\frac{\log p}\pi(1-\cos(2t\log p))\,dt$. Consequently, if the angles $\theta_p$ are independent with the Sato Tate law and $x_p=2\cos\theta_p$, the Thorin point process of the random Euler product $\Phi_P(s)=\prod_{p\le P}(2-x_p)/(2\cosh(\sqrt s\log p)-x_p)$, whose Thorin measure is $\sum_{p\le P}\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{((\theta_p+2\pi k)/\log p)^2}$, has intensity $I_P(t)\,dt$ on the ordinate axis, with $I_P(t)=\frac1\pi\sum_{p\le P}\log p\,(1-\cos(2t\log p))$. (3) $\mathbb{E}[(2-x_p)^{-1}]=1$, so the local law, the generalized gamma convolution with Laplace transform $(2-x_p)/(2\cosh(\sqrt s\log p)-x_p)$ and mean $(\log p)^2/(2-x_p)$, has expected mean $(\log p)^2$.
results.label: prop:10csatotate

results.name: Thorin criterion for the Riemann hypothesis of curves over finite fields
results.summary: For a curve over a finite field with q elements, none of whose Frobenius eigenvalues equals the square root of q, the reciprocal of its completed zeta function in the squared variable is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann hypothesis for the curve holds, so by Weil's theorem global Thorin holds unconditionally there, with a Thorin measure made of finitely many periodic combs.
results.statement: Let $C$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus $g\ge1$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, with zeta function $Z(C,u)=P(u)/((1-u)(1-qu))$, $P(u)=\prod_{j=1}^{2g}(1-\alpha_ju)\in\mathbb{Z}[u]$, $u=q^{-s}$. Pair the roots under $\alpha\mapsto q/\alpha$, put $c_j=(\alpha_j+q/\alpha_j)/\sqrt q$ for $1\le j\le g$, $\Xi_C(z)=q^{gz}P(q^{-1/2-z})=\prod_{j=1}^g(2\cosh(z\log q)-c_j)$ and $F_C(s)=\Xi_C(\sqrt s)/\Xi_C(0)$. Assume $P(q^{-1/2})\ne0$, that is, no $\alpha_j$ equals $\sqrt q$. Then $s\mapsto1/F_C(s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds for $C$, that is, $|\alpha_j|=\sqrt q$ for all $j$, equivalently $c_j=2\cos\theta_j\in[-2,2]$ with $\alpha_j=\sqrt q\,e^{i\theta_j}$. In that case the Thorin measure is the finite superposition of periodic combs $\tau_C=\sum_{j=1}^g\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{((\theta_j+2\pi k)/\log q)^2}$, and the law is that of $\sum_j\sum_kE_{j,k}(\log q)^2/(\theta_j+2\pi k)^2$, with $E_{j,k}$ independent standard exponential variables, with mean $(\log q)^2\sum_j(2-c_j)^{-1}$. By Weil's theorem all of this holds unconditionally.
results.label: thm:10ccurve

results.name: Thorin criterion for Ramanujan graphs and supersingular isogeny graphs
results.summary: A finite connected regular graph of degree q plus one, without the eigenvalue twice the square root of q, is Ramanujan exactly when the reciprocal of its completed Ihara zeta function, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, and both hold unconditionally for supersingular isogeny graphs.
results.statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected $(q+1)$ regular graph with adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_j$, put $\Xi_G(z)=\prod_{|\lambda_j|<q+1}(2\cosh(z\log q)-\lambda_j/\sqrt q)$ and $F_G(s)=\Xi_G(\sqrt s)/\Xi_G(0)$, and suppose that no eigenvalue of $G$ equals $2\sqrt q$. Then $G$ is Ramanujan (every eigenvalue $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|\ne q+1$ satisfies $|\lambda|\le2\sqrt q$) if and only if $1/F_G$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, and then its Thorin measure is $\sum_j\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{((\theta_j+2\pi k)/\log q)^2}$ over the nontrivial eigenvalues $\lambda_j=2\sqrt q\cos\theta_j$. For the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graphs $G_N(\ell)$ (vertices the supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ up to isomorphism, one edge for each subgroup of order $\ell$ of a curve), with $N\equiv1\bmod12$ and $\ell\ne N$ primes, both hold unconditionally.
results.label: thm:10cihara

results.name: Thorin structure of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree
results.summary: The first time that continuous time simple random walk on a regular tree (the Hecke walk, on the Bruhat Tits tree when the degree is a prime plus one) reaches distance n from its start is a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin atoms, given by the zeros of the sphere polynomials of the tree, lie in the Kesten band and follow the arcsine law as n grows, with an exact mean, a variance linear in n and a central limit theorem; Thorin support in the Kesten band is the random walk form of the Ramanujan bound, and this unconditional theorem about the tree proves no case of the Ramanujan conjecture for automorphic forms.
results.statement: Let $q\ge2$ be an integer, $\rho=2\sqrt q/(q+1)$ the Kesten spectral radius, and run continuous time simple random walk on the $(q+1)$ regular tree (the Bruhat Tits tree of $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_q)$ for $q$ prime), jumping at rate $1$ to a uniformly chosen neighbour; this is the Hecke walk with generator $(q+1)^{-1}A-I$, $A$ the adjacency operator. Let $T_n$ be the first time at distance $n$ from the starting vertex. The distance from the start is a birth death process with birth rates $b_0=1$ and $b_k=\frac q{q+1}$, and death rates $d_k=\frac1{q+1}$, for $k\ge1$; let $\lambda_1<\dots<\lambda_n$ be the Thorin atoms of $T_n$, the eigenvalues of minus its generator restricted to $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ (killed at $n$), so that by Keilson's theorem $T_n$ has the law of $\sum_{j=1}^nE_j/\lambda_j$ with independent standard exponential $E_j$, a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure $\sum_{j=1}^n\delta_{\lambda_j}$. (1) $\lambda_j=1-\frac{\sqrt q}{q+1}x_j$, where $x_1>\dots>x_n$ are the zeros of the polynomial $U_n(x/2)-q^{-1}U_{n-2}(x/2)$, with $U_k$ the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind and $U_{-1}=0$, which expresses the normalised sphere operator $q^{-n/2}A_n$ of the tree ($A_n$ summing over the vertices at distance $n$) in terms of $q^{-1/2}A$. All $x_j$ lie in $(-2,2)$, so all rates lie in the Kesten band $(1-\rho,1+\rho)$. (2) $\frac1n\sum_j\delta_{\lambda_j}$ converges weakly to the law of $1-\rho\cos(\pi U)$, $U$ uniform on $(0,1)$: the arcsine law on the Kesten band. (3) $\mathbb{E}T_n=\frac{n(q+1)}{q-1}-\frac{2q(1-q^{-n})}{(q-1)^2}$, and $\mathbb{E}T_n/n\to\frac{q+1}{q-1}=\frac1{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}=\int_0^1\frac{du}{1-\rho\cos\pi u}$. The escape speed of the walk is $\frac{q-1}{q+1}=\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$. (4) $\operatorname{Var}T_n/n\to(\frac{q+1}{q-1})^3=(1-\rho^2)^{-3/2}$, and $(T_n-\mathbb{E}T_n)/\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}T_n}$ converges in law to a standard normal.
results.label: thm:10ctree

results.name: Large deviations of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree
results.summary: Passage times of the Hecke walk on a regular tree satisfy a large deviation principle with an explicit rate function, computed from the arcsine limit of their Thorin atoms.
results.statement: Let $q\ge2$ be an integer, $\rho=2\sqrt q/(q+1)$, and let $T_n$ be the first time at distance $n$ from the start of continuous time simple random walk on the $(q+1)$ regular tree, jumping at rate $1$ to a uniformly chosen neighbour. For $\theta\le1-\rho$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\mathbb{E}e^{\theta T_n}=\Lambda(\theta)=-\log\frac{(q+1)(1-\theta+\sqrt{(1-\theta)^2-\rho^2})}{2q}$, and the limit is $+\infty$ for $\theta>1-\rho$. In particular $\Lambda(1-\rho)=\frac12\log q$. The function $\Lambda$ is steep, $\Lambda'(\theta)=((1-\theta)^2-\rho^2)^{-1/2}\to\infty$ as $\theta\uparrow1-\rho$, so $T_n/n$ satisfies a large deviation principle with good rate function $\Lambda^*(y)=y-\sqrt{1+\rho^2y^2}+\log\frac{(q+1)(1+\sqrt{1+\rho^2y^2})}{2qy}$, $y>0$, which vanishes only at $y=\frac{q+1}{q-1}$.
results.label: thm:10cldp

results.name: Exponential approximation of hitting times on Ramanujan graphs
results.summary: On a Ramanujan graph that is not bipartite, all Dirichlet rates of a target but the slowest lie in the Kesten band, and the hitting time of any vertex from the uniform start is exponential up to an explicit error of order one over the number of vertices.
results.statement: Let $G$ be a connected $(q+1)$ regular graph on a vertex set $V$ of size $h$, not bipartite, with symmetric adjacency matrix $A$ (loops and multiple edges allowed); let $P=(q+1)^{-1}A$ have eigenvalues $1=p_1>p_2\ge\dots\ge p_h>-1$, and run the continuous time walk with generator $P-I$ started from the uniform law $\pi$. For a target $v$ let $\tau_v$ be its hitting time, let $P_v$ be the principal submatrix of $P$ on $V\setminus\{v\}$, with eigenvalues $r_1\ge\dots\ge r_{h-1}$, and let $\mu_j=1-r_j$ be the Dirichlet rates; put $\rho=2\sqrt q/(q+1)$ and let $\tau_2=1/(1-p_2)$ be the relaxation time. If $G$ is Ramanujan, that is $p_2,\dots,p_h\in[-\rho,\rho]$, then $\mu_2,\dots,\mu_{h-1}\in[1-\rho,1+\rho]$, so only the slowest Dirichlet rate $\mu_1\le1-p_2$ can leave the Kesten band. Moreover, for every target $v$, $\sup_{t\ge0}|\mathbb{P}_\pi(\tau_v>t)-e^{-t/\mathbb{E}_\pi\tau_v}|\le\tau_2/\mathbb{E}_\pi\tau_v\le(q+1)h/((\sqrt q-1)^2(h-1)^2)\le2(q+1)/((\sqrt q-1)^2(h-1))$.
results.label: thm:10cexpo

results.name: Unconditional exponential law for hitting times on supersingular isogeny graphs
results.summary: On supersingular isogeny graphs the hitting time of any curve by a continuous time random walk from a uniform start is unconditionally exponential up to an explicit error of order one over the number of vertices.
results.statement: Let $N>13$ be a prime with $N\equiv1\bmod12$, so that $h=(N-1)/12\ge2$, let $\ell\ne N$ be prime, and let $G_N(\ell)$ be the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph in characteristic $N$ (vertices the $h$ supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ up to isomorphism, one edge for each of the $\ell+1$ subgroups of order $\ell$ of a curve, joining it to the quotient curve). For simple random walk in continuous time at rate $1$ on $G_N(\ell)$, started from the uniform law $\pi$, the hitting time $\tau_v$ of every vertex $v$ satisfies $\sup_{t\ge0}|\mathbb{P}_\pi(\tau_v>t)-e^{-t/\mathbb{E}_\pi\tau_v}|\le2(\ell+1)/((\sqrt\ell-1)^2(h-1))$, and all Dirichlet rates but the slowest (the numbers $1-r$, $r$ an eigenvalue of the transition matrix restricted to the vertices other than $v$) lie in the Kesten band $[1-\rho_\ell,1+\rho_\ell]$, $\rho_\ell=2\sqrt\ell/(\ell+1)$.
results.label: cor:10cisogeny

results.name: Max infinite divisibility of the extreme value law of the Dedekind eta function
results.summary: The maximum of scaled exponential variables whose distribution function is the product behind the Dedekind eta function is max infinitely divisible, with a completely monotone exponent function, an exponent measure built from divisor sums, a Poisson splitting and the same structure for every multiplicative eta product; the Mellin transform of the exponent, also stated, is classical.
results.statement: Let $E_1,E_2,\dots$ be independent standard exponential variables, $M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)$, $P(y)=\mathbb{P}(M\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})$ for $y>0$, and $\sigma_{-1}(m)=\sum_{d\mid m}d^{-1}$. (1) $G=-\log P$ satisfies $G(y)=\sum_{m\ge1}\sigma_{-1}(m)e^{-2\pi my}$ for $y>0$; hence $G$ is completely monotone, $G(y)=\int e^{-yu}\nu(du)$ with $\nu=\sum_{m\ge1}\sigma_{-1}(m)\delta_{2\pi m}$, and $M$ is max infinitely divisible. (2) For each $n$, $E_n/(2\pi n)$ has the law of $\max_{k\ge1}\max_{i\le N_k}E_{k,i}/(2\pi nk)$, where the $E_{k,i}$ are standard exponential, $N_k$ is Poisson of mean $1/k$, and all variables are independent. Consequently $M$ has the law of $\max_{m\ge1}\max_{i\le N'_m}E'_{m,i}/(2\pi m)$ with independent standard exponential $E'_{m,i}$ and independent $N'_m$ Poisson of mean $\sigma_{-1}(m)$. (3) For $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, $\int_0^\infty G(y)y^{s-1}dy=\Gamma(s)(2\pi)^{-s}\zeta(s)\zeta(s+1)$; the right side continues meromorphically to $\mathbb{C}$ with poles only at $s=0,\pm1$, and is invariant under $s\mapsto-s$. (4) For $f=\prod_m\eta(m\tau)^{r_m}$ with $r_m\ge0$ and $\sum_mmr_m=24$, let $M_f$ be the maximum, over all $m$, of $r_m$ independent copies of $M/m$, so that $\mathbb{P}(M_f\le y)=\prod_mP(my)^{r_m}$. Then $-\log\mathbb{P}(M_f\le y)=\sum_mr_mG(my)$ is completely monotone with exponent measure $\sum_n(\sum_{m\mid n}r_m\sigma_{-1}(n/m))\delta_{2\pi n}$, and its Mellin transform is $\Gamma(s)(2\pi)^{-s}\zeta(s)\zeta(s+1)\sum_mr_mm^{-s}$.
results.label: prop:10cmaxid

results.name: Duality of imaginary zeros, Thorin's condition, van Dantzig pairs and Wald couples
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, arXiv:1804.10043.
results.summary: A real entire function of order at most one that is symmetric about a point has all its zeros on the vertical line through that point exactly when Thorin's condition holds (its reciprocal, centred there and evaluated along the square root, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution); when the centred function is also a moment generating function, this yields a van Dantzig pair and a Wald couple.
results.statement: Let $f$ be a real entire function of order at most one, symmetric about $\alpha$ in the sense $f(\alpha + s) = f(\alpha - s)$, with $f(\alpha) > 0$. The zeros of $s\mapsto f(\alpha + s)$ are purely imaginary, $\pm i\rho_k$, if and only if Thorin's condition holds: $\frac{f(\alpha)}{f(\alpha + \sqrt{s})} = \mathbb{E}\, e^{-sH}$ for $s > 0$, for a generalized gamma convolution $H$ (a law on $[0,\infty)$ that is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws). In that case the Thorin measure of $H$ is $\sum_k \delta_{\rho_k^2}$; if moreover $f(\alpha + \cdot)/f(\alpha)$ is the moment generating function of a symmetric random variable $X$, then $[f_\alpha, g_\alpha]$, with $f_\alpha(t) = f(\alpha + it)/f(\alpha)$ and $g_\alpha(t) = f(\alpha)/f(\alpha + t)$, is a van Dantzig pair (both $f_\alpha$ and $g_\alpha(t) = 1/f_\alpha(it)$ are characteristic functions of real random variables), and $(X, H)$ is a Wald couple: $\mathbb{E}\, e^{sX}\, \mathbb{E}\, e^{-s^2 H} = 1$ for all $s$ in some interval $[0, s_0)$ with $s_0 > 0$.
results.supersedes: Theorem 12 of Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), arXiv:1804.10043, which also asserts that $X$ is infinitely divisible. That cannot hold when $f$ has zeros: the characteristic function $t\mapsto f(\alpha+it)/f(\alpha)$ of $X$ then vanishes at the real points $\pm\rho_k$, while the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible law has no real zero.
results.label: thm:10dduality

results.name: Generalized Riemann hypothesis as a van Dantzig pair, a Wald couple and Lukacs class membership
results.summary: For an automorphic L function whose Pólya kernel is nonnegative, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to three probabilistic statements (a Pólya frequency partner law, a Wald couple with a generalized gamma convolution, membership in the Lukacs class), as Roynette and Yor, Polson, and Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar showed for the Riemann zeta function; these are reformulations and prove no case of the hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$, $n \ge 1$, with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$, with completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation and contragredient $\tilde\pi$; put $r = \operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)$ and $\Xi_\pi(z) = \Lambda(\tfrac12 + z,\pi)\Lambda(\tfrac12 + z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}$; or let $\Xi_\pi(z) = \xi(\tfrac12 + z)$ with $\xi(s) = \tfrac12 s(s - 1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\tfrac s2)\zeta(s)$. List the zeros of $\Xi_\pi$ in pairs $\pm i\gamma_k$ with multiplicity. Suppose the P\'olya kernel $\Phi_\pi$, the even function with $\Xi_\pi(z)/\Xi_\pi(0) = \int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_\pi(u)e^{zu}\,du$ for all complex $z$, is nonnegative, so that the P\'olya variable $W_\pi$ with density $\Phi_\pi$ exists (for instance for $\xi$, for the modular discriminant $\Delta$ and for every multiplicative eta product, using the self dual completion $\Lambda(\tfrac12 + z,\pi)/z^r$ in place of $\Xi_\pi$). Let $E_1, E_2, \dots$ be independent standard exponential variables and $L_1, L_2, \dots$ independent standard Laplace variables (density $\tfrac12 e^{-|x|}$), and put $Z_\pi = \sum_k E_k/\gamma_k^2$ and $V_\pi = \sum_k L_k/\gamma_k$ whenever all $\gamma_k$ are real. The following are equivalent. (a) The generalized Riemann hypothesis holds for $\pi$ (the Riemann hypothesis in the case of $\xi$): every $\gamma_k$ is real, that is, all zeros of $\Xi_\pi$ are purely imaginary. (b) $t\mapsto \Xi_\pi(0)/\Xi_\pi(t)$ is the characteristic function of a symmetric P\'olya frequency density (a probability density $g$ with $\det[g(x_i - y_j)]_{i,j \le m} \ge 0$ whenever $x_1 < \dots < x_m$ and $y_1 < \dots < y_m$); equivalently, of a series $\sum_k L_k/c_k$ with real $c_k$ and $\sum_k c_k^{-2} < \infty$. Then $c_k = \gamma_k$, $[\,\Xi_\pi(it)/\Xi_\pi(0),\ \Xi_\pi(0)/\Xi_\pi(t)\,]$ is the van Dantzig pair of $(W_\pi, V_\pi)$, and $V_\pi = \sum_k L_k/\gamma_k$ has the law of $\sqrt{2Z_\pi}\,N$ with $N$ standard normal and independent of $Z_\pi$. (c) There is a generalized gamma convolution $H$ such that $(W_\pi, H)$ is a Wald couple, that is $\mathbb{E}\, e^{sW_\pi}\, \mathbb{E}\, e^{-s^2 H} = 1$ for all $s$ in some interval $[0, s_0)$ with $s_0 > 0$; then $H$ has the law of $Z_\pi$. (d) $t\mapsto \Xi_\pi(it)/\Xi_\pi(0)$ belongs to the Lukacs class: even characteristic functions that are real entire functions with value $1$ at $0$ and locally uniform limits of real polynomials with only real zeros.
results.label: thm:10dvdp

results.name: Sine squared transport from a Lévy measure to a Thorin density
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, arXiv:1804.10043.
results.summary: When the logarithm of a positive analytic function has a Lévy Khintchine representation with a positive measure at a basepoint, its reciprocal along the square root is, up to a stable factor, a generalized gamma convolution transform whose Thorin density is the sine squared transport of that measure and can be read from the logarithmic derivative on one vertical line.
results.statement:
Let $f$ be holomorphic and zero free on $\operatorname{Re}w > \alpha - \eta$ for some $\eta > 0$, positive on $(\alpha,\infty)$, and suppose that for $s \ge 0$ we have $\log f(\alpha + s) - \log f(\alpha) - bs = \int_0^\infty (e^{-sx} - 1 + sx)\, rac{
u(dx)}{x}$, where $b = f'(\alpha)/f(\alpha)$ and $
u$ is a positive measure on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_0^\infty \min(1,x)\,
u(dx) < \infty$. Then for $s > 0$, $ rac{f(\alpha)}{f(\alpha + \sqrt{s})} = e^{-b\sqrt{s}}\,\mathbb{E}\, e^{-sH}$, where $H$ is a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin density $U(z) =  rac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{z}}\int_0^\infty 2\sin^2 igl( rac{x\sqrt{z}}{2} igr)\,
u(dx) =  rac{\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha + i\sqrt{z}) - b}{2\pi\sqrt{z}}$. If $b \ge 0$, $e^{-b\sqrt{s}}$ is the Laplace transform of a positive $	frac12$ stable law, a generalized gamma convolution with Thorin density $b/(2\pi\sqrt{z})$, and then $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha + \sqrt{s})$ is itself a generalized gamma convolution transform with Thorin density $\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha + i\sqrt{z})/(2\pi\sqrt{z})$. The hypothesis with $
u \ge 0$ holds if and only if $s\mapsto (\log f)''(\alpha + s)$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$ and tends to $0$ at infinity.
results.label: lem:10dsin2

results.name: Shifted Thorin representation of completed automorphic L functions and a Thorin form of the Hinkkanen Lagarias criterion
results.summary: Moving the basepoint of a completed automorphic L function to the right of all its zeros makes its reciprocal along the square root a generalized gamma convolution transform with an explicit Thorin density, unconditionally from the edge of the critical strip on, and the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the positivity of these densities for every positive shift; this extends to automorphic L functions what Polson proved for the Riemann xi function.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$, with completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation, and let $\Xi_\pi(z) = \Lambda(\tfrac12 + z,\pi)\Lambda(\tfrac12 + z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}$ with $\tilde\pi$ the contragredient and $r = \operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)$; or let $\Xi_\pi(z) = \xi(\tfrac12 + z)$ with $\xi$ the Riemann xi function. Let $a > 0$ and put $V_a(z) = \frac{\operatorname{Re}(\Xi_\pi'/\Xi_\pi)(a + i\sqrt{z})}{2\pi\sqrt{z}}$ for $z > 0$. (i) If every zero $z_k$ of $\Xi_\pi$ satisfies $|\operatorname{Re}z_k| < a$, then $V_a \ge 0$ and $\Xi_\pi(a)/\Xi_\pi(a + \sqrt{s}) = \mathbb{E}\, e^{-sH_a}$ for $s > 0$, with $H_a$ a generalized gamma convolution of drift zero and Thorin density $V_a$. (ii) If $\Xi_\pi(a)/\Xi_\pi(a + \sqrt{s})$ is a generalized gamma convolution transform on $(0,\infty)$, every zero satisfies $|\operatorname{Re}z_k| \le a$. (iii) Unconditionally, (i) holds for every $a \ge \tfrac12$, that is for every basepoint $\alpha = \tfrac12 + a \ge 1$ in the variable $s$ of $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ in the unitary normalisation. (iv) The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\pi$ (the Riemann hypothesis in the case of $\xi$) holds if and only if $V_a \ge 0$ for every $a > 0$, if and only if the conclusion of (i) holds for every $a > 0$. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, with the zeros of $\Xi_\pi$ written $\pm i\gamma_k$, $V_a(z)\,dz \to \sum_k \delta_{\gamma_k^2}$ vaguely and $H_a \to Z_\pi = \sum_k E_k/\gamma_k^2$ in law as $a \downarrow 0$, where the $E_k$ are independent standard exponential variables.
results.label: thm:10dshift

results.name: Damped cosine Lévy measure of the zeros and its sine squared transport
results.status_text: conditional on the generalized Riemann hypothesis for L(s, pi)
results.conditions: the generalized Riemann hypothesis for L(s, pi)
results.summary: Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the reciprocal of a completed automorphic L function with its basepoint moved a distance epsilon to the right of the centre, evaluated along the square root, factors into a positive one half stable transform and the exponential of a Thorin type integral whose density, a signed combination of Poisson kernels at the ordinates of the zeros, is the sine squared transport of the damped cosine measure of the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\Xi_\pi(z) = \Lambda(\tfrac12 + z,\pi)\Lambda(\tfrac12 + z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}$ be the self dual completion of a cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of $\mathrm{GL}_1$ (with $\tilde\pi$ the contragredient and $r = \operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)$), or $\Xi_\pi(z) = \xi(\tfrac12 + z)$ with $\xi$ the Riemann xi function. Assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\pi$ (the Riemann hypothesis in the case of $\xi$), so that the zeros of $\Xi_\pi$ are $\pm i\gamma_k$ with $\gamma_k$ real, and let $\epsilon > 0$. With $P_\epsilon(u) = \epsilon/(\epsilon^2 + u^2)$ and $b_\epsilon = (\Xi_\pi'/\Xi_\pi)(\epsilon) = \sum_{\gamma_k > 0} 2P_\epsilon(\gamma_k)$, we have $\frac{\Xi_\pi(\epsilon)}{\Xi_\pi(\epsilon + \sqrt{s})} = e^{-b_\epsilon\sqrt{s}}\exp\Bigl(-\int_0^\infty \log\bigl(1 + \frac{s}{z}\bigr)U_\epsilon(z)\,dz\Bigr)$ with $U_\epsilon(z) = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{z}}\sum_{\gamma_k > 0}\bigl[P_\epsilon(\sqrt{z} - \gamma_k) + P_\epsilon(\sqrt{z} + \gamma_k) - 2P_\epsilon(\gamma_k)\bigr]$, and $U_\epsilon(z) = (2\pi\sqrt{z})^{-1}\int_0^\infty 2\sin^2(x\sqrt{z}/2)\,e^{-\epsilon x}\,(-\mu)(dx)$ is the sine squared transport of the damped cosine measure, where $\mu(dx) = 2\sum_{\gamma_k > 0}\cos(\gamma_k x)\,dx$ is the cosine L\'evy measure of the zeros, the integral being taken term by term in $k$.
results.label: prop:10dsmooth

results.name: Marginal law of the zeta subordinator through generalized divisor functions
results.summary: The compound Poisson subordinator built from the Euler product of the Riemann zeta function takes values in the logarithms of the positive integers, with probabilities given by the Dirichlet coefficients of a real power of zeta.
results.statement: Fix $\sigma > 1$ and let $X$ be the compound Poisson subordinator with L\'evy measure $\Pi_\sigma = \sum_{n \ge 2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^\sigma \log n}\,\delta_{\log n}$, where $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function, so that $\mathbb{E}\, e^{-\lambda X_t} = \bigl(\zeta(\sigma + \lambda)/\zeta(\sigma)\bigr)^t$ for $\lambda \ge 0$ and $t \ge 0$. Let $d_t(m)$ be the Dirichlet coefficients of $\zeta^t = \exp(t\log\zeta)$, so that $d_t$ is multiplicative with $d_t(p^k) = \binom{t + k - 1}{k}$. For $t > 0$, $X_t$ takes values in $\{\log m : m \ge 1\}$ and $\mathbb{P}(X_t = \log m) = d_t(m)\,m^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)^t$.
results.label: prop:10dsublaw

results.name: First passage law of the zeta subordinator with drift, a ballot formula in generalized divisor functions
results.summary: When a linear drift minus the zeta subordinator first passes above a level, the passage time is fixed by a random positive integer, the exponential of the subordinator at that time, whose law is an explicit ballot formula in generalized divisor functions, a Lagrange inversion for Dirichlet series.
results.statement: Let $\sigma > 1$, $c > 0$ and $x > 0$. Let $X$ be the compound Poisson subordinator with L\'evy measure $\sum_{n \ge 2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^\sigma\log n}\,\delta_{\log n}$, where $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function, so that $\mathbb{E}\, e^{-\lambda X_t} = (\zeta(\sigma + \lambda)/\zeta(\sigma))^t$, and let $d_t(m)$ be the Dirichlet coefficients of $\zeta^t$. Let $Z_t = t/c - X_t$, with Laplace exponent $\psi(\lambda) = \lambda/c + \log(\zeta(\sigma + \lambda)/\zeta(\sigma))$ and $\Phi$ the right inverse of $\psi$; let $\tau_x = \inf\{t : Z_t > x\}$ and $M_x = e^{X_{\tau_x}} \in \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$, so that $\tau_x = c(x + \log M_x)$ on $\{\tau_x < \infty\}$. For every integer $m \ge 1$, $\mathbb{P}(M_x = m) = \frac{x}{x + \log m}\cdot\frac{d_t(m)\,m^{-\sigma}}{\zeta(\sigma)^t}$ with $t = c(x + \log m)$, and $\sum_m \mathbb{P}(M_x = m)\,e^{-qc(x + \log m)} = e^{-x\Phi(q)}$ for $q \ge 0$. If $1/c \ge -\zeta'(\sigma)/\zeta(\sigma)$, then $\tau_x < \infty$ almost surely.
results.label: thm:10dballot

results.name: Hausdorff moment test for membership of completed L functions in the Patie class of van Dantzig solutions
results.summary: If a completed L function belonged to the class of van Dantzig solutions that Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar build from Bernstein gamma functions, the ratios of its central Taylor coefficients would be the values of the Laplace exponent at the integers and their second differences would form a completely monotone sequence, a necessary condition that can be tested numerically.
results.statement: Let $\Psi(u) = -\kappa + au + \tfrac12\sigma^2u^2 - \int_0^\infty\bigl(1 - e^{-ur} - ur\,\mathrm{1}_{\{r < 1\}}\bigr)\,\Pi(dr)$ be the Laplace exponent of a possibly killed spectrally negative L\'evy process, with $\kappa \ge 0$, $\sigma^2 \ge 0$ and $\int_0^\infty \min(1, r^2)\,\Pi(dr) < \infty$, the process not being the negative of a subordinator, and with $\Psi(\tfrac12) \ge 0$; put $W_\Psi(n + 1) = \Psi(1)\cdots\Psi(n)$ and $J_\Psi(t) = \sum_{n \ge 0}(-1)^n t^{2n}/W_\Psi(n + 1)$. Let $\Xi_\pi$ be the even self dual completion of an automorphic $L$ function (for example $\Xi_\pi(z) = \xi(\tfrac12 + z)$ with $\xi$ the Riemann xi function), with Taylor expansion $\Xi_\pi(z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} a_n z^{2n}$ and all $a_n > 0$, and suppose $\Xi_\pi(it)/\Xi_\pi(0) = J_\Psi(t)$ for some such $\Psi$. Then $\Psi(n) = a_{n-1}/a_n$ for $n \ge 1$, and the sequence $\delta_n = \Psi(n + 2) - 2\Psi(n + 1) + \Psi(n)$ is completely monotone in the sense of Hausdorff: $(-1)^k \Delta^k \delta_n \ge 0$ for all $k \ge 0$ and $n \ge 1$, where $\Delta\delta_n = \delta_{n+1} - \delta_n$.
results.label: prop:10dpatietest

results.name: Squarefree constant as two tilted Pólya means and a sum over the zeros of zeta
results.summary: The constant in the asymptotic formula for the sum of the reciprocals of the squarefree integers up to x is an explicit elementary constant plus a combination of two tilted means of the Pólya law of the Riemann xi function, equivalently a sum over the zeros of zeta.
results.statement: Let $\kappa$ be the constant in $\sum_{n \le x}\mu(n)^2/n = \frac{6}{\pi^2}(\log x + \kappa) + O(x^{-1/2})$, where $\mu$ is the M\"obius function. Let $\xi(s) = \tfrac12 s(s - 1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\tfrac s2)\zeta(s)$, let $T$ be the random variable with $\mathbb{E}\, e^{\theta T} = \xi(\tfrac12 + \tfrac{\theta}{2})/\xi(\tfrac12)$ for all $\theta$ (half the P\'olya variable of $\zeta$, which exists because P\'olya's kernel is positive), with density $p$, and let $\mathbb{E}_\theta$ denote expectation under the tilted law $e^{\theta t}p(t)/\mathbb{E}\, e^{\theta T}$. Index the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ as $\rho = \tfrac12 + i\gamma_\rho$ and let $\sum_\rho$ run over those with $\operatorname{Re}\gamma_\rho > 0$, with multiplicity. Then $\kappa = 2 + \log 2 - \tfrac12\log\pi - \tfrac12\gamma_{\mathrm{E}} + 2\,\mathbb{E}_1[T] - 4\,\mathbb{E}_3[T] = 2 + \log 2 - \tfrac12\log\pi - \tfrac12\gamma_{\mathrm{E}} + \sum_\rho\Bigl(\frac{4}{1 + 4\gamma_\rho^2} - \frac{24}{9 + 4\gamma_\rho^2}\Bigr)$, where $\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}$ is Euler's constant.
results.label: thm:sf:const

results.name: Riemann hypothesis as the generalized gamma convolution property of the reciprocal xi function
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2017, version 26 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
results.summary: The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the reciprocal of the Riemann xi function, centred at one half and evaluated along the square root, being the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, whose Thorin atoms are then the squared ordinates of the zeros; this is a reformulation, not a proof.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s) = \tfrac12 s(s - 1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\tfrac s2)\zeta(s)$ and write the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ as $\tfrac12 \pm i\gamma_k$, $k \ge 1$, with $\operatorname{Re}\gamma_k > 0$ and multiplicity. The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if $u\mapsto \xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12 + \sqrt{u})$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (a law on $[0,\infty)$ that is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws). Then $\frac{\xi(\frac12)}{\xi(\frac12 + \sqrt{u})} = \prod_{k \ge 1}\Bigl(1 + \frac{u}{\gamma_k^2}\Bigr)^{-1} = \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{-uY}\bigr]$ with $Y = \sum_{k \ge 1}E_k/\gamma_k^2$, the $E_k$ being independent standard exponential variables, with drift $0$ and Thorin measure $\sum_k \delta_{\gamma_k^2}$. Moreover $\mathbb{E}[Y] = 2\operatorname{Var}(T)$, where $T$ is the random variable with $\mathbb{E}\, e^{\theta T} = \xi(\tfrac12 + \tfrac{\theta}{2})/\xi(\tfrac12)$, half the P\'olya variable of $\zeta$.
results.label: prop:sf:thorin

results.name: Riemann hypothesis for a Dedekind zeta function as a generalized gamma convolution property
results.summary: For a number field whose Dedekind zeta function does not vanish at the centre, the Riemann hypothesis for that function is equivalent to the reciprocal of its completion along the square root being a generalized gamma convolution transform with Thorin atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros; this is a reformulation, not a proof.
results.statement: Let $K$ be a number field with discriminant $d_K$, $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places and Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$, and let $\xi_K(s) = s(s - 1)|d_K|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_K(s)$ with $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s) = \pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\tfrac s2)$ and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s) = 2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$. If $\zeta_K(\tfrac12) \ne 0$, then $u\mapsto \xi_K(\tfrac12)/\xi_K(\tfrac12 + \sqrt{u})$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (a law on $[0,\infty)$ that is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws) if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds for $\zeta_K$, and its Thorin measure is then $\sum_k \delta_{\gamma_k^2}$ over the positive ordinates $\gamma_k$ of the zeros of $\zeta_K$.
results.label: prop:sf:thorinK

results.name: Riemann hypothesis and the exponentially smoothed squarefree count
results.summary: The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to an error of order x to the power one quarter plus epsilon in the exponentially smoothed count of squarefree integers, and under the Riemann hypothesis with simple zeros the smoothed count has an explicit expansion over the halved zeros.
results.statement: Let $S(x) = \sum_{n \ge 1}\mu(n)^2 e^{-n/x}$, where $\mu$ is the M\"obius function. The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if $S(x) = 6x/\pi^2 + O_\varepsilon(x^{1/4 + \varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$. Under the Riemann hypothesis with simple zeros, writing the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane as $\rho_k = \tfrac12 + i\gamma_k$ and summing over $\gamma_k < T_\nu$ for a suitable sequence $T_\nu \to \infty$, $S(x) = \frac{6}{\pi^2}x + 1 + 2\operatorname{Re}\sum_k \frac{\Gamma(\rho_k/2)\,\zeta(\rho_k/2)}{2\,\zeta'(\rho_k)}\,x^{\rho_k/2} - \frac{\zeta(-1)}{2\zeta'(-2)}\,\frac{\log x}{x} + O\Bigl(\frac{1}{x}\Bigr)$.
results.label: thm:sf:smooth

results.name: Riemann hypothesis and the mean square of the squarefree error
results.summary: The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to a bound of order X to the power three halves plus epsilon for the integral, over the dyadic interval from X to 2X, of the square of the error term in the count of squarefree integers.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(x) = \sum_{n \le x}\mu(n)^2 - 6x/\pi^2$, where $\mu$ is the M\"obius function. The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if $\int_X^{2X}\Delta(x)^2\,dx \ll_\varepsilon X^{3/2 + \varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.
results.label: thm:sf:meansq

results.name: Gamma smoothed squarefree count under the Riemann hypothesis, uniformly in the shape
results.summary: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, averaging the squarefree count over a Gamma law of shape n at least one and mean x gives an error of order x to the one quarter times n to the one eighth, up to epsilon powers, uniformly in n.
results.statement: Let $Q(x) = \sum_{n \le x}\mu(n)^2$ count the squarefree integers up to $x$, and let $G_{n,x}$ have the Gamma($n$) law with mean $x$. Under the Riemann hypothesis, uniformly in $n \ge 1$, $\mathbb{E}\,Q(G_{n,x}) = \frac{6}{\pi^2}x + O_\varepsilon\bigl(x^{1/4 + \varepsilon}n^{1/8 + \varepsilon}\bigr)$.
results.label: prop:sf:gamman

results.name: Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree error as an average of the Mertens function
results.summary: After smoothing by a Gamma(2) law the error in the count of squarefree integers is exactly minus one half of the mean of the Mertens function at a random point with an explicit density, and that density is twice the gap between a continuous and an integer rate mixture of Gamma(2) densities.
results.statement: Let $Q(x) = \sum_{n \le x}\mu(n)^2$, let $M(t) = \sum_{d \le t}\mu(d)$ be the Mertens function, and for $X > 0$ let $G_X$ have the Gamma(2) density $\lambda^2 t e^{-\lambda t}$ with $\lambda = 2/X$, so that $\mathbb{E}\,G_X = X$. Put $g(\theta) = \frac{2}{\theta} - \frac{1}{e^\theta - 1} - \frac{\theta}{4\sinh^2(\theta/2)}$. The function $f_V(v) = -2g'(v) = \frac{4}{v^2} - \frac{v\cosh(v/2)}{2\sinh^3(v/2)}$, $v > 0$, is a probability density with $\mathbb{P}(V \ge v) = 2g(v)$ and $\mathbb{E}[V^s] = -2\Gamma(s + 2)\zeta(s)$ for $0 < \operatorname{Re}s < 1$, and, with $V$ of density $f_V$, $\mathbb{E}\,Q(G_X) = \frac{6}{\pi^2}X - \frac12\,\mathbb{E}\Bigl[M\bigl(\sqrt{XV/2}\bigr)\Bigr]$. Moreover, with $\gamma_{2,\lambda}(v) = \lambda^2 v e^{-\lambda v}$, $f_V(v) = 2\Bigl(\int_0^\infty \gamma_{2,\lambda}(v)\,d\lambda - \sum_{m \ge 1}\gamma_{2,m}(v)\Bigr)$.
results.label: thm:sf:mertens

results.name: Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree count, the Riemann hypothesis and its explicit expansion
results.summary: The Gamma(2) smoothed count of squarefree integers has an error smaller than the square root of X unconditionally, the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to an error of order X to the one quarter plus epsilon, and under the Riemann hypothesis with simple zeros the smoothed count has an explicit expansion over the halved zeros.
results.statement: Let $Q(x) = \sum_{n \le x}\mu(n)^2$, where $\mu$ is the M\"obius function, and let $G_X$ have the Gamma(2) law with mean $X$ (density $\lambda^2 t e^{-\lambda t}$ with $\lambda = 2/X$). (i) Unconditionally $\mathbb{E}\,Q(G_X) = 6X/\pi^2 + o(X^{1/2})$. (ii) The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if $\mathbb{E}\,Q(G_X) = 6X/\pi^2 + O_\varepsilon(X^{1/4 + \varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$. (iii) Under the Riemann hypothesis with simple zeros, writing the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane as $\rho_k = \tfrac12 + i\gamma_k$ and summing over $\gamma_k < T_\nu$ for a suitable sequence $T_\nu \to \infty$, $\mathbb{E}\,Q(G_X) = \frac{6}{\pi^2}X + 1 + 2\operatorname{Re}\sum_k \Bigl(1 + \frac{\rho_k}{2}\Bigr)\frac{\Gamma(\rho_k/2)\,\zeta(\rho_k/2)}{2\,\zeta'(\rho_k)}\Bigl(\frac{X}{2}\Bigr)^{\rho_k/2} - \frac{\pi^2}{3\zeta(3)\,X} + O\Bigl(\frac{1}{X^2}\Bigr)$.
results.label: cor:sf:mertens

results.summary: Smoothing the count of squarefree integers by a Gamma law of shape nu turns its error into an average of the Mertens function with positive weights exactly when nu is at most 2, so Gamma(2) is the largest shape for which this holds.

results.name: Constant of the logarithmic squarefree ideal sum over a number field as a sum over Dedekind zeros
results.summary: Over any number field, the constant in the asymptotic formula for the sum of the reciprocal norms of the squarefree ideals is an explicit term in the discriminant and the signature plus a sum over the zeros of the Dedekind zeta function.
results.statement: Let $K$ be a number field with discriminant $d_K$, $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places, Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$ with residue $c_K$ at $s = 1$, and Euler Kronecker constant $\gamma_K$, defined by $\zeta_K(s) = c_K/(s - 1) + c_K\gamma_K + O(s - 1)$. Let $\kappa_K = \gamma_K - 2\zeta_K'(2)/\zeta_K(2)$, the constant in $\sum_{N(\mathfrak a) \le x}\mu^2(\mathfrak a)/N(\mathfrak a) = \frac{c_K}{\zeta_K(2)}(\log x + \kappa_K) + o(1)$, where $\mathfrak a$ runs over the nonzero ideals of the ring of integers and $\mu^2(\mathfrak a)$ is $1$ for squarefree ideals and $0$ otherwise. With the zeros of $\zeta_K$ in the critical strip written $\tfrac12 + i\gamma_\rho$ and summed over all of them with multiplicity, $\kappa_K = A_K + \sum_\rho\Bigl(\frac{2}{1 + 4\gamma_\rho^2} - \frac{12}{9 + 4\gamma_\rho^2}\Bigr)$, where $A_K = 2 + \tfrac12\log|d_K| + r_1\bigl(\log 2 - \tfrac12\log\pi - \tfrac12\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}\bigr) + r_2\bigl(2 - \gamma_{\mathrm{E}} - \log 2\pi\bigr)$ and $\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}$ is Euler's constant.
results.label: thm:sf:constK

results.name: Brownian subordination of the reciprocal xi function off the critical line
results.summary: With its basepoint at or to the right of the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function in the critical strip, the reciprocal xi function along the square root is, unconditionally, the Laplace transform of a sum over pairs of conjugate zeros of an exponential time plus a Brownian first passage time, so each Thorin atom is smeared by its own Brownian clock.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s) = \tfrac12 s(s - 1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\tfrac s2)\zeta(s)$, let $\beta^* = \sup\{\operatorname{Re}\rho : \zeta(\rho) = 0,\ 0 < \operatorname{Re}\rho < 1\}$, and for $\sigma \ge \tfrac12$ let $\varphi_\sigma(u) = \xi(\sigma)/\xi(\sigma + \sqrt{u})$ for $u \in \mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty, 0]$, with the principal root. For $\sigma \ge \beta^*$, $\varphi_\sigma(u) = \mathbb{E}[e^{-uY_\sigma}]$ with $Y_\sigma = \sum_{\rho = \beta + it_\rho,\ t_\rho > 0}\Bigl(\frac{E_\rho}{c_\rho} + T_\rho\Bigr)$ and $c_\rho = (\sigma - \beta)^2 + t_\rho^2$, the sum running over the nontrivial zeros $\rho = \beta + it_\rho$ of $\zeta$ with $t_\rho > 0$, counted with multiplicity, where the $E_\rho$ are independent standard exponential variables and, given $E_\rho$, $T_\rho$ is the first passage time of an independent standard Brownian motion to the level $\sqrt{2}(\sigma - \beta)E_\rho/c_\rho$.
results.label: cor:sf:sub

results.name: Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic Dedekind zeta function and its positivity for small discriminants
results.summary: The completed Dedekind zeta function of an imaginary quadratic field is the Fourier transform of an explicit even, doubly exponentially decaying kernel built from ideal counts, and this kernel is positive for the four fields whose discriminant is smaller than pi squared in absolute value.
results.statement: Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant $d$, let $\chi_d$ be its Kronecker character, $a_n = \sum_{m \mid n}\chi_d(m)$ the number of ideals of norm $n$, $\lambda_n = 2\pi n/\sqrt{|d|}$, $F(k) = k(k - 2)e^{-k}$, $\Lambda_K(s) = (\sqrt{|d|}/2\pi)^s\Gamma(s)\zeta_K(s)$ and $\xi_K(s) = 2s(s - 1)\Lambda_K(s)$. Let $H_K(x) = \sum_{n \ge 1}a_n F(\lambda_n x)$ and $\Phi_K(v) = e^{v/2}H_K(e^v)$. Then $\Phi_K$ is even, decays doubly exponentially, and $\xi_K(\tfrac12 + iz) = 2\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_K(v)e^{izv}\,dv$. If $|d| < \pi^2$, that is $d \in \{-3, -4, -7, -8\}$, then $\Phi_K > 0$; consequently $\xi_K(\tfrac12 + w)/\xi_K(\tfrac12)$ is the moment generating function of a probability density, and $\zeta_K(\tfrac12) < 0$.
results.label: thm:sf:kernel

results.name: Pólya kernels of imaginary quadratic fields in which 2 and 3 are inert take negative values
results.summary: For every imaginary quadratic field in which both 2 and 3 are inert, a set of infinitely many fields that includes those with discriminants -19, -43, -67 and -163, the Pólya kernel of the Dedekind zeta function takes negative values.
results.statement: Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant $d$, let $a_n$ be the number of ideals of $K$ of norm $n$, $F(k) = k(k - 2)e^{-k}$, and let $\Phi_K(v) = e^{v/2}\sum_{n \ge 1}a_n F\bigl(2\pi n e^v/\sqrt{|d|}\bigr)$ be the P\'olya kernel of $K$, for which $\xi_K(\tfrac12 + iz) = 2\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_K(v)e^{izv}\,dv$ with $\xi_K(s) = 2s(s - 1)(\sqrt{|d|}/2\pi)^s\Gamma(s)\zeta_K(s)$. If $2$ and $3$ are both inert in $K$, then $\Phi_K$ takes negative values. This holds for infinitely many fields, among them $d = -19, -43, -67, -163$.
results.label: thm:sf:inert

results.name: How often the Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field is positive
results.summary: The book asks whether a positive proportion of imaginary quadratic fields have a positive Pólya kernel, and whether finitely many splitting conditions on small primes force positivity.
results.statement: For an imaginary quadratic field $K$ of discriminant $d$, let $a_n$ be the number of ideals of $K$ of norm $n$, $F(k) = k(k - 2)e^{-k}$, and $\Phi_K(v) = e^{v/2}\sum_{n \ge 1}a_n F\bigl(2\pi n e^v/\sqrt{|d|}\bigr)$, the P\'olya kernel of $K$. Does the set of negative fundamental discriminants $d$ with $\Phi_K > 0$ have positive lower density? Is there a finite set of splitting conditions on small primes under which $\Phi_K > 0$ for every $d$ that satisfies them, a positive counterpart of the theorem that $\Phi_K$ takes negative values whenever $2$ and $3$ are both inert in $K$?
results.label: op:sfdensity

results.name: Lévy form of the completed Dirichlet beta function
results.summary: To the right of the critical strip the logarithm of the completed Dirichlet beta function has a Lévy Khintchine form whose Lévy measure is signed, a positive archimedean density plus prime atoms carrying the signs of the character modulo 4.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$ its completed function and $c_\alpha=\Lambda'(\alpha)/\Lambda(\alpha)$. For $\alpha>1$ and $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$, \[\log\frac{\Lambda(\alpha+s)}{\Lambda(\alpha)}-c_\alpha s=\int_0^\infty\bigl(e^{-sx}-1+sx\bigr)e^{-\alpha x}\,\frac{\mu_\beta(dx)}{x},\] with the signed measure \[\mu_\beta(dx)=\frac{dx}{2\sinh x}+\sum_{n\ge2}\chi_{-4}(n)\,\Lambda(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx),\] where $\Lambda(n)$ in the sum is the von Mangoldt function and $\delta_{\log n}$ is the unit mass at $\log n$.
results.label: beta:thm:levy

results.name: Signed sine squared lemma for Thorin densities
results.summary: The sine squared lemma of Polson (2018), with a first step of Roynette and Yor, which turns the Lévy measure of a function into the Thorin density of its shifted reciprocal, extends linearly to signed Lévy measures once the positivity conclusion is dropped.
results.statement: Let $f$ be analytic and nonvanishing near $[\alpha,\infty)$, let $c=f'(\alpha)/f(\alpha)$, and suppose that for $s\ge0$ \[\log\frac{f(\alpha+s)}{f(\alpha)}-cs=\int_0^\infty\bigl(e^{-sx}-1+sx\bigr)\,m(dx)\] for a signed measure $m$ with $\int\min(x,x^2)\,|m|(dx)<\infty$. Put \[T(y)=\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt y}\Bigl[c+\int_0^\infty2\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{x\sqrt y}{2}\Bigr)x\,m(dx)\Bigr],\qquad y>0.\] Then for every $v>0$, \[\frac{f(\alpha)}{f(\alpha+\sqrt v)}=\exp\Bigl(-\int_0^\infty\log\Bigl(1+\frac vy\Bigr)T(y)\,dy\Bigr).\] The map $m\mapsto T$ is linear and positivity preserving, and $c\ge0$ contributes the positive stable part $c/(2\pi\sqrt y)$.
results.label: beta:lem:2sin2

results.name: Thorin density of the reciprocal completed Dirichlet beta function
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, arXiv:1804.10043.
results.summary: To the right of the critical strip the shifted reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet beta function has an explicit Thorin representation whose density is the real part of the logarithmic derivative on a vertical line divided by an explicit factor.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, $c_\alpha=\Lambda'(\alpha)/\Lambda(\alpha)$, $\psi$ the digamma function, and $\mu_\beta(dx)=dx/(2\sinh x)+\sum_{n\ge2}\chi_{-4}(n)\Lambda(n)\delta_{\log n}(dx)$, where $\Lambda(n)$ in sums over integers $n$ is the von Mangoldt function and $\delta_{\log n}$ is the unit mass at $\log n$. For $\alpha>1$ and $v>0$, \[\frac{\Lambda(\alpha)}{\Lambda(\alpha+\sqrt v)}=\exp\Bigl(-\int_0^\infty\log\Bigl(1+\frac vy\Bigr)T_\alpha(y)\,dy\Bigr),\] where \[T_\alpha(y)=\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt y}\Bigl[c_\alpha+\int_0^\infty2\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{x\sqrt y}{2}\Bigr)e^{-\alpha x}\mu_\beta(dx)\Bigr]=\frac{c_\alpha+G_\alpha(\sqrt y)+P_\alpha(\sqrt y)}{2\pi\sqrt y}=\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt y}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}\bigl(\alpha+i\sqrt y\bigr),\] with the archimedean and prime parts $G_\alpha(t)=\frac12\bigl[\operatorname{Re}\psi\bigl(\frac{\alpha+1+it}{2}\bigr)-\psi\bigl(\frac{\alpha+1}{2}\bigr)\bigr]\ge0$ and $P_\alpha(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\chi_{-4}(n)\Lambda(n)n^{-\alpha}\bigl(1-\cos(t\log n)\bigr)$. Equivalently, \[\log\frac{\Lambda(\alpha+\sqrt v)}{\Lambda(\alpha)}=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\log\Bigl(1+\frac{v}{t^2}\Bigr)\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+it)\,dt.\]
results.label: beta:thm:thorin

results.name: GGC property of the shifted reciprocal Dirichlet beta function for basepoints at least one
results.summary: Unconditionally, for every basepoint at least one, the shifted reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet beta function is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and a positive Thorin density; for basepoints above one this is a case of a theorem of Polson (2018).
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, and $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\bigl(-av-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+v/t)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)$, with drift $a\ge0$ and a positive measure $\tau$, its Thorin measure. For every $\alpha\ge1$ there is a GGC random variable $H^\beta_\alpha\ge0$, with drift zero and Thorin density $T_\alpha>0$, such that \[\frac{\Lambda(\alpha)}{\Lambda(\alpha+\sqrt v)}=\mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{-vH^\beta_\alpha}\bigr],\qquad v>0.\] In particular $\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2}\big/\Lambda(1+\sqrt v)$ is a GGC Laplace transform.
results.label: beta:thm:uncond

results.name: Termwise Thorin positivity threshold for the Dirichlet beta function
results.summary: Bounding the prime atoms of the Dirichlet beta function by their absolute values proves positivity of its Thorin density at every height only for basepoints above an explicit threshold close to 2.28.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$, $\psi$ the digamma function, \[A_\alpha(t)=\tfrac12\log\frac4\pi+\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\Bigl(\frac{\alpha+1+it}{2}\Bigr),\qquad S(\alpha)=\sum_{n\text{ odd}}\Lambda(n)n^{-\alpha}=-\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha)-\frac{\log2}{2^\alpha-1},\] with $\Lambda(n)$ the von Mangoldt function, so that $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+it)=A_\alpha(t)+\operatorname{Re}\frac{\beta'}{\beta}(\alpha+it)$ and $\bigl|\frac{\beta'}{\beta}(\alpha+it)\bigr|\le S(\alpha)$ for $\alpha>1$. Then $A_\alpha(t)$ increases in $t$, $A_\alpha(0)$ increases in $\alpha$, and $S(\alpha)$ decreases. Let $\alpha_c$ be the root of $A_\alpha(0)=S(\alpha)$, numerically $\alpha_c=2.28231064$. For $\alpha\ge\alpha_c$ the bound $A_\alpha(t)-S(\alpha)$ proves $T_\alpha(t^2)>0$ for all $t>0$; for $1<\alpha<\alpha_c$ it fails near $t=0$, although $T_\alpha>0$ for every $\alpha\ge1$ by the unconditional generalized gamma convolution property.
results.label: beta:prop:crude

results.name: GRH for the Dirichlet beta function as Thorin positivity
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2018, version 9 of 2026), Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, arXiv:1804.10043.
