results.summary: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet beta function is equivalent to the generalized gamma convolution property of its shifted reciprocals at every basepoint right of the critical line, and to positivity of the real part of its logarithmic derivative there (the criterion of Hinkkanen and Lagarias), a reformulation and not a proof.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, and $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\bigl(-av-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+v/t)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)$, with $a\ge0$ and a positive measure $\tau$, its Thorin measure. The following are equivalent. (i) The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$, that every zero of $\Lambda$ lies on $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$. (ii) For every $\alpha>\frac12$, $v\mapsto\Lambda(\alpha)/\Lambda(\alpha+\sqrt v)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (iii) $\operatorname{Re}(\Lambda'/\Lambda)(s)>0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac12$. In this case the Thorin measures $T_\alpha(y)\,dy$ converge vaguely on $(0,\infty)$, as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$, to $\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$, the sum over the positive ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros of $\Lambda$ counted with multiplicity, which is the Thorin measure of $\Lambda(\frac12)/\Lambda(\frac12+\sqrt v)$. The equivalence of (i) and (iii) is the criterion of Hinkkanen (1997) and Lagarias (1999) for $\chi_{-4}$.
results.label: beta:thm:grh

results.name: Thorin domination in the Gaussian field
results.summary: Through the factorisation of the Dedekind zeta function of the Gaussian field, the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is that of the Gaussian field minus that of the Riemann zeta function, and the generalized Riemann hypothesis for beta is equivalent to the first dominating the second on every line right of the critical line.
results.statement: Let $K=\mathbb{Q}(i)$ with Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, $\xi_K(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s}\Gamma(s)\zeta_K(s)$, $\chi_{-4}$ the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$ and $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, so that $\Lambda=2\sqrt\pi\,\xi_K/\xi$. For $f\in\{\Lambda,\xi_K,\xi\}$ the function $T^f_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}{f}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$, $y>0$, is the Thorin density of $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt v)$ whenever this function is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution; write $T^\beta_\alpha$, $T^K_\alpha$, $T^\xi_\alpha$ for $f=\Lambda,\xi_K,\xi$. Then $T^\beta_\alpha=T^K_\alpha-T^\xi_\alpha$. For $\alpha\ge1$ all three densities are positive and there are independent random variables $H^\xi_\alpha$ and $H^\beta_\alpha$, whose laws are generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) with Laplace transforms $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt v)$ and $\Lambda(\alpha)/\Lambda(\alpha+\sqrt v)$, with $H^K_\alpha\overset{d}{=}H^\xi_\alpha+H^\beta_\alpha$, where $H^K_\alpha$ is the GGC variable with Laplace transform $\xi_K(\alpha)/\xi_K(\alpha+\sqrt v)$. The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$ holds if and only if $T^K_\alpha\ge T^\xi_\alpha$ for every $\alpha>\frac12$; if Thorin's condition holds for $\xi$ (that $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt v)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC), this says that $H^\xi_\alpha$ is a GGC factor of $H^K_\alpha$ for every $\alpha>\frac12$.
results.label: beta:thm:dom

results.name: Kronecker sharpness of termwise Thorin bounds for the Dirichlet beta function
results.summary: By Kronecker's theorem, bounds on the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function that use only the sizes of the prime atoms are sharp, so they prove positivity on a line only above a height that grows exponentially as the basepoint approaches one.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$, $A_\alpha(t)=\frac12\log\frac4\pi+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\bigl(\frac{\alpha+1+it}{2}\bigr)$ with $\psi$ the digamma function, and $S(\alpha)=\sum_{n\text{ odd}}\Lambda(n)n^{-\alpha}=-\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha)-\frac{\log2}{2^\alpha-1}$ with $\Lambda(n)$ the von Mangoldt function. For $\alpha>1$ and every $T>0$, \[\inf_{t\ge T}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\beta'}{\beta}(\alpha+it)=-S(\alpha).\] Hence a bound on the prime part that uses only $|\chi_{-4}(p)|$ proves $T_\alpha(t^2)>0$ exactly for $t>t_0(\alpha)$, where $A_\alpha(t_0)=S(\alpha)$ (and $t_0=0$ for $\alpha\ge\alpha_c$, where $\alpha_c=2.28231064$ is the root of $A_\alpha(0)=S(\alpha)$), and $\log t_0(\alpha)=2/(\alpha-1)+O(1)$ as $\alpha\downarrow1$.
results.label: beta:prop:kron

results.name: Unconditional Thorin positivity of the Dirichlet beta function near the real axis
results.summary: On every line right of the critical line the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is positive near the origin, unconditionally, because the logarithm of the completed function is the cumulant generating function of a symmetric law with a positive density.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, $c_\alpha=\Lambda'(\alpha)/\Lambda(\alpha)$ and $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$. For every $\alpha>\frac12$, unconditionally, $c_\alpha>0$, and hence $T_\alpha(y)\sim c_\alpha/(2\pi\sqrt y)>0$ as $y\downarrow0$.
results.label: beta:thm:realaxis

results.name: Localisation of negative Thorin density for the Dirichlet beta function below the verified height
results.summary: Read as a statement on Thorin densities, the grouping of zeros of Levinson and Montgomery shows that the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is positive on every line right of the critical line up to half a unit below the height to which its generalized Riemann hypothesis has been verified, and that a failure of the hypothesis could make it negative only in windows of half width less than one half around ordinates of zeros off the line.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$, and $H_0=2.5\times10^{7}$ the height to which the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$ has been verified (Platt 2016, by a rigorous computation). For every $\alpha>\frac12$, $T_\alpha(y)>0$ for $0<\sqrt y<H_0-\frac12$. If the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$ fails, the set where $T_\alpha<0$ lies in windows of half width less than $\frac12$ in $\sqrt y$, centred at ordinates of zeros with real part exceeding $\alpha$, all above $H_0-\frac12$. The same holds for $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ below the height $3\times10^{12}$ to which the Riemann hypothesis has been verified (Platt and Trudgian 2021).
results.label: beta:cor:height

results.name: Comparison lemma for pairs of zeros with sharp constant one plus root two
results.summary: An elementary lemma with a sharp constant on how the contribution of a symmetric pair of zeros to the real part of a logarithmic derivative, divided by the distance to the critical line, varies with that distance.
results.statement: For $a>0$, $0\le B<\frac12$ and real $u$ let \[Q_B(a,u)=\frac{a-B}{(a-B)^2+u^2}+\frac{a+B}{(a+B)^2+u^2},\] the contribution of a pair of zeros $\frac12\pm B+i\gamma$ of a completed $L$ function $\Lambda$ to $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\frac12+a+it)$, where $u=t-\gamma$. If $|u|\ge(1+\sqrt2)B$, then $a\mapsto Q_B(a,u)/a$ is nonincreasing on $a>0$. The constant $1+\sqrt2$ is sharp.
results.label: beta:lem:comp

results.name: Comparison of the logarithmic derivative across vertical lines
results.summary: At heights not too close to a zero off the critical line, and so unconditionally at heights up to 1.21 below the height to which the generalized Riemann hypothesis for beta has been verified, the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function divided by the distance to the critical line does not increase as the line moves right, and the same holds for the Riemann xi function and for real primitive characters.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$ and $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$. Fix $t$, and suppose every zero $\frac12+B+i\gamma$ of $\Lambda$ with $B>0$ satisfies $|t-\gamma|\ge(1+\sqrt2)B$. Then \[\alpha\mapsto\frac{1}{\alpha-\frac12}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+it)\quad\text{is nonincreasing on }\alpha>\tfrac12.\] The hypothesis holds for every $t$ under the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$, and unconditionally when $t$ is at distance at least $(1+\sqrt2)/2=1.2071$ from every off line ordinate, in particular for $|t|\le H_0-1.2071$, where $H_0=2.5\times10^{7}$ is the height to which the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$ has been verified (Platt 2016, by a rigorous computation). The same holds for $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ and for every completed $L$ function of a real primitive Dirichlet character.
results.label: beta:thm:comp

results.name: Explicit lower bound for the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function
results.summary: At heights not too close to a zero off the critical line, the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function on lines right of the critical line has an explicit lower bound that grows like a multiple of the logarithm of the height.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$, $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$, $A_\alpha(t)=\frac12\log\frac4\pi+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\bigl(\frac{\alpha+1+it}{2}\bigr)$ with $\psi$ the digamma function, and $S(\alpha)=-\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha)-\frac{\log2}{2^\alpha-1}$. Fix $t$ and suppose every zero $\frac12+B+i\gamma$ of $\Lambda$ with $B>0$ satisfies $|t-\gamma|\ge(1+\sqrt2)B$. Then for $\delta>0$ and $\frac12<\alpha\le1+\delta$, \[2\pi t\,T_\alpha(t^2)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+it)\ge\frac{\alpha-\frac12}{\frac12+\delta}\Bigl(A_{1+\delta}(t)-S(1+\delta)\Bigr),\] and the right side is $\frac{\alpha-\frac12}{1+2\delta}\log t+O(1)$ as $t\to\infty$.
results.label: beta:cor:lower

results.name: Minimum on the real axis of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function
results.summary: On each line right of the critical line with real part at most 3.15, the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function is smallest on the real axis, unconditionally at heights up to 1.21 below the height to which its generalized Riemann hypothesis has been verified, and that hypothesis is equivalent to this minimum property at every height on the lines up to real part one.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$ its completed function, $c_\alpha=\Lambda'(\alpha)/\Lambda(\alpha)$, $V=(\log\Lambda)''(\frac12)=0.156030$, $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$, and $H_0=2.5\times10^{7}$ the height to which the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$ has been verified (Platt 2016, by a rigorous computation). (i) For every $\alpha>\frac12$, unconditionally, $0<c_\alpha\le(\alpha-\frac12)V$. (ii) For $\frac12<\alpha\le3.15$, unconditionally, $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+it)>c_\alpha$ for $0<|t|\le H_0-1.2071$. (iii) The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$ holds if and only if, for every $\alpha\in(\frac12,1]$, the minimum over $t\in\mathbb{R}$ of $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+it)$ is $c_\alpha$, attained only at $t=0$; equivalently, $T_\alpha(y)>c_\alpha/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for all $y>0$, so the Thorin density dominates its own stable part, that is, the density $\bigl(\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)-c_\alpha\bigr)/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ that remains when the stable part $c_\alpha/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ is removed is positive. For the completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\chi)$ alone with $\chi$ a complex character the analogue can fail (Polson, Riemann, Thorin, van Dantzig pairs, Wald couples and Hadamard factorisation, Remark 31).
results.label: beta:thm:minall

results.name: Thorin measure of the Dirichlet beta function as its argument
results.summary: Extending a theorem of Polson (2017) for the Riemann xi function, the cumulative Thorin measure of the shifted completed Dirichlet beta function on a zero free vertical line equals its argument divided by pi, which gives a Riemann von Mangoldt type asymptotic and, under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the zero counting function in the limit at the critical line.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$ and $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$. Let $\alpha>\frac12$ with $\Lambda$ zero free on $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$, and let $\tau_\alpha(dy)=T_\alpha(y)\,dy$, the Thorin measure of $\Lambda(\alpha)/\Lambda(\alpha+\sqrt v)$ when every zero of $\Lambda$ has real part less than $\alpha$, and a signed measure in general. Then \[\tau_\alpha\bigl((0,t^2]\bigr)=\frac1\pi\arg\Lambda(\alpha+it),\] the argument being continuous along $[\alpha,\alpha+it]$ and zero at $\alpha$. As $t\to\infty$, \[\tau_\alpha\bigl((0,t^2]\bigr)=\frac{t}{2\pi}\log\frac{2t}{\pi e}+\frac\alpha4+\frac1\pi\arg\beta(\alpha+it)+O(t^{-1}),\] and under the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$, $\tau_\alpha((0,t^2])\to N(t)$ as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$, where $N(t)$ counts the zeros with ordinate $0<\gamma\le t$, with half weight at an ordinate.
results.label: beta:thm:arg

results.name: GRH for the Dirichlet beta function as a monotone argument
results.summary: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet beta function is equivalent to the argument of its completed function being nondecreasing along every zero free vertical line right of the critical line (for the Riemann xi function, part of a theorem of Polson 2017), a reformulation and not a proof.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$ and $T_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$ for $y>0$. The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$ holds if and only if $t\mapsto\arg\Lambda(\alpha+it)$ is nondecreasing on every line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha>\frac12$ on which $\Lambda$ has no zero. The argument decreases exactly where $T_\alpha$ is negative, and that set is contained in a union of intervals of half width less than $\frac12$ centred at ordinates of zeros with real part exceeding $\alpha$.
results.label: beta:cor:argmono

results.name: Eta cube kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not completely monotone
results.summary: Neither the one sided Pólya kernel of the Dirichlet beta function, divided by its variable, nor the cube of the eta function on the imaginary axis is completely monotone, so the kernel is not a positive mixture of gamma densities of shape two.
results.statement: Let $\eta$ be the Dedekind eta function and $\Phi_\beta(u)=e^{3u/2}\eta(ie^{2u})^3$, the even, strictly positive kernel with $\Lambda(\frac12+w)=\sqrt\pi\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{wu}\Phi_\beta(u)\,du$ for $w\in\mathbb{C}$, where $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)$ is the completed Dirichlet beta function, $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$ with $\chi_{-4}$ the nontrivial character modulo $4$. Neither $\Phi_\beta(u)/u$ on $u>0$ nor $\eta(ix)^3$ on $x>0$ is completely monotone; in particular $\Phi_\beta1_{\{u>0\}}$ is not a positive mixture of $\Gamma(2)$ densities.
results.label: beta:prop:nocm

results.name: Thorin domination, localisation and comparison for real primitive characters
results.summary: The Thorin decomposition through the quadratic field, the generalized gamma convolution property for basepoints at least one (above one a theorem of Polson 2018), the domination criterion for the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the localisation of negative density by the grouping of zeros of Levinson and Montgomery, and the comparison across vertical lines extend from the Dirichlet beta function to every real primitive character, as does positivity near the real axis when the theta kernel of the character is positive.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a real primitive Dirichlet character of conductor $q$ and parity $\mathfrak a\in\{0,1\}$, $\chi(-1)=(-1)^{\mathfrak a}$, with quadratic field $K$ of discriminant $d_K$ and Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$; let $\Lambda_\chi(s)=(q/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+\mathfrak a}{2}\bigr)L(s,\chi)$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, and $\xi_K(s)=\frac12s(s-1)|d_K|^{s/2}(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)\zeta_K(s)$ for imaginary $K$, $\xi_K(s)=\frac12s(s-1)|d_K|^{s/2}\pi^{-s}\Gamma(\frac s2)^2\zeta_K(s)$ for real $K$. For $f\in\{\Lambda_\chi,\xi_K,\xi\}$ let $T^f_\alpha(y)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}{f}(\alpha+i\sqrt y)\big/(2\pi\sqrt y)$, $y>0$. Then $T^{\Lambda_\chi}_\alpha=T^{\xi_K}_\alpha-T^{\xi}_\alpha$; the reciprocal $\Lambda_\chi(\alpha)/\Lambda_\chi(\alpha+\sqrt v)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution for $\alpha\ge1$; the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $\chi$ is equivalent to $T^{\xi_K}_\alpha\ge T^{\xi}_\alpha$ for every $\alpha>\frac12$; for $\alpha>\frac12$ and real $t$, $T^{\Lambda_\chi}_\alpha(t^2)>0$ unless some zero $b+i\gamma$ of $\Lambda_\chi$ with $b>\alpha$ satisfies $|t-\gamma|^2<(b-\frac12)^2-(\alpha-\frac12)^2<\frac14$; $\alpha\mapsto(\alpha-\frac12)^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda_\chi'}{\Lambda_\chi}(\alpha+it)$ is nonincreasing on $\alpha>\frac12$ whenever every zero $\frac12+B+i\gamma$ of $\Lambda_\chi$ with $B>0$ satisfies $|t-\gamma|\ge(1+\sqrt2)B$; and, when the theta kernel of $\chi$ is positive, $c_\alpha=\Lambda_\chi'(\alpha)/\Lambda_\chi(\alpha)>0$ for every $\alpha>\frac12$, and hence $T^{\Lambda_\chi}_\alpha(y)\sim c_\alpha/(2\pi\sqrt y)>0$ as $y\downarrow0$.
results.label: beta:thm:realchar

results.name: Coupling of the Thorin variables of the Gaussian field below basepoint one
results.summary: Asks for a construction from the Gaussian primes of the splitting of the Thorin variable of the Gaussian field into Riemann zeta and Dirichlet beta parts that could survive to the left of basepoint one, using the phases of the prime atoms.
results.statement: Let $K=\mathbb{Q}(i)$ with Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, $\xi_K(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s}\Gamma(s)\zeta_K(s)$, $\chi_{-4}$ the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$ and $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$. For $\alpha\ge1$ there are independent random variables $H^\xi_\alpha$ and $H^\beta_\alpha$, with generalized gamma convolution laws and Laplace transforms $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt v)$ and $\Lambda(\alpha)/\Lambda(\alpha+\sqrt v)$, whose sum has the law of the variable $H^K_\alpha$ with Laplace transform $\xi_K(\alpha)/\xi_K(\alpha+\sqrt v)$. Construct this coupling $H^K_\alpha\overset{d}{=}H^\xi_\alpha+H^\beta_\alpha$ from the Gaussian primes in a form that could survive below $\alpha=1$. Since bounds that use only the sizes of the prime atoms are sharp, by Kronecker's theorem, the construction must use the phases $\chi_{-4}(p)p^{-it}$, not only the sizes of the atoms. A first computation is the smallest margin of $\operatorname{Re}\xi_K'/\xi_K-\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi$ on lines $\frac12<\alpha<1$.
results.label: op:betacoupling

results.name: Lower bound for the decrease of the argument in a negative window
results.summary: Asks for a lower bound on how much a hypothetical pair of zeros off the critical line makes the argument of the completed Dirichlet beta function decrease, strong enough to be contradicted by a mean value estimate.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$ and $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$ the completed Dirichlet beta function. A pair of zeros $\frac12\pm B+i\gamma$ with $\frac12+B>\alpha>\frac12$ can make $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+it)$, the derivative of $t\mapsto\arg\Lambda(\alpha+it)$, negative only in the window $|t-\gamma|^2<B^2-(\alpha-\frac12)^2$. Find a lower bound for the decrease of $\arg\Lambda(\alpha+it)$ across this window caused by the pair, in terms of $B$, $\alpha$ and the local density of zeros, that a mean value estimate for $\operatorname{Re}\Lambda'/\Lambda$ over intervals of length one could contradict.
results.label: op:betawindows

results.name: Minimum on the real axis on all lines to the right
results.summary: Asks to extend the minimum on the real axis of the logarithmic derivative of the completed Dirichlet beta function to every line right of the critical line below the verified height, and to every height on the lines with real part at least one.
results.statement: Let $\chi_{-4}$ be the nontrivial Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_{-4}(n)n^{-s}$ the completed Dirichlet beta function, and $H_0=2.5\times10^{7}$ the height to which its generalized Riemann hypothesis has been verified (Platt 2016, by a rigorous computation). It is proved that for $\frac12<\alpha\le3.15$ and $0<|t|\le H_0-1.2071$ one has $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha+it)>\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(\alpha)$, so that the minimum over these $t$ is at $t=0$. Extend this to every $\alpha>\frac12$ at these heights, either by optimising as a function of $\alpha$ the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1+\delta$ with which the comparison across vertical lines is made or by a direct argument for large $\alpha$, where the prime part is small, and to every height for $\alpha\ge1$. Numerically the minimum over $t\in[0,40]$ is at $t=0$ for $\alpha=1.5,2,3,3.15$ and $5$. For the completed Riemann zeta function the statement at every height is Lagarias's theorem under the Riemann hypothesis, and unconditionally it is known for $\alpha\ge1$ (Garunkštis).
results.label: op:betalines

results.name: Positivity on the reciprocal side from eta products
results.summary: Asks whether the complete monotonicity of the reciprocals of the eta cube and eta products passes, through incomplete Mellin transforms, to a positive representation on the reciprocal side of the completed Dirichlet beta function or of the L function of the character modulo 12.
results.statement: Let $\eta$ be the Dedekind eta function, $q=e^{-2\pi x}$, $\Lambda(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma\bigl(\frac{s+1}{2}\bigr)\beta(s)=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2}\int_0^\infty x^{(s-1)/2}\eta(ix)^3\,dx$ the completed Dirichlet beta function, where $\beta(s)=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n(2n+1)^{-s}$, and $\Lambda_{12}(s)=(12/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)L(s,\chi_{12})=\int_0^\infty x^{s/2-1}\eta(ix)\,dx$, with $\chi_{12}$ the real even primitive character modulo $12$. The functions $e^{-\pi x/4}/\eta(ix)^3=\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{-3}$ and $e^{-\pi x/12}/\eta(ix)=\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{-1}$ are completely monotone, with representing measures at the points $2\pi n$, $n\ge0$, whose weights are the coefficients of $\prod_m(1-q^m)^{-3}$ and $\prod_m(1-q^m)^{-1}$ as power series in $q$. Decide whether this positivity passes, through incomplete Mellin transforms, to a positive representation on the reciprocal side of $\Lambda$ or of $\Lambda_{12}$.
results.label: op:betarecip

results.name: Negative lobe of the signed Thorin density
results.summary: In the signed Thorin density obtained by Stieltjes inversion of the logarithmic derivative of an automorphic clock, zeros on the critical line give positive Lorentzians, a pair of zeros off the line contributes a term of total mass zero, negative near its centre when the smoothing width is below twice the ordinate times the distance of the zero from the line and tending to zero with the width, and with no real zeros positivity at every width is equivalent to all zeros lying on the line.
results.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a self dual cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, or $\zeta$, or the discriminant modular form $\Delta$, with completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ (conductor factor included), entire of order one and symmetric about its centre $c$ ($c= rac12$ in the unitary normalisation, $c=6$ for $\Delta$ in the classical one), every zero $c+\delta+i\gamma$ having $|\delta|< rac12$, and suppose $\Lambda(c,\pi)
e0$. Let $G_\pi(s)=\Lambda(c+\sqrt s,\pi)/\Lambda(c,\pi)$, so that $ rac{G_\pi'}{G_\pi}(s)=\sum_k rac{1}{s+t_k}= rac{1}{2\sqrt s} rac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(c+\sqrt s,\pi)$, where the zeros of $z\mapsto\Lambda(c+z,\pi)$ are listed in pairs $\pm i\gamma_k$ with multiplicity and $t_k=\gamma_k^2$, and for $\varepsilon>0$ and real $z$ let $u_\varepsilon(z)=- rac1\pi\operatorname{Im} rac{G_\pi'}{G_\pi}(-z+i\varepsilon)$. (i) A zero $c+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, of multiplicity $m$ contributes to $u_\varepsilon$ the Lorentzian $ rac m\pi\,\varepsilon/((z-\gamma^2)^2+\varepsilon^2)$, of mass $m$ and height $m/(\pi\varepsilon)$, centred at $\gamma^2$. (ii) A zero $c+\delta+i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$ and $\delta
e0$, together with its reflection $c-\delta+i\gamma$, contributes \[ rac1\pi\, rac{B+\varepsilon}{(z-A)^2+(B+\varepsilon)^2}- rac1\pi\, rac{B-\varepsilon}{(z-A)^2+(B-\varepsilon)^2},\qquad A=\gamma^2-\delta^2,\quad B=2\gamma|\delta|.\] For $\varepsilon<B$ this is negative exactly on $|z-A|<(B^2-\varepsilon^2)^{1/2}$ and equals $-2\varepsilon/(\pi(B^2-\varepsilon^2))$ at $z=A$; its integral over $z$ is $0$, and its absolute value is at most $2\varepsilon/(\pi(B-\varepsilon)^2)$. (iii) A real zero $c\pm eta$, $0< eta< rac12$, contributes a Lorentzian centred at $- eta^2$, positive at every $z$. (iv) If $\Lambda(\sigma,\pi)
e0$ for every real $\sigma$, then $u_\varepsilon(z)\ge0$ for all real $z$ and all $\varepsilon>0$ (away from the poles of $G_\pi'/G_\pi$) if and only if every zero lies on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=c$. If moreover no zero has ordinate in $(0, rac12]$, the same holds with $z$ restricted to $(0,\infty)$.
results.label: prop:scholzelobe

results.name: Characterising positive Pólya kernels of self dual L functions
results.summary: Asks which self dual L functions with root number one have a positive Pólya kernel, and whether at fixed degree positivity is decided by finitely many coefficients and the conductor.
results.statement: For a self dual $L$ function with completed function $\Lambda(s,\pi)$, centre $c$ and root number $+1$, let $r$ be the order of $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ at $s=c$; the Pólya kernel is the function $\Phi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ such that $\Lambda(c+z,\pi)/z^r$ is a positive multiple of $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\Phi(u)e^{zu}\,du$ (for example Pólya's kernel for $\zeta$, $e^{u/2}\eta(ie^{2u})$ for the real even character modulo $12$, with $\eta$ the Dedekind eta function, and $\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}$ for the discriminant modular form $\Delta$). Characterise the self dual $L$ functions with root number $+1$ whose Pólya kernel is positive; for a form of level one, positivity fails as soon as the form has a zero of odd order on the imaginary axis. Is positivity, at fixed degree, decided by finitely many coefficients and the conductor?
results.label: op:scholzekernel

results.name: Masking of the negative lobe of a signed Thorin density
results.summary: Asks under which conditions on the nearby zeros positivity of the signed Thorin density at a single smoothing width rules out a zero off the critical line, given that a zero on the line can mask the negative lobe.
results.statement: Let $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ be the completed $L$ function of a self dual automorphic representation $\pi$, with centre $c$ and $\Lambda(c,\pi)\ne0$, let $G_\pi(s)=\Lambda(c+\sqrt s,\pi)/\Lambda(c,\pi)$, and for $\varepsilon>0$ and real $z$ let $u_\varepsilon(z)=-\frac1\pi\operatorname{Im}\frac{G_\pi'}{G_\pi}(-z+i\varepsilon)$, the signed Thorin density. A zero $c+\delta+i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$ and $\delta\ne0$, with its reflection $c-\delta+i\gamma$, contributes to $u_\varepsilon$, when $\varepsilon<B$, a negative lobe of depth $2\varepsilon/(\pi(B^2-\varepsilon^2))$ at $z=A$, where $A=\gamma^2-\delta^2$ and $B=2\gamma|\delta|$, and a zero on the line with squared ordinate $A$ can mask it. Find conditions on the zeros near height $\gamma$ under which $u_\varepsilon\ge0$ at one $\varepsilon$ excludes a zero $c+\delta+i\gamma$ with $2\gamma|\delta|>\varepsilon$; equivalently, compare the depth $2\varepsilon/(\pi(B^2-\varepsilon^2))$ of the lobe of an off line pair with the contribution of the neighbouring atoms near $z=A$.
results.label: op:scholzelobe

results.name: Reciprocity in law between Artin and cuspidal automorphic representations
results.summary: On a probability space of prime powers weighted by Dirichlet's measure, asymptotic agreement in mean square of Frobenius traces with Hecke eigenvalues follows from reciprocity, determines the partner up to isomorphism on either side, forces irreducibility and gives agreement within any tolerance outside a set of primes of density zero, but asserts no existence.
results.statement: Fix a finite set $S$ of primes and, for $\sigma>1$, let $\mathbb{P}_\sigma$ be the probability measure on the prime powers $p^m$ with $p\notin S$ and $m\ge1$ given by $\mathbb{P}_\sigma(\{p^m\}) = p^{-m\sigma}/(mZ_\sigma)$, where $Z_\sigma = \sum_{p\notin S,\,m\ge1}p^{-m\sigma}/m$, with expectation $\mathbb{E}_\sigma$. An Artin representation $\rho$ unramified outside $S$ defines the random variable $a_\rho(p^m) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)$, and a unitary cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ unramified outside $S$, with Satake parameters $\alpha_{1,p},\dots,\alpha_{n,p}$ at $p$, defines $a_\pi(p^m) = \sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_{i,p}^m$. Call $\rho$ and $\pi$ reciprocal in law if $\mathbb{E}_\sigma|a_\rho - a_\pi|^2\to0$ as $\sigma\downarrow1$. Let $\rho,\rho'$ be Artin representations and $\pi,\pi'$ unitary cuspidal automorphic representations, all unramified outside $S$. (i) If $\rho$ and $\pi$ correspond in the sense of Langlands reciprocity, that is $L(s,\rho_p) = L(s,\pi_p)$ for every place $p$, they are reciprocal in law. (ii) If $\rho$ is reciprocal in law with $\pi$ and with $\pi'$, then $\pi\cong\pi'$. If $\rho$ and $\rho'$ are both reciprocal in law with $\pi$, then $\rho\cong\rho'$. (iii) If $\rho$ is reciprocal in law with a cuspidal $\pi$, then $\rho$ is irreducible. (iv) If $\rho$ is reciprocal in law with $\pi$, then for every $\epsilon>0$ the primes with $|a_\rho(p) - a_\pi(p)|>\epsilon$ have Dirichlet density zero. (v) If $\rho$ is automorphic, corresponding to $\pi_0$ in the sense of Langlands reciprocity, then $\rho$ is reciprocal in law with $\pi$ only for $\pi\cong\pi_0$.
results.label: cor:reciplaw

results.name: Congruence conditions see exactly the abelian part of an Artin representation
results.summary: The limiting conditional mean of the trace of an irreducible Artin representation given a congruence condition modulo N on the prime power is nonzero only for one dimensional representations that factor through the field of N th roots of unity, a reformulation of Chebotarev's theorem for the compositum with a cyclotomic field in which the Kronecker Weber theorem becomes measurability with respect to congruences.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible Artin representation and $N\ge1$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes containing the primes dividing $N$ and those at which $\rho$ ramifies. For $\sigma>1$ let $\mathbb{P}_\sigma$ be the probability measure on the prime powers $p^m$ with $p\notin S$ and $m\ge1$ given by $\mathbb{P}_\sigma(\{p^m\}) = p^{-m\sigma}/(mZ_\sigma)$, where $Z_\sigma = \sum_{p\notin S,\,m\ge1}p^{-m\sigma}/m$, with expectation $\mathbb{E}_\sigma$; let $a_\rho(p^m) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)$, and let $\mathcal{F}_N$ be the sigma algebra generated by the residue of $p^m$ modulo $N$. For every residue $r$ prime to $N$, $\lim_{\sigma\downarrow1}\mathbb{E}_\sigma\bigl[a_\rho\bigm|p^m\equiv r\bmod N\bigr]$ equals $\rho(r)$ if $\rho$ is inflated from $A_N = \operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)/\mathbb{Q})\cong(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$, where $\rho(r)$ is $\rho$ evaluated at the element $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^r$ of $A_N$, and equals $0$ otherwise; the first case occurs only when $\dim\rho = 1$, and in it $a_\rho$ is itself $\mathcal{F}_N$ measurable. In particular the Kronecker Weber theorem is equivalent to the statement that every one dimensional Artin representation is $\mathcal{F}_N$ measurable for some $N$, and no irreducible Artin representation of dimension at least two has a nonzero limiting conditional mean given any congruence.
results.label: prop:recipcongruence

results.name: Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer
results.summary: As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, the logarithms of its prime power factors, multiplied by the parameter minus one and labelled by any equidistributed sequence of points such as Frobenius classes or Sato Tate angles, converge in law to the jumps of a standard Gamma subordinator carrying independent labels drawn from the equidistribution law, and the labelled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma random measure, so that equidistribution becomes a Gamma process.
results.statement:
Let $Y$ be a compact metric space, $S$ a finite set of primes, and $(	heta_p)_{p
otin S}$ points of $Y$ equidistributed with respect to a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $Y$, in the sense that $\pi(t)^{-1}\sum_{p\le t,\,p
otin S}f(	heta_p)	o\int f\,d\mu$ as $t	o\infty$ for every continuous $f$ on $Y$, where $\pi(t)$ is the number of primes up to $t$. For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma = \prod_pp^{e_p}$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = n) = n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$ for $n\ge1$, and define the random measure $\Xi_\sigma = \sum_{p
otin S}(\sigma - 1)e_p\log p\;\delta_{	heta_p}$ on $Y$ and the marked point process $\mathcal{M}_\sigma = \sum_{p
otin S,\,e_p\ge1}\delta_{((\sigma - 1)e_p\log p,\;	heta_p)}$. Let $\Gamma_\mu$ be the Gamma random measure with shape measure $\mu$, which takes independent values on disjoint Borel sets with $\Gamma_\mu(B)\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(\mu(B),1)$, the gamma law of shape $\mu(B)$ and rate $1$. As $\sigma\downarrow1$: (i) $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ converges in law, vaguely on $(0,\infty)	imes Y$, to the Poisson process with intensity $x^{-1}e^{-x}dx\otimes\mu$, so the rescaled sizes $(\sigma - 1)e_p\log p$ of the prime factors of $N_\sigma$ are asymptotically the jumps of a standard Gamma subordinator on $[0,1]$, and their labels $	heta_p$ are asymptotically independent of the sizes and independent of one another, with law $\mu$; (ii) $\Xi_\sigma$ converges in law to $\Gamma_\mu$, that is, for every continuous $\lambda\ge0$ on $Y$, $\mathbb{E}\exp igl(-\int_Y\lambda\,d\Xi_\sigma igr)	o\exp igl(-\int_Y\log(1 + \lambda)\,d\mu igr)$.
results.label: thm:recipgammaproc

results.name: Chebotarev as a Gamma process with Dirichlet class shares and an arithmetic arcsine law
results.summary: The parts of the logarithm of a zeta distributed random integer carried by the primes of each Frobenius class are independent and asymptotically Gamma with shape the Chebotarev density, their shares are asymptotically Dirichlet and independent of the exponential total, and for a quadratic character the share carried by the inert primes converges in law to the arcsine law.
results.statement: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finite Galois extension with group $G$, unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes. For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma = \prod_pp^{e_p}$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = n) = n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, and for a conjugacy class $C$ of $G$ let $L_C(\sigma) = (\sigma - 1)\sum_{p\notin S,\,\operatorname{Frob}_p\in C}e_p\log p$, the rescaled part of $\log N_\sigma$ carried by primes with Frobenius in $C$. As $\sigma\downarrow1$: (i) the $L_C(\sigma)$, $C$ running over the conjugacy classes of $G$, are independent for every $\sigma$, and $L_C(\sigma)$ converges in law to $\mathrm{Gamma}(|C|/|G|,1)$, the gamma law of shape $|C|/|G|$ and rate $1$; (ii) the shares $L_C/\sum_{C'}L_{C'}$ have a Dirichlet limit law with parameters $(|C|/|G|)_C$, independent of the total, which is standard exponential; (iii) for a quadratic character $\chi$, the share of $\log N_\sigma$ carried by the primes with $\chi(p) = -1$ converges in law to the arcsine law $\pi^{-1}(u(1 - u))^{-1/2}\,du$ on $(0,1)$.
results.label: cor:recipchebgamma

results.name: Frobenius functionals of a zeta random integer converge to generalized gamma convolutions
results.summary: Weighting the rescaled logarithms of the prime power factors of a zeta distributed random integer by a nonnegative continuous function of equidistributed labels, such as Frobenius data, gives in the limit a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is an image of the label law, and, when the set where the weight is positive is a continuity set of that law, the probability that the weighted sum vanishes is the parameter minus one raised to the Thorin mass, to leading logarithmic order.
results.statement:
Let $Y$ be a compact metric space, $S$ a finite set of primes, and $(	heta_p)_{p
otin S}$ points of $Y$ equidistributed with respect to a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $Y$, that is $\pi(t)^{-1}\sum_{p\le t,\,p
otin S}f(	heta_p)	o\int f\,d\mu$ as $t	o\infty$ for every continuous $f$ on $Y$, where $\pi(t)$ is the number of primes up to $t$, and for $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma = \prod_pp^{e_p}$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = n) = n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp igl(-a\lambda - \int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1 + \lambda/t)\,	au(dt) igr)$, $\lambda\ge0$, where $a\ge0$ is the drift and $	au$ the Thorin measure; its Thorin mass is $	au((0,\infty))$. Let $Q\ge0$ be continuous on $Y$. Then $\Xi_\sigma(Q) = (\sigma - 1)\sum_{p
otin S}e_p\log p\;Q(	heta_p)$ converges in law, as $\sigma\downarrow1$, to a GGC with drift zero and Thorin measure $	au_Q$, the image of $\mu$ restricted to $\{Q>0\}$ under $	heta\mapsto1/Q(	heta)$. Its mean is $\int Q\,d\mu$ and its Thorin mass is $\mu(Q>0)$. Moreover, if $\{Q>0\}$ is a $\mu$ continuity set, $\log\mathbb{P} igl(\Xi_\sigma(Q) = 0 igr) = -\mu(Q>0)\log rac{1}{\sigma - 1} + o igl(\log rac{1}{\sigma - 1} igr)$.
results.label: thm:recipggcfun

results.name: Thorin criteria for reciprocity laws as vanishing of Thorin measures
results.summary: For pairs of Artin representations, abelian characters, quadratic reciprocity and pairs of elliptic curves, the squared discrepancy of Frobenius data gives in the limit a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure vanishes exactly when the two kinds of data agree, which restates Kronecker Weber and quadratic reciprocity and computes the shape of their failure, for example a scaled chi squared law when the sign factor is omitted from quadratic reciprocity.
results.statement:
For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma = \prod_pp^{e_p}$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = n) = n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, and for a nonnegative function $Q(p)$ of the Frobenius data at $p$ put $\Xi_\sigma(Q) = (\sigma - 1)\sum_{p
otin S}e_p\log p\;Q(p)$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp igl(-a\lambda - \int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1 + \lambda/t)\,	au(dt) igr)$, with drift $a\ge0$, Thorin measure $	au$ and Thorin mass $	au((0,\infty))$. In each case below, $S$ is a finite set of primes containing those at which the data are ramified (in (b) those ramified in $K(\zeta_N)$, in (c) $2$ and $q$, in (d) the primes of bad reduction of $E$ and $E'$), and $\Xi_\sigma(Q)$ converges in law as $\sigma\downarrow1$ to the GGC with drift zero and Thorin measure $	au_Q$, the image under $1/Q$ of the limiting law of the Frobenius data restricted to $\{Q>0\}$. (a) Artin representations. Let $ho,ho'$ be Artin representations unramified outside $S$, with fields $K,K'$ (the fixed fields of their kernels), put $H = \operatorname{Gal}(KK'/\mathbb{Q})$ and let $Q = |\chi_ho - \chi_{ho'}|^2$ on the conjugacy classes of $H$, evaluated at $\operatorname{Frob}_p$. Then $	au_Q$ is the image of Haar probability measure on $\{\chi_ho
e\chi_{ho'}\}\subset H$ under $1/|\chi_ho - \chi_{ho'}|^2$. The limit law has mean $\|\chi_ho - \chi_{ho'}\|^2_{L^2(H)}$, which is $2$ for nonisomorphic irreducible $ho,ho'$, and $	au_Q = 0$ if and only if $ho\congho'$. (b) Abelian reciprocity. Let $\psi$ be a character of finite order of $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$, $K$ its field, $\chi$ a Dirichlet character modulo $N$, and $Q = |\psi(\operatorname{Frob}_p) - \chi(p)|^2$. If $\psi
e\chi$ as characters of $\operatorname{Gal}(K(\zeta_N)/\mathbb{Q})$ and $\psi ar\chi$ has order $d$, then $	au_Q =  rac{1}{d}\sum_{j=1}^{d - 1}\delta_{1/(4\sin^2(\pi j/d))}$, and the limit law has mean $2$ and Thorin mass $1 -  rac{1}{d}$; otherwise $	au_Q = 0$. The Kronecker Weber theorem is equivalent to the statement that for every $\psi$ there are $N$ and $\chi$ with $	au_Q = 0$. (c) Quadratic reciprocity. Let $q\equiv3 mod4$ be prime. For $Q =  igl|\left( rac{q}{p}ight) - \left( rac{p}{q}ight) igr|^2$ the limit law is the gamma law of shape $ rac12$ and rate $ rac14$, that is $2\chi^2_1$, with Thorin measure $ rac12\delta_{1/4}$; for $Q =  igl|\left( rac{q}{p}ight) - \left( rac{p}{q}ight)\left( rac{-1}{p}ight) igr|^2$ the limit is $\delta_0$. For $q\equiv1 mod4$ the first $Q$ already gives $\delta_0$. (d) Elliptic curves. Let $E,E'$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication and not geometrically isogenous, with normalised traces $x_p = a_p(E)/\sqrt p$ and $x'_p = a_p(E')/\sqrt p$, and $Q = (x_p - x'_p)^2$. Then $	au_Q$ is the law of $1/(X - X')^2$ for independent $X,X'$ with the Sato Tate law $ rac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx$ on $[-2,2]$, so the Thorin mass is $1$ and the limit law has mean $2$. If instead $E'$ is isogenous to $E$, then $Q = 0$ for all good $p$ and the limit is $\delta_0$.
results.label: thm:recipthorin

results.name: Zero two law for the discrepancy subordinator of two Artin or two cuspidal representations
results.summary: When the squared discrepancy between the Frobenius traces of two Artin representations, or between the Hecke eigenvalues of two cuspidal automorphic representations, sets the intensity of a random integer, its rescaled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma law whose integer shape is the squared distance between the two, which is zero or two when both are irreducible Artin representations or both are cuspidal.
results.statement: Let $S$ be a finite set of primes containing those at which the data below ramify. For two Frobenius variables $a,b$, each either $a_\rho(p^m) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)$ for an Artin representation $\rho$ or $a_\pi(p^m) = \sum_i\alpha_{i,p}^m$ for a unitary cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi$ with Satake parameters $\alpha_{i,p}$ at $p$, put $Q_m(p) = |a(p^m) - b(p^m)|^2$, let $D_Q(s) = \sum_{k\ge1}d_Q(k)k^{-s}$ be the Dirichlet series with $\log D_Q(s) = \sum_{p\notin S,\,m\ge1}Q_m(p)m^{-1}p^{-ms}$, and for $\sigma>1$ let $X_\sigma = \log N_{Q,\sigma}$, where $N_{Q,\sigma}$ is the random integer with $\mathbb{P}(N_{Q,\sigma} = k)\propto d_Q(k)k^{-\sigma}$ (the discrepancy subordinator). Write $\mathrm{Gamma}(\alpha)$ for the gamma law of shape $\alpha$ and rate $1$, with $\mathrm{Gamma}(0) = \delta_0$. (a) For Artin representations $\rho,\rho'$ with $a = \operatorname{tr}\rho$ and $b = \operatorname{tr}\rho'$, $(\sigma - 1)X_\sigma$ converges in law as $\sigma\downarrow1$ to $\mathrm{Gamma}(\|\chi_\rho - \chi_{\rho'}\|^2)$, the norm being that of $L^2$ of Haar probability measure on the Galois group of the compositum of their fields; this is a generalized gamma convolution with Thorin measure $\|\chi_\rho - \chi_{\rho'}\|^2\delta_1$ and integer shape, and for irreducible $\rho,\rho'$ the shape is $0$ or $2$. (b) For unitary cuspidal automorphic representations $\pi,\pi'$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_{n'}(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ with $a = a_\pi$ and $b = a_{\pi'}$, the limit is $\delta_0$ if $\pi\cong\pi'$ and $\mathrm{Gamma}(2)$ otherwise.
results.label: thm:recipzerotwo

results.name: Mixed zero two law conjecture for an Artin and a cuspidal automorphic representation
results.summary: The book conjectures that for an irreducible Artin representation and a cuspidal automorphic representation of the same dimension the rescaled discrepancy subordinator has as limit either a point mass at zero or a Gamma law of shape two, the former exactly when their local factors agree at almost all primes, which is the orthogonality half of reciprocity and asserts no existence.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible Artin representation of dimension $n$ and $\pi$ a unitary cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$, both unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes, with $a(p^m) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)$ and $b(p^m) = a_\pi(p^m) = \sum_i\alpha_{i,p}^m$, the $\alpha_{i,p}$ being the Satake parameters of $\pi$ at $p$. Put $Q_m(p) = |a(p^m) - b(p^m)|^2$, let $D_Q(s) = \sum_{k\ge1}d_Q(k)k^{-s}$ be the Dirichlet series with $\log D_Q(s) = \sum_{p\notin S,\,m\ge1}Q_m(p)m^{-1}p^{-ms}$, and for $\sigma>1$ let $X_\sigma = \log N_{Q,\sigma}$, where $\mathbb{P}(N_{Q,\sigma} = k)\propto d_Q(k)k^{-\sigma}$. Conjecture: $(\sigma - 1)X_\sigma$ converges in law as $\sigma\downarrow1$ to $\delta_0$ or to $\mathrm{Gamma}(2)$, the gamma law of shape $2$ and rate $1$, and to $\delta_0$ exactly when $L(s,\rho_p) = L(s,\pi_p)$ for almost all $p$.
results.label: conj:recipmixed

results.name: Mixed zero two law for automorphic Artin representations and unconditional moment bounds
results.summary: The mixed zero two law holds whenever the Artin representation is automorphic, hence in dimension one, for odd two dimensional representations and for two dimensional representations with solvable image, the rescaled discrepancy has bounded first and second moments unconditionally, and a limit concentrated at zero implies reciprocity in law.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible Artin representation of dimension $n$ and $\pi$ a unitary cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$, both unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes, with $a(p^m) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)$ and $b(p^m) = a_\pi(p^m) = \sum_i\alpha_{i,p}^m$ ($\alpha_{i,p}$ the Satake parameters of $\pi$ at $p$). Put $Q_m(p) = |a(p^m) - b(p^m)|^2$, let $D_Q(s) = \sum_{k\ge1}d_Q(k)k^{-s}$ with $\log D_Q(s) = \sum_{p\notin S,\,m\ge1}Q_m(p)m^{-1}p^{-ms}$, and for $\sigma>1$ let $X_\sigma = \log N_{Q,\sigma}$ with $\mathbb{P}(N_{Q,\sigma} = k)\propto d_Q(k)k^{-\sigma}$. The mixed zero two law for $\rho$ and $\pi$ is the statement that $(\sigma - 1)X_\sigma$ converges in law as $\sigma\downarrow1$ to $\delta_0$ or to $\mathrm{Gamma}(2)$ (shape $2$, rate $1$), and to $\delta_0$ exactly when $L(s,\rho_p) = L(s,\pi_p)$ for almost all $p$. (i) If $\rho$ is automorphic, the mixed zero two law holds for $\rho$ and every $\pi$; hence it holds for $n = 1$, for odd two dimensional $\rho$, and for two dimensional $\rho$ with solvable image. (ii) Unconditionally, $\limsup_{\sigma\downarrow1}\mathbb{E}[(\sigma - 1)X_\sigma]\le4$ and $\mathbb{E}[((\sigma - 1)X_\sigma)^2]$ stays bounded, so under the mixed zero two law $\mathbb{E}[(\sigma - 1)X_\sigma]$ tends to $0$ or $2$. (iii) If the limit is $\delta_0$, then $\rho$ and $\pi$ are reciprocal in law, that is $\mathbb{E}_\sigma|a_\rho - a_\pi|^2\to0$ as $\sigma\downarrow1$ under the probability measure $\mathbb{P}_\sigma(\{p^m\})\propto p^{-m\sigma}/m$ on the prime powers $p^m$ with $p\notin S$; so $\pi$ is unique up to isomorphism and, for every $\epsilon>0$, $|a_\rho(p) - a_\pi(p)|\le\epsilon$ outside a set of primes of Dirichlet density zero.
results.label: prop:recipmixed

results.name: Euler Kronecker drift in the Gamma limit of Chebotarev classes
results.summary: The rescaled part of the logarithm of a zeta distributed random integer carried by the primes of a Frobenius class approaches its Gamma limit at a rate linear in the parameter minus one, with an explicit drift built from logarithmic derivatives of Artin L functions at one and a prime power term, and for the primes that split completely the drift is Ihara's Euler Kronecker constant of the field, with the Euler factors at the excluded primes removed, divided by the degree, plus a nonnegative term.
results.statement:
Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finite Galois extension with group $G$, unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes, let $C$ be a conjugacy class of $G$ and $\mu(C) = |C|/|G|$. For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma = \prod_pp^{e_p}$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = n) = n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, and let $L_C(\sigma) = (\sigma - 1)\sum_{p
otin S,\,\operatorname{Frob}_p\in C}e_p\log p$. For a character $\chi$ of $G$ put $\gamma^S(\chi) = \lim_{s	o1} igl( rac{(L^S)'}{L^S}(s,\chi) +  rac{\delta_{\chi=1}}{s - 1} igr)$, where the Artin $L$ function $L^S(s,\chi)$ omits the Euler factors at $S$, and let $\gamma_K^S = \lim_{s	o1} igl( rac{(\zeta_K^S)'}{\zeta_K^S}(s) +  rac{1}{s - 1} igr)$ be the Euler Kronecker constant of $K$ in Ihara's sense, computed for the Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K^S$ with the Euler factors above $S$ removed. Then, uniformly for $\lambda$ in compact subsets of $[0,\infty)$, as $\sigma\downarrow1$, $\log\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda L_C(\sigma)} = -\mu(C)\log(1 + \lambda) + \kappa_C\,\lambda\,(\sigma - 1) + O((\sigma - 1)^2)$ with $\kappa_C = \mu(C)\sum_\chi\overline{\chi(C)}\,\gamma^S(\chi) - \sum_{p
otin S}\sum_{m\ge2} igl[\mathsf{1}_C(\operatorname{Frob}_p) - \mathsf{1}_C(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m) igr](\log p)\,p^{-m}$, the first sum running over the irreducible characters of $G$. In particular $\mathbb{E}L_C(\sigma) = \mu(C) - \kappa_C(\sigma - 1) + O((\sigma - 1)^2)$, so to first order the Gamma limit is shifted by the deterministic amount $-\kappa_C(\sigma - 1)$. For the class of primes that split completely, $\kappa_{\{1\}} =  rac{\gamma_K^S}{|G|} + \sum_{p
otin S,\,\operatorname{Frob}_p
e1}\;\sum_{m\ge2,\,\operatorname{Frob}_p^m = 1}(\log p)\,p^{-m}$, the Euler Kronecker constant of $K$ with the Euler factors above $S$ removed, divided by the degree, plus a nonnegative prime power term. For a class function $Q\ge0$ with value $Q_C$ on $C$ and $\Xi_\sigma(Q) = \sum_CQ_C\,L_C(\sigma)$, independence of the $L_C(\sigma)$ gives $\log\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda\Xi_\sigma(Q)} = -\sum_C\mu(C)\log(1 + \lambda Q_C) + \kappa_Q\lambda(\sigma - 1) + O((\sigma - 1)^2)$ with $\kappa_Q = \sum_CQ_C\,\kappa_C$.
results.label: thm:recipdrift

results.name: Hecke's criterion as the symmetry of a Pólya kernel built from Frobenius traces
results.summary: A restatement of Hecke's theorem in which the functional equation of a Dirichlet series with polynomially bounded coefficients becomes the evenness or oddness of its Pólya kernel, so that at level one the modularity of Galois data is the symmetry of one function on the line built from Frobenius traces.
results.statement: Let $k\ge1$ and $N\ge1$ be integers, $f(z) = \sum_{n\ge1}a_ne^{2\pi inz}$ with $a_n = O(n^{(k - 1)/2 + \epsilon})$, $\Lambda(s) = (\sqrt N/2\pi)^s\Gamma(s)\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}$, and $\Phi_f(u) = f(ie^u/\sqrt N)\,e^{ku/2}$, the Pólya kernel of the coefficient sequence, so that $\Lambda(\frac k2 + t) = \int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_f(u)e^{tu}\,du$ for $\operatorname{Re}t$ large. For $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$ the following are equivalent. (i) $\Phi_f(-u) = \varepsilon\,\Phi_f(u)$ for all real $u$. (ii) $f(-1/(Nz)) = \varepsilon\,i^{-k}N^{k/2}z^kf(z)$ for all $z$ in the upper half plane. (iii) $\Lambda$ extends to an entire function, bounded in vertical strips, with $\Lambda(k - s) = \varepsilon\Lambda(s)$. For $N = 1$, $k$ even and $\varepsilon = (-1)^{k/2}$ these are equivalent to the statement that $f$ is a cusp form of weight $k$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$.
results.label: prop:recipsym

results.name: Gamma shape of the Rankin Selberg subordinator detects irreducibility of an Artin representation
results.summary: The rescaled Rankin Selberg subordinator of an Artin representation, built from squared Frobenius traces, converges to a Gamma law whose shape is the sum of the squared multiplicities of its irreducible constituents, so the representation is irreducible exactly when the limit is exponential, the Galois counterpart of cuspidality on the automorphic side.
results.statement:
Let $ho$ be an Artin representation, $S$ the set of primes at which it ramifies, and $D^S(s) = L^S(s,ho\otimes\checkho) = \prod_{p
otin S}\det igl(1 - (ho\otimes\checkho)(\operatorname{Frob}_p)p^{-s} igr)^{-1}$, so that $\log D^S(s) = \sum_{p
otin S}\sum_{j\ge1}|\operatorname{tr}ho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^j)|^2j^{-1}p^{-js}$ has nonnegative coefficients. For $\sigma>1$ let $X_\sigma$ be the compound Poisson random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda X_\sigma} = D^S(\sigma + \lambda)/D^S(\sigma)$ for $\lambda\ge0$, whose Lévy measure is $\sum_{p
otin S,\,j\ge1}|\operatorname{tr}ho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^j)|^2j^{-1}p^{-j\sigma}\delta_{j\log p}$. Let $m = \langleho,hoangle$, the sum of the squares of the multiplicities of the irreducible constituents of $ho$. As $\sigma\downarrow1$, $(\sigma - 1)X_\sigma$ converges in law to the Gamma law with shape $m$ and scale $1$. In particular $ho$ is irreducible if and only if the limit is the standard exponential law.
results.label: thm:recipgamma

results.name: Complete monotonicity of the Galois heat trace as a criterion for holomorphy and GRH
results.summary: For a self dual L function with meromorphic continuation of finite order and a functional equation, a heat trace computed from Frobenius traces, the conductor and the gamma factor equals half the sum over zeros minus half the sum over poles of a Gaussian in the ordinate, and it is completely monotone exactly when the L function is entire with all zeros on the critical line, a restricted form of Weil's positivity criterion that reformulates Artin's conjecture together with GRH and proves neither.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be a self dual Galois representation (an Artin representation, or a geometric $\ell$ adic representation, pure of some weight, made complex through a fixed isomorphism $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell\cong\mathbb{C}$), in the unitary normalisation, with conductor $N_\rho$, gamma factor $\gamma(s,\rho)$ and completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\rho) = N_\rho^{s/2}\gamma(s,\rho)L(s,\rho)$, and let $\Lambda_\rho(n)$ be the coefficients of $-L'/L(s,\rho)$, so that $\Lambda_\rho(p^m) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)\log p$ at unramified $p$. For $x>0$ the Galois heat trace is $\mathcal{W}_\rho(x) = \frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{-xt^2}\bigl(\log N_\rho + 2\operatorname{Re}\frac{\gamma'}{\gamma}(\tfrac12 + it,\rho)\bigr)\,dt - \frac{1}{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda_\rho(n)}{\sqrt n}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{x}}\,e^{-(\log n)^2/(4x)}$. Suppose that $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ has meromorphic continuation of finite order with $\Lambda(s,\rho) = \pm\Lambda(1 - s,\rho)$, and write its zeros and poles as $\frac12\pm i\gamma$. Then (i) $\mathcal{W}_\rho(x) = \frac12\sum_{\text{zeros}}e^{-x\gamma^2} - \frac12\sum_{\text{poles}}e^{-x\gamma^2}$, with multiplicity, the sums absolutely convergent for $x>0$; (ii) $\mathcal{W}_\rho$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$ if and only if $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ is entire and all its zeros lie on $\operatorname{Re}s = \frac12$. In particular, for an Artin representation with real character and no trivial constituent (a trivial constituent of multiplicity $r$ adds the pole term $-re^{x/4}$), Artin's conjecture together with GRH for $L(s,\rho)$ is equivalent to the complete monotonicity of a function computed from Frobenius traces.
results.label: thm:recipcm

results.name: The Galois heat trace detects a change of Frobenius data at a single prime
results.summary: Changing the local factors of an L function that is entire with all zeros on the critical line at a nonempty set of primes thin enough that the sum of log p over the square root of p converges, a single prime included, while keeping the conductor, the gamma factor and Satake parameters of absolute value at most one, destroys the complete monotonicity of the Galois heat trace, unlike any statement about the distribution of Frobenius data.
results.statement: For self dual Galois data $\rho$ with conductor $N_\rho$, gamma factor $\gamma(s,\rho)$, completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\rho) = N_\rho^{s/2}\gamma(s,\rho)L(s,\rho)$ and $\Lambda_\rho(n)$ the coefficients of $-L'/L(s,\rho)$, let $\mathcal{W}_\rho(x) = \frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{-xt^2}\bigl(\log N_\rho + 2\operatorname{Re}\frac{\gamma'}{\gamma}(\tfrac12 + it,\rho)\bigr)\,dt - \frac{1}{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda_\rho(n)}{\sqrt n}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{x}}\,e^{-(\log n)^2/(4x)}$, $x>0$, be its Galois heat trace. Let $\rho$ be self dual with $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ meromorphic of finite order, $\Lambda(s,\rho) = \pm\Lambda(1 - s,\rho)$, entire and with all its zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s = \frac12$ (equivalently, $\mathcal{W}_\rho$ completely monotone). Let $\rho'$ be self dual Galois data with the same conductor and the same gamma factor, whose local factors differ from those of $\rho$ at a nonempty set $P$ of primes with $\sum_{p\in P}p^{-1/2}\log p<\infty$, and suppose that the Satake parameters of $\rho$ and $\rho'$ have absolute value at most $1$. Then $\mathcal{W}_{\rho'}$ is not completely monotone. In particular, if $\Lambda(s,\rho')$ has meromorphic continuation of finite order with $\Lambda(s,\rho') = \pm\Lambda(1 - s,\rho')$, it has a pole or a zero off the critical line.
results.label: prop:reciprigid

results.name: Euler half line Thorin criterion for holomorphy, functional equation and GRH
results.summary: If the reciprocal of a self dual completed Euler product, read on the half line beyond one after a square root change of variable, is a constant times the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a sum of point masses of positive integer weight, then the completed L function is entire, satisfies its functional equation, is bounded in vertical strips and has all zeros on the critical line, and conversely for an entire completion of order one with nonzero central value and all zeros on the critical line.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be a self dual Galois representation with conductor $N_\rho$, gamma factor $\gamma(s,\rho)$ and completion $\Lambda(s,\rho) = N_\rho^{s/2}\gamma(s,\rho)L(s,\rho)$ in the unitary normalisation, defined for $\operatorname{Re}s>1$ by its Euler product, and let $s_0>\frac14$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\bigl(-a\lambda - \int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1 + \lambda/t)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)$, with drift $a\ge0$ and Thorin measure $\tau$. Suppose that for $s>\frac14$, $\frac{\Lambda(\frac12 + \sqrt{s_0},\rho)}{\Lambda(\frac12 + \sqrt s,\rho)} = C\,\mathbb{E}e^{-sH}$ for a constant $C>0$ and a GGC $H$ whose Thorin measure is $\sum_kc_k\delta_{u_k}$ with positive integers $c_k$ and $u_k>0$. Then $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ extends to an entire function of finite order, $\Lambda(s,\rho) = \Lambda(1 - s,\rho)$, every zero lies on $\operatorname{Re}s = \frac12$, and $\Lambda$ is bounded in vertical strips. Conversely, if $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ is entire of order one with this functional equation, $\Lambda(\frac12,\rho)\ne0$ and all zeros $\frac12\pm i\gamma_k$ on the critical line, then the hypothesis holds with $u_k = \gamma_k^2$.
results.label: thm:recipeuler

results.name: Thorin converse theorem at level one
results.summary: A Thorin form of Hecke's converse theorem in which self dual Galois data of conductor one, with the gamma factor of a weight divisible by four and the Ramanujan bound, come from a cusp form for the full modular group satisfying GRH whenever the normalised reciprocal Euler product is a constant times the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a sum of point masses of positive integer weight, a hypothesis stated on the Euler half line and stronger than reciprocity since it contains GRH.
results.statement: Let $k\equiv0\bmod4$ and let $(a_p)$ be the Frobenius traces of a self dual Galois representation of conductor $1$ with gamma factor $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s + \frac{k - 1}{2})$, where $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s) = \Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s + 1) = 2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, satisfying the Ramanujan bound, with $a_n$ the Dirichlet coefficients of its $L$ function in the unitary normalisation and $\Lambda(s)$ its completion. If, for some $s_0>\frac14$, the normalised Euler product $\Lambda(\frac12 + \sqrt{s_0})/\Lambda(\frac12 + \sqrt s)$, $s>\frac14$, is a constant times the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\bigl(-a\lambda - \int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1 + \lambda/t)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)$, $a\ge0$) whose Thorin measure $\tau$ is a sum of point masses with positive integer weights, then $\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{(k - 1)/2}e^{2\pi inz}$ is a cusp form of weight $k$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, and it satisfies GRH.
results.label: cor:recipconverse

results.name: Unconditional generalized gamma convolution family from the Rankin Selberg square of an Artin representation
results.summary: For every Artin representation and every base point beyond one, the normalised reciprocal of the completed Rankin Selberg square is an explicit exponential factor times the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin density is the sine squared transport of a measure built from squared Frobenius traces plus a gamma factor term, so positivity holds unconditionally on the Euler half line.
results.statement:
Let $ho$ be an Artin representation, $S$ the set of primes at which it ramifies, and $F(s) = \Lambda^S(s,ho\otimes\checkho)$ the completion, with conductor and gamma factor, of $L^S(s,ho\otimes\checkho) = \prod_{p
otin S}\det igl(1 - (ho\otimes\checkho)(\operatorname{Frob}_p)p^{-s} igr)^{-1}$. For every $\alpha>1$ there is a generalized gamma convolution $H_\alpha$ (a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp igl(-a\lambda - \int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1 + \lambda/t)\,	au(dt) igr)$, $a\ge0$, $	au$ its Thorin measure) with $ rac{F(\alpha)}{F(\alpha + \sqrt s)} = e^{-b_\alpha\sqrt s}\,\mathbb{E}e^{-sH_\alpha}$ for $s>0$, $b_\alpha =  rac{F'(\alpha)}{F(\alpha)}$, whose Thorin density is the $2\sin^2$ transport $
u\mapsto U(z) =  rac{1}{2\pi\sqrt z}\int_0^\infty2\sin^2 igl( rac{x\sqrt z}{2} igr)\,
u(dx)$ of the measure $
u = \sum_{p
otin S,\,m\ge1}|\operatorname{tr}ho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)|^2(\log p)\,p^{-m\alpha}\delta_{m\log p}$ ($x$ times the Lévy measure of the Rankin Selberg subordinator at $\alpha$) together with the gamma factor contribution. It is computed from Frobenius traces alone.
results.label: prop:recipfamily

results.name: Thorin converse theorem for twists that are not self dual
results.summary: The book asks for a version of its Euler half line Thorin criterion for twists that are not self dual, strong enough to combine with the converse theorem of Cogdell and Piatetski Shapiro.
results.statement: For a self dual Galois representation $\rho$ with completed $L$ function $\Lambda(s,\rho)$, the Euler half line criterion of this chapter says that if, for some $s_0>\frac14$ and all $s>\frac14$, the ratio $\Lambda(\frac12 + \sqrt{s_0},\rho)/\Lambda(\frac12 + \sqrt s,\rho)$ is a positive constant times the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is $\sum_kc_k\delta_{u_k}$ with positive integers $c_k$ and $u_k>0$, then $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ is entire of finite order, satisfies $\Lambda(s,\rho) = \Lambda(1 - s,\rho)$, has all its zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s = \frac12$ and is bounded in vertical strips. Formulate and prove a version of this criterion for twists $\rho\times\pi'$ that are not self dual, strong enough to combine with the converse theorem of Cogdell and Piatetski Shapiro. The obstacle is that the self dual completion $\Xi_\rho$, built from $\Lambda(\frac12 + z,\rho)\Lambda(\frac12 + z,\check\rho)$, controls the product of two $L$ functions, whereas converse theorems need each one.
results.label: op:recipgln

results.name: Descending the base point of transported Thorin densities of the Rankin Selberg square
results.summary: The book asks whether the transported Thorin densities of the Rankin Selberg square of an automorphic Artin representation, with the drift split off, stay nonnegative for base points between the centre and the edge of the critical strip, and which features of Frobenius data control their sign.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an automorphic Artin representation, let $F_0(s)$ be the complete Rankin Selberg function $\Lambda(s,\rho\otimes\check\rho)$, with all Euler factors included and its poles at $s = 0$ and $s = 1$ removed, and for $\alpha\in(\frac12,1]$ let $V_{\alpha - 1/2}(z) = \operatorname{Re}(F_0'/F_0)(\alpha + i\sqrt z)/(2\pi\sqrt z)$ for $z>0$ and $b_\alpha = F_0'(\alpha)/F_0(\alpha)$. Positivity of the transported Thorin densities $V_{\alpha - 1/2}$, with the drift kept inside, for every $\alpha\in(\frac12,1]$ is GRH for $L(s,\rho\otimes\check\rho)$. Decide whether the densities $V_{\alpha - 1/2} - b_\alpha/(2\pi\sqrt z)$, with the drift split off, also stay nonnegative there (for the Riemann xi function this holds under the Riemann hypothesis and is proved unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$ and, for $\frac12<\alpha<1$, below height $3\times10^{12}$), and identify the obstruction to positivity below $\alpha = 1$ in terms of Frobenius data alone. Which features of the Lévy measure $\sum_{p\notin S,\,m\ge1}|\operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)|^2m^{-1}p^{-m\alpha}\delta_{m\log p}$ of the Rankin Selberg subordinator at $\alpha>1$, with $S$ the ramified primes, control the sign of the transported density at $\alpha<1$?
results.label: op:recipdescent

results.name: Signed Thorin measures separating Artin's conjecture from GRH
results.summary: The book asks for a property of Frobenius data on the Euler half line that forces the integer weights of the signed Thorin measure of an Artin L function to be positive, which is Artin's conjecture, without forcing its atoms to be real, which is GRH.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an Artin representation with real character, no trivial constituent, root number $1$ and $\Lambda(\frac12,\rho)$ finite and nonzero, where $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ is its completed $L$ function. Brauer's theorem and Hadamard factorisation give, for a fixed $s_0>\frac14$, $\Lambda(\frac12 + \sqrt{s_0},\rho)/\Lambda(\frac12 + \sqrt s,\rho) = C\prod_k(1 + s/u_k)^{-c_k}$ with nonzero integers $c_k$ and complex $u_k = \gamma_k^2$, where $\frac12\pm i\gamma_k$ run over the zeros and poles, $c_k<0$ exactly at poles, and $u_k\notin(0,\infty)$ exactly at zeros and poles off the critical line; Artin's conjecture for $\rho$ is the statement that every $c_k$ is positive. Find a property of the signed Lévy measure of $\log\Lambda(s,\rho)$ on the Euler half line $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, that is of Frobenius data, which forces every $c_k$ to be positive without forcing the $u_k$ to be real, so that holomorphy is separated from GRH.
results.label: op:recipsigned

results.name: A Fejér summation for primes making the Galois heat trace positive
results.summary: The book asks for positive Fejér type weights on prime powers under which positivity of the weighted Galois heat trace follows from Frobenius data alone, as Fejér positivity does for the heat trace of the circle, which through the complete monotonicity criterion would give holomorphy and GRH.
results.statement: For a self dual Galois representation $\rho$ with conductor $N_\rho$, gamma factor $\gamma(s,\rho)$ and $\Lambda_\rho(n)$ the coefficients of $-L'/L(s,\rho)$, the Galois heat trace is $\mathcal{W}_\rho(x) = \frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{-xt^2}\bigl(\log N_\rho + 2\operatorname{Re}\frac{\gamma'}{\gamma}(\tfrac12 + it,\rho)\bigr)\,dt - \frac{1}{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda_\rho(n)}{\sqrt n}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{x}}\,e^{-(\log n)^2/(4x)}$ for $x>0$; when $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ has meromorphic continuation of finite order and a functional equation, it is completely monotone if and only if $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ is entire with all zeros on the critical line. For the circle, the winding number terms $\sqrt{\pi/x}\,e^{-\pi^2n^2/x}$ summed with the Fejér weights $1 - |n|/N$ form the Laplace transform of the positive density $F_N(\sqrt z)z^{-1/2}$, with $F_N$ Fejér's kernel. Find positive weights $w_N(n)\le1$ with $w_N(n)\to1$ such that the prime side of $\mathcal{W}_\rho$, with $\Lambda_\rho(n)$ replaced by $w_N(n)\Lambda_\rho(n)$ and the archimedean term adjusted accordingly, is the Laplace transform of a positive measure, and such that positivity for each $N$ follows from Frobenius data alone, as Fejér positivity does for the circle; otherwise $w_N\equiv1$ works whenever holomorphy and GRH hold. By the complete monotonicity criterion this would prove holomorphy and GRH for $L(s,\rho)$; the problem is to see what positivity of this kind forces on Frobenius data.
results.label: op:recipfejer

results.name: Reciprocity in law versus reciprocity
results.summary: The book asks to show that an irreducible Artin representation reciprocal in law with a cuspidal automorphic representation agrees with it at all but finitely many primes, a strong multiplicity one statement across the Galois and automorphic sides.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible Artin representation of dimension $n$ and $\pi$ a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$, unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes, with $a_\rho(p^m) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)$ and $a_\pi(p^m)$ the $m$th power sum of the Satake parameters of $\pi$ at $p$, and call them reciprocal in law if $\mathbb{E}_\sigma|a_\rho - a_\pi|^2\to0$ as $\sigma\downarrow1$ under the probability measure $\mathbb{P}_\sigma(\{p^m\})\propto p^{-m\sigma}/m$ on the prime powers $p^m$ with $p\notin S$. Show that if $\rho$ is reciprocal in law with $\pi$, then $a_\rho(p) = a_\pi(p)$ for all but finitely many $p$. This holds whenever $\rho$ is known to be automorphic; for $n = 2$, where this leaves the even icosahedral $\rho$, it would follow from a refinement of Ramakrishnan's theorem to the case in which one member is Galois and the agreement is only approximate (within every $\epsilon>0$ outside a set of primes of Dirichlet density zero); in general it is a strong multiplicity one statement across the two sides.
results.label: op:reciplaw

results.name: The mixed zero two law under meromorphy and for an even icosahedral representation
results.summary: The book asks to derive the dichotomy of its mixed zero two law from meromorphy of the mixed Rankin Selberg L function near the edge of the critical strip, to reduce the rest of the conjecture to reciprocity in law, and to prove the conjecture for one even icosahedral Artin representation.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible Artin representation of dimension $n$ and $\pi$ a unitary cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$, unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes, with $a(p^m) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)$ and $b(p^m) = \sum_i\alpha_{i,p}^m$ ($\alpha_{i,p}$ the Satake parameters of $\pi$ at $p$), $Q_m(p) = |a(p^m) - b(p^m)|^2$, $D_Q(s) = \sum_{k\ge1}d_Q(k)k^{-s}$ with $\log D_Q(s) = \sum_{p\notin S,\,m\ge1}Q_m(p)m^{-1}p^{-ms}$, and $X_\sigma = \log N_{Q,\sigma}$ with $\mathbb{P}(N_{Q,\sigma} = k)\propto d_Q(k)k^{-\sigma}$ for $\sigma>1$. The mixed zero two law conjecture states that $(\sigma - 1)X_\sigma$ converges in law as $\sigma\downarrow1$ to $\delta_0$ or to the gamma law of shape $2$ and rate $1$, and to $\delta_0$ exactly when $L(s,\rho_p) = L(s,\pi_p)$ for almost all $p$. Show that meromorphy of $L(s,\rho\times\tilde\pi)$ near $\operatorname{Re}s = 1$, with at most a simple pole at $s = 1$ and no zeros on the line, gives the dichotomy of the conjecture by the argument that proves the zero two law for two Artin or two cuspidal representations, and reduces the rest of the conjecture to a form of the problem of reciprocity in law versus reciprocity (whether reciprocity in law forces $a(p) = b(p)$ for all but finitely many $p$), and prove the conjecture for one even icosahedral Artin representation.
results.label: op:recipmixed

results.name: Joint marked Gamma processes of an Artin and a cuspidal representation
results.summary: The book asks whether the joint limit of the Frobenius labelled Gamma processes of an Artin representation and a cuspidal automorphic representation exists, and whether its label law either sits on the set where the two traces agree or gives their squared discrepancy a Thorin mass bounded below in terms of the dimension.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an Artin representation and $\pi$ a cuspidal automorphic representation of the same dimension $n$, unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes, with $a_\rho(p) = \operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p)$ and $a_\pi(p)$ the sum of the Satake parameters of $\pi$ at $p$. For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma = \prod_pp^{e_p}$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = k) = k^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, and let $\mathcal{M}_\sigma = \sum_{p\notin S,\,e_p\ge1}\delta_{((\sigma - 1)e_p\log p,\;\theta_p)}$ be the marked point process of its rescaled prime factors, labelled by $\theta_p$, the Frobenius data of $\rho$ and of $\pi$ at $p$ taken together; for labels equidistributed with respect to a law $\mu$ it converges in law to the Poisson process with intensity $x^{-1}e^{-x}dx\otimes\mu$. Show that the joint limit of these marked processes exists for $\rho$ and $\pi$; it is not determined by the two marginal limits. Is the joint label law either supported on $\{a_\rho = a_\pi\}$, or such that the Thorin measure of $|a_\rho - a_\pi|^2$ has mass bounded below by a constant depending only on $n$?
results.label: op:recipjoint

results.name: Signs of the Euler Kronecker drifts of Chebotarev classes
results.summary: The book asks to characterise the Galois number fields whose split primes approach their Gamma limit from above, which requires a negative Euler Kronecker constant, and to relate the signs of the drifts of the Frobenius classes to Chebotarev biases and races.
results.statement: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finite Galois extension with group $G$, unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes, and for $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma = \prod_pp^{e_p}$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = n) = n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$. For a conjugacy class $C$ let $L_C(\sigma) = (\sigma - 1)\sum_{p\notin S,\,\operatorname{Frob}_p\in C}e_p\log p$ and let $\kappa_C$ be its Euler Kronecker drift, defined by $\log\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda L_C(\sigma)} = -\frac{|C|}{|G|}\log(1 + \lambda) + \kappa_C\lambda(\sigma - 1) + O((\sigma - 1)^2)$, so that $\mathbb{E}L_C(\sigma) = \frac{|C|}{|G|} - \kappa_C(\sigma - 1) + O((\sigma - 1)^2)$; for the class of the identity, $\kappa_{\{1\}}$ is $\gamma_K^S/|G|$ plus a nonnegative prime power term, where $\gamma_K^S$ is Ihara's Euler Kronecker constant of $K$ with the Euler factors above $S$ removed. When does the split class approach its Gamma limit from above, that is $\kappa_{\{1\}}<0$? This requires $\gamma_K^S<0$. Characterise such fields, and relate the signs of the $\kappa_C$ to the bias between Frobenius classes of the primes, as measured in the book for the splitting field of $x^3 - x - 1$, and to Chebotarev races.
results.label: op:recipdrift

results.name: Two prime Kemeny formula for supersingular isogeny walks
results.summary: Kemeny's constant of the random walk along isogenies of prime degree ℓ between the supersingular elliptic curves in characteristic N is a harmonic sum of the factors of the number of points of J_0(N) over the field with ℓ elements, and, when every newform of level N is rational, ℓ+1 times the sum of the reciprocal point counts modulo ℓ of the isogeny classes of elliptic curves of conductor N.
results.statement: Let $N$ be a prime and $\ell\ne N$ a prime. Let $E_1,\dots,E_h$ be the supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ up to isomorphism, let the Brandt matrix $B(\ell)$ have entries $B(\ell)_{ij}$ equal to the number of cyclic subgroups $C\subset E_i$ of order $\ell$ with $E_i/C\cong E_j$, and let the isogeny walk be the Markov chain on $\{E_1,\dots,E_h\}$ with transition matrix $P=B(\ell)/(\ell+1)$. Let $f$ run over the $g=\dim S_2(\Gamma_0(N))$ normalised Hecke eigenforms of weight two and level $N$, and let $a_\ell(f)$ be the eigenvalue of the Hecke operator $T_\ell$ on $f$. Then Kemeny's constant of the isogeny walk, $K_N(\ell)=\sum_y\pi(y)\,\mathbb{E}_x\tau_y$, where $\pi$ is the stationary law of $P$ and $\tau_y$ is the first time $t\ge0$ at which the walk is at $E_y$ (the expected hitting time of a target drawn from $\pi$, which does not depend on the starting curve $E_x$ and equals $\sum_{j\ge2}(1 - \mu_j)^{-1}$, where $1=\mu_1,\mu_2,\dots,\mu_h$ are the eigenvalues of $P$), is \[ K_N(\ell)=\sum_f\frac{\ell+1}{\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)}. \] In particular, if every newform of level $N$ has rational coefficients, \[ K_N(\ell)=(\ell+1)\sum_{E}\frac{1}{|E(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|}, \] the sum over the isogeny classes of elliptic curves $E$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ of conductor $N$, which correspond to the newforms with rational coefficients by Eichler and Shimura and the modularity of semistable elliptic curves (Wiles; Taylor and Wiles). In general the contribution of a Galois orbit of forms, attached to an abelian variety $A_f$ with coefficient field $K_f$, is $(\ell+1)\operatorname{Tr}_{K_f/\mathbb{Q}}\bigl(1/(\ell+1 - a_\ell(f))\bigr)$.
