results.label: thm:hitkemeny

results.name: Isomorphism criterion for sandpile groups of supersingular isogeny graphs and the modular Jacobian
results.summary: For a prime N congruent to 1 modulo 12 and primes r outside a finite set, the r part of the critical (sandpile) group of the supersingular ℓ isogeny graph in characteristic N, which Munier and Shnidman identify with a quotient of the Hecke algebra, is isomorphic to the r part of the group of points of J_0(N) over the field with ℓ elements exactly when Frobenius at ℓ acts nontrivially on each torsion module of J_0(N) cut out by a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra above r; the criterion is new.
results.statement:
Let $N\equiv 1 mod 12$ and $\ell
e N$ be primes and $h=(N - 1)/12$. Let $G_N(\ell)$ be the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph, the $(\ell+1)$ regular multigraph on the $h$ supersingular elliptic curves $E_1,\dots,E_h$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ whose adjacency matrix is the Brandt matrix $B(\ell)$, with $B(\ell)_{ij}$ the number of cyclic subgroups $C\subset E_i$ of order $\ell$ with $E_i/C\cong E_j$. Let $X=\mathbb{Z}^h$ be the divisors on the supersingular curves, $X^0$ those of degree zero and $L=(\ell+1)I - B(\ell)$ the Laplacian, so that the critical group (sandpile group) of $G_N(\ell)$ is $X^0/L(X)$. Let $\mathbb{T}$ be the ring generated by the Hecke operators $T_m$, $N
mid m$, on $S_2(\Gamma_0(N))$, which acts on the Jacobian $J_0(N)$ of $X_0(N)$ and, through the Brandt matrices, on $X^0$, and for a prime $r$ put $\mathbb{T}_r=\mathbb{T}\otimes\mathbb{Z}_r$. Let $r
e\ell$ be a prime that divides neither $hN$ nor the discriminant of $\mathbb{T}$. Then the $r$ part of the critical group of $G_N(\ell)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{T}_r/(\ell+1 - T_\ell)\mathbb{T}_r$ (this first statement is due to Munier and Shnidman). It is isomorphic to the $r$ part of $J_0(N)(\mathbb{F}_\ell)$ if and only if Frobenius at $\ell$ acts nontrivially on $J_0(N)[\lambda]$ for every maximal ideal $\lambda$ of $\mathbb{T}$ above $r$; otherwise the two are not isomorphic even as groups.
results.label: prop:hitsandpile

results.name: Resistances and commute times of supersingular isogeny graphs
results.summary: For a prime N congruent to 1 modulo 12, the sum of all effective resistances (the Kirchhoff index) of the supersingular ℓ isogeny graph in characteristic N and the mean commute time between its vertices are explicit multiples of its Kemeny constant, a harmonic sum of the factors of the number of points of J_0(N) over the field with ℓ elements.
results.statement: Let $N\equiv 1\bmod 12$ and $\ell\ne N$ be primes and $h=(N - 1)/12$. Let $G_N(\ell)$ be the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph, the $(\ell+1)$ regular multigraph on the $h$ supersingular elliptic curves $E_1,\dots,E_h$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ whose adjacency matrix is the Brandt matrix $B(\ell)$, with $B(\ell)_{ij}$ the number of cyclic subgroups $C\subset E_i$ of order $\ell$ with $E_i/C\cong E_j$, and let $K_N(\ell)$ be Kemeny's constant of the random walk with transition matrix $B(\ell)/(\ell+1)$. Let $f$ run over the normalised Hecke eigenforms of $S_2(\Gamma_0(N))$, with $T_\ell$ eigenvalues $a_\ell(f)$, and let $R(x,y)$ be the effective resistance between vertices of $G_N(\ell)$ with unit conductance on each edge. Then \[ \sum_{\{x,y\}}R(x,y)=h\sum_f\frac{1}{\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)}=\frac{h\,K_N(\ell)}{\ell+1}, \] the sum over unordered pairs of vertices, and the commute time $\kappa(x,y)=\mathbb{E}_x\tau_y+\mathbb{E}_y\tau_x=h(\ell+1)R(x,y)$, where $\tau_y$ is the hitting time of $y$ by the walk, has mean $2hK_N(\ell)/(h - 1)$ over unordered pairs of distinct vertices.
results.label: thm:hitresist

results.name: Hasse Weil bounds for Kemeny constants and spanning tree counts of isogeny graphs
results.summary: The Weil bound on Hecke eigenvalues becomes two sided bounds, linear in the genus, on the Kemeny constant of every supersingular isogeny walk of prime level and, for prime levels congruent to 1 modulo 12, two sided bounds, exponential in the genus, on the number of spanning trees of the isogeny graph.
results.statement: Let $N$ be a prime, $\ell\ne N$ a prime and $g$ the genus of $X_0(N)$, the dimension of $S_2(\Gamma_0(N))$. Let $K_N(\ell)$ be Kemeny's constant of the isogeny walk, the Markov chain on the supersingular elliptic curves $E_1,\dots,E_h$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ (up to isomorphism) with transition matrix $B(\ell)/(\ell+1)$, where the Brandt matrix entry $B(\ell)_{ij}$ is the number of cyclic subgroups $C\subset E_i$ of order $\ell$ with $E_i/C\cong E_j$. Then \[ \frac{g(\ell+1)}{(\sqrt\ell+1)^2}\le K_N(\ell)\le\frac{g(\ell+1)}{(\sqrt\ell - 1)^2}, \] and for $N\equiv 1\bmod 12$, with $h=(N - 1)/12$ and $\tau(G_N(\ell))$ the number of spanning trees of the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph $G_N(\ell)$, the multigraph on these curves with adjacency matrix $B(\ell)$, \[ (\sqrt\ell - 1)^{2g}\le h\,\tau(G_N(\ell))\le(\sqrt\ell+1)^{2g}. \]
results.label: cor:hithasse

results.name: Tree entropy of the regular tree as the asymptotic class number of J_0(N) over a finite field
results.summary: As the prime level N grows, the exponential growth rate per unit of genus of the number of points of J_0(N) over the field with ℓ elements, an asymptotic class number given by a theorem of Tsfasman and Vlăduţ, is the spanning tree entropy of the (ℓ+1) regular tree, which therefore also governs the spanning tree counts of the supersingular isogeny graphs of levels congruent to 1 modulo 12; the reading as a tree entropy is, as far as the authors know, new.
results.statement: Fix a prime $\ell$. For a prime $N$ let $J_0(N)$ be the Jacobian of the modular curve $X_0(N)$ and $g$ its genus. As $N\to\infty$ through primes, \[ \frac1g\log|J_0(N)(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|\longrightarrow\log\frac{\ell^\ell}{(\ell^2 - 1)^{(\ell - 1)/2}}. \] The limit is the spanning tree entropy of the $(\ell+1)$ regular tree, so for $N\equiv 1\bmod 12$ also $h^{-1}\log\tau(G_N(\ell))$ converges to it, where $h=(N - 1)/12$ and $\tau(G_N(\ell))$ is the number of spanning trees of the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph, the $(\ell+1)$ regular multigraph on the $h$ supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ whose adjacency matrix is the Brandt matrix $B(\ell)$.
results.label: thm:hitentropy

results.name: Chebotarev densities as hitting rates of the largest prime factors of a random integer
results.summary: For a zeta distributed random integer whose prime factors carry equidistributed labels such as Frobenius classes, in the limit as the zeta parameter tends to one, the largest prime factor with label in a given set arrives, on the scale of the exponential integral, after an exponential time whose rate is the measure of that set, so that reciprocity laws say that a discrepancy set is hit at rate zero; for a single label this is Lloyd's limit law, and the labelled form is new.
results.statement:
Let $Y$ be a compact metric space, $S$ a finite set of primes, and $(	heta_p)_{p
otin S}$ points of $Y$ (labels, such as Frobenius classes or Satake parameters) equidistributed with respect to a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $Y$, that is $\pi(t)^{-1}\sum_{p\le t,\,p
otin S}f(	heta_p)	o\int f\,d\mu$ for every continuous $f$. For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, and let $e_p$ be the exponent of $p$ in $N_\sigma$. For a Borel set $B\subset Y$ let $P_B^+$ be the largest prime factor $p
otin S$ of $N_\sigma$ with $	heta_p\in B$, and $V_B=(\sigma - 1)\log P_B^+$ ($V_B=0$ if there is none); write $E_1(v)=\int_v^\infty e^{-x}x^{-1}\,dx$. Let $B$ be a $\mu$ continuity set, that is $\mu(\partial B)=0$. As $\sigma\downarrow1$: (i) $\mathbb{P}(V_B\le v)	o\exp(-\mu(B)E_1(v))$ for every $v>0$; if $\mu(B)>0$, equivalently, $E_1(V_B)$ converges in law to the exponential law with rate $\mu(B)$, and if $\mu(B)=0$, then $V_B	o0$ in probability; (ii) the label of the largest prime factor of $N_\sigma$ outside $S$ lies in $B$ with probability tending to $\mu(B)$, and the labels of the $k$ largest prime factors are asymptotically independent with law $\mu$, independent of their sizes; (iii) for two continuous functions $a$ and $b$ on $Y$, for example the characters of two Artin representations as functions on the conjugacy classes of a finite Galois group, whose discrepancy set $D=\{a
e b\}$ is a $\mu$ continuity set, (i) holds for $B=D$, and $\mu(D)$ is the mass of the Thorin measure $	au_Q$ of the generalized gamma convolution that is the limit in law of $\Xi_\sigma(Q)=(\sigma - 1)\sum_{p
otin S}e_p\log p\,Q(	heta_p)$ for $Q=|a - b|^2$, namely the image of $\mu$ restricted to $\{Q>0\}$ under $	heta\mapsto1/Q(	heta)$; in particular $V_D	o0$ in probability if and only if $	au_Q=0$.
results.label: thm:hitrate

results.name: Explosion time criterion for zeros on the critical line
results.summary: A symmetric entire function of order at most one, nonzero at the centre, has all its zeros on the critical line exactly when a normalised reciprocal of its values along a half line is the Laplace transform of the explosion time of a pure birth process, whose birth rates are then the squared ordinates of the zeros; this is an equivalence restating the book's Thorin duality, after Polson (2018), and proves no Riemann hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $\Lambda(s)$ be entire of order at most one with $\Lambda(s)=\Lambda(1 - s)$ and $\Lambda(\tfrac12)\ne0$, and write its zeros as $\tfrac12\pm i\gamma_k$, with multiplicity. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a nonnegative random variable $T$ with $\mathbb{E}e^{-sT}=\exp\bigl(-as - \int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)$ for a drift $a\ge0$ and a Thorin measure $\tau$; a pure birth process on $\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ started at $0$ with rates $u_1\le u_2\le\dots$ (repetitions allowed) and $\sum_k1/u_k<\infty$ explodes at the time $T=\sum_k\mathcal{E}_k/u_k$, with $\mathcal{E}_k$ independent standard exponential variables. The following are equivalent. (i) Every $\gamma_k$ is real. (ii) There is a GGC $T$ with $\mathbb{E}e^{-sT}=\Lambda(\tfrac12)/\Lambda(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$ for all $s>\tfrac14$. (iii) $\Lambda(\tfrac12)/\Lambda(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$, $s>\tfrac14$, is the Laplace transform of the explosion time of a pure birth process. In that case the birth rates are the $\gamma_k^2$, $T$ is infinitely divisible with L\'evy density $\mathcal{W}(x)/x$, where $\mathcal{W}(x)=\sum_{\gamma_k>0}e^{-x\gamma_k^2}$ is the heat trace, and the cumulants of $T$ are \[ \kappa_m(T)=(m - 1)!\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2m}=\int_0^\infty x^{m-1}\mathcal{W}(x)\,dx,\qquad \mathbb{E}T=\sum_k\frac{1}{\gamma_k^2}=\frac12\,\frac{\Lambda''}{\Lambda}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr). \]
results.label: thm:hitexplosion

results.name: Thorin converse theorem at level one as an explosion time
results.summary: If a normalised reciprocal of the completed L function of a self dual Galois representation of conductor one, along a half line, is the Laplace transform of the explosion time of a pure birth process, then the representation comes from a level one cusp form satisfying the generalized Riemann hypothesis, and conversely, with a Wald couple between the explosion time and the Pólya variable when the Pólya kernel is nonnegative; the hypothesis contains the generalized Riemann hypothesis, so no new case of reciprocity follows.
results.statement: Let $k\equiv 0\bmod 4$ and let $(a_p)$ be the Frobenius traces of a self dual Galois representation of conductor $1$ with the gamma factor $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s+\tfrac{k - 1}{2})$, where $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, satisfying the Ramanujan bound, with Dirichlet coefficients $a_n$, and let $\Lambda$ be its completion, defined on $\operatorname{Re}s>1$ by the Euler product. If for some constant $c>0$ the function $c/\Lambda(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$, $s>\tfrac14$, is the Laplace transform of the explosion time $T$ of a pure birth process, that is of a sum $T=\sum_k\mathcal{E}_k/u_k$ of independent standard exponential variables $\mathcal{E}_k$ with rates $u_k>0$ and $\sum_k1/u_k<\infty$, then $f=\sum_na_nn^{(k-1)/2}q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, is a cusp form of weight $k$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfying the generalized Riemann hypothesis, and $c=\Lambda(\tfrac12)\ne0$. Conversely, if $f$ is such a cusp form satisfying the generalized Riemann hypothesis with $\Lambda(\tfrac12)\ne0$, this holds with $c=\Lambda(\tfrac12)$. If moreover the P\'olya kernel $\Phi_f(u)=f(ie^u)e^{ku/2}$ is nonnegative, as for $\Delta$ (but not for one of the two eigenforms of weight $24$), then the P\'olya variable $W_f$, whose density is proportional to $\Phi_f$, and $T$ form a Wald couple: $\mathbb{E}e^{tW_f}\,\mathbb{E}e^{-t^2T}=1$ for all real $t$.
results.label: cor:hitconverse

results.name: A new proof of the functional equation of odd primitive Dirichlet L functions by a signed Brownian exit law
results.summary: Weighting the starting point of a Brownian motion killed at the ends of an interval by an odd primitive Dirichlet character, the image and eigenfunction expansions of the resulting signed exit law give the classical theta transformation formula and functional equation of the L function, with its Gauss sum root number, extending to every odd primitive character a derivation known for the character modulo 4 (Biane, Pitman and Yor; Salminen and Vignat).
results.statement: Let $q\ge3$, let $B$ be standard Brownian motion started at $r\in(0,q)$, so that $\mathbb{E}(B_t - r)^2=t$, let $\tau$ be its exit time from $(0,q)$, and let $f_r^0(t)$ and $f_r^q(t)$ be the densities of $\tau$ on the events of exit at $0$ and at $q$. Let $\chi$ be an odd primitive Dirichlet character modulo $q$ and $g(\chi)=\sum_r\chi(r)e^{2\pi ir/q}$ its Gauss sum. For every $t>0$, \[ \sum_{r=1}^{q-1}\chi(r)\bigl(f_r^0(t) - f_r^q(t)\bigr)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi t^3}}\sum_{m\ge1}\chi(m)\,m\,e^{-m^2/(2t)}=-\frac{4\pi i\,g(\chi)}{q^2}\sum_{j\ge1}\bar\chi(j)\,j\,e^{-2\pi^2j^2t/q^2}. \] Consequently $\vartheta_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi(n)\,n\,e^{-\pi n^2x/q}$ satisfies \[ \vartheta_\chi(1/x)=\frac{g(\chi)}{i\sqrt q}\,x^{3/2}\,\vartheta_{\bar\chi}(x), \] and $\Lambda(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\tfrac{s+1}{2})L(s,\chi)$ satisfies $\Lambda(s,\chi)=\frac{g(\chi)}{i\sqrt q}\Lambda(1 - s,\bar\chi)$.
results.label: thm:hitexit

results.name: Limiting law of sandpile groups of supersingular isogeny graphs in the level aspect
results.summary: Find the limiting law, as the prime level grows, of the r parts of the critical groups of supersingular isogeny graphs, a question raised by Munier and Shnidman, describe the critical groups at the primes that the isomorphism criterion excludes, and extend the comparison with the modular Jacobian to the prime 2 and to other levels.
results.statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and let $N	o\infty$ through primes $N\equiv 1 mod 12$, with $h=(N - 1)/12$. Let $G_N(\ell)$ be the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph, the $(\ell+1)$ regular multigraph on the $h$ supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ whose adjacency matrix is the Brandt matrix $B(\ell)$, with Laplacian $L=(\ell+1)I - B(\ell)$ and critical group $X^0/L(X)$, where $X=\mathbb{Z}^h$ and $X^0$ is its sublattice of degree zero; let $\mathbb{T}$ be the ring generated by the Hecke operators $T_m$, $N
mid m$, on $S_2(\Gamma_0(N))$, $\mathbb{T}_r=\mathbb{T}\otimes\mathbb{Z}_r$, and $C_N$ the cuspidal subgroup of the Jacobian $J_0(N)$ of $X_0(N)$. Find the limiting law of the $r$ part of the critical group of $G_N(\ell)$, a question Munier and Shnidman raise. For $r
e\ell$ prime to $hN$ and to the discriminant of $\mathbb{T}$ this $r$ part is $\mathbb{T}_r/(\ell+1 - T_\ell)\mathbb{T}_r$, so it is governed by the valuations of $\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)$ at the primes above $r$ of the Hecke fields, and, as Munier and Shnidman note, it needs an $r$ adic analogue of Serre's vertical equidistribution of the Hecke eigenvalues $a_\ell(f)$. For the primes $r$ dividing $h$ or the discriminant of $\mathbb{T}$, describe the critical group, and decide when the class of $L\delta_E$, where $\delta_E\in X$ is the divisor of a vertex $E$, corresponds to the cuspidal subgroup $C_N$. Extend the comparison between the critical group and $J_0(N)(\mathbb{F}_\ell)$ to $\ell=2$ and to levels $N
ot\equiv 1 mod 12$, where the graph is weighted by automorphisms.
results.label: op:hitsandpile

results.name: Vertex hitting times of isogeny walks and Gross's formula
results.summary: Find the distribution over discriminants of the combination of central values of quadratic twists that Gross's formula attaches to hitting times between the reductions of curves with complex multiplication, and decide what the hitting time of the support of the Gross divisor computes.
results.statement: Let $N\equiv 1\bmod 12$ and $\ell\ne N$ be primes, and consider the simple random walk on the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph in characteristic $N$, the $(\ell+1)$ regular multigraph on the supersingular elliptic curves $E_y$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N$ whose adjacency matrix is the Brandt matrix $B(\ell)$, with stationary law $\pi$ and hitting times $\tau_y$; let $\phi_f$ be the quaternionic forms attached to the newforms $f$ of level $N$ by the Jacquet Langlands correspondence, common eigenvectors of the Brandt matrices orthonormal in $L^2(\pi)$. Let $D<0$ be a fundamental discriminant with $N$ inert in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt D)$, and let $e_D=\sum_yc_y[E_y]$ be the divisor of Gross's formula, whose coefficient $c_y$ counts the curves with complex multiplication by the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt D)$ that reduce to $E_y$. The mean of hitting times between the reductions of these curves satisfies \[ \sum_{x,y}c_xc_y\mathbb{E}_x\tau_y=(\deg e_D)\sum_yc_y\mathbb{E}_\pi\tau_y-(\ell+1)\sum_f\frac{\bigl|\sum_yc_y\phi_f(y)\bigr|^2}{\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)}, \] where $\deg e_D=\sum_yc_y$, $a_\ell(f)$ is the eigenvalue of the Hecke operator $T_\ell$ on $f$ and $\mathbb{E}_\pi$ is the expectation for the walk started from $\pi$, and Gross's formula turns the last sum into a combination, with positive coefficients that do not depend on $\ell$, of the values $L(f,1)L(f\otimes\chi_D,1)/(\ell+1 - a_\ell(f))$ over the newforms $f$ of level $N$, where $\chi_D$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt D)$. For fixed $N$ and $\ell$, find the distribution of this combination over $D$, a question about the central values of the quadratic twists of the newforms of level $N$. Find also the law of the hitting time of the support of $e_D$ from stationarity, and decide which arithmetic quantities it computes: its Laplace transform involves the values $\phi_f(x)\overline{\phi_f(y)}$ at pairs of points of the support, not only the linear forms $\sum_yc_y\phi_f(y)$ of Gross's formula.
results.label: op:hitgross

results.name: Gamma law of the Eisenstein discrepancy of an elliptic curve
results.summary: For an elliptic curve and a prime p, the rescaled logarithmic weight that a zeta distributed random integer puts on the primes at which p does not divide the number of points of the curve converges to a Gamma law whose shape, the classical local density at p in Koblitz's conjecture (Koblitz; Zywina), is also the rate at which the prime factors of the integer hit those primes; the reading of this density as the shape of a Gamma law and as a hitting rate is the book's.
results.statement:
Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve of conductor $N$ and $p$ a prime. Let $G_{E,p}\subset\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ be the image of the mod $p$ Galois representation $ arho_{E,p}$, with Haar probability measure $\mu_{G_{E,p}}$, and let the Eisenstein Thorin shape be $c(E,p)=\mu_{G_{E,p}}\{g\in G_{E,p}:\det(1 - g)
e0\}$. Let the Eisenstein discrepancy be $Q_{E,p}(\ell)=\mathsf{1}\{p
mid|E(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|\}$ for primes $\ell
mid pN$. For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma$ be a zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, with $e_\ell$ the exponent of the prime $\ell$ in $N_\sigma$, and let $\Xi_\sigma(Q_{E,p})=(\sigma - 1)\sum_{\ell
mid pN}e_\ell\log\ell\,Q_{E,p}(\ell)$. Then, as $\sigma\downarrow1$, $\Xi_\sigma(Q_{E,p})$ converges in law to the Gamma law with shape $c(E,p)$ and scale $1$. Its Thorin measure is $c(E,p)\,\delta_1$, and $c(E,p)$ is the rate at which the prime factors of $N_\sigma$ hit the primes $\ell$ with $p
mid|E(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|$: if $P^+$ is the largest prime factor $\ell
mid pN$ of $N_\sigma$ with $p
mid|E(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|$ and $V=(\sigma - 1)\log P^+$ ($V=0$ if there is none), then $\mathbb{P}(V\le v)	o\exp(-c(E,p)E_1(v))$ for every $v>0$, where $E_1(v)=\int_v^\infty e^{-x}x^{-1}\,dx$.
results.label: prop:flteisgamma

results.name: Fermat's last theorem restated as two Thorin statements
results.summary: Given the modularity of semistable elliptic curves (Wiles; Taylor and Wiles), Ribet's level lowering theorem and Mazur's torsion theorem, the known proof of Fermat's last theorem for prime exponents at least five is restated as the incompatibility of a positive Eisenstein Thorin shape of the Frey curve with the empty Hecke Thorin measure at level two; no step of the proof is reproved, and its content stays in those theorems.
results.statement: Assume the following theorems, which are used and not reproved: the modularity of semistable elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ (Wiles; Taylor and Wiles), Ribet's level lowering theorem for weight two newforms with trivial character (Ribet), and Mazur's torsion theorem (Mazur), which through an argument of Serre gives the positivity in (i) below. Let $p\ge5$ be prime, suppose $a^p+b^p=c^p$ with $abc\ne0$, normalised so that $\gcd(a,b,c)=1$, $a\equiv -1\bmod 4$ and $b$ is even, and let $E$ be its Frey curve $y^2=x(x - a^p)(x+b^p)$. Say that two systems of mod $p$ Frobenius traces have zero discrepancy Thorin mass when the set of primes at which they differ has Dirichlet density zero, equivalently when the functional $(\sigma - 1)\sum_\ell e_\ell\log\ell\,\mathsf{1}\{\ell\text{ in that set}\}$ of a zeta distributed random integer, with $e_\ell$ the exponent of $\ell$, converges to $0$ as $\sigma\downarrow1$. Then the mod $p$ representation $\bar\rho_{E,p}$ would have zero discrepancy Thorin mass against some weight two Hecke eigensystem of level $2$. But (i) against the Eisenstein system $a_\ell=\ell+1$ the discrepancy is the Gamma law of shape $c(E,p)>0$, where $c(E,p)$ is the Haar measure of the set of elements without eigenvalue $1$ in the image of $\bar\rho_{E,p}$ in $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$; and (ii) there is no cuspidal system, because the Hecke Thorin measure of level $2$, the Thorin measure $\sum_f\delta_{\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)}$ over the normalised eigenforms $f$ of $S_2(\Gamma_0(2))$, is empty. Hence there is no such solution.
results.label: thm:flttwo

results.name: Hasse Weil bound from hitting times on supersingular isogeny graphs
results.summary: Find a probabilistic proof, for instance through hitting times or a heat kernel on the supersingular isogeny graph, of the bound of Eichler and Shimura with Weil on the Hecke eigenvalues of weight two newforms of prime level.
results.statement: Give a probabilistic proof of the bound $|a_\ell(f)|\le2\sqrt\ell$ of Eichler and Shimura with Weil for the Hecke eigenvalues $a_\ell(f)$, $\ell\ne N$ prime, of the weight two newforms $f$ of prime level $N$, for instance through hitting times or a heat kernel on the supersingular $\ell$ isogeny graph in characteristic $N$. The positivity of the Thorin atoms $\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)$ of the Hecke generalized gamma convolution $H_N(\ell)$, whose Thorin measure is $\sum_f\delta_{\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)}$, needs only $a_\ell(f)<\ell+1$, which the Perron Frobenius theorem gives; the bound itself gives the Hasse Weil bounds on the Kemeny constants and spanning tree counts of the isogeny graphs. Compare the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture for Maass forms, where no geometric proof is available.
results.label: op:flthasse

results.name: Taylor Wiles patching as a Gamma process
results.summary: Ask whether the auxiliary primes of the Taylor Wiles patching method can be taken as the atoms, in a fixed Chebotarev class, of the Gamma process of the prime factors of a zeta distributed random integer, with the patched objects as limits in law.
results.statement: The Taylor Wiles method chooses, for each $n$, finite sets of auxiliary primes $q\equiv 1\bmod p^n$ at which $\bar\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ has distinct eigenvalues, where $\bar\rho$ is the residual mod $p$ Galois representation; by Chebotarev's theorem and the hitting rate theorem for the largest prime factors of a zeta distributed random integer $N_\sigma$, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, such primes occur among the large prime factors of $N_\sigma$ at a positive rate. Is there a formulation of the patching argument in which the auxiliary sets are the atoms of the Gamma process (the Poisson limit, as $\sigma\downarrow1$, of the rescaled sizes $(\sigma - 1)\log q$ of the prime factors $q$ of $N_\sigma$ together with their Frobenius labels) in a fixed Chebotarev class, and the patched objects are limits in law as $\sigma\downarrow1$?
results.label: op:fltpatch

results.name: A probabilistic Mazur theorem for Eisenstein shapes of curves with rational 2 torsion
results.summary: Ask for a proof through the Gamma law of the Eisenstein discrepancy and isogeny walks, rather than through Mazur's torsion theorem, that an elliptic curve over the rationals with all its 2 torsion rational has positive Eisenstein shape at every prime at least five.
results.statement: For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ and a prime $p$ let the Eisenstein Thorin shape $c(E,p)$ be the Haar measure of the set of elements without eigenvalue $1$ in the image of the mod $p$ Galois representation of $E$ in $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$, equivalently the density of the primes $\ell$ with $p\nmid|E(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|$. Serre's argument from Mazur's torsion theorem gives $c(E,p)>0$ for $p\ge5$ and every curve with $E[2]\subset E(\mathbb{Q})$. One rational point of order $2$ is not enough: the semistable curve $y^2+xy=x^3 - 45x+81$ of conductor $66$ has torsion $\mathbb{Z}/10$, so $c(E,5)=0$. Is there a proof of this positivity through the Gamma law of the Eisenstein discrepancy, the limit law with shape $c(E,p)$ of the functional $(\sigma - 1)\sum_\ell e_\ell\log\ell\,\mathsf{1}\{p\nmid|E(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|\}$ of a zeta distributed random integer with exponents $e_\ell$, and the supersingular isogeny walks? Such a proof must use an input special to $\mathbb{Q}$: over some quadratic fields there are curves with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/2\times\mathbb{Z}/10$, whose analogue of the Eisenstein shape at $5$, over the primes of the field, vanishes.
results.label: op:fltmazur

results.name: Explicit Gaussian window error for Bohr inversion of the sine squared transport
results.summary: A quantitative form of Bohr's mean value inversion, in which Gaussian averages of the one minus cosine transform of a discrete signed measure recover the weight of each atom with an explicit, exponentially small error, so that the transform is injective.
results.statement:
Let $
u=\sum_jc_j\delta_{x_j}$ be a discrete signed measure with distinct atoms $x_j>0$ and $\sum_j|c_j|<\infty$, and let $g(r)=\int(1-\cos rx)\,
u(dx)$. For $R>0$ and a function $h$ on $[0,\infty)$ write $\mathcal{G}_R[h]=\int_0^\infty h(r)e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr ig/\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr$. Then for every $k$ \[ \mathcal{G}_R igl[g(r)\cos(rx_k) igr]=\sum_jc_j\Bigl[e^{-x_k^2R^2/2}-	frac12e^{-(x_j-x_k)^2R^2/2}-	frac12e^{-(x_j+x_k)^2R^2/2}\Bigr], \] so that, with $\delta_k=\min igl(x_k,\inf_{j
e k}|x_j-x_k| igr)$ assumed positive, \[ \Bigl|c_k+2\mathcal{G}_R igl[g(r)\cos(rx_k) igr]\Bigr|\le2\Bigl(\sum_j|c_j|\Bigr)e^{-\delta_k^2R^2/2}. \] In particular $c_k=-2\lim_{R	o\infty}\mathcal{G}_R[g(r)\cos(rx_k)]$, the same limit holds for the plain Bohr mean, that is $c_k=-2\lim_{R	o\infty} rac1R\int_0^Rg(r)\cos(rx_k)\,dr$, and the map $
u\mapsto g$ is injective.
results.label: thm:lapbohr

results.name: Frobenius traces recovered from the transported density with explicit error
results.summary: The von Mangoldt coefficients of an L function, and so the Frobenius traces of an Artin representation, are read off Gaussian averages of its sine squared transported density, with an explicit error bound at every finite window.
results.statement: Let $L(s)=\sum_na_nn^{-s}$ have an Euler product with $-L'/L(s)=\sum_n\Lambda_L(n)n^{-s}$ absolutely convergent for $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, as for Artin L functions and, by the Rankin Selberg method of Jacquet and Shalika and the Cauchy Schwarz inequality, for cuspidal automorphic ones. For $\alpha>1$ let \[ g_\alpha(r)=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda_L(n)}{n^\alpha}\bigl(1-\cos(r\log n)\bigr) \] be the transported density, which equals $\operatorname{Re}\frac{L'}{L}(\alpha+ir)-\frac{L'}{L}(\alpha)$ when the $\Lambda_L(n)$ are real, and for $R>0$ let $\mathcal{G}_R[h]=\int_0^\infty h(r)e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr\big/\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr$. Then for $n\ge2$ \[ \Lambda_L(n)=-2n^\alpha\lim_{R\to\infty}\mathcal{G}_R\bigl[g_\alpha(r)\cos(r\log n)\bigr], \] and the error at a finite $R$ is at most \[ 2n^\alpha\Bigl(\sum_m|\Lambda_L(m)|m^{-\alpha}\Bigr)e^{-\delta_n^2R^2/2},\qquad\delta_n=\log(1+1/n). \] If $L=L(s,\rho)$ for an Artin representation $\rho$ unramified at $p$, then $\Lambda_L=\Lambda_\rho$ and $\operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)=\Lambda_\rho(p^m)/\log p$, so, since two such Euler products whose transported densities agree on an interval of $r$ have the same coefficients, the transported density on any interval of $r$ determines every Frobenius trace.
results.label: cor:lapfrob

results.name: Thorin measure at a shifted basepoint as zeros plus folded Cauchy noise
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2017, version 26 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
results.summary: For a self dual L function the Thorin measure of the completed function, at a basepoint to the right of all zeros, is half a sum of folded Cauchy laws centred at the ordinates of the zeros, and moving the basepoint adds Cauchy noise, which restates for every self dual L function what Polson (2017) proved for the Riemann xi function.
results.statement: Let $\pi$ be self dual, and let $\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(w)$ be the completed L function $\Lambda(\tfrac12+w,\pi)$ divided by the power of $w$ that removes any zero at $w=0$; for the Riemann zeta function use $\Xi_\zeta(w)=\xi(\tfrac12+w)$ in its place. This function is even and entire of order at most one; its zeros $z=\beta+i\gamma$, counted with multiplicity, form a multiset $\mathcal{Z}$ closed under $z\mapsto-z$ and $z\mapsto\bar z$, and $|\beta|<\tfrac12$. Let $C$ be a standard Cauchy variable, with density $1/(\pi(1+x^2))$. Let $a>|\beta|$ for every $z=\beta+i\gamma$ in $\mathcal{Z}$; this holds unconditionally for $a\ge\tfrac12$. Let $H_a$ be the generalized gamma convolution with $\mathbb{E}e^{-sH_a}=\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(a)/\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(a+\sqrt s)$ and $V_a$ its Thorin density. In the variable $r>0$, the square root of the Thorin variable, the Thorin measure of $H_a$ is \[ V_a(r^2)\,2r\,dr=\frac12\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}}\mathrm{Law}\bigl(|\gamma+(a-\beta)C|\bigr)(dr),\qquad r>0. \] Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis this is $\sum_{\gamma>0}\mathrm{Law}(|\gamma+aC|)$ for every $a>0$, a superposition of folded Cauchy laws centred at the ordinates with common scale $a$. For $b>0$, $V_{a+b}$ is obtained from $V_a$ by adding independent Cauchy noise of scale $b$ before folding, and, for $a>\tfrac12$, this is multiplication by $e^{-bx}$ of the whole Lévy measure of $\log\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi$ at basepoint $a$, archimedean and polynomial factors included.
results.label: thm:lapcauchy

results.name: Sato Tate law as the Good and Gaskins roughness minimiser, with shrinkage of symmetric power moments
results.summary: The Sato Tate law is the unique minimiser of the Good and Gaskins roughness penalty among densities on the alcove whose square root vanishes on the walls (an inequality of Huber for SU(2) and the Rayleigh principle in general), and for SU(2), near it, the penalised likelihood estimate shrinks each empirical symmetric power moment by an explicit factor.
results.statement: Let $G$ be a compact connected simply connected Lie group, such as $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ or $\mathrm{USp}(2n)$, with alcove $\mathcal{A}$, positive roots $\alpha$ and half sum of the positive roots $\rho_G$, the Lie algebra of a maximal torus carrying the invariant inner product in which, for $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ and $\mathrm{USp}(2n)$, the eigenvalue angles are orthonormal coordinates. Let $f_G=c|\Delta_G|^2$ on $\mathcal{A}$, with $\Delta_G=\prod_{\alpha>0}(e^{i\alpha/2}-e^{-i\alpha/2})$ and $c$ a normalising constant, be the Sato Tate law, the image of Haar measure on conjugacy classes. Among densities $f$ on $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\sqrt f$ vanishes on the boundary $\partial\mathcal{A}$ and $\int_{\mathcal{A}}|\nabla\sqrt f|^2<\infty$, the Good and Gaskins roughness $\int_{\mathcal{A}}|\nabla\sqrt f|^2$, one quarter of the trace of the Fisher information for location, is at least $|\rho_G|^2$, with equality exactly for the Sato Tate law $f_G$. For $G=\mathrm{SU}(2)$, with $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ and $\sqrt f=\sqrt{2/\pi}\sum_jb_j\sin j\theta$, $\sum_jb_j^2=1$, \[ \int_0^\pi\bigl((\sqrt f)'\bigr)^2d\theta=\sum_jj^2b_j^2,\qquad \frac{\sin j\theta}{\sin\theta}=\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Sym}^{j-1}\begin{pmatrix}e^{i\theta}&0\\0&e^{-i\theta}\end{pmatrix}, \] so the roughness is the Laplace eigenvalue energy $\sum_\lambda|\lambda+\rho_G|^2b_\lambda^2$, which is $|\rho_G|^2$ plus the Casimir energy, in the basis of symmetric power characters, and the Sato Tate law is $b=e_1$. Given angles $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n$, put $\hat m_j=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Sym}^{j-1}(\theta_i)$, the trace being that of the matrix above at $\theta=\theta_i$. Near the Sato Tate law, the maximiser of $\frac1n\sum_i\log f(\theta_i)-\omega\int_0^\pi\bigl((\sqrt f)'\bigr)^2d\theta$ over $\sqrt f=\sqrt{2/\pi}\sum_{j\le J}b_j\sin j\theta$ satisfies \[ b_j=\frac{\hat m_j}{2+\omega(j^2-1)}+O\Bigl(\max_{2\le l\le2J-1}\hat m_l^2\Bigr),\qquad 2\le j\le J. \]
results.label: thm:lapgg

results.name: Stable recovery of Frobenius traces from a finite window of the transported density
results.summary: Asks whether stable recovery of the coefficient at n of an L function from its transported density needs a window of length of order n, which would be an uncertainty principle for the Galois side.
results.statement: Let $L$ have an Euler product with $-L'/L(s)=\sum_n\Lambda_L(n)n^{-s}$ absolutely convergent for $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, and for $\alpha>1$ let $g_\alpha(r)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda_L(n)n^{-\alpha}\bigl(1-\cos(r\log n)\bigr)$ be its transported density. The restriction of $g_\alpha$ to any interval $[0,r_0)$ determines every $\Lambda_L(n)$, but only through analytic continuation, which is unstable. Suppose $g_\alpha$ is known on $[0,r_1]$ to within $\eta$. The Gaussian means $-2n^\alpha\mathcal{G}_R[g_\alpha(r)\cos(r\log n)]$, with $\mathcal{G}_R[h]=\int_0^\infty h(r)e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr\big/\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr$ truncated at $r_1$, recover $\Lambda_L(n)$ to within $\varepsilon$ once $\eta$ is of order $\varepsilon n^{-\alpha}$ and $r_1$ of order $n\log(n^\alpha/\varepsilon)$. Is an interval of length of order $n$, the reciprocal of the gap $\log(1+1/n)$ between the frequencies $\log n$ and $\log(n+1)$, necessary for every stable method, as Ingham's inequality for nonharmonic Fourier series suggests? A positive answer would be an uncertainty principle for the Galois face, comparable with the bounds in effective Chebotarev theorems.
results.label: op:lapwindow

results.name: Good and Gaskins penalised likelihood for Thorin densities of L functions
results.summary: Asks for a roughness penalised likelihood estimate of the Thorin density of an L function from finitely many zeros or from a noisy transported density, the form of its maximiser, and a comparison of its error with exact inversion by Gaussian means.
results.statement: The inversions of the transported density and of the Thorin law of an L function are exact but need exact input. Treat the ordinates $0<\gamma_1\le\dots\le\gamma_K$ of its zeros as a sample from the normalised counting measure of the zeros, or the transported density $g_\alpha(r)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda_L(n)n^{-\alpha}\bigl(1-\cos(r\log n)\bigr)$, $\alpha>1$, on a grid as noisy data; define the penalised likelihood of Good and Gaskins for the square root of the Thorin density $U_\alpha(z)=g_\alpha(\sqrt z)/(2\pi\sqrt z)$, or for the density of the Thorin variable $H$ with $\mathbb{E}e^{-sH}=e^{b\sqrt s}L(\alpha)/L(\alpha+\sqrt s)$, $b=\frac{L'}{L}(\alpha)$; identify its maximiser, as de Montricher, Tapia and Thompson did for the classical penalised likelihood; and compare its error with that of the Gaussian mean inversion of the transported density on the same input.
results.label: op:lapgg

results.name: Chebotarev as a Dirichlet process for the labelled factorisation of a random integer
results.summary: As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, its prime factorisation labelled by Frobenius classes, normalised, converges to Ferguson's Dirichlet process with Haar measure as base measure, and every Frobenius functional converges to an exponential variable times a Dirichlet mean.
results.statement: Let $Y$ be a compact metric space, $\mu$ a probability measure on $Y$, and $(\theta_p)$ labels in $Y$ attached to the primes and equidistributed with respect to $\mu$ outside a finite set $S$ of primes (for Frobenius classes in a finite Galois group, $\mu$ is the image of Haar measure on the set of conjugacy classes and Chebotarev's theorem supplies the hypothesis). For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma$ be the zeta random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, with prime exponents $e_p$, let $\Xi_\sigma=\sum_{p\notin S}(\sigma-1)e_p\log p\,\delta_{\theta_p}$ be its labelled factorisation, and let $A_\sigma$ be the event that $N_\sigma$ has no prime factor outside $S$. The Dirichlet process with base measure $\mu$ is the random probability measure $\Gamma_\mu/\Gamma_\mu(Y)$, with $\Gamma_\mu$ the Gamma random measure with shape measure $\mu$. As $\sigma\downarrow1$: (i) the normalised labelled factorisation $\mathcal{P}_\sigma=\Xi_\sigma/\Xi_\sigma(Y)$, set equal to $\mu$ on $A_\sigma$, converges in law, as a random probability measure on $Y$ with the weak topology, to the Dirichlet process $P$ with base measure $\mu$, and jointly with it the total mass $\Xi_\sigma(Y)=(\sigma-1)\sum_{p\notin S}e_p\log p$ converges to a standard exponential variable $E$ independent of $P$; (ii) for every continuous $Q\ge0$ on $Y$ the Frobenius functional $\Xi_\sigma(Q)$ converges in law to $E\int_YQ\,dP$, a standard exponential variable times a Dirichlet mean, and for $\lambda\ge0$ \[ \mathbb{E}\exp\Bigl(-\lambda\,E\int_YQ\,dP\Bigr)=\mathbb{E}\Bigl(1+\lambda\int_YQ\,dP\Bigr)^{-1}=\exp\Bigl(-\int_Y\log(1+\lambda Q)\,d\mu\Bigr); \] (iii) for a partition of $Y$ into $\mu$ continuity sets $B_1,\dots,B_k$ with $\mu(B_i)>0$, the shares $\mathcal{P}_\sigma(B_i)$ converge jointly in law to the Dirichlet law with parameters $\mu(B_1),\dots,\mu(B_k)$, so that each share $\mathcal{P}_\sigma(B)$ converges to a Beta variable with parameters $(\mu(B),1-\mu(B))$, of mean $\mu(B)$.
results.label: thm:pddirichlet

results.name: Labelled Ewens family from the random integers weighted by the coefficients of powers of zeta
results.summary: For random integers weighted by the Dirichlet coefficients of a power of the zeta function, the labelled prime factorisation converges to a Gamma random measure and its normalisation to a Dirichlet process, so powers of zeta realise the whole Ewens family with Frobenius labels; the unlabelled limits for this random integer are due to W. Sun (2026).
results.statement: Fix $\vartheta>0$, let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a compact metric space $Y$ and $(\theta_p)$ labels in $Y$ equidistributed with respect to $\mu$ outside a finite set $S$ of primes, and let $d_\vartheta(n)$ be the Dirichlet coefficients of $\zeta(s)^\vartheta$, multiplicative with $d_\vartheta(p^k)=\binom{\vartheta+k-1}{k}$. For $\sigma>1$ let the random integer $N_\sigma^{(\vartheta)}$ have the law $d_\vartheta(n)n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)^\vartheta$, with prime exponents $e_p$, and let $\Xi^{(\vartheta)}_\sigma=\sum_{p\notin S}(\sigma-1)e_p\log p\,\delta_{\theta_p}$ be its labelled factorisation. Then the prime exponents are independent negative binomial variables, $\mathbb{P}(e_p=k)=\binom{\vartheta+k-1}{k}(1-p^{-\sigma})^\vartheta p^{-k\sigma}$, and as $\sigma\downarrow1$: (i) the marked process $\sum_{p\notin S,\,e_p\ge1}\delta_{((\sigma-1)e_p\log p,\,\theta_p)}$ converges in law, vaguely on $(0,\infty)\times Y$, to the Poisson process with intensity $\vartheta x^{-1}e^{-x}dx\otimes\mu$; (ii) the labelled factorisation $\Xi^{(\vartheta)}_\sigma$ converges in law to the Gamma random measure $\Gamma_{\vartheta\mu}$ with shape measure $\vartheta\mu$, its total mass, which is $(\sigma-1)\log N^{(\vartheta)}_\sigma$ up to the primes in $S$, to a Gamma variable with shape $\vartheta$, and the normalised factorisation to the Dirichlet process $\Gamma_{\vartheta\mu}/\Gamma_{\vartheta\mu}(Y)$ with base measure $\vartheta\mu$; (iii) the ranked normalised sizes of the prime factors converge to the Poisson Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(\vartheta)$, and for every continuous $Q\ge0$ on $Y$ the functional $\Xi^{(\vartheta)}_\sigma(Q)$ converges to a generalized gamma convolution with Thorin measure $\vartheta$ times the image of $\mu$ restricted to $\{Q>0\}$ under $1/Q$.
results.label: thm:pdtheta

results.name: Expansion in 1/log x of the Frobenius class of a size biased prime factor of a random integer
results.summary: The probability that a size biased prime factor of a uniform random integer below x has Frobenius in a given conjugacy class is the Chebotarev density plus an explicit term of order 1/log x built from Euler's constant and the Euler Kronecker constant of the class; this is part (ii) of a theorem whose parts on the largest prime factor (Dawsey) and on distinct prime factors (Mertens's theorem per class, after Bardestani and Freiberg) are known.
results.statement: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finite Galois extension with group $G$, let $C\subset G$ be a conjugacy class with $\delta(C)=|C|/|G|$, write $p\in C$ when the Frobenius class of the unramified prime $p$ is $C$, and leave the ramified primes out of every class. Let $n$ be uniform on $\{2,\dots,x\}$ with prime factorisation $n=\prod_pp^{e_p}$, and call a prime factor $p$ of $n$ chosen with probability $e_p\log p/\log n$ a size biased prime factor. By the prime number theorem for $K$ in the form $\pi_C(t)=\delta(C)\operatorname{li}(t)+O\bigl(t\exp(-a_K\sqrt{\log t})\bigr)$ of Lagarias and Odlyzko, with $\pi_C(t)$ the number of primes $p\le t$ in $C$ and $a_K>0$ a constant depending on $K$, the limit $c_C=\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigl(\sum_{p\le t,\,p\in C}\frac{\log p}{p}-\delta(C)\log t\bigr)$ exists. Let $\kappa_C=-c_C-\sum_{p\in C}\frac{\log p}{p(p-1)}$, which by the Abelian theorem is the Euler Kronecker drift of the class $C$ for the set of ramified primes, so that $\sum_C\bigl(\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}\delta(C)-\kappa_C\bigr)=-\sum_{p\text{ ramified}}\frac{\log p}{p-1}$, with $\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}$ Euler's constant. Then, as $x\to\infty$, the size biased prime factor lies in $C$ with probability \[ \delta(C)+\frac{\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}\delta(C)-\kappa_C}{\log x-1}+O\bigl((\log x)^{-2}\bigr). \]
results.label: thm:pdmertens

results.name: Asymptotic independence of the Frobenius class and the share of a size biased prime factor
results.summary: The share of a size biased prime factor of a random integer is asymptotically uniform, as Donnelly and Grimmett showed, and asymptotically independent of its Frobenius class, which follows the Chebotarev densities, both for uniform integers below x and for the zeta random integer.
results.statement: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finite Galois extension with group $G$, and for a conjugacy class $C$ of $G$ let $\delta(C)=|C|/|G|$. Let $n$ be uniform on $\{2,\dots,x\}$ with prime factorisation $n=\prod_pp^{e_p}$, let $p^*$ be a size biased prime factor of $n$, chosen with probability $e_p\log p/\log n$, and let $F^*=e_{p^*}\log p^*/\log n$ be its share. As $x\to\infty$, $p^*$ is unramified with probability tending to $1$, and the pair $(F^*,\text{Frobenius class of }p^*)$ converges in law to the product of the uniform law on $(0,1)$ and the law $C\mapsto\delta(C)$ on the conjugacy classes. The same holds for the zeta random integer $N_\sigma$, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, as $\sigma\downarrow1$, for a finite set $S$ of primes containing the ramified ones: off the event $A_\sigma$ that $N_\sigma$ has no prime factor outside $S$, pick $p^*$ among the prime factors of $N_\sigma$ outside $S$, with probability proportional to $e_p\log p$, $e_p$ now the exponent of $p$ in $N_\sigma$, and take its share relative to their part $\sum_{p\notin S}e_p\log p$ of $\log N_\sigma$.
results.label: thm:pdsizebiased

results.name: Empty Chebotarev classes and a lower bound for the rate of the Dirichlet process limit
results.summary: For the zeta random integer with parameter close to one, a Frobenius class is empty with probability of exact order a power of the distance to one, the exponent being the Chebotarev density of the class and the constant an explicit classical one, and this atom at zero bounds from below the Kolmogorov distance between the share of the class and its Beta limit; these are parts (i) and (ii) of a theorem whose part (iii) is a case of Serre's theorem on frobenian sets.
results.statement:
Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finite Galois extension with nontrivial group $G$, $S$ the set of ramified primes, $C$ a conjugacy class with $\delta(C)=|C|/|G|$, and $\delta_{\min}=\min_C\delta(C)$. For $\sigma>1$ let $N_\sigma$ be the zeta random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, with prime exponents $e_p$; let $L_C(\sigma)=(\sigma-1)\sum_{p
otin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}e_p\log p$ be the mass of the class $C$; let $A_\sigma$ be the event that $N_\sigma$ has no prime factor outside $S$; and let $\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C)$ be the share of $C$, equal to $L_C(\sigma)/\sum_{C'}L_{C'}(\sigma)$ off $A_\sigma$ and to $\delta(C)$ on $A_\sigma$. Let $P_C(s)=\sum_{p
otin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}\sum_{m\ge1}p^{-ms}/m$; the function $h_C(s)=P_C(s)-\delta(C)\log rac1{s-1}$ is real analytic near $s=1$, and $h_C(1)=b_C-\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}\delta(C)+\sum_{p
otin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}\sum_{m\ge2} rac{p^{-m}}{m}$, where $b_C=\lim_{t	o\infty} igl(\sum_{p\le t,\,p
otin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C} rac1p-\delta(C)\log\log t igr)$ and $\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}$ is Euler's constant. (i) $\mathbb{P}(L_C(\sigma)=0)=e^{-P_C(\sigma)}=e^{-h_C(1)}(\sigma-1)^{\delta(C)} igl(1+O(\sigma-1) igr)$. (ii) The Kolmogorov distance between the law of $\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C)$ and its limit $\mathrm{Beta}(\delta(C),1-\delta(C))$ is at least \[ \mathbb{P}(L_C(\sigma)=0)-\mathbb{P}(A_\sigma)=e^{-h_C(1)}(\sigma-1)^{\delta(C)} igl(1+o(1) igr), \] hence at least of order $(\sigma-1)^{\delta_{\min}}$ for the smallest class.
results.label: thm:pdrate

results.name: Ewens parameters of Euler products are pole orders
results.summary: For a random integer weighted by an Euler product whose logarithm has nonnegative coefficients, given at the primes by a continuous function of equidistributed labels, the normalised labelled factorisation converges to a Dirichlet process with the weighted equidistribution measure as base measure, and the Poisson Dirichlet parameter is the exponent of the singularity at s equal to one, the order of the pole when there is one; the unlabelled Poisson Dirichlet limits for weighted integers below x are due to Elboim and Gorodetsky (2024), and for arithmetic semigroups to Arratia, Kochman and Miller (2014).
results.statement: Let $D(s)=\sum_na(n)n^{-s}=\exp\bigl(\sum_p\sum_{m\ge1}w_m(p)p^{-ms}/m\bigr)$ be an Euler product with $w_m(p)\ge0$ bounded, and suppose the labels $(\theta_p)$ are equidistributed with respect to a probability measure $\mu$ on a compact metric space $Y$ and $w_1(p)=w(\theta_p)$ outside a finite set $S$ of primes, for a continuous $w\ge0$ on $Y$ with $\int w\,d\mu>0$. For $\sigma>1$ let $N^D_\sigma$ have the law $a(n)n^{-\sigma}/D(\sigma)$, with prime exponents $e_p$. Then the prime exponents of $N^D_\sigma$ are independent, $e_p=\sum_mmM(p^m)$ with independent Poisson variables $M(p^m)$ of means $w_m(p)p^{-m\sigma}/m$, and as $\sigma\downarrow1$ the labelled factorisation $\sum_{p\notin S}(\sigma-1)e_p\log p\,\delta_{\theta_p}$ converges in law to the Gamma random measure with shape measure $w\mu$, the normalised factorisation to the Dirichlet process with base measure $w\mu$, and the ranked normalised sizes of the prime factors to the Poisson Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(\vartheta)$ with \[ \vartheta=\int_Yw\,d\mu=\lim_{s\downarrow1}\frac{\log D(s)}{\log\frac1{s-1}}, \] the order of the pole of $D$ at $s=1$ when $D$ continues meromorphically. In particular, for $D=L(s,\rho\otimes\check\rho)$ with $\rho$ an Artin representation, $w=|\chi_\rho|^2$ and $\vartheta=\langle\rho,\rho\rangle$, the shape of the Gamma limit of the Rankin Selberg random integer; and for $D=\zeta_K$ with $K/\mathbb{Q}$ of degree $n$ and Galois closure of group $G$ acting on the $n$ embeddings, $w(g)$ is the number of fixed points of $g$ and $\vartheta=1$ by Burnside's lemma.
results.label: thm:pdewens

results.name: Upper bound for the rate of the Dirichlet process limit of Chebotarev shares
results.summary: Asks for an upper bound matching the lower bound for the Kolmogorov distance between the share of a Frobenius class in a zeta random integer and its Beta limit, and for a Wasserstein bound on the share vector at the rate at which the means converge.
results.statement: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finite Galois extension with nontrivial group $G$ and set of ramified primes $S$, let $C$ run over the conjugacy classes, with $\delta(C)=|C|/|G|$ and $\delta_{\min}=\min_C\delta(C)$, and for the zeta random integer $N_\sigma$, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, with prime exponents $e_p$, let $\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C)$ be the share of the class $C$, the proportion of $\sum_{p\notin S}e_p\log p$ carried by the primes with Frobenius in $C$ (set to $\delta(C)$ when $N_\sigma$ has no prime factor outside $S$). As $\sigma\downarrow1$ the vector of shares converges to the Dirichlet law with parameters $\delta(C)$, and in the Kolmogorov distance of the shares the limit is approached no faster than $(\sigma-1)^{\delta_{\min}}$. Prove the matching upper bound: that the Kolmogorov distance between the law of $\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C)$ and $\mathrm{Beta}(\delta(C),1-\delta(C))$ is $O\bigl((\sigma-1)^{\delta(C)}\bigr)$, and that, for the Euclidean distance between share vectors, the Wasserstein distance between the laws of $(\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C))_C$ and of its Dirichlet limit is $O\bigl((\sigma-1)\log\frac1{\sigma-1}\bigr)$, the order at which the means converge.
results.label: op:pdrate

results.name: Signs of the Mertens deficits of the identity class in symmetric group fields
results.summary: Asks how the sign of the deficit of the identity Frobenius class among the distinct prime factors of random integers is distributed over number fields with symmetric Galois group ordered by discriminant, and along families of trinomials.
results.statement:
For a finite Galois extension $K/\mathbb{Q}$ with group $G$ and set of ramified primes $S$, the Mertens constants per class $b_C=\lim_{t	o\infty} igl(\sum_{p\le t,\,p
otin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C} rac1p-\delta(C)\log\log t igr)$ and $c_C=\lim_{t	o\infty} igl(\sum_{p\le t,\,p
otin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C} rac{\log p}{p}-\delta(C)\log t igr)$, with $\delta(C)=|C|/|G|$, are expressed through the values $L(1,\chi)$ and $ rac{L'}{L}(1,\chi)$ of the Artin L functions of the irreducible characters $\chi$ of $G$. For the splitting field of a polynomial of degree $n$ with group $S_n$, the deficit of the identity class, which governs the share of that class among the distinct unramified prime factors of a uniform random integer, is $b_{\{1\}}-\delta(\{1\})B'=\lim_{t	o\infty}\sum_{p\le t,\,p
otin S} igl(\mathsf{1}_{\{1\}}(\mathrm{Frob}_p)-\delta(\{1\}) igr)/p$, where $B'=B-\sum_{p\in S}1/p$ and $B$ is the Mertens constant; it is negative for $x^3-x-1$, whose smallest completely split prime is $59$. A prime $p<n$ splits completely only if it divides the index of $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$, with $\alpha$ a root of the polynomial, and this happens: in Dedekind's field of $x^3-x^2-2x-8$ the prime $2$ splits completely and adds $ rac5{12}$ to the sum. Read from the primes below $10^7$, the deficit is positive for Dedekind's field and for $x^3-x+15$, in which $3$ and $5$ split completely, so both signs occur already with group $S_3$. Determine the distribution of the sign of the deficit over the fields with group $S_n$ ordered by discriminant, and its sign along a family such as $x^n-x-1$. This is the analogue, for the weights $1/p$, of the problem of the signs of the Euler Kronecker drifts.
results.label: op:pdmertens

results.name: An arithmetic operation realising the product closure of generalized gamma convolutions
results.summary: Asks which operation on representations or L functions, if any, realises Bondesson's closure of generalized gamma convolutions under products of independent variables for the limits of Frobenius functionals.
results.statement: For a finite Galois extension with labels $\theta_p$ the Frobenius classes, equidistributed with respect to the image $\mu$ of Haar measure, and the zeta random integer $N_\sigma$, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, with prime exponents $e_p$, the Frobenius functional of a function $Q\ge0$ on the classes is $\Xi_\sigma(Q)=(\sigma-1)\sum_{p}e_p\log p\,Q(\theta_p)$, the sum over the unramified primes; as $\sigma\downarrow1$ it converges to a generalized gamma convolution with Thorin measure the image of $\mu$ restricted to $\{Q>0\}$ under $1/Q$. By Bondesson the product of two independent generalized gamma convolution variables is a generalized gamma convolution, so the product of independent copies of the limits of $\Xi_\sigma(Q_1)$ and $\Xi_\sigma(Q_2)$ is one, with a Thorin measure $\tau_{Q_1,Q_2}$. Multiplying Dirichlet series realises the additive closure, the Frobenius functional of the product of two independent random integers being the sum of two independent ones, and tensor products, as in Rankin Selberg convolution, give the functional of $Q_1Q_2$. Find the arithmetic operation, if any, that realises the multiplicative closure, a representation or an L function whose Frobenius functional has Thorin measure $\tau_{Q_1,Q_2}$; and compute $\tau_{Q_1,Q_2}$ for $Q_1=Q_2=\operatorname{tr}^2$, the squared trace of the two dimensional irreducible representation of $S_3$. For a finite group the Thorin measure of a limiting Frobenius functional is finitely supported and that of such a product is not, so the operation, if any, leads to an infinite label space, such as a Sato Tate group.
results.label: op:pdproduct

results.name: Complex multiplication doubles the Gamma shape of the Rankin Selberg subordinator
results.summary: Over its CM field the Rankin Selberg Euler product of an elliptic curve with complex multiplication is exactly the square of its Euler product over the rationals, so the limiting Gamma shape of the associated subordinator doubles from 1 to 2, while a curve without complex multiplication by that field keeps shape 1, which gives an unconditional test for complex multiplication.
results.statement: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve of conductor $N_E$, $\rho$ its normalised $\ell$ adic representation, $K$ an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant $d_K$ and $\chi_K$ its quadratic character. For $\sigma > 1$ let $X_\sigma$ be the Rankin Selberg subordinator of $\rho$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, the nonnegative random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda X_\sigma} = D^S(\sigma+\lambda)/D^S(\sigma)$, $\lambda \ge 0$, where $D^S(s) = L^S(s,\rho\otimes\check\rho)$ is the Rankin Selberg L function with the Euler factors at the primes dividing $N_E d_K$ removed, and let $X^K_\sigma$ be the same subordinator built over $K$, with Laplace transform $D^S_K(\sigma+\lambda)/D^S_K(\sigma)$, where $D^S_K(s) = L^S_K(s,\rho|_K\otimes\check\rho|_K)$ is the Euler product over the primes of $K$ not dividing $N_E d_K$ attached to the restriction of $\rho$ to $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/K)$. (i) $D^S_K(s) = D^S(s)\,L^S(s,\rho\otimes\check\rho\otimes\chi_K)$, the partial products being over the primes not dividing $N_E d_K$. (ii) If $E$ has complex multiplication by $K$ then $D^S_K(s) = D^S(s)^2$ exactly, so that $X^K_\sigma$ has the law of the sum of two independent copies of $X_\sigma$ for every $\sigma > 1$, and $(\sigma-1)X^K_\sigma$ converges in law as $\sigma \downarrow 1$ to the Gamma law of shape $2$ and scale $1$. (iii) If $E$ has no complex multiplication by $K$ then $(\sigma-1)X^K_\sigma$ converges in law as $\sigma \downarrow 1$ to the standard exponential law, the Gamma shape being $1$.
results.label: thm:gl1cmshape

results.name: Thorin form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for a real Dirichlet character
results.summary: For a real primitive Dirichlet character whose L function does not vanish at the centre, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to a generalized gamma convolution representation of the completed L function with Thorin measure on the squared heights of the zeros, and a shifted representation holds unconditionally; this reformulates the hypothesis and does not prove it.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a primitive real Dirichlet character modulo $q \ge 3$ and $\kappa \in \{0,1\}$ its parity, so that $\Lambda(s,\chi) = (q/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+\kappa}{2})L(s,\chi)$ satisfies $\Lambda(s,\chi) = \Lambda(1-s,\chi)$. Put $\Xi_\chi(w) = \Lambda(\frac12+w,\chi)$, an even entire function of order one, and write its zeros, with multiplicity, as the pairs $\pm i\gamma_k$, one $\gamma_k$ taken from each pair (only $\gamma_k^2$ enters below). Suppose $L(\frac12,\chi) \ne 0$. Then $\Xi_\chi(\sqrt\lambda)/\Xi_\chi(0) = \prod_k(1+\lambda/\gamma_k^2)$ for $\lambda \ge 0$, the product converging absolutely, and the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ holds if and only if $\lambda \mapsto \Xi_\chi(0)/\Xi_\chi(\sqrt\lambda)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, in which case the Thorin measure is $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$ and the generalized gamma convolution is $\sum_k E_k/\gamma_k^2$ with $E_k$ independent standard exponential random variables. Moreover, without assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis, for every $a \ge \frac12$ (basepoint $\frac12+a \ge 1$) the function $V_a(z) = \operatorname{Re}(\Xi_\chi'/\Xi_\chi)(a+i\sqrt z)/(2\pi\sqrt z)$, $z > 0$, is nonnegative and $\Xi_\chi(a)/\Xi_\chi(a+\sqrt\lambda) = \mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda H_a}$ for $\lambda > 0$, where $H_a$ is a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin density $V_a$.
results.label: thm:gl1thorin

results.name: Limit law for the discrepancy of the Hecke angles of Gaussian primes
results.summary: Asks whether the normalised discrepancy of the Hecke angles of Gaussian primes has a limit law, the Kolmogorov law that a Brownian bridge predicts or a different law forced by arithmetic, and the same for the other imaginary quadratic fields of class number one.
results.statement: For a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ write $p = \pi\bar\pi$ with $\pi$ a primary Gaussian prime ($\pi \equiv 1$ modulo $2+2i$) and let $\theta_p = |\arg\pi| \in [0,\pi]$; by Hecke's theorem the angles $4\theta_p$ are equidistributed modulo $2\pi$. Let $\pi_1(x)$ be the number of primes $p \le x$ with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and $D(x)$ the discrepancy of the angles $4\theta_p$, $p \le x$, from the uniform law. Determine whether $\sqrt{\pi_1(x)}\,D(x)$ has a limit law as $x \to \infty$ (the Kolmogorov law would be the Brownian bridge prediction, as for the discrepancy of Sato Tate angles), or whether the arithmetic of the Hecke L functions $L(s,\lambda_k)$, $\lambda_k((\alpha)) = (\alpha/|\alpha|)^{4k}$, forces a different law; and the same question for the imaginary quadratic fields of class number one.
results.label: op:gl1disc

results.name: Euler Kronecker constants of Hecke characters and the rate of the Gaussian prime Dirichlet process
results.summary: Asks for the constants that govern how fast the Dirichlet process of Gaussian prime angles is approached, the sign pattern of the deficits of arcs, and an analogue for arcs of the theorem on atoms at zero.
results.statement: Let $N_\sigma$ be the zeta distributed random integer, $\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = n) = n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)$, and colour each prime factor $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ by its Hecke angle $4\theta_p$ on the circle, where $\theta_p = |\arg\pi|$ for a primary Gaussian prime $\pi$ dividing $p$; as $\sigma \downarrow 1$ the labelled factorisation converges to a Dirichlet process whose base measure is $\frac12$ times the uniform probability on the circle. The rate of convergence of this Dirichlet process is governed, for the means, by the constants $(L'/L)(1,\lambda_k)$ of the Hecke L functions of the characters $\lambda_k((\alpha)) = (\alpha/|\alpha|)^{4k}$ of $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, in the same way that the drift of the Frobenius Gamma process of a finite Galois extension is governed by Euler Kronecker constants. Compute these constants for $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ and $k \le 20$, determine the sign pattern of the deficits of the arcs (the differences between the mean shares of the arcs and their limiting values), and find the analogue for the circle, where no arc is a finite union of classes, of the theorem giving the atoms at zero and a lower bound for the rate of convergence of the shares of the classes.
results.label: op:gl1rate

results.name: An effective Gamma shape test for complex multiplication
results.summary: Asks for an explicit bound on the number of primes after which the empirical Gamma shape provably decides whether an elliptic curve has complex multiplication by a given field.
results.statement: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve of conductor $N_E$ with normalised $\ell$ adic representation $\rho$, $K$ an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant $d_K$ with quadratic character $\chi_K$, and $X^K_\sigma$ the Rankin Selberg subordinator of $\rho$ over $K$, the nonnegative random variable with Laplace transform $D^S_K(\sigma+\lambda)/D^S_K(\sigma)$, where $D^S_K(s) = L^S_K(s,\rho|_K\otimes\check\rho|_K)$ is the Rankin Selberg Euler product over the primes of $K$ not dividing $N_E d_K$ attached to the restriction $\rho|_K$ of $\rho$ to $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/K)$, so that as $\sigma \downarrow 1$ the law of $(\sigma-1)X^K_\sigma$ tends to the Gamma law of shape $2$ if $E$ has complex multiplication by $K$ and of shape $1$ otherwise. By Faltings' theorem finitely many $a_p$ determine $\rho$ up to isomorphism, so finitely many primes decide whether $\rho\otimes\chi_K \cong \rho$. Find an explicit bound, in terms of $N_E$ and $d_K$, on the primes needed so that the empirical Laplace transform of $(\sigma-1)X^K_\sigma$ at a suitable $\sigma$ separates shape $1$ from shape $2$ with a proof, and compare with the bound from the effective Chebotarev theorem.
results.label: op:gl1cm

results.name: Ramanujan conjecture at a prime as local Thorin positivity for Maass forms
results.summary: A normalised Euler factor of a Hecke Maass form at a prime, read in the square root of the Laplace variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, and then of a generalized gamma convolution with an explicit Thorin comb, exactly when the Hecke eigenvalue obeys the Ramanujan bound with the value 2 excluded, which restates the Ramanujan conjecture at that prime without proving it.
results.statement: Let $u$ be a Hecke Maass eigenform with Hecke eigenvalue $\lambda(p)$ at the prime $p$, and $L_p(s,u) = (1-\lambda(p)p^{-s}+p^{-2s})^{-1}$ its Euler factor at $p$. The function $s \mapsto \frac{2-\lambda(p)}{p^{\sqrt s}+p^{-\sqrt s}-\lambda(p)} = (2-\lambda(p))\,p^{-\sqrt s}L_p(\sqrt s,u)$, $s > 0$, is the Laplace transform of a probability law on $[0,\infty)$ if and only if $-2 \le \lambda(p) < 2$, in which case, writing $\lambda(p) = 2\cos\theta_p$ with $0 < \theta_p \le \pi$, the law is the generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure (Thorin comb) $\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{t_k}$, $t_k = ((\theta_p+2\pi k)/\log p)^2$. In particular the Ramanujan conjecture $|\lambda(p)| \le 2$ at $p$ (with $\lambda(p) \ne 2$) holds if and only if the local factor of $u$ at $p$ is a generalized gamma convolution transform in the variable $\sqrt s$.
results.label: cor:msramanujan

results.name: Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture is equivalent to complete monotonicity of the Maass cusp form heat trace
results.summary: Proves an equivalence and not the conjecture, which is open in general, namely that Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture for a congruence subgroup holds if and only if the heat trace of its Maass cusp forms, with every eigenvalue lowered by one quarter, is completely monotone; unconditionally it proves complete monotonicity only with the eigenvalues lowered by the smaller amount that the Kim Sarnak bound allows, for every congruence subgroup (part ii), and the full statement for SL(2, Z), where the conjecture is known (part iii), while Weyl's law keeps the spectrum from being a Thorin measure.
results.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a congruence subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, let $\lambda_j = \frac14+r_j^2$, $j \ge 1$, be the Laplace eigenvalues of the Maass cusp forms on $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$, and let $\Theta_\Gamma(t) = \sum_{j\ge1}e^{-t\lambda_j}$ be their heat trace. (i) $e^{t/4}\Theta_\Gamma(t) = \sum_j e^{-tr_j^2}$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$ if and only if $\lambda_j \ge \frac14$ for every $j$, that is if and only if Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture holds for $\Gamma$; in that case its Bernstein measure is $\sum_j\delta_{r_j^2}$. (ii) Unconditionally, $e^{t(\frac14-(7/64)^2)}\Theta_\Gamma(t)$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$. (iii) For $\Gamma = \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ the equivalent conditions of (i) hold, and $\sum_j e^{-tr_j^2} \sim \frac{1}{12t}$ as $t \to 0$. (iv) The measure $\sum_j\delta_{r_j^2}$ is not a Thorin measure, since $\sum_j r_j^{-2} = \infty$. Part (i) is an equivalence and does not prove Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture, which is open in general; part (ii) rests on the bound $\lambda_j \ge \frac14-(\frac{7}{64})^2$ of Kim and Sarnak, valid for every congruence subgroup, and part (iii) on the fact that every cuspidal eigenvalue of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ exceeds $\frac14$.
results.label: thm:mscm

results.name: Thorin representation of the geodesic Euler product Z(s+1)/Z(s)
results.summary: At every basepoint to the right of 1, the ratio of values of the geodesic Euler product Z(s+1)/Z(s) of a compact hyperbolic surface or of the modular surface, read in the square root of the Laplace variable, is unconditionally the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution with an explicit nonnegative Thorin density divided by that of a one half stable law, and the same holds for Dedekind zeta functions and for the Rankin Selberg L function of an automorphic representation with its contragredient.
results.statement: Let $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$ be a compact hyperbolic surface, with primitive closed geodesics $P$ of length $\ell(P)$ and norm $N(P) = e^{\ell(P)}$, Selberg zeta function $Z(s) = \prod_P\prod_{k\ge0}(1-N(P)^{-(s+k)})$, and $R(s) = Z(s+1)/Z(s) = \prod_P(1-N(P)^{-s})^{-1}$ for $\operatorname{Re}s > 1$. Let $\alpha > 1$. Then for $\lambda > 0$, $R(\alpha)/R(\alpha+\sqrt\lambda) = e^{-b\sqrt\lambda}\,\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda H}$ with $b = (R'/R)(\alpha) = -\sum_P\sum_{k\ge1}\ell(P)N(P)^{-k\alpha}$, where $H$ is a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin density $U(z) = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt z}\sum_P\sum_{k\ge1}\ell(P)N(P)^{-k\alpha}\,2\sin^2\bigl(\frac{k\ell(P)\sqrt z}{2}\bigr) \ge 0$, equal to $(\operatorname{Re}(R'/R)(\alpha+i\sqrt z)-b)/(2\pi\sqrt z)$. The same holds for the modular surface $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$, and for the Dedekind zeta function of any number field and the Rankin Selberg L function $L(s,\pi\times\tilde\pi)$ of an automorphic representation $\pi$ and its contragredient $\tilde\pi$, whose logarithmic coefficients are nonnegative, with the primes of the field or the Rankin Selberg coefficients in place of the geodesics.
results.label: thm:msthorin

results.name: Poisson Dirichlet limit for random geodesic integers
results.summary: A random product of closed geodesics drawn with zeta type weights near the pole behaves like a random integer, with Gamma process and Poisson Dirichlet limits, Dickman's law for the largest factor and a normal law for the number of distinct factors.
results.statement: Let the geodesic integers $\mathfrak n$ be the elements of the free abelian monoid generated by the primitive closed geodesics $P$ of a compact hyperbolic surface or of the modular surface, with the multiplicative norm $N(\mathfrak n)$ extending $N(P) = e^{\ell(P)}$, $\ell(P)$ the length, and let $R(\sigma) = \sum_{\mathfrak n}N(\mathfrak n)^{-\sigma} = Z(\sigma+1)/Z(\sigma)$ for $\sigma > 1$, $Z$ the Selberg zeta function. Let $\mathfrak n_\sigma$ be the random geodesic integer with $\mathbb{P}(\mathfrak n_\sigma = \mathfrak n) = N(\mathfrak n)^{-\sigma}/R(\sigma)$. Its exponents $e_P$ are independent geometric variables with $\mathbb{P}(e_P \ge k) = N(P)^{-k\sigma}$, and as $\sigma \downarrow 1$ the point process of the rescaled sizes $(\sigma-1)e_P\ell(P)$ converges to the Poisson process with intensity $x^{-1}e^{-x}\,dx$, the Gamma process; the ranked normalised sizes $e_P\ell(P)/\log N(\mathfrak n_\sigma)$ converge in law to the Poisson Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(1)$; the normalised size of the largest primitive geodesic factor has Dickman's law in the limit; and the number of distinct primitive factors is asymptotically normal with mean and variance $\log\frac{1}{\sigma-1}$.
results.label: thm:mspd

results.name: Thorin representation of the geodesic Euler product at the centre
results.summary: Asks whether, closer to the centre of the critical strip, the geodesic Euler product of a compact surface still has a positive Thorin density once its pole is removed, despite divergent spectral sums.
results.statement: Let $R(s) = Z(s+1)/Z(s)$ for a compact hyperbolic surface with Selberg zeta function $Z$, and $R^*(s) = (s-1)R(s)$. Determine for which $a \in (0,\frac12)$ the function $\lambda \mapsto R^*(\frac12+a)/R^*(\frac12+a+\sqrt\lambda)$ is, after removal of a drift factor $e^{|b|\sqrt\lambda}$ for a suitable real constant $b$, the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, and compute its Thorin density numerically for the Bolza surface or for a Hurwitz surface of small genus, where the spectrum and the geodesics are both available. The question is whether the logarithmic divergences coming from the Laplace spectrum, whose spectral parameters $r_j$ (eigenvalues $\frac14+r_j^2$) satisfy $\sum_j r_j^{-2} = \infty$, cancel into a positive density.
results.label: op:mscentre

results.name: A Chebotarev theorem for the closed geodesics of the modular surface
results.summary: Asks for the densities of arithmetic labels of the closed geodesics of the modular surface ordered by length, and for the matching Dirichlet process limit and Mertens constants.
results.statement: Order the primitive closed geodesics $P$ of the modular surface $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$ by norm $N(P) = e^{\ell(P)}$, $\ell(P)$ the length (they correspond to the narrow classes of primitive binary quadratic forms of positive nonsquare discriminant $d$), and colour each by the residue of its discriminant $d$ modulo $q$, or by whether $d$ is fundamental. Determine the densities of the colours, prove the Dirichlet process limit as $\sigma \downarrow 1$, with that base measure, of the labelled factorisation of the random geodesic integer $\mathfrak n_\sigma$, where the geodesic integers $\mathfrak n$ are the finite products of primitive geodesics with the multiplicative norm $N(\mathfrak n)$, $R(\sigma) = \sum_{\mathfrak n}N(\mathfrak n)^{-\sigma}$ for $\sigma > 1$, and $\mathbb{P}(\mathfrak n_\sigma = \mathfrak n) = N(\mathfrak n)^{-\sigma}/R(\sigma)$, and identify the analogue of the values $L(1,\chi)$ in the Mertens constants.
results.label: op:mschebotarev

results.name: Even icosahedral Artin representations and Maass forms of eigenvalue one quarter
results.summary: Proposes testing numerically the complete monotonicity of the Galois heat trace of an even icosahedral Artin representation and searching for the Maass form of eigenvalue one quarter that Artin's conjecture predicts.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be an even icosahedral two dimensional Artin representation of conductor $N$ (even meaning $\det\rho(c) = 1$ for complex conjugation $c$) with $\rho(c) = I$ and trivial determinant, so that $\rho$ is self dual, the case in which its heat trace is computed with the gamma factor of a Maass form. Compute from its Frobenius traces the Galois heat trace $\mathcal{W}^+_\rho(x)$, $x > 0$, the explicit formula expression built from $N$, the gamma factor $\Gamma_\mathbb{R}(s)^2$ of a Maass form of eigenvalue $\frac14$ ($\Gamma_\mathbb{R}(s) = \pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$) and the traces $\operatorname{tr}\rho(\mathrm{Frob}_p)$, which equals half the sum of $e^{-x\gamma^2}$ over the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of the completed L function $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ when $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ is entire, and which is completely monotone if and only if $\Lambda(s,\rho)$ is entire and all its zeros lie on $\operatorname{Re}s = \frac12$; test its complete monotonicity numerically; and search by Hejhal's algorithm for a Maass form of eigenvalue $\frac14$ on $\Gamma_0(N)$ whose Hecke eigenvalues are $\operatorname{tr}\rho(\mathrm{Frob}_p)$. A single such form would be the first even icosahedral instance of reciprocity; the computation is within reach for the smallest conductors.
results.label: op:mseven

results.name: Cutoff for Brownian motion on the principal congruence covers X(N)
results.summary: Asks whether Brownian motion on the principal congruence covers of the modular surface mixes abruptly, with cutoff at a time of order log N as for random walks on expanders, and how the cusps affect the profile.
results.statement: Let $X(N) = \Gamma(N)\backslash\mathbb{H}$ be the principal congruence cover of level $N$ of the modular surface, whose area grows like $N^3$ while its first nonzero Laplace eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ stays bounded below by $\frac{975}{4096} = \frac14-(\frac{7}{64})^2$, the bound of Kim and Sarnak. Determine whether Brownian motion on $X(N)$ started at a fixed point exhibits cutoff in total variation at a time of order $\log N$, as random walks on expander graphs do, and how the cusps, whose number grows with $N$, affect the profile.
results.label: op:mscutoff

results.name: Product formula of the Dedekind eta function as the distribution function of a maximum of exponential clocks
results.summary: The infinite product in the Dedekind eta function, read on the imaginary axis, is the distribution function of the maximum of independent exponential clocks with rates proportional to the positive integers, with explicit tails and a density given by the weight two Eisenstein series.
results.statement: Let $E_1,E_2,\ldots$ be independent standard exponential variables, let $M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)$, and let $P(y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})$ for $y>0$, so that the Dedekind eta function $\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)$, $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, satisfies $\eta(iy)=e^{-\pi y/12}P(y)$. The variable $M$ is almost surely finite and positive, and $\mathbb{P}(M\le y)=P(y)$ for $y>0$. The function $P$ is continuous and strictly increasing, and $1-P(y)\sim e^{-2\pi y}$ as $y\to\infty$, while $P(y)\sim y^{-1/2}e^{-\pi/(12y)}$ as $y\to0$. The density of $M$ is $\frac{2\pi}{24}\bigl(1-E_2(iy)\bigr)P(y)$, where $E_2(\tau)=1-24\sum_{N\ge1}\sigma(N)q^N$, with $\sigma(N)$ the sum of the divisors of $N$, is the quasimodular Eisenstein series of weight two.
results.label: prop:ch11M

results.name: Extreme value representation of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta
results.summary: At every complex point the L function of Ramanujan's Delta function equals the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at a maximum of independent exponential clocks, and at positive real points it is the probability that an independent gamma variable beats that maximum.
results.statement: Let $E_{j,n}$ ($1\le j\le24$, $n\ge1$) be independent standard exponential variables and $M^*=\max_{j\le24,\,n\ge1}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)$, so that $\mathbb{P}(M^*\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})^{24}$ for $y>0$. For complex $s$ and $c>0$ let $Q(s,c)=\Gamma(s,c)/\Gamma(s)=\Gamma(s)^{-1}\int_c^\infty t^{s-1}e^{-t}\,dt$ be the regularised upper incomplete gamma function, which is entire in $s$ and vanishes at $s=0,-1,-2,\ldots$. Let $\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, be Ramanujan's cusp form of weight $12$, and $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ its $L$ function, continued to an entire function. For every complex $s$, $L(s,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[Q(s,2\pi M^*)\bigr]$. For real $s>0$, equivalently, $L(s,\Delta)=\mathbb{P}(G_s\ge2\pi M^*)$, where $G_s$ has the gamma law of shape $s$ and unit rate and is independent of $M^*$.
results.label: thm:ch11main

results.name: L values of Ramanujan's Delta at positive real points lie strictly between 0 and 1
results.summary: Every value of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta function at a positive real point lies strictly between zero and one, being the probability of an event that has positive probability together with its complement.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, be Ramanujan's cusp form of weight $12$, and $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ its $L$ function, continued to an entire function. For real $s>0$, $0<L(s,\Delta)<1$.
results.label: cor:ch11bounds

results.name: Strict monotonicity of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta on the positive real axis
results.summary: On the positive real axis the L function of Ramanujan's Delta function increases strictly and tends to one, proved by a coupling of gamma variables.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, be Ramanujan's cusp form of weight $12$, and $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$ its $L$ function, continued to an entire function. On $s>0$, $L(s,\Delta)$ is strictly increasing, and $L(s,\Delta)\uparrow1$ as $s\to\infty$.
results.label: cor:ch11monotone

results.name: Modularity of Ramanujan's Delta as self similarity of an extreme value law
results.summary: The modular transformation of Ramanujan's Delta function becomes an exact self similarity of the law of the maximum of exponential clocks behind it, which exchanges the two tails of that law.
