results.statement: Let $E_{j,n}$ ($1\le j\le24$, $n\ge1$) be independent standard exponential variables, $M^*=\max_{j\le24,\,n\ge1}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)$, and $F(y)=\mathbb{P}(M^*\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})^{24}$ for $y>0$, so that Ramanujan's cusp form $\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}$, $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, satisfies $\Delta(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}F(y)$. For all $y>0$, $F(y)=y^{-12}e^{2\pi(y-1/y)}F(1/y)$. Consequently $F(y)\sim y^{-12}e^{-2\pi/y}$ as $y\to0$, and $1-F(y)\sim24e^{-2\pi y}$ as $y\to\infty$.
results.label: prop:ch11selfsim

results.name: Pólya kernel of Ramanujan's Delta as a Bayesian posterior
results.summary: The Pólya kernel of Ramanujan's Delta function is the law of the logarithm of a gamma variable of shape six and rate two pi, conditioned to exceed the maximum of exponential clocks behind Delta, so its moment generating function is a ratio of completed L values.
results.statement: Let $E_{j,n}$ ($1\le j\le24$, $n\ge1$) be independent standard exponential variables and $M^*=\max_{j\le24,\,n\ge1}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)$, let $G_6$ have the gamma law of shape $6$ and unit rate, independent of $M^*$, and let $W=\log(G_6/2\pi)$. Let $\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}$, $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, be Ramanujan's cusp form of weight $12$, let $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)=\int_0^\infty\Delta(iy)y^{s-1}\,dy$ be its completed $L$ function, and let $\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)$, $u\in\mathbb{R}$, be its P\'olya kernel. Conditionally on $\{G_6\ge2\pi M^*\}$, $W$ has density $\Phi_\Delta$, and for every complex $z$, $\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)/\Lambda(6,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{zW}\bigm|G_6\ge2\pi M^*\bigr]$.
results.label: prop:ch11posterior

results.name: Extreme value representation of L functions of eta products
results.summary: For every eta product, that is every product of the functions eta(m tau) raised to nonnegative integer powers r_m with the sum of m r_m equal to 24 (the thirty multiplicative eta products among them), the L function is entire and equals at every complex point the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at an explicit maximum of exponential clocks, so its values at positive real points are probabilities strictly between zero and one that increase strictly to one.
results.statement: Let $\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)$, $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, be the Dedekind eta function, and let $f(\tau)=\prod_m\eta(m\tau)^{r_m}=q\prod_m\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^{mn})^{r_m}=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nq^n$, where the product runs over positive integers $m$, the $r_m\ge0$ are integers and $\sum_mm\,r_m=24$; let $L(s,f)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}$, which converges absolutely in a right half plane. Let $E_{m,j,n}$ ($m$ with $r_m>0$, $1\le j\le r_m$, $n\ge1$) be independent standard exponential variables and $M_f=\max_m\max_{j\le r_m}\max_{n\ge1}E_{m,j,n}/(2\pi mn)$, whose distribution function is $F_f(y)=\mathbb{P}(M_f\le y)=\prod_mP(my)^{r_m}$ with $P(y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})$, and for $c>0$ let $Q(s,c)=\Gamma(s)^{-1}\int_c^\infty t^{s-1}e^{-t}\,dt$ be the regularised upper incomplete gamma function, entire in $s$ and zero at $s=0,-1,-2,\ldots$. Then $f(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}F_f(y)$ for $y>0$, $L(s,f)$ continues to an entire function, and for every complex $s$, $L(s,f)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[Q(s,2\pi M_f)\bigr]$. For real $s>0$, $L(s,f)=\mathbb{P}(G_s\ge2\pi M_f)$, where $G_s$ has the gamma law of shape $s$ and unit rate and is independent of $M_f$; in particular $0<L(s,f)<1$, and $L(s,f)$ increases strictly to $1$ as $s\to\infty$.
results.label: thm:ch11general

results.name: Squared Kolmogorov variable as a maximum of exponentials and an identity in law with the eta extreme value
results.summary: The square of the largest absolute value of a Brownian bridge, whose law is Kolmogorov's, is in law a maximum of independent exponential variables, and Jacobi's triple product becomes an identity in law linking it to the extreme value law behind the Dedekind eta function.
results.statement: Let $K=\sup_{t\le1}|b_t|$ for a standard Brownian bridge $b$, so that $\mathbb{P}(K\le x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}(-1)^ne^{-2n^2x^2}$ (Kolmogorov's law). Then $K^2$ has the law of the maximum of independent exponential variables, one of rate $2j$ for each even $j\ge2$ and two of rate $2j$ for each odd $j\ge1$. Moreover, let $M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)$ with $E_1,E_2,\ldots$ independent standard exponential variables, so that $\mathbb{P}(M\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})$, and let $M_1,M_2,M_3$ be independent copies of $M$, with $K$ independent of $M_3$. Then $\max(M_1,M_2)\overset{d}{=}\max\bigl(K^2/\pi,\,M_3/2\bigr)$.
results.label: prop:ch11kolmogorov

results.name: Brownian or Bessel functional with the extreme value law behind the Dedekind eta function
results.summary: Asks for a natural Brownian or Bessel functional whose law is the extreme value law behind the Dedekind eta function or Ramanujan's Delta function, or a proof that no first passage or last exit time of a one dimensional diffusion has it.
results.statement: Let $M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)$ with $E_1,E_2,\ldots$ independent standard exponential variables, so that $\mathbb{P}(M\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})$ for $y>0$, and let $M^*$ be the maximum of $24$ independent copies of $M$. Find a natural Brownian or Bessel functional with the law of $M$, or of $M^*$, or show that none exists among first passage and last exit times of one dimensional diffusions.
results.label: prob:ch11brownian

results.name: Reference prior for a conjugacy class of a compact Lie group observed through class function noise
results.summary: When an element of a compact connected simple Lie group is observed through noise whose density is a class function with finite nonsingular Fisher information, Jeffreys' prior is Haar measure, whose image on conjugacy classes is the Sato Tate measure, while the Berger Bernardo reference prior for the class is uniform on the maximal torus, which for SU(2) gives the arcsine law instead of the semicircle law.
results.statement: Let $K$ be a compact, connected and simple Lie group with Haar probability measure $dh$, let $T$ be a maximal torus with Haar probability measure $dt$, $W$ the Weyl group and $T^+$ a Weyl chamber, and let $\varphi\ge0$ be a smooth class function on $K$ with $\int\varphi\,dh=1$. Observe $Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ independent with density $p(y\mid M)=\varphi(M^{-1}y)$ with respect to $dh$, that is $Y=M\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon$ of density $\varphi$, where $M=\eta t\eta^{-1}$ with class parameter $t\in T^+$ and nuisance parameter $u=\eta T\in K/T$. Suppose the Fisher information of this model at $M=e$ is finite and nonsingular. Then: (i) the Fisher metric is $c\,n$ times a fixed bi invariant Riemannian metric on $K$, for a constant $c=c(\varphi)>0$; Jeffreys' prior for $M$ is Haar measure, and its image on conjugacy classes has the Weyl density $|W|^{-1}\prod_{\alpha}|e^{i\alpha(t)}-1|$ (product over all roots $\alpha$) with respect to $dt$, that is, it is the Sato Tate measure of $K$; (ii) the reference prior of the two group algorithm of Berger and Bernardo, ordered as (class, conjugator), namely $\pi(u\mid t)\propto|I_{22}(t,u)|^{1/2}$ and $\pi(t)\propto\exp\bigl\{\int\pi(u\mid t)\log|I_{11\cdot2}(t,u)|^{1/2}\,du\bigr\}$, where $I=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}I_{11}&I_{12}\\I_{21}&I_{22}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ is the Fisher information matrix in the coordinates $(t,u)$ and $I_{11\cdot2}=I_{11}-I_{12}I_{22}^{-1}I_{21}$, is the product of the $K$ invariant probability measure on $K/T$ and the uniform (Haar) measure $dt$ on the Weyl chamber, and its image on classes is the image of Haar measure on $T$. For $K=\mathrm{SU}(2)$ the reference prior for the angle $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ is $d\theta/\pi$, so $x=2\cos\theta$ has the arcsine law, against the Sato Tate prior $\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$; for $K=\mathrm{USp}(4)$ it is uniform on $0\le\theta_2\le\theta_1\le\pi$, against the density proportional to $(\cos\theta_1-\cos\theta_2)^2\sin^2\theta_1\sin^2\theta_2$ given by the Weyl integration formula.
results.label: thm:11brefprior

results.name: Consistency of Bayes factors under equidistribution
results.summary: For any deterministic sequence, such as normalised Frobenius traces, that is equidistributed for a true law with finitely many atoms and finite Kullback Leibler divergence from one candidate law, and with a log likelihood ratio continuous off the atoms, the clipped log Bayes factor between two candidate laws is asymptotically linear in the number of observations, and as the clipping level grows its slope tends to the difference of the divergences of the true law from the two candidates, with no independence assumed.
results.statement:
Fix a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}$, a finite set $D\subset K$, and let $
u$ be Lebesgue measure on $K$ plus counting measure on $D$. Let the candidate laws $P_0,P_1$ and the true law $\mu_0$ be probability measures on $K$ with $
u$ densities $f_0,f_1,m$, so that their atoms lie in $D$. Write $h=\log(f_1/f_0)$, with values in $[-\infty,\infty]$; for a clipping level $M>0$ write $h_M=\max(-M,\min(M,h))$; and for a deterministic sequence $(x_k)$ in $K$ define the clipped log Bayes factor $\log B_n^M=\sum_{k\le n}h_M(x_k)$. Call $(x_k)$ equidistributed for $\mu_0$ relative to $D$ if $n^{-1}\#\{k\le n:x_k=a\}	o\mu_0(\{a\})$ for each $a\in D$ and $n^{-1}\sum_{k\le n,\,x_k
otin D}\delta_{x_k}$ converges weakly to the restriction of $\mu_0$ to $K\setminus D$. Suppose that $(x_k)$ is equidistributed for $\mu_0$ relative to $D$, that $h$ is finite on $D$, that on $K\setminus D$ the function $h$ agrees almost everywhere with a continuous map $	ilde h:K	o[-\infty,\infty]$, through which $h$ is evaluated off $D$, and that $\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_0)<\infty$, where $\mathrm{KL}$ denotes the Kullback Leibler divergence. Then for every $M>0$, $\lim_{n	o\infty}n^{-1}\log B_n^M=\int h_M\,d\mu_0$, and as $M	o\infty$ the right side tends to $\int h\,d\mu_0=\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_0)-\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_1)\in[-\infty,\infty)$. In particular, if $\mu_0=P_0$ the double limit is $-\mathrm{KL}(P_0\|P_1)$.
results.label: thm:12consist

results.name: Bayes factor rates for detecting complex multiplication of elliptic curves
results.summary: For an elliptic curve over the rationals, the clipped Bayes factor of a complex multiplication model against a Sato Tate model with a small atom at zero, computed from the normalised Frobenius traces at the good primes, has an explicit limiting rate per prime, as the clipping level grows, that is negative without complex multiplication and positive with it.
results.statement: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve and $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$, and let $x_p=a_p/\sqrt p\in[-2,2]$ be its normalised Frobenius traces at the primes $p$ of good reduction, $p_1<p_2<\cdots$. Compare the models $M_{\mathrm{ST}}$, under which $x_p\sim(1-\varepsilon)\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}+\varepsilon\delta_0$, and $M_{\mathrm{CM}}$, under which $x_p\sim\frac12\delta_0+\frac12\,\mathrm{arcsine}$, where the Sato Tate law $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$ has density $(2\pi)^{-1}\sqrt{4-x^2}$ and the arcsine law has density $(\pi\sqrt{4-x^2})^{-1}$ on $[-2,2]$. With densities taken with respect to Lebesgue measure on $[-2,2]$ plus counting measure at $0$, the log likelihood ratio of $M_{\mathrm{CM}}$ to $M_{\mathrm{ST}}$ is $h(x)=-\log(1-\varepsilon)-\log(4-x^2)$ for $x\neq0$ and $h(0)=\log\frac1{2\varepsilon}$; for $M>0$ let $h_M=\max(-M,\min(M,h))$ and $\log B_n^M=\sum_{k\le n}h_M(x_{p_k})$. If $E$ has no complex multiplication, $\lim_{M\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\log B_n^M=-1-\log(1-\varepsilon)$. If $E$ has complex multiplication, the limit is $\frac12\log\frac1{2\varepsilon}-\frac12\log(1-\varepsilon)>0$.
results.label: thm:12elliptic

results.name: Brownian bridge limit of the Sato Tate empirical process in families of elliptic curves
results.summary: Asks for which growth rates of the number of primes, measured against the conductor, the normalised Sato Tate empirical process of a random elliptic curve converges to a Brownian bridge and its scaled discrepancy to the Kolmogorov law.
results.statement: (Part (b) of the problem; part (a), the bound $D_n=O(n^{-1/2+\delta})$ for every $\delta>0$ for a single curve, is the conjecture of Akiyama and Tanigawa.) For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication let $p_1<p_2<\cdots$ be its primes of good reduction, $x_p=a_p(E)/\sqrt p\in[-2,2]$ with $a_p(E)=p+1-\#E(\mathbb{F}_p)$, $F_n$ the empirical distribution function of $x_{p_1},\dots,x_{p_n}$, $F_{\mathrm{ST}}$ the distribution function of the Sato Tate law $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}(dx)=(2\pi)^{-1}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx$ on $[-2,2]$, and $D_n=\sup_x|F_n(x)-F_{\mathrm{ST}}(x)|$. Question: let $E$ be chosen uniformly among the curves without complex multiplication of conductor at most $X$, and let $n=\lfloor X^c\rfloor$ with $c>0$ fixed. For which $c$ does $\sqrt n\,(F_n-F_{\mathrm{ST}})\circ F_{\mathrm{ST}}^{-1}$ converge in law to a Brownian bridge as $X\to\infty$, and $\sqrt n\,D_n$ to the Kolmogorov law?
results.label: op:disc

results.name: Inverse problem for automorphy from twisted sums over primes
results.summary: Asks whether rates and fluctuations of the twisted prime sums of a sequence, at the square root scale and uniformly over Dirichlet characters, can decide whether the sequence is close to the normalised Hecke eigenvalues of a holomorphic newform.
results.statement: Question: is there a criterion, stated through quantitative properties of the twisted sums $\sum_{p\le x}x_p\chi(p)\log p$ at the square root scale (rates in the law of large numbers, mean squares on the logarithmic scale, large deviation rates), uniform over Dirichlet characters $\chi$ of growing conductor, that decides whether a sequence $(x_p)$ in $[-2,2]$ indexed by the primes is close to the normalised Hecke eigenvalues $x_p(f)=a_p(f)/p^{(k-1)/2}$ of a holomorphic newform $f$ of weight $k$ with trivial nebentypus, in the sense that $\sum_{p\le x}(x_p-x_p(f))\chi(p)\log p=o(\sqrt x)$ for every $\chi$?
results.label: op:inverse

results.name: Hilbert's eighth problem for GL2 in Thorin form
results.summary: Asks for a probabilistic proof that the heat sum over the zeros of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta is completely monotone, a statement the book shows to be equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis for that L function.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, be Ramanujan's cusp form of weight $12$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$, and let $\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)$. Write the zeros of $\Lambda(s,\Delta)$ as $6\pm i\gamma_k$ with $\operatorname{Re}\gamma_k>0$, and let $k_\Delta(x)=\sum_k e^{-\gamma_k^2x}$ for $x>0$. Prove by a probabilistic argument that $k_\Delta$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$.
results.label: op:thorin

results.name: Extreme value representation for locating zeros and for other newforms
results.summary: Asks whether the law of the maximum in the extreme value representation of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta can locate or count its zeros, and which newforms admit a representation of the same kind.
results.statement: Let $\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$, $q=e^{2\pi iz}$, be Ramanujan's cusp form of weight $12$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with $L$ function $L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}$. Let $M^*$ be the maximum of $24$ independent copies of $M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)$, with $E_n$ independent standard exponential variables, so that $L(s,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\,Q(s,2\pi M^*)$ for every complex $s$, where $Q(s,c)=\Gamma(s,c)/\Gamma(s)$ is the regularised upper incomplete gamma function. (a) Question: can properties of the law of $M^*$, such as the self similarity $F(y)=y^{-12}e^{2\pi(y-1/y)}F(1/y)$ of its distribution function $F$ given by modularity, be used to locate or count the zeros of $L(s,\Delta)$? (b) Question: for which newforms $f$ is there a random variable $M_f$, the maximum of countably many independent variables with distribution functions of the form $(1-e^{-cy})^{\kappa}$ with $c,\kappa>0$, such that $f(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}\,\mathbb{P}(M_f\le y)$ for all $y>0$?
results.label: op:ev

results.name: Second order term of Kemeny constants of supersingular 2 isogeny graphs
results.summary: Asks whether the correction to the first order law for Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs has a limiting distribution across the characteristics, and whether it stays bounded.
results.statement: For primes $N\equiv1\bmod12$ let $K_N$ be the Kemeny constant of simple random walk on the supersingular $2$ isogeny graph in characteristic $N$, which is $3$ regular on $h=(N-1)/12$ vertices; thus $K_N=\sum_{j=2}^{h}(1-\lambda_j/3)^{-1}$, where $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_h$ are the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix other than the eigenvalue $3$, and $K_N/h\to2$ as $N\to\infty$ through these primes. Question: does the empirical distribution of $K_N-2h$ over the primes $N\le Y$ with $N\equiv1\bmod12$ converge as $Y\to\infty$, and is $K_N-2h$ bounded?
results.label: op:kemeny

results.name: Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups for abelian surfaces and effective bounds
results.summary: Asks to extend the book's consistency theorem for Bayes factors between Sato Tate groups to the groups of abelian surfaces and to motives of higher rank, and to bound, polynomially in the logarithm of the conductor and without the Riemann hypothesis, how many primes the identification needs.
results.statement:
The book's consistency theorem for Bayesian identification states the following. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}$ be compact, $D\subset K$ finite, and $
u$ Lebesgue measure on $K$ plus counting measure on $D$; let candidate laws $P_0$, $P_1$ and a true law $\mu_0$ have $
u$ densities $f_0$, $f_1$, $m$, let $h=\log(f_1/f_0)$, with values in $[-\infty,\infty]$, and for a clipping level $M>0$ let $h_M=\max(-M,\min(M,h))$ and $\log B_n^M=\sum_{k\le n}h_M(x_k)$ for a sequence $(x_k)$ in $K$. Suppose that $(x_k)$ is equidistributed for $\mu_0$ relative to $D$, meaning that $n^{-1}\#\{k\le n:x_k=a\}	o\mu_0(\{a\})$ for each $a\in D$ and that $n^{-1}\sum_{k\le n,\,x_k
otin D}\delta_{x_k}$ converges weakly to the restriction of $\mu_0$ to $K\setminus D$; that $h$ is finite on $D$; that on $K\setminus D$ it agrees almost everywhere with a continuous map $K	o[-\infty,\infty]$ through which it is evaluated there; and that the Kullback Leibler divergence $\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_0)$ is finite. Then for every $M$, $\lim_{n	o\infty}n^{-1}\log B_n^M=\int h_M\,d\mu_0$, and as $M	o\infty$ this tends to $\int h\,d\mu_0=\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_0)-\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_1)\in[-\infty,\infty)$. Problem: (a) extend this theorem to the $52$ Sato Tate groups of abelian surfaces, whose laws of the normalised coefficients $(a_1,a_2)$ of the characteristic polynomials of Frobenius can have atoms and components on lower dimensional sets, and to motives of higher rank; (b) make it effective, by bounding the number of primes after which the log Bayes factor favours the true group against every other candidate, polynomially in the logarithm of the conductor and without assuming the Riemann hypothesis.
results.label: op:bayes

results.name: Family limit law of the rank bias of elliptic curves
results.summary: Asks whether, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for the L function of each curve, the fluctuations of the rank bias in weighted sums of Frobenius traces, normalised by the logarithm of the conductor, have a limit law over the elliptic curves of a fixed analytic rank, zero or one, and whether it is the law predicted by their low lying zeros.
results.statement: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ have conductor $N_E$ and analytic rank $r_E$, let $a_p=p+1-\#E(\mathbb{F}_p)$ and $S_E(x)=\sum_{p\le x,\,p\nmid N_E}a_p\log p/p$, and assume the Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,E)$. Then $S_E(x)-(\tfrac12-r_E)\log x$, with $\log x$ uniform on $[0,Y]$ and $Y\to\infty$, converges in law to a distribution $\mu_E$ with mean $C_E$; let $Z_E$ have the law $\mu_E$ shifted to mean zero. Question: as $E$ runs through the curves of conductor at most $X$ and analytic rank $r\in\{0,1\}$, does the law of $Z_E/\log N_E$ converge as $X\to\infty$, and is the limit the one predicted by the low lying zeros of the corresponding orthogonal family?
results.label: op:rankbias
